t: CVE-2020-17103 - BlockedApps Symlink and Windir Registry Manipulation (AbortHydration EoP)
de: Detects the registry manipulation phase of CVE-2020-17103 AbortHydration EoP. Covers two behaviours: 1. An ImagePath value written under the CloudFiles BlockedApps registry key pointing to a user-writable volume path, indicating the symbolic link redirection of BlockedApps to the DEFAULT user's Volatile Environment hive. 2. The windir value under HKU\.DEFAULT\Volatile Environment being overwritten to point to a user-controlled directory (e.g. C:\Users\*), redirecting wermgr.exe resolution to an attacker-planted binary.
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where (RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)^HKEY_USERS.*$" and RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\Software\\Policies\\Microsoft\\CloudFiles\\BlockedApps.*$" and RegistryKey endswith "\\ImagePath" and (RegistryValueData contains "\\Device\\HarddiskVolume" and RegistryValueData contains "\\Users\\")) or (RegistryKey =~ "HKEY_USERS\\.DEFAULT\\Volatile Environment\\windir" and RegistryValueData startswith "C:\\Users\\")

t: CVE-2026-41940 cPanel Service Daemon Suspicious Child Process
de: Detects post-exploitation command execution from CVE-2026-41940, a critical authentication bypass in cPanel and WHM (CVSS 9.8). After bypassing authentication via CRLF injection into cpsrvd session files, attackers execute arbitrary commands through the cpsrvd or cpdavd daemon running as root. Spawning shells, recon tools, download utilities, or interpreters as direct children of these daemons is strongly anomalous.
fp: Custom cPanel plugins or hooks that legitimately invoke shell scripts as cpsrvd children
Administrative cPanel update processes that temporarily spawn interpreters
Monitoring agents operating under the cPanel process context
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/cpsrvd" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/cpsrvd-ssl" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/cpdavd" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/cpdavd-ssl") and ((FolderPath endswith "/bash" or FolderPath endswith "/sh" or FolderPath endswith "/dash" or FolderPath endswith "/zsh" or FolderPath endswith "/ksh" or FolderPath endswith "/tcsh") or (FolderPath endswith "/whoami" or FolderPath endswith "/id" or FolderPath endswith "/uname" or FolderPath endswith "/hostname" or FolderPath endswith "/ifconfig" or FolderPath endswith "/ip" or FolderPath endswith "/netstat" or FolderPath endswith "/ss" or FolderPath endswith "/ps" or FolderPath endswith "/ls") or (FolderPath endswith "/curl" or FolderPath endswith "/wget" or FolderPath endswith "/fetch" or FolderPath endswith "/tftp" or FolderPath endswith "/ftp") or (FolderPath endswith "/python" or FolderPath endswith "/python2" or FolderPath endswith "/python3" or FolderPath endswith "/perl" or FolderPath endswith "/ruby" or FolderPath endswith "/php" or FolderPath endswith "/node"))

t: Atomic MacOS Stealer - Cryptocurrency Wallet Application Replaced
de: Detects Atomic MacOS Stealer replacing an installed cryptocurrency wallet application with an attacker-supplied build. The stealer terminates the running application with pkill, deletes the bundle from /Applications as root using a password phished from the user, downloads a replacement archive and unpacks it back into /Applications with ditto. Ledger Wallet, Trezor Suite and Exodus are the observed targets, fetched as app.zip, apptwo.zip and appex.zip from a /zxc/ path. Those archive names have stayed constant across at least three unrelated hosts since 2025-11, which makes the path segment worth matching independently of the domain. This is distinct from the collection behaviour covered by proc_creation_macos_malware_amos_curl_post.yml: the wallet is not read, it is replaced. A user who subsequently enters a seed phrase enters it into code the operator controls, so a hit warrants treating the wallet contents as lost rather than merely exposed.
fp: Wallet vendors ship their own updaters, but those replace the bundle under the user's own privileges from the vendor domain, not via sudo -S from a /zxc/ path.
An administrator removing one of these applications by hand would match the removal selection only if they used sudo -S with a piped password.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessCommandLine contains "/Applications/Ledger Wallet.app" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/Applications/Trezor Suite.app" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/Applications/Exodus.app") or (FolderPath endswith "/curl" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "/zxc/app.zip" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/zxc/apptwo.zip" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/zxc/appex.zip")) or (FolderPath endswith "/ditto" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "-x -k" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/Applications") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "/tmp/app.zip" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/tmp/apptwo.zip" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/tmp/appex.zip"))
pr: #6209 macOS: cover `launchctl bootstrap`, add AMOS LaunchDaemon install and wallet replacement rules

t: Atomic MacOS Stealer - LaunchDaemon Installed With Piped Password
de: Detects the privilege-escalation step recent Atomic MacOS Stealer variants use to install their LaunchDaemon. The stealer phishes the user's password with a fake system dialog, validates it locally with dscl, then pipes it into sudo to copy a payload to a root-owned location, chown it to root:wheel and bootstrap it as a system daemon. The observable is the piped credential rather than the daemon itself: legitimate tooling that installs a LaunchDaemon runs with privileges it already holds, and does not feed a password into sudo -S on stdin. Complements file_event_macos_malware_amos_persistence.yml, which matches the dropped artefacts of one specific build. Daemon labels vary between builds - com.finder.helper is documented, samples in 2026-08 use labels imitating Apple services such as com.apple.accountsd.helper and com.apple.metadata.mds.worker - so this rule deliberately keys on the installation sequence instead of on a label.
fp: Automation that deliberately supplies a sudo password on stdin, for example unattended provisioning scripts. These are rare on end-user endpoints and worth finding regardless.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessCommandLine contains "sudo -S" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "launchctl bootstrap system" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/Library/LaunchDaemons/" or ProcessCommandLine contains "chown root:wheel")

t: BTR Reforged Kernel Driver Service Changelist ADS Registration

DeviceRegistryEvents

t: ChainDrop Supply-Chain Attack Credential Access via Bun - Linux
de: Detects the ChainDrop (Mini Shai-Hulud variant) second-stage payload harvesting credentials by spawning cloud and code-hosting CLI tools from the Bun runtime. After the "setup.mjs" dropper launches the obfuscated payload under Bun, the malware shells out to "gh", "gcloud", "az" and "azd" to mint access tokens, and on GitHub Actions runners dumps the "Runner.Worker" process memory to recover masked secrets. This rule targets the behaviour rather than the payload filename, so it remains effective if the campaign rotates its script names.

DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/bun" and (InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "node_modules" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "bun-dl-") and ((ProcessCommandLine contains "gh auth token" or ProcessCommandLine contains "gcloud config config-helper" or ProcessCommandLine contains "az account get-access-token" or ProcessCommandLine contains "azd auth token") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "/proc/" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/mem")) and (not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "/node_modules/.bin/"))

t: Change Default File Association To Executable Via Assoc
de: Detects when a program changes the default file association of any extension to an executable. When a file is opened, the default program used to open the file (also called the file association or handler) is checked. File association selections are stored in the Windows Registry and can be edited by users, administrators, or programs that have Registry access or by administrators using the built-in assoc utility. Applications can modify the file association for a given file extension to call an arbitrary program when a file with the given extension is opened.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "Cmd.Exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "assoc " and ProcessCommandLine contains "exefile")) and (not(ProcessCommandLine contains ".exe=exefile"))

t: Chmod Recursive World-Writable Mode on System Directories
de: Detects recursive chmod invocations that grant world-writable permissions on the filesystem root, system directories or home directories. A mode is world-writable when the others-writable bit (value 2) is set, i.e. the octal mode ends in 2/3/6/7 (verified against POSIX bit semantics, 16/16 case consistency). The octal mode is anchored to the chmod argument position to avoid matching unrelated numeric tokens. Recursive world-writable modes on these paths enable backdoor persistence and privilege escalation. The same command on application subdirectories is a common (risky) deployment practice, so only system-critical targets are matched to keep the false- positive rate low.
fp: Rare administrative recursion over system paths, e.g. restoring permissions from a backup script. Apply additional filters as needed before pushing to production.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "/chmod" and ProcessCommandLine matches regex "\\s-[a-zA-Z]*R[a-zA-Z]*(?:\\s|[0-9])|\\s--recursive(?:\\s|$)" and ProcessCommandLine matches regex "chmod(?:\\s+--?[a-zA-Z]+)*\\s+[0-7]*[2367]\\b" and ProcessCommandLine matches regex "\\s/(?:etc|usr|var|boot|home|root|lib|lib64|bin|sbin)(?:\\s|$|/)|\\s/(?:\\s|$)" and (not((ProcessCommandLine contains " /tmp" or (InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "/var/lib/dpkg/info/" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains ".postinst configure"))))
pr: #6529 feat(rules): detect recursive world-writable chmod on system directories

t: Claude Code Session Token Or Bearer Header In Command Line - Linux
de: Detects credential leakage where a Claude or generic LLM bearer token appears in the visible command line of a process. Looks for sk-ant-... session strings and 'Authorization: Bearer sk-' style headers passed via curl, wget, or direct API invocation. Anything in argv is readable by any local user via /proc and is preserved in shell history and audit logs.
fp: Internal red-team or pentest tooling that intentionally passes tokens via curl for replay testing

q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "/curl" or FolderPath endswith "/wget" or FolderPath endswith "/http" or FolderPath endswith "/httpie") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "Authorization: Bearer sk-" or ProcessCommandLine contains "x-api-key: sk-ant-" or ProcessCommandLine contains "x-api-key:sk-ant-")

de: Detects cmd.exe invoked with the environment gate MSBUILDENABLEALLPROPERTYFUNCTIONS=1 on its command line. t: COM TypeLib Hijack Via Scriptlet Or Remote Moniker
de: Detects a type library whose win32/win64 path is set to a "script:" moniker, a ".sct" scriptlet or a URL. Type libraries are registered to DLL, OCX or TLB files. Windows resolves a "script:" path through scrobj.dll and runs the scriptlet in whichever process loads the type library. Attackers register the hijack under the user's own HKCU\Software\Classes\TypeLib (no admin rights needed) for a type library that Explorer loads at logon, such as the Microsoft Scriptlet Library {EAB22AC0-30C1-11CF-A7EB-0000C05BAE0B}.
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\TypeLib.*$" and (RegistryKey contains "\\win32" or RegistryKey contains "\\win64") and ((RegistryValueData startswith "script:" or RegistryValueData startswith "http:" or RegistryValueData startswith "https:") or RegistryValueData contains ".sct")

t: Command Execution via Git Ext Transport - Linux
de: Detects Git's "ext::" remote helper transport, which runs the command named in the remote URL and wires its stdin and stdout to the Git protocol stream. Git classifies "ext" as a known- dangerous protocol and ships it with a default policy of "never", so the helper runs only after protocol.ext.allow or GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL loosens that policy, frequently on the attacker's own command line. The URL reaches Git from the command line, from a repository-local config, or from a .gitmodules entry during recursive submodule initialization, so the scheme does not always appear in the invoking command.
fp: Deliberate use of the ext transport to customize a connection, such as an "ext::ssh -i /path/to/key user@host %S repo" remote. This requires an administrator to override the default protocol policy first and is worth confirming regardless.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "/git" and ProcessCommandLine contains " remote-ext ") and (not(ProcessCommandLine contains " remote-ext --help"))) or (((FolderPath endswith "/git" and ProcessCommandLine contains "ext::") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " clone " or ProcessCommandLine contains " fetch " or ProcessCommandLine contains " pull " or ProcessCommandLine contains " push " or ProcessCommandLine contains " remote " or ProcessCommandLine contains " ls-remote " or ProcessCommandLine contains " submodule" or ProcessCommandLine contains " archive " or ProcessCommandLine contains " config ")) and (not(((ProcessCommandLine contains " help " or ProcessCommandLine contains "--help") or (ProcessCommandLine contains " commit " or ProcessCommandLine contains " tag " or ProcessCommandLine contains " -m "))))) or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/git" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains " remote-ext ")
pr: #6217 new: Command Execution via Git Ext Transport

t: Command Execution via Git Ext Transport - Windows
de: Detects Git's "ext::" remote helper transport, which runs the command named in the remote URL and wires its stdin and stdout to the Git protocol stream. Git classifies "ext" as a known- dangerous protocol and ships it with a default policy of "never", so the helper runs only after protocol.ext.allow or GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL loosens that policy, frequently on the attacker's own command line. Git for Windows exposes the helper either as a git.exe subcommand or as a separate git-remote-ext.exe, so this rule covers both invocation forms.
fp: Deliberate use of the ext transport to customize a connection, such as an "ext::ssh -i /path/to/key user@host %S repo" remote. This requires an administrator to override the default protocol policy first and is worth confirming regardless.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (((FolderPath endswith "\\git.exe" and ProcessCommandLine contains " remote-ext ") or FolderPath endswith "\\git-remote-ext.exe") and (not(ProcessCommandLine contains " remote-ext --help"))) or (((FolderPath endswith "\\git.exe" and ProcessCommandLine contains "ext::") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " clone " or ProcessCommandLine contains " fetch " or ProcessCommandLine contains " pull " or ProcessCommandLine contains " push " or ProcessCommandLine contains " remote " or ProcessCommandLine contains " ls-remote " or ProcessCommandLine contains " submodule" or ProcessCommandLine contains " archive " or ProcessCommandLine contains " config ")) and (not(((ProcessCommandLine contains " help " or ProcessCommandLine contains "--help") or (ProcessCommandLine contains " commit " or ProcessCommandLine contains " tag " or ProcessCommandLine contains " -m "))))) or ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\git.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\git-remote-ext.exe") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "remote-ext")

de: Detects execution of DAEMON Tools Lite binaries with file versions known to be compromised (12.5.0.2421 to 12.5.0.2434). As part of a supply chain attack discovered in early May 2026, attackers trojanized three binaries inside DAEMON Tools Lite installations signed by Disc Soft Limited: DTHelper.exe, DiscSoftBusServiceLite.exe, and DTShellHlp.exe. The malicious payloads include an information collector, a minimalistic backdoor (shell command execution, file download, in-memory shellcode execution), and QUIC RAT — a C++ implant that injects into notepad.exe and conhost.exe and supports multiple C2 protocols. The campaign commenced on April 8, 2026 and affected users across more than 100 countries.

DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\DTHelper.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\DTProHelper.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\DiscSoftBusServiceLite.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\DTShellHlp.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("DTHelper.exe", "DTProHelper.exe", "DiscSoftBusServiceLite.exe", "DTShellHlp.exe"))) and (ProcessVersionInfoProductVersion in~ ("12.5.0.2421", "12.5.0.2422", "12.5.0.2423", "12.5.0.2424", "12.5.0.2425", "12.5.0.2426", "12.5.0.2427", "12.5.0.2428", "12.5.0.2429", "12.5.0.2430", "12.5.0.2431", "12.5.0.2432", "12.5.0.2433", "12.5.0.2434"))

t: Contagious Interview Implant Run Key Persistence
de: Detects the HKCU Run values registered by the components of a DPRK "Contagious Interview" chain. The Node.js implant uses "reg.exe add" to set "Microsoft Realtime Aggregator" to "wscript.exe <home>\.vs_cache\main.vbs" for itself and "SettingSyncResCache" to "wscript.exe <...>\Win32\ResCache\nsm-launch.vbs" for the NetSupport client it installs; the native PrintHost.exe collector sets "PrintSpoolHost" to its own path with "--background". On the operator self-delete command (ss_del) the implant deletes its own value and the names "NvidiaDriverUpdate", "VScode.Update.Publisher" and "Microsoft Realtime Agreegator" (likely earlier builds); the misspelt one is kept here.
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run.*$" and ((RegistryKey endswith "\\SettingSyncResCache" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Microsoft Realtime Aggregator" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Microsoft Realtime Agreegator" or RegistryKey endswith "\\PrintSpoolHost") or (RegistryValueData contains "\\.vs_cache\\main.vbs" or RegistryValueData contains "\\Win32\\ResCache\\nsm-launch.vbs" or RegistryValueData contains "\\Microsoft\\Windows\\PrintHost\\PrintHost.exe"))
pr: #6500 new: Contagious Interview (DPRK) EtherHiding Chain - Emerging Threat And Hunting Rules

t: Contagious Interview Loader Artefacts Created In User .vs_cache Folder - Windows

DeviceFileEvents
| where FolderPath contains "\\.vs_cache\\" and (FolderPath endswith "\\main.js" or FolderPath endswith "\\main.vbs" or FolderPath endswith "\\key-agent.js" or FolderPath endswith "\\vs.sid" or FolderPath endswith "\\mmc.pid" or FolderPath endswith "\\mmc.log" or FolderPath endswith "\\log.log")

t: Creation Exe for Service with Unquoted Path
de: Adversaries may execute their own malicious payloads by hijacking vulnerable file path references. Adversaries can take advantage of paths that lack surrounding quotations by placing an executable in a higher level directory within the path, so that Windows will choose the adversary's executable to launch.
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where FolderPath =~ "C:\\program.exe"

t: Creation of a Local Hidden User Account by Registry
de: Detects creation or modification of local account name entries ending with a dollar sign under the SAM Users Names registry path. | where (ActionType =~ "RegistryKeyCreated" and RegistryKey endswith "$" and RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\SAM\\SAM\\Domains\\Account\\Users\\Names.*$") or (ActionType =~ "RegistryValueSet" and RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\SAM\\SAM\\Domains\\Account\\Users\\Names.*$" and RegistryKey endswith "$\\(Default)")

de: Detects changes to the "Ports" registry key with data that includes a Windows path or a file with a suspicious extension. This could be an attempt to exploit CVE-2020-1048 - a Windows Print Spooler elevation of privilege vulnerability.
fp: New printer port install on host

| where RegistryKey contains "\\Microsoft\\Windows NT\\CurrentVersion\\Ports" and (RegistryValueData contains ".bat" or RegistryValueData contains ".com" or RegistryValueData contains ".dll" or RegistryValueData contains ".exe" or RegistryValueData contains ".ps1" or RegistryValueData contains ".vbe" or RegistryValueData contains ".vbs" or RegistryValueData contains "C:")

t: CVE-2020-17103 - Fake wermgr.exe Process Execution (AbortHydration EoP)
de: Detects the process execution phase of CVE-2020-17103 AbortHydration EoP. Covers two behaviours: 1. A non-standard wermgr.exe (outside System32) spawning conhost.exe as SYSTEM, indicating successful WER task hijack and SYSTEM token capture. 2. A non-standard wermgr.exe launched by svchost.exe with the -upload argument at System integrity, indicating the WER QueueReporting task executing the attacker-planted binary.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\Windows\\System32\\conhost.exe" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\wermgr.exe" and ProcessIntegrityLevel =~ "System") or (FolderPath endswith "\\wermgr.exe" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "wermgr.exe" and ProcessCommandLine contains "-upload") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\Windows\\System32\\svchost.exe" and ProcessIntegrityLevel =~ "System")) and (not((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\Windows\\System32\\wermgr.exe" and FolderPath endswith "\\Windows\\System32\\wermgr.exe")))
pr: #6022 NEWRULE: AbortHydration MiniPlasma Behaviour (Nightmare Eclipse)

t: CVE-2026-21509 Microsoft Office Zero-Day Exploitation - APT28 Operation Neusploit
de: Detects exploitation attempts of CVE-2026-21509, a Microsoft Office security feature bypass vulnerability actively exploited by APT28 (Fancy Bear/UAC-0001) in Operation Neusploit. The vulnerability allows attackers to bypass OLE mitigations through specially crafted RTF documents, leading to WebDAV connections, malicious DLL downloads, and deployment of MiniDoor email stealer or PixyNetLoader/Covenant Grunt implants. This rule detects key indicators including suspicious Office process behavior, WebDAV connections, malicious file creation, and associated network activity.
fp: Legitimate Office macros or add-ins that use WebDAV functionality
Corporate environments with legitimate WebDAV-based document collaboration
Scheduled tasks created by IT administrators using rundll32
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\WINWORD.EXE" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\EXCEL.EXE" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\POWERPNT.EXE" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\OUTLOOK.EXE") and (FolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\regsvr32.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "WebClient" or ProcessCommandLine contains "WebDAV" or ProcessCommandLine contains "davclnt" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\\\@SSL")) or ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\WINWORD.EXE" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\EXCEL.EXE" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\POWERPNT.EXE") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "net use" or ProcessCommandLine contains "WebClient" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\\\@SSL\\")) or ((FolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\regsvr32.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "UIClassRegister" or ProcessCommandLine contains "EhStorShell.dll")) or (FolderPath endswith "\\schtasks.exe" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "/Create" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/SC ONLOGON" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/SC DAILY") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "rundll32" and ProcessCommandLine contains ".dll")) or (FolderPath endswith "\\outlook.exe" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "/regserver" or ProcessCommandLine contains "VbaProject.OTM"))
pr: #5870 CVE-2026-21509 APT28 Office Exploitation Detection Rules

de: Detects exploitation of CVE-2026-31431 (Copy Fail) execution patterns. the reference PoC's os.system() pattern (python3 spawns "sh -c <suid_binary>") and download of the public exploit from copy.fail. For broader shellcode-execution and SUID-spawn patterns derived from this exploit, see the companion generic rules.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/python" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/python3" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/python3.10" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/python3.11" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/python3.12" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/python3.13") and (FolderPath endswith "/sh" or FolderPath endswith "/dash" or FolderPath endswith "/bash" or FolderPath endswith "/ksh" or FolderPath endswith "/zsh" or FolderPath endswith "/ash" or FolderPath endswith "/tcsh" or FolderPath endswith "/csh") and ProcessCommandLine contains "-c " and (ProcessCommandLine endswith "su" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "sudo" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "passwd" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "mount" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "newgrp" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "gpasswd" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "chfn" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "chsh" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "ping" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "newuidmap" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "newgidmap" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "pkexec" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "fusermount" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "fusermount3" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "expiry")) or ((FolderPath endswith "/curl" or FolderPath endswith "/wget") and ProcessCommandLine contains "https://copy.fail/exp")
pr: #5968 new: CVE-2026-31431 Copy Fail Exploit Detection Rules

de: Detects exploitation of CVE-2026-41651, a TOCTOU race condition in PackageKit (versions 1.0.2-1.3.4) that allows an unprivileged user to escalate privileges to root by abusing the InstallFiles() D-Bus method with the SIMULATE flag to bypass polkit authorization. The exploit crafts a malicious .deb package whose postinst script runs as root, creating a SUID copy of bash in a user-writable directory. Two detection angles are covered: - (1) the postinst script invoking 'install' to stamp a SUID bit on bash and drop it into a writable path (/tmp or /home). - (2) subsequent execution of that SUID shell with the '-p' flag to retain the elevated effective UID. Note: /tmp is the original exploit target; systems with nosuid on /tmp force the attacker to use other writable location
fp: Legitimate packaging or build scripts installing bash with elevated permissions outside standard system paths (very unlikely)
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "/install" and ProcessCommandLine startswith "install -m 4755 /bin/bash" and ProcessCommandLine endswith ".suid_bash") or ProcessCommandLine contains ".suid_bash -p -c id" or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/packagekitd" and FolderPath endswith "/dpkg" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "--unpack" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/.pk-payload-"))
pr: #5960 new: CVE-2026-41651 Pack2TheRoot detection rules and generic Linux LPE coverage

t: CVE-2026-41940 cPanel Session File Written by Unexpected Process
de: Detects suspicious writes to cPanel session files by processes other than the legitimate cpsrvd daemon, or session files with malformed names containing URL-encoded CRLF characters as a direct artifact of CVE-2026-41940 exploitation. Requires auditd with session directory monitoring or Sysmon for Linux.
fp: Administrative backup or migration tools in cPanel that copy session directories
Development or testing environments with custom cPanel session handling
Legitimate session filenames may contain hex strings but never URL-encoded CR/LF
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where ((FolderPath startswith "/var/cpanel/sessions/" or FolderPath startswith "/usr/local/cpanel/sessions/") and (not((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/cpsrvd" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/cpsrvd-ssl" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/cpdavd" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/cpdavd-ssl")))) or ((FolderPath startswith "/var/cpanel/sessions/" or FolderPath startswith "/usr/local/cpanel/sessions/") and (FolderPath contains "%0d" or FolderPath contains "%0a"))
pr: #6006 CVE-2026-41940 - cPanel and WHM CRLF authentication bypass detection

de: Detects indicators of the DAEMON Tools supply chain attack, which involves the use of a backdoor in DAEMON Tools software to download and execute malicious payloads. The detection focuses on specific parent processes and command line patterns associated with the attack.

| where ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\DTHelper.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\DTProHelper.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\DiscSoftBusServiceLite.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\DTShellHlp.exe") and FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" and ProcessCommandLine contains "powershell -NoProfile -Command") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "http://38.180.107.76" or (ProcessCommandLine contains "New-Object System.Net.WebClient" and ProcessCommandLine contains "DownloadFile" and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Windows\\Temp\\envchk.exe") or ((ProcessCommandLine contains "\\ProgramData\\Microsoft\\mcrypto.chiper" or ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Windows\\Temp\\crypto.dll") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "DownloadFile" and ProcessCommandLine contains "rundll32.exe" and ProcessCommandLine contains "mcrypto_clean")))
pr: #5988 new: add DAEMON Tools Lite supply chain attack detection rules

de: Detects execution of the legitimate Autoit3 utility from a suspicious parent process. AutoIt3.exe is used within the DarkGate infection chain to execute shellcode that performs process injection and connects to the DarkGate command-and-control server.

| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\Autoit3.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "AutoIt3.exe") and (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\KeyScramblerLogon.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\msiexec.exe")) and (not((FolderPath endswith ":\\Program Files (x86)\\AutoIt3\\AutoIt3.exe" or FolderPath endswith ":\\Program Files\\AutoIt3\\AutoIt3.exe")))

| where (FolderPath endswith "\\net.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\net1.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "user" and ProcessCommandLine contains "add" and ProcessCommandLine contains "DarkGate" and ProcessCommandLine contains "SafeMode")

t: Default RDP Port Changed to Non Standard Port
de: Detects changes to the default RDP port. Remote desktop is a common feature in operating systems. It allows a user to log into a remote system using an interactive session with a graphical user interface. Microsoft refers to its implementation of the Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) as Remote Desktop Services (RDS).
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where RegistryKey endswith "\\Control\\Terminal Server\\WinStations\\RDP-Tcp\\PortNumber" and (not(RegistryValueData =~ "DWORD (0x00000d3d)"))

q:

| where FolderPath endswith "\\schtasks.exe" and (ProcessCommandLine contains " /delete " and ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)/tn .*" and ProcessCommandLine contains " /f")

q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\schtasks.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "schtasks.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "-delete" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/delete" or ProcessCommandLine contains "–delete" or ProcessCommandLine contains "—delete" or ProcessCommandLine contains "―delete") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Windows\\BitLocker" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Windows\\ExploitGuard" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Windows\\SystemRestore\\SR" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Windows\\UpdateOrchestrator\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Windows\\Windows Defender\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Windows\\WindowsBackup\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Windows\\WindowsUpdate\\")

t: Deletion of Volume Shadow Copies via WMI with PowerShell
de: Detects deletion of Windows Volume Shadow Copies with PowerShell code and Get-WMIObject. This technique is used by numerous ransomware families such as Sodinokibi/REvil

t: Directory Service Restore Mode(DSRM) Registry Value Tampering
de: Detects changes to "DsrmAdminLogonBehavior" registry value. During a Domain Controller (DC) promotion, administrators create a Directory Services Restore Mode (DSRM) local administrator account with a password that rarely changes. The DSRM account is an “Administrator” account that logs in with the DSRM mode when the server is booting up to restore AD backups or recover the server from a failure. Attackers could abuse DSRM account to maintain their persistence and access to the organization's Active Directory. If the "DsrmAdminLogonBehavior" value is set to "0", the administrator account can only be used if the DC starts in DSRM. If the "DsrmAdminLogonBehavior" value is set to "1", the administrator account can only be used if the local AD DS service is stopped. If the "DsrmAdminLogonBehavior" value is set to "2", the administrator account can always be used.
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where RegistryKey endswith "\\Control\\Lsa\\DsrmAdminLogonBehavior" and (not(RegistryValueData =~ "DWORD (0x00000000)"))

q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where (RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)^HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet001\\Control\\Session Manager\\kernel.*$" and (RegistryKey contains "MitigationOptions" or RegistryKey contains "MitigationAuditOptions")) and (not((RegistryValueData in~ ("-", "(empty)"))))
pr: #5895 feat: addition of EDR disabling through mitigation options

de: Detects email exfiltration via powershell cmdlets
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "Add-PSSnapin" and ProcessCommandLine contains "Get-Recipient" and ProcessCommandLine contains "-ExpandProperty" and ProcessCommandLine contains "EmailAddresses" and ProcessCommandLine contains "SmtpAddress" and ProcessCommandLine contains "-hidetableheaders")

de: Detects the Emotet Epoch4 loader as reported by @malware_traffic back in 2022. The ".lnk" file was delivered via phishing campaign.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\explorer.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe") and (FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "findstr" and ProcessCommandLine contains ".vbs" and ProcessCommandLine contains ".lnk")

de: Detects changes to the "NoLMHash" registry value in order to allow Windows to store LM Hashes. By setting this registry value to "0" (DWORD), Windows will be allowed to store a LAN manager hash of your password in Active Directory and local SAM databases.
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where RegistryKey endswith "System\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\Lsa\\NoLMHash" and RegistryValueData =~ "DWORD (0x00000000)"

de: Detects changes to the "NoLMHash" registry value in order to allow Windows to store LM Hashes. By setting this registry value to "0" (DWORD), Windows will be allowed to store a LAN manager hash of your password in Active Directory and local SAM databases.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessCommandLine contains "\\System\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\Lsa" and ProcessCommandLine contains "NoLMHash" and ProcessCommandLine contains " 0"

t: Esentutl Volume Shadow Copy Service Keys
de: Detects the volume shadow copy service initialization and processing via esentutl. Registry keys such as HKLM\\System\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\VSS\\Diag\\VolSnap\\Volume are captured.
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where (RegistryKey contains "System\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\VSS" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "esentutl.exe") and (not(RegistryKey contains "System\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\VSS\\Start"))

t: Esentutl Write To Alternate Data Stream
de: Detects usage of "esentutl.exe" in its copy/duplicate mode (/y /d) where the destination is an NTFS Alternate Data Stream (ADS). Adversaries abuse this LOLBin to stash an executable payload inside an ADS in order to hide it from directory listings and evade detection.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\esentutl.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "esentutl.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " /y" and ProcessCommandLine contains " /d") and ProcessCommandLine matches regex "\\\\[^\\\\ ]+:[^\\\\/ ]"
pr: #6092 Add ADS abuse and signed-binary LOLBIN detection rules

t: ESXi Admin Permission Assigned To Account Via ESXCLI
de: Detects execution of the "esxcli" command with the "system" and "permission" flags in order to assign admin permissions to an account.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "/esxcli" and ProcessCommandLine contains "system" and (ProcessCommandLine contains " permission " and ProcessCommandLine contains " set" and ProcessCommandLine contains "Admin")

t: ETW Logging Disabled In .NET Processes - Sysmon Registry
de: Potential adversaries stopping ETW providers recording loaded .NET assemblies.
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where (RegistryKey endswith "SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\.NETFramework\\ETWEnabled" and RegistryValueData =~ "DWORD (0x00000000)") or ((RegistryKey endswith "\\COMPlus_ETWEnabled" or RegistryKey endswith "\\COMPlus_ETWFlags") and (RegistryValueData in~ ("0", "DWORD (0x00000000)")))

t: ETW Logging Tamper In .NET Processes Via CommandLine
de: Detects changes to environment variables related to ETW logging via the CommandLine. This could indicate potential adversaries stopping ETW providers recording loaded .NET assemblies.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessCommandLine contains "COMPlus_ETWEnabled" or ProcessCommandLine contains "COMPlus_ETWFlags"

t: ETW Tampering (disable event tracing / unhook ntdll)
au: Entroprism (Beijing Yijun Foreign Trade Co., Ltd.)
de: Detects attempts to tamper with ETW or unhook ntdll to impair event tracing defenses.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessCommandLine contains "EtwEventWrite" or ProcessCommandLine contains "ntdll!Etw") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "NtProtectVirtualMemory" or ProcessCommandLine contains "ntdll.dll")
pr: #6557 Add Entroprism AIP self-built detection rules (6 rules)

au: @neu5ron, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Jonhnathan Ribeiro, oscd.community
de: Detects command line activity that attempts to tamper with Event Tracing for Windows (ETW) by clearing or disabling trace logs or providers. Adversaries may target ETW to blind security tooling and evade detection by removing visibility into process activity, network connections, and other telemetry sources. Techniques include clearing logs via wevtutil, disabling trace sessions via logman, and removing or modifying ETW providers using PowerShell cmdlets such as Remove-EtwTraceProvider and Set-EtwTraceProvider.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\wevtutil.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "wevtutil.exe") and (((ProcessCommandLine contains " cl " or ProcessCommandLine contains "clear-log") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "-Trace" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/Trace" or ProcessCommandLine contains "–Trace" or ProcessCommandLine contains "—Trace" or ProcessCommandLine contains "―Trace")) or ((ProcessCommandLine contains " sl " or ProcessCommandLine contains "set-log") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "-e:false" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/e:false" or ProcessCommandLine contains "–e:false" or ProcessCommandLine contains "—e:false" or ProcessCommandLine contains "―e:false")))) or ((FolderPath endswith "\\logman.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "Logman.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "update" and ProcessCommandLine contains "trace" and ProcessCommandLine contains "--p" and ProcessCommandLine contains "-ets")) or (((FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.dll"))) and (ProcessCommandLine contains "Remove-EtwTraceProvider" or (ProcessCommandLine contains "Set-EtwTraceProvider" and ProcessCommandLine contains "0x11") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "Set-EtwTraceProvider" and ProcessCommandLine contains " 17") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "Set-EtwTraceProvider" and ProcessCommandLine contains "'17'") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "Set-EtwTraceProvider" and ProcessCommandLine contains "\"17\"")))

de: Detects the deletion of the Exchange PowerShell cmdlet History logs which may indicate an attempt to destroy forensic evidence
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where ActionType =~ "FileDeleted" and (FolderPath contains "\\Logging\\CmdletInfra\\LocalPowerShell\\Cmdlet\\" and FolderPath contains "_Cmdlet_")

de: Detects adding and using Exchange PowerShell snap-ins to export mailbox data. As seen used by HAFNIUM and APT27
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (((FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("PowerShell.EXE", "pwsh.dll"))) and ProcessCommandLine contains "Add-PSSnapin" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "Microsoft.Exchange.Powershell.Snapin" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Microsoft.Exchange.Management.PowerShell.SnapIn")) and (not((InitiatingProcessFolderPath =~ "C:\\Windows\\System32\\msiexec.exe" and ProcessCommandLine contains "$exserver=Get-ExchangeServer ([Environment]::MachineName) -ErrorVariable exerr 2> $null")))

de: Detects indirect command execution via Program Compatibility Assistant "pcwrun.exe" leveraging the follina (CVE-2022-30190) vulnerability
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\pcwrun.exe" and ProcessCommandLine contains "../"

t: Execution DLL of Choice Using WAB.EXE
de: This rule detects that the path to the DLL written in the registry is different from the default one. Launched WAB.exe tries to load the DLL from Registry.
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where RegistryKey endswith "\\Software\\Microsoft\\WAB\\DLLPath" and (not(RegistryValueData =~ "%CommonProgramFiles%\\System\\wab32.dll"))

t: Execution Of Binary Dropped By Compromised Jscrambler Npm Package
de: Detects execution of the binary dropped (infostealer) by the compromised jscrambler npm package. The loader (dist/setup.js) decompresses a platform-matched payload from dist/intro.js into a randomly named with a .exe suffix inside the OS temp directory and launches it.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\node" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "dist/setup.js" and ProcessCommandLine endswith ".exe" and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\"
pr: #6157 Adding jscrambler npm supply chain attack detection case

de: Detects process creation events where the Image field lacks an absolute path, which occurs when the backing file no longer exists on disk at the time of logging - commonly caused by Process Ghosting or other unorthodox process creation techniques.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (not(FolderPath contains "\\")) and (not((isnull(FolderPath) or (FolderPath in~ ("-", "")) or ((FolderPath in~ ("MemCompression", "Registry", "System", "vmmem", "vmmemWSL")) or (ProcessCommandLine in~ ("MemCompression", "Registry", "vmmem", "vmmemWSL"))))))

t: Execution of Powershell Script in Public Folder
de: This rule detects execution of PowerShell scripts located in the "C:\Users\Public" folder
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "-f C:\\Users\\Public" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-f \"C:\\Users\\Public" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-f %Public%" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-fi C:\\Users\\Public" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-fi \"C:\\Users\\Public" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-fi %Public%" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-fil C:\\Users\\Public" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-fil \"C:\\Users\\Public" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-fil %Public%" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-file C:\\Users\\Public" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-file \"C:\\Users\\Public" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-file %Public%")

de: Detects the use of stordiag.exe to execute schtasks.exe systeminfo.exe and fltmc.exe
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\stordiag.exe" and (FolderPath endswith "\\schtasks.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\systeminfo.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\fltmc.exe")) and (not((InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "c:\\windows\\system32\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "c:\\windows\\syswow64\\")))

de: Detects using WorkFolders.exe to execute an arbitrary control.exe
fp: Legitimate usage of the uncommon Windows Work Folders feature.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\control.exe" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\WorkFolders.exe") and (not(FolderPath =~ "C:\\Windows\\System32\\control.exe"))

t: Expand Write To Alternate Data Stream
de: Detects usage of "expand.exe" where the destination is an NTFS Alternate Data Stream (ADS). Adversaries abuse "expand.exe" to copy a (potentially remote) file into an ADS in order to hide a payload and evade detection.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\expand.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "expand.exe") and ProcessCommandLine matches regex "\\\\[^\\\\ ]+:[^\\\\/ ]"
pr: #6092 Add ADS abuse and signed-binary LOLBIN detection rules

t: Exploitation Attempt Of CVE-2020-1472 - Execution of ZeroLogon PoC
de: Detects the execution of the commonly used ZeroLogon PoC executable.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" and (FolderPath endswith "\\cool.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\zero.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "Administrator" and ProcessCommandLine contains "-c")) and ((ProcessCommandLine contains "taskkill" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/f" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/im") or ProcessCommandLine contains "powershell")

de: Detects the exploitation of Zoho ManageEngine Desktop Central Java Deserialization vulnerability reported as CVE-2020-10189
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "DesktopCentral_Server\\jre\\bin\\java.exe" and (FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\bitsadmin.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\systeminfo.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\net.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\net1.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\reg.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\query.exe")

au: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), oscd.community, Jonhnathan Ribeiro
de: Detects exploitation attempt of privilege escalation vulnerability via SetupComplete.cmd and PartnerSetupComplete.cmd described in CVE-2019-1378
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "\\cmd.exe" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "/c" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "C:\\Windows\\Setup\\Scripts\\") and (InitiatingProcessCommandLine endswith "SetupComplete.cmd" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine endswith "PartnerSetupComplete.cmd")) and (not((FolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\System32\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\WinSxS\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\Setup\\")))

de: Detects suspicious starts of explorer.exe that use the /NOUACCHECK flag that allows to run all sub processes of that newly started explorer.exe without any UAC checks
fp: Unknown how many legitimate software products use that method
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\explorer.exe" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/NOUACCHECK") and (not((InitiatingProcessCommandLine =~ "C:\\Windows\\system32\\svchost.exe -k netsvcs -p -s Schedule" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath =~ "C:\\Windows\\System32\\svchost.exe")))

t: Exports Critical Registry Keys To a File
de: Detects the export of a crital Registry key to a file.
fp: Dumping hives for legitimate purpouse i.e. backup or forensic investigation
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\regedit.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "REGEDIT.EXE") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " -E " or ProcessCommandLine contains " /E " or ProcessCommandLine contains " –E " or ProcessCommandLine contains " —E " or ProcessCommandLine contains " ―E ") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "hklm" or ProcessCommandLine contains "hkey_local_machine") and (ProcessCommandLine endswith "\\system" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "\\sam" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "\\security")

de: Detects initial execution of FakeUpdates/SocGholish malware via wscript that later executes commands via cmd or powershell.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\wscript.exe" and (InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains ".zip" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "update" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains ".js") and (InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "Chrome" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "Edge" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "Firefox" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "Opera" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "Brave" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "Vivaldi") and (FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe")

t: Fax Service Binary Path Modified via Sc.exe
de: Detects attempts to modify the Fax service binary path using sc.exe.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\sc.exe" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "config" and ProcessCommandLine contains "Fax" and ProcessCommandLine contains "binPath")
pr: #6535 Add Fax service configuration detection and regression tests

t: Fax Service DLL Search Order Hijack
de: The Fax service attempts to load ualapi.dll, which is non-existent. An attacker can then (side)load their own malicious DLL using this service.
q:
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\fxssvc.exe" and FolderPath endswith "ualapi.dll") and (not(FolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\WinSxS\\"))

t: Fax Service DLL Search Order Hijack
de: The Fax service attempts to load ualapi.dll, which is non-existent. An attacker can then (side)load their own malicious DLL using this service.
q:
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\fxssvc.exe" and FolderPath endswith "ualapi.dll") and (not(FolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\WinSxS\\"))
pr: #6279 🩺 add regression data from evtx-attack-samples

t: Fax Service ImagePath Modified to PowerShell
de: Detects modification of the Fax service ImagePath to point to PowerShell.
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where RegistryKey endswith "\\Services\\Fax\\ImagePath" and RegistryValueData contains "powershell.exe"
pr: #6535 Add Fax service configuration detection and regression tests

t: File Creation In Suspicious Directory By Msdt.EXE
de: Detects msdt.exe creating files in suspicious directories which could be a sign of exploitation of either Follina or Dogwalk vulnerabilities
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\msdt.exe" and (FolderPath contains "\\Desktop\\" or FolderPath contains "\\Start Menu\\Programs\\Startup\\" or FolderPath contains "C:\\PerfLogs\\" or FolderPath contains "C:\\ProgramData\\" or FolderPath contains "C:\\Users\\Public\\")

t: File Decoded From Base64/Hex Via Certutil.EXE
au: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Jonhnathan Ribeiro, oscd.community
de: Detects the execution of certutil with either the "decode" or "decodehex" flags to decode base64 or hex encoded files. This can be abused by attackers to decode an encoded payload before execution
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\certutil.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "CertUtil.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "-decode " or ProcessCommandLine contains "/decode " or ProcessCommandLine contains "–decode " or ProcessCommandLine contains "—decode " or ProcessCommandLine contains "―decode " or ProcessCommandLine contains "-decodehex " or ProcessCommandLine contains "/decodehex " or ProcessCommandLine contains "–decodehex " or ProcessCommandLine contains "—decodehex " or ProcessCommandLine contains "―decodehex ")

t: File Deletion via Find and Shred
de: Detects the find command executing shred via the -exec flag to perform bulk secure deletion of files. Unlike plain rm, shred overwrites file contents before unlinking, making recovery significantly harder. Attackers use this combination to wipe forensic artifacts such as logs, credentials, and shell history across entire directory trees in a single command.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "/find" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "-exec" and ProcessCommandLine contains "shred")
pr: #6242 update: linux anti forensics rules

t: File Download And Execution Via IEExec.EXE
de: Detects execution of the IEExec utility to download and execute files
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\IEExec.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "IEExec.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "http://" or ProcessCommandLine contains "https://")

t: File Download From IP Based URL Via CertOC.EXE
de: Detects when a user downloads a file from an IP based URL using CertOC.exe
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\certoc.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "CertOC.exe") and ProcessCommandLine matches regex "://[0-9]{1,3}\\.[0-9]{1,3}\\.[0-9]{1,3}\\.[0-9]{1,3}" and ProcessCommandLine contains "-GetCACAPS"

t: File Download Using Notepad++ GUP Utility
de: Detects execution of the Notepad++ updater (gup) from a process other than Notepad++ to download files.
fp: Other parent processes other than notepad++ using GUP that are not currently identified
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\GUP.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "gup.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " -unzipTo " and ProcessCommandLine contains "http")) and (not(InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\notepad++.exe"))

t: File Download Via Bitsadmin To A Suspicious Target Folder
au: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
de: Detects usage of bitsadmin downloading a file to a suspicious target folder
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\bitsadmin.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "bitsadmin.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " /transfer " or ProcessCommandLine contains " /create " or ProcessCommandLine contains " /addfile ") and (ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Perflogs" or ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\ProgramData\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Temp\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Users\\Public\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Windows\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\$Recycle.Bin\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\AppData\\Local\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\AppData\\Roaming\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Contacts\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Desktop\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Favorites\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Favourites\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\inetpub\\wwwroot\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Music\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Pictures\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Start Menu\\Programs\\Startup\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Users\\Default\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Videos\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "%ProgramData%" or ProcessCommandLine contains "%public%" or ProcessCommandLine contains "%temp%" or ProcessCommandLine contains "%tmp%")

t: File Download Via Windows Defender MpCmpRun.EXE
de: Detects the use of Windows Defender MpCmdRun.EXE to download files
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "MpCmdRun.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\MpCmdRun.exe" or ProcessCommandLine contains "MpCmdRun.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoFileDescription =~ "Microsoft Malware Protection Command Line Utility") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "DownloadFile" and ProcessCommandLine contains "url")

de: Detects execution of chromium based browser in headless mode using the "dump-dom" command line to download files
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\brave.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\chrome.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\msedge.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\opera.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\vivaldi.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "--headless" and ProcessCommandLine contains "dump-dom" and ProcessCommandLine contains "http")) and (not((((FolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Microsoft\\Edge\\Application\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Microsoft\\EdgeCore\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Microsoft\\EdgeWebView\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files\\Microsoft\\Edge\\Application\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files\\Microsoft\\EdgeCore\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files\\Microsoft\\EdgeWebView\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files\\WindowsApps\\Microsoft.MicrosoftEdge") and (FolderPath endswith "\\msedge.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\msedgewebview2.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\MicrosoftEdge.exe") and ProcessCommandLine contains "--headless --disable-gpu --disable-extensions --disable-plugins --mute-audio --no-first-run --incognito --aggressive-cache-discard --dump-dom") or ((FolderPath contains "\\AppData\\Local\\Microsoft\\WindowsApps\\" or FolderPath contains "\\Windows\\SystemApps\\Microsoft.MicrosoftEdge") and (FolderPath endswith "\\msedge.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\MicrosoftEdge.exe") and ProcessCommandLine contains "--headless --disable-gpu --disable-extensions --disable-plugins --mute-audio --no-first-run --incognito --aggressive-cache-discard --dump-dom"))))

t: File Encryption/Decryption Via Gpg4win From Suspicious Locations
de: Detects usage of Gpg4win to encrypt/decrypt files located in potentially suspicious locations.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\gpg.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\gpg2.exe") or ProcessVersionInfoProductName =~ "GNU Privacy Guard (GnuPG)" or ProcessVersionInfoFileDescription =~ "GnuPG’s OpenPGP tool") and ProcessCommandLine contains "-passphrase" and (ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\PerfLogs\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Temp\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Users\\Public\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Windows\\Temp\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\AppData\\Roaming\\")

t: File Explorer Folder Opened Using Explorer Folder Shortcut Via Shell
de: Detects the initial execution of "cmd.exe" which spawns "explorer.exe" with the appropriate command line arguments for opening the "My Computer" folder.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe") and FolderPath endswith "\\explorer.exe" and ProcessCommandLine contains "shell:mycomputerfolder"

t: File In Suspicious Location Encoded To Base64 Via Certutil.EXE
de: Detects the execution of certutil with the "encode" flag to encode a file to base64 where the files are located in potentially suspicious locations
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\certutil.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "CertUtil.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "-encode" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/encode" or ProcessCommandLine contains "–encode" or ProcessCommandLine contains "—encode" or ProcessCommandLine contains "―encode") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "\\AppData\\Roaming\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Desktop\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Local\\Temp\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\PerfLogs\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Users\\Public\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Windows\\Temp\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "$Recycle.Bin")

t: File With Suspicious Extension Downloaded Via Bitsadmin
au: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
de: Detects usage of bitsadmin downloading a file with a suspicious extension
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\bitsadmin.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "bitsadmin.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " /transfer " or ProcessCommandLine contains " /create " or ProcessCommandLine contains " /addfile ") and (ProcessCommandLine contains ".7z" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".asax" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".ashx" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".asmx" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".asp" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".aspx" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".bat" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".cfm" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".cgi" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".chm" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".cmd" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".dll" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".gif" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".jpeg" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".jpg" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".jsp" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".jspx" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".log" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".png" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".ps1" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".psm1" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".rar" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".scf" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".sct" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".txt" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".vbe" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".vbs" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".war" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".wsf" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".wsh" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".xll" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".zip")

t: File With Uncommon Extension Created By An Office Application
au: Vadim Khrykov (ThreatIntel), Cyb3rEng (Rule), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
de: Detects the creation of files with an executable or script extension by an Office application.
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\excel.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\msaccess.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\mspub.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\powerpnt.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\visio.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\winword.exe") and (FolderPath endswith ".bat" or FolderPath endswith ".cmd" or FolderPath endswith ".com" or FolderPath endswith ".dll" or FolderPath endswith ".exe" or FolderPath endswith ".hta" or FolderPath endswith ".ocx" or FolderPath endswith ".proj" or FolderPath endswith ".ps1" or FolderPath endswith ".scf" or FolderPath endswith ".scr" or FolderPath endswith ".sys" or FolderPath endswith ".vbe" or FolderPath endswith ".vbs" or FolderPath endswith ".wsf" or FolderPath endswith ".wsh")) and (not((FolderPath contains "\\AppData\\Local\\assembly\\tmp\\" and FolderPath endswith ".dll"))) and (not((((FolderPath contains "C:\\Users\\" and FolderPath contains "\\AppData\\Local\\Microsoft\\Office\\" and FolderPath contains "\\WebServiceCache\\AllUsers") and FolderPath endswith ".com") or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\winword.exe" and FolderPath contains "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\webexdelta\\" and (FolderPath endswith ".dll" or FolderPath endswith ".exe")) or ((FolderPath contains "C:\\Users\\" and FolderPath contains "\\AppData\\Local\\Microsoft\\Office\\" and FolderPath contains "\\BackstageInAppNavCache\\") and FolderPath endswith ".com"))))

de: Look for the encrypted cpassword value within Group Policy Preference files on the Domain Controller. This value can be decrypted with gpp-decrypt.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\find.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\findstr.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("FIND.EXE", "FINDSTR.EXE"))) and (ProcessCommandLine contains "cpassword" and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\sysvol\\" and ProcessCommandLine contains ".xml")

de: Detects execution of the "finger.exe" utility. Finger.EXE or "TCPIP Finger Command" is an old utility that is still present on modern Windows installation. It Displays information about users on a specified remote computer (typically a UNIX computer) that is running the finger service or daemon. Due to the old nature of this utility and the rareness of machines having the finger service. Any execution of "finger.exe" can be considered "suspicious" and worth investigating.
fp: Admin activity (unclear what they do nowadays with finger.exe)
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "finger.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\finger.exe"

de: Detects Archer malware invocation via rundll32
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessCommandLine contains "rundll32.exe" and ProcessCommandLine contains "InstallArcherSvc"

t: Folder Removed From Exploit Guard ProtectedFolders List - Registry
de: Detects the removal of folders from the "ProtectedFolders" list of of exploit guard. This could indicate an attacker trying to launch an encryption process or trying to manipulate data inside of the protected folder
fp: Legitimate administrators removing applications (should always be investigated)
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where (ActionType in~ ("RegistryKeyDeleted", "RegistryValueDeleted")) and (ActionType =~ "DeleteValue" and RegistryKey contains "SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender\\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\\Controlled Folder Access\\ProtectedFolders")

t: Forest Blizzard APT - Custom Protocol Handler Creation
de: Detects the setting of a custom protocol handler with the name "rogue". Seen being created by Forest Blizzard APT as reported by MSFT.
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where RegistryKey contains "\\PROTOCOLS\\Handler\\rogue\\CLSID" and RegistryValueData =~ "{026CC6D7-34B2-33D5-B551-CA31EB6CE345}"

t: Forest Blizzard APT - Custom Protocol Handler DLL Registry Set
de: Detects the setting of the DLL that handles the custom protocol handler. Seen being created by Forest Blizzard APT as reported by MSFT.
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where RegistryKey contains "\\CLSID\\{026CC6D7-34B2-33D5-B551-CA31EB6CE345}\\Server" and RegistryValueData endswith ".dll"

t: Forest Blizzard APT - File Creation Activity
de: Detects the creation of specific files inside of ProgramData directory. These files were seen being created by Forest Blizzard as described by MSFT.
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where ((FolderPath startswith "C:\\ProgramData\\Microsoft\\v" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\ProgramData\\Adobe\\v" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\ProgramData\\Comms\\v" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\ProgramData\\Intel\\v" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\ProgramData\\Kaspersky Lab\\v" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\ProgramData\\Bitdefender\\v" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\ProgramData\\ESET\\v" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\ProgramData\\NVIDIA\\v" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\ProgramData\\UbiSoft\\v" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\ProgramData\\Steam\\v") and (FolderPath contains "\\prnms003.inf_" or FolderPath contains "\\prnms009.inf_")) or (FolderPath startswith "C:\\ProgramData\\" and ((FolderPath endswith ".save" or FolderPath endswith "\\doit.bat" or FolderPath endswith "\\execute.bat" or FolderPath endswith "\\servtask.bat") or (FolderPath contains "\\wayzgoose" and FolderPath endswith ".dll")))

t: Forfiles Command Execution From Alternate Data Stream
de: Detects usage of "forfiles.exe" where the "/c" command argument references an NTFS Alternate Data Stream (ADS). Adversaries abuse "forfiles.exe" as an execution proxy to launch a payload that was previously hidden inside an ADS, evading detection.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\forfiles.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "forfiles.exe") and ProcessCommandLine contains " /c " and ProcessCommandLine matches regex "\\\\[^\\\\ ]+:[^\\\\/ ]"
pr: #6092 Add ADS abuse and signed-binary LOLBIN detection rules

de: Detects the execution of "forfiles" from a non-default location, in order to potentially spawn a custom "cmd.exe" from the current working directory.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((InitiatingProcessCommandLine endswith ".exe" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine endswith ".exe\"") and FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" and ProcessCommandLine startswith "/c echo \"") and (not(((InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains ":\\Windows\\System32\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains ":\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\forfiles.exe" and (FolderPath contains ":\\Windows\\System32\\" or FolderPath contains ":\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\") and FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe")))

au: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), oscd.community, Jonhnathan Ribeiro
de: Detects Formbook like process executions that inject code into a set of files in the System32 folder, which executes a special command command line to delete the dropper from the AppData Temp folder. We avoid false positives by excluding all parent process with command line parameters.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((InitiatingProcessCommandLine startswith "C:\\Windows\\System32\\" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine startswith "C:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine endswith ".exe") and ((ProcessCommandLine contains "/c" and ProcessCommandLine contains "del" and ProcessCommandLine contains "C:\\Users\\" and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "/c" and ProcessCommandLine contains "del" and ProcessCommandLine contains "C:\\Users\\" and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Desktop\\") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "/C" and ProcessCommandLine contains "type nul >" and ProcessCommandLine contains "C:\\Users\\" and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Desktop\\")) and ProcessCommandLine endswith ".exe"

de: Detects suspicious parameters of fsutil (deleting USN journal, configuring it with small size, etc). Might be used by ransomwares during the attack (seen by NotPetya and others).
fp: Scripts and administrative tools used in the monitored environment
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\fsutil.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "fsutil.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "deletejournal" or ProcessCommandLine contains "createjournal" or ProcessCommandLine contains "setZeroData")

t: GAC DLL Loaded Via Office Applications
de: Detects any GAC DLL being loaded by an Office Product
fp: Legitimate macro usage. Add the appropriate filter according to your environment
q:
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\excel.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\mspub.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\onenote.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\onenoteim.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\outlook.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\powerpnt.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\winword.exe") and FolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\Microsoft.NET\\assembly\\GAC_MSIL"

t: GitHub Token Access Via GH CLI Spawned By Script Interpreters
de: Detects the GitHub CLI (gh) being executed to access stored GitHub authentication tokens, when spawned by build tools such as bun, node, or Python. Malicious packages published to npm, JSR, or PyPI have been observed running these commands during install/postinstall hooks to silently exfiltrate the victim's stored GitHub authentication token.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\bun.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\node.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\py.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\pyw.exe") or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\python") and ((ProcessCommandLine contains "gh " and ProcessCommandLine contains " auth " and ProcessCommandLine contains "token") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "gh " and ProcessCommandLine contains "config" and ProcessCommandLine contains " get" and ProcessCommandLine contains "oauth_token"))
pr: #6054 new: susp package execution

de: Detects command line parameters used by Bloodhound and Sharphound hack tools
fp: Other programs that use these command line option and accepts an 'All' parameter

DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessVersionInfoProductName contains "SharpHound" or ProcessVersionInfoFileDescription contains "SharpHound" or (ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName contains "SpecterOps" or ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName contains "evil corp") or (FolderPath contains "\\Bloodhound.exe" or FolderPath contains "\\SharpHound.exe")) or (ProcessCommandLine contains " -CollectionMethod All " or ProcessCommandLine contains " --CollectionMethods Session " or ProcessCommandLine contains " --Loop --Loopduration " or ProcessCommandLine contains " --PortScanTimeout " or ProcessCommandLine contains ".exe -c All -d " or ProcessCommandLine contains "Invoke-Bloodhound" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Get-BloodHoundData") or (ProcessCommandLine contains " -JsonFolder " and ProcessCommandLine contains " -ZipFileName ") or (ProcessCommandLine contains " DCOnly " and ProcessCommandLine contains " --NoSaveCache ")

de: Detects execution of BloodyAD, an Active Directory privilege escalation framework that supports DACL manipulation, password resets, group membership changes, RBCD configuration, UAC flag modification, and computer account creation.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath contains "\\bloodyAD" or ((FolderPath contains "\\python" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName contains "python") and ProcessCommandLine contains "bloodyAD")
pr: #5945 new: add new rules for several AD related hacktools

de: Detects Certify a tool for Active Directory certificate abuse based on PE metadata characteristics and common command line arguments.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\Certify.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "Certify.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoFileDescription contains "Certify") or ((ProcessCommandLine contains ".exe cas " or ProcessCommandLine contains ".exe find " or ProcessCommandLine contains ".exe pkiobjects " or ProcessCommandLine contains ".exe request " or ProcessCommandLine contains ".exe download ") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " /vulnerable" or ProcessCommandLine contains " /template:" or ProcessCommandLine contains " /altname:" or ProcessCommandLine contains " /domain:" or ProcessCommandLine contains " /path:" or ProcessCommandLine contains " /ca:"))

de: Detects Certipy execution, a tool for Active Directory Certificate Services enumeration and abuse based on PE metadata characteristics and common command line arguments.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\Certipy.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "Certipy.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoFileDescription contains "Certipy") or ((ProcessCommandLine contains " account " or ProcessCommandLine contains " auth " or ProcessCommandLine contains " cert " or ProcessCommandLine contains " find " or ProcessCommandLine contains " forge " or ProcessCommandLine contains " ptt " or ProcessCommandLine contains " relay " or ProcessCommandLine contains " req " or ProcessCommandLine contains " shadow " or ProcessCommandLine contains " template ") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " -bloodhound" or ProcessCommandLine contains " -ca-pfx " or ProcessCommandLine contains " -dc-ip " or ProcessCommandLine contains " -kirbi" or ProcessCommandLine contains " -old-bloodhound" or ProcessCommandLine contains " -pfx " or ProcessCommandLine contains " -target" or ProcessCommandLine contains " -template" or ProcessCommandLine contains " -username " or ProcessCommandLine contains " -vulnerable" or ProcessCommandLine contains "auth -pfx" or ProcessCommandLine contains "shadow auto" or ProcessCommandLine contains "shadow list"))

de: Detects execution of certsync, a tool that abuses Active Directory Certificate Services to synchronise all domain hashes. It performs a Golden Certificate attack by requesting a certificate for every domain user and recovering their NT hashes via UnPAC-the-Hash, effectively replicating the impact of DCSync without using the replication RPC interface.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath contains "\\certsync" or ((FolderPath contains "\\python" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName contains "python") and ProcessCommandLine contains "certsync")
pr: #5945 new: add new rules for several AD related hacktools

| where ((FolderPath contains "\\dfscoerce" or FolderPath contains "\\coercer" or FolderPath contains "\\ShadowCoerce" or FolderPath contains "\\CredCoerce") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "Coerce" and ProcessCommandLine contains "-u" and ProcessCommandLine contains "-p")) or ((FolderPath contains "\\python" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName contains "python") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "dfscoerce" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Coercer" or ProcessCommandLine contains "ShadowCoerce" or ProcessCommandLine contains "CredCoerce"))
pr: #5945 new: add new rules for several AD related hacktools

de: Detects execution of "gogo" (chainreactors/gogo), a high-performance open-source automated scanning engine designed for red teams. The tool uses distinctive Gogo-specific port-preset tags (e.g. "top1", "top2", "top3", "win", "db", "docker", "oracle") with the "-p" flag, supersmart scan modes ("-m ss", "-m sc"), and config-listing commands ("-P port", "-P workflow"). Cisco Talos documented its use by the China-nexus APT group UAT-8302 in their May 2026 report, where the operators downloaded "gogo_windows_amd64.exe" from the official GitHub releases and used it for internal network reconnaissance.
fp: Legitimate use of gogo by security professionals or system administrators for authorized network assessment.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\gogo.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\gogo_windows_amd64.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\gogo_windows_386.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " -p top1" or ProcessCommandLine contains " -p top2" or ProcessCommandLine contains " -p top3" or ProcessCommandLine contains " -p win" or ProcessCommandLine contains " -p db" or ProcessCommandLine contains " -p docker" or ProcessCommandLine contains " -p oracle" or ProcessCommandLine contains " -p dubbo" or ProcessCommandLine contains " -p lotus" or ProcessCommandLine contains " -m ss" or ProcessCommandLine contains " -m sc" or ProcessCommandLine contains " -P port" or ProcessCommandLine contains " -P workflow")
pr: #6035 Add HackTool - Gogo Scanner Execution Rule

| where FolderPath endswith "\\HiveSwarming.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "HiveSwarming.exe"

de: Detects execution of impacket attack scripts via the Python interpreter on Windows. Impacket provides Python implementations of various Windows network protocols and is widely used for lateral movement (wmiexec, psexec, smbexec), credential access (secretsdump), Kerberos abuse (GetNPUsers, GetUserSPNs), NTLM relay (ntlmrelayx), and Active Directory enumeration and manipulation.
