DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath contains "\\python" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName contains "python") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "secretsdump.py" or ProcessCommandLine contains "wmiexec.py" or ProcessCommandLine contains "psexec.py" or ProcessCommandLine contains "smbexec.py" or ProcessCommandLine contains "atexec.py" or ProcessCommandLine contains "dcomexec.py" or ProcessCommandLine contains "ntlmrelayx.py" or ProcessCommandLine contains "smbrelayx.py" or ProcessCommandLine contains "GetNPUsers.py" or ProcessCommandLine contains "GetUserSPNs.py" or ProcessCommandLine contains "getTGT.py" or ProcessCommandLine contains "getST.py" or ProcessCommandLine contains "ticketer.py" or ProcessCommandLine contains "ticketConverter.py" or ProcessCommandLine contains "goldenPac.py" or ProcessCommandLine contains "raiseChild.py" or ProcessCommandLine contains "dacledit.py" or ProcessCommandLine contains "owneredit.py" or ProcessCommandLine contains "rbcd.py" or ProcessCommandLine contains "addcomputer.py" or ProcessCommandLine contains "lookupsid.py" or ProcessCommandLine contains "findDelegation.py" or ProcessCommandLine contains "GetADUsers.py" or ProcessCommandLine contains "GetADComputers.py" or ProcessCommandLine contains "samrdump.py" or ProcessCommandLine contains "rpcdump.py" or ProcessCommandLine contains "rpcmap.py" or ProcessCommandLine contains "services.py" or ProcessCommandLine contains "reg.py" or ProcessCommandLine contains "wmiquery.py" or ProcessCommandLine contains "dpapi.py")

de: Detects the execution of Kerbrute, a tool used to enumerate valid Active Directory accounts and to brute-force or spray passwords via Kerberos Pre-Authentication. Its "userenum" mode enumerates valid domain usernames without generating failed logon events (Event ID 4625), making it a stealthy discovery technique, while its "passwordspray", "bruteuser" and "bruteforce" modes increment failed login counters and can lock out accounts. Beyond red team usage, the tool has been observed in real intrusions and has been associated with RansomHub ransomware operations, the FIN12 threat actor group and Alloy Taurus.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\kerbrute.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\kerbrute_windows_386.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\kerbrute_windows_amd64.exe") or ((ProcessCommandLine contains " userenum " or ProcessCommandLine contains " passwordspray " or ProcessCommandLine contains " bruteuser " or ProcessCommandLine contains " bruteforce ") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " --dc " or ProcessCommandLine contains " -d " or ProcessCommandLine contains " --domain "))
pr: #6195 Add rule: HackTool - Kerbrute Execution

The vulnerability exploits a registry symbolic link race condition to overwrite restricted system registry keys.

de: Detects the execution of SharpSCCM, a post-exploitation tool that abuses Microsoft Endpoint Configuration Manager (SCCM/ConfigMgr) for credential gathering and lateral movement without requiring access to the SCCM administration console. The tool extracts DPAPI-protected policy secrets-such as Network Access Account (NAA) credentials, task sequence variables, and collection variables-from the local WMI repository or CIM store. It can also coerce NTLM authentication from SCCM servers in sites where automatic site-wide client push installation is enabled, potentially leading to site takeover. Because SCCM service accounts are frequently highly privileged, successful use of this tool often results in the disclosure of domain-level administrative credentials.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\SharpSCCM.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "SharpSCCM.exe") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "invoke client-push" or ProcessCommandLine contains "get site-push-settings") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "local site-info" or ProcessCommandLine contains "local user-sid")

de: Detects forced shutdown of Hyper-V virtual machines via PowerShell Stop-VM cmdlet. Ransomware operators commonly shut down VMs before encryption to release file locks on VHDX files, enabling successful encryption. This technique was observed in Kyber ransomware (Rapid7, 2026) and other campaigns targeting virtualized environments. The rule focuses on forced shutdown operations (-Force, -TurnOff) and bulk VM shutdown patterns (Get-VM combined with Stop-VM) which are strong indicators of malicious intent. Note: This rule intentionally does not detect Stop-VM -Save (graceful shutdown with state save) to reduce false positives from legitimate VM maintenance. Ransomware typically uses -Force or -TurnOff for immediate impact.
fp: Legitimate Hyper-V administration and maintenance activities
Disaster recovery testing and failover procedures
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe") and ProcessCommandLine contains "Stop-VM" and ((ProcessCommandLine contains "-Force" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-TurnOff") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "Get-VM" and ProcessCommandLine contains "Stop-VM"))
pr: #6034 Add detection for Hyper-V VM forced shutdown (ransomware preparation)

au: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
de: Detects Kapeka backdoor process execution pattern, where the dropper launch the backdoor binary by calling rundll32 and passing the backdoor's first export ordinal (#1) with a "-d" argument.

de: Detects Kapeka backdoor persistence activity. Depending on the process privileges, the Kapeka dropper then sets persistence for the backdoor either as a scheduled task (if admin or SYSTEM) or autorun registry (if not). For the scheduled task, it creates a scheduled task called "Sens Api" via schtasks command, which is set to run upon system startup as SYSTEM. To establish persistence through the autorun utility, it adds an autorun entry called "Sens Api" under HKCU\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run via the "reg add" command. Both persistence mechanisms are set to launch the binary by calling rundll32 and passing the backdoor's first export ordinal (#1) without any additional argument.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (((FolderPath endswith "\\schtasks.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "schtasks.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "create" and ProcessCommandLine contains "ONSTART")) or ((FolderPath endswith "\\reg.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "reg.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "add" and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run"))) and ((ProcessCommandLine contains "rundll32" and ProcessCommandLine contains ".wll" and ProcessCommandLine contains "#1") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "Sens Api" or ProcessCommandLine contains "OneDrive"))

t: Kernel Driver Service Registered From Suspicious Path
de: Detects creation/modification of a service ImagePath pointing to a .sys driver located in a user-writable or non-standard directory. This is a strong indicator of Bring-Your-Own- Vulnerable-Driver (BYOVD): legitimate drivers load from System32\drivers, whereas attackers drop and register vulnerable/malicious drivers from temp, download or profile paths. Complements the static known-bad name/hash driver_load rules by catching the install step regardless of driver name.
fp: Some legitimate software installs drivers from ProgramData or vendor temp paths; baseline and filter known-good driver paths
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where ((RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\Services.*$" and RegistryKey endswith "\\ImagePath" and RegistryValueData endswith ".sys") and (RegistryValueData contains "\\Users\\" or RegistryValueData contains "\\Temp\\" or RegistryValueData contains "\\Tmp\\" or RegistryValueData contains "\\AppData\\" or RegistryValueData contains "\\ProgramData\\" or RegistryValueData contains "\\Windows\\Temp\\" or RegistryValueData contains "\\PerfLogs\\" or RegistryValueData contains "\\Downloads\\" or RegistryValueData contains "\\Public\\" or RegistryValueData contains "\\Windows\\Tasks\\")) and (not(RegistryValueData contains "\\ProgramData\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender\\"))

t: Linux Covert SSH Tunnel via GSocket
de: Detects execution of gsocket, gs-netcat, or associated binaries that provide SSH-like access over the Global Socket Relay Network (GSRN) without requiring an exposed TCP port. GSSocket authenticates using a shared secret and routes traffic through a relay, making it invisible to network-level monitoring tools that look for direct inbound connections. Attackers use it to maintain persistent backdoor access on hosts behind NAT or strict firewalls.
fp: Legitimate use of gsocket by authorized administrators for secure remote access
Security team using gsocket in an approved red team exercise
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "/gsocket" or FolderPath endswith "/gs-netcat" or FolderPath endswith "/gs-sftp" or FolderPath endswith "/gs-mount"

t: Linux Dangerous Capability Set via Setcap
de: Detects use of setcap to assign dangerous Linux capabilities to an executable file. Capabilities such as cap_setuid, cap_sys_admin, cap_sys_ptrace, cap_sys_module, and cap_net_raw enable privilege escalation without a SUID bit, making them harder to detect. Attackers assign these capabilities to binaries they control to maintain persistent elevated access or to facilitate lateral movement by enabling low-privileged accounts to perform root-level operations.
fp: Package installation scripts that legitimately set capabilities on ping or similar utilities
Container runtime configuration setting required capabilities
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "/setcap" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "cap_setuid" or ProcessCommandLine contains "cap_setgid" or ProcessCommandLine contains "cap_sys_admin" or ProcessCommandLine contains "cap_sys_module" or ProcessCommandLine contains "cap_sys_ptrace" or ProcessCommandLine contains "cap_sys_rawio" or ProcessCommandLine contains "cap_dac_override" or ProcessCommandLine contains "cap_dac_read_search" or ProcessCommandLine contains "cap_net_raw" or ProcessCommandLine contains "cap_net_admin" or ProcessCommandLine contains "cap_bpf" or ProcessCommandLine contains "cap_setpcap" or ProcessCommandLine contains "cap_mac_admin")) and (not(ProcessCommandLine contains "cap_net_raw+ep /bin/ping"))

DNS traffic is permitted in most network environments and is rarely inspected, making dnscat an effective covert channel for C2 communication, data exfiltration, and remote command execution that bypasses traditional network security controls.

Security research in an isolated lab environment
q:

| where (FolderPath endswith "/dnscat" or FolderPath endswith "/dnscat2") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "dnscat" or ProcessCommandLine contains "dnscat2")

t: Linux Fileless Execution via Memfd Create
de: Detects execution of processes whose image path contains the memfd: prefix, indicating the binary was loaded from an anonymous in-memory file created via the memfd_create syscall rather than from disk. This is a common fileless malware technique that allows execution of payloads without writing to the filesystem, evading file-based antivirus and integrity monitoring. Legitimate use of memfd_create occurs in specific container runtimes and JIT compilers but is rare in production server workloads.
fp: Container runtimes using memfd_create for legitimate process bootstrapping
JIT compilers or language runtimes that use anonymous memory execution
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath startswith "memfd:" and (not((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/runc" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/containerd-shim" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/nvidia-container-runtime")))

t: Linux Privilege Escalation via GDB Debugger
de: Detects use of the GDB debugger to attach to running processes or execute shell commands, which can be leveraged for privilege escalation. When executed with sudo or against privileged processes via --pid, GDB can inject and execute arbitrary code in the context of that process. This technique allows attackers to spawn root shells by calling system() or execve() within a privileged process without writing files to disk.
fp: Legitimate developer debugging of processes in a development environment
Security researchers analyzing binaries in an isolated sandbox
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "/gdb" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "--pid" or ProcessCommandLine contains " -p " or ProcessCommandLine contains "--eval-command" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-ex " or ProcessCommandLine contains "call system" or ProcessCommandLine contains "call execve")) or (ProcessCommandLine contains "sudo" and ProcessCommandLine contains "gdb")
pr: #6001 new: 13 Linux detection rules

t: Linux Privilege Escalation via Niche GTFOBins Binaries
de: Detects privilege escalation attempts via niche GTFOBins-listed binaries invoked with sudo. These binaries are not commonly used for privilege escalation and may evade detection rules focused on well-known bins like python or perl. Covered binaries include csvtool, emacs, gem, mysql, composer, cpulimit, and debugfs, each of which can spawn a privileged shell when executed with sudo and specific flags.
fp: Legitimate administrative use of these binaries with sudo in approved workflows
Authorized red team exercise or offensive security testing
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessCommandLine contains "csvtool" and ProcessCommandLine contains "call" and ProcessCommandLine contains "sudo") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "emacs" and ProcessCommandLine contains "--eval" and ProcessCommandLine contains "sudo") or (FolderPath endswith "/gem" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "open -e" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-c sudo")) or (FolderPath endswith "/mysql" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "-e" and ProcessCommandLine contains "sudo" and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\!")) or (ProcessCommandLine contains "composer" and ProcessCommandLine contains "run-script" and ProcessCommandLine contains "sudo") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "sudo" and ProcessCommandLine contains "cpulimit" and ProcessCommandLine contains "-l" and ProcessCommandLine contains "-f") or (FolderPath endswith "/debugfs" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "!/bin/sh" or ProcessCommandLine contains "!/bin/bash"))
pr: #6001 new: 13 Linux detection rules

de: Detects execution of docker run or docker exec with the --privileged flag. A privileged container has full access to the host kernel, all devices, and bypasses Docker namespace isolation. Attackers exploit this to mount the host filesystem, load kernel modules, access raw devices, and escape the container to gain root on the underlying host. The --restart=always flag combined with --privileged additionally establishes persistent access.
fp: Legitimate use of privileged containers by platform or infrastructure teams
Container runtime components that require privileged mode for system operations
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "/docker" and ProcessCommandLine contains "--privileged") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " run " or ProcessCommandLine contains " exec ")
pr: #6001 new: 13 Linux detection rules

de: Detects events with patterns found in commands used for reconnaissance on linux systems
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessCommandLine contains " -name .htpasswd" or ProcessCommandLine contains " -perm -4000 "

t: Linux Reverse Shell or Code Execution via Rview Binary
de: Detects suspicious use of the rview binary with embedded scripting arguments that can spawn shells, establish network connections, or load shared libraries. Rview is the restricted view mode of Vim, but it supports Python and Lua scripting via :py and :lua commands, enabling full shell execution despite its restricted designation. When combined with os.execl, os.execute, or socket.connect patterns, rview can be used to establish reverse shells or execute arbitrary commands, particularly when run with SUID or sudo.
fp: Security researchers testing GTFOBins techniques in an isolated environment
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "/rview" or FolderPath endswith "/rvim") and (ProcessCommandLine contains ":py" or ProcessCommandLine contains ":lua" or ProcessCommandLine contains "os.execl" or ProcessCommandLine contains "os.execute" or ProcessCommandLine contains "exec sh" or ProcessCommandLine contains "pty.spawn" or ProcessCommandLine contains "socket.connect" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/bin/sh" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/bin/bash" or ProcessCommandLine contains "cap_setuid" or ProcessCommandLine contains "sudo rview")
pr: #6001 new: 13 Linux detection rules

t: Linux Reverse Shell via Socat or Cryptcat
de: Detects execution of socat or cryptcat with arguments indicative of a reverse shell setup. Socat is a powerful networking utility that can redirect standard I/O to a network socket, making it a common tool for establishing reverse shells that bypass firewall rules. Cryptcat adds encryption on top, evading plaintext content inspection. Unlike netcat, socat is less commonly flagged by default endpoint controls.
fp: Legitimate use of socat for authorized port forwarding or debugging
Security researchers testing in sandboxed environments
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "/socat" or FolderPath endswith "/cryptcat") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "EXEC:" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/bin/sh" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/bin/bash" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/bin/zsh" or ProcessCommandLine contains "pty")
pr: #6001 new: 13 Linux detection rules

t: Linux TLS Reverse Shell via OpenSSL
de: Detects execution of openssl with the s_client subcommand combined with -connect and shell indicators. Attackers use openssl to establish encrypted reverse shells that bypass simple cleartext detection of tools like netcat. The technique typically involves mkfifo or /dev/tcp alongside openssl to create a bidirectional encrypted channel to an attacker-controlled listener.
fp: Unlikely in production systems; security testing with explicit authorization
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "/openssl" and ProcessCommandLine contains "s_client" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "/bin/sh" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/bin/bash" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/bin/zsh" or ProcessCommandLine contains "bash -i" or ProcessCommandLine contains "sh -i")
pr: #6001 new: 13 Linux detection rules

au: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
de: Detects suspicious sub processes of web server processes
fp: Web applications that invoke Linux command line tools
q:

t: LiteLLM PyPI Compromise File Creation Indicators - Linux
de: Detects file creation indicators of the compromised LiteLLM 1.107.0 release published to PyPI and Docker Hub on October 21, 2026. Every 1.107.0 wheel installs cook.pth and cook.py into the Python package directory (site-packages or dist-packages), so the payload runs on every Python interpreter start without litellm being imported. The payload steals credentials, writes a marker file once exfiltration succeeds, and starts an hourly remote code loader that holds a lock file in /tmp.
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "/site-packages/cook.pth" or FolderPath endswith "/site-packages/cook.py" or FolderPath endswith "/dist-packages/cook.pth" or FolderPath endswith "/dist-packages/cook.py") or (FolderPath in~ ("/tmp/.pc_once_72129118c59f5636c0bb", "/tmp/remote_code_loader.lock")) or (FolderPath startswith "/tmp/.pc_sq_" or FolderPath startswith "/tmp/.pc_e_")
pr: #6503 new: LiteLLM PyPI Compromise Indicators (1.107.0)

t: LiteLLM PyPI Compromise File Creation Indicators - MacOS
de: Detects file creation indicators of the compromised LiteLLM 1.107.0 release published to PyPI on October 21, 2026. Every 1.107.0 wheel installs cook.pth and cook.py into the root of site- packages, so the payload runs on every Python interpreter start without litellm being imported. The payload steals credentials, writes a marker file once exfiltration succeeds, and starts an hourly remote code loader that holds a lock file in /tmp.
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "/site-packages/cook.pth" or FolderPath endswith "/site-packages/cook.py") or (FolderPath in~ ("/tmp/.pc_once_72129118c59f5636c0bb", "/tmp/remote_code_loader.lock"))
pr: #6503 new: LiteLLM PyPI Compromise Indicators (1.107.0)

t: LiteLLM PyPI Compromise File Creation Indicators - Windows
de: Detects file creation indicators of the compromised LiteLLM 1.107.0 release published to PyPI on October 21, 2026. Every 1.107.0 wheel, including win_amd64, installs cook.pth and cook.py into the root of site-packages, so the payload runs on every Python interpreter start without litellm being imported. On Windows the remote code loader fails, but the credential stealer still runs and creates its working directories in the temp folder.
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\site-packages\\cook.pth" or FolderPath endswith "\\site-packages\\cook.py") or (FolderPath contains "\\Temp\\.pc_sq_" or FolderPath contains "\\Temp\\.pc_e_")
pr: #6503 new: LiteLLM PyPI Compromise Indicators (1.107.0)

t: LiveKD Driver Creation By Uncommon Process
de: Detects the creation of the LiveKD driver by a process image other than "livekd.exe".
fp: Administrators might rename LiveKD before its usage which could trigger this. Add additional names you use to the filter
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where FolderPath =~ "C:\\Windows\\System32\\drivers\\LiveKdD.SYS" and (not((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\livekd.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\livek64.exe")))

t: LiveKD Kernel Memory Dump File Created
de: Detects the creation of a file that has the same name as the default LiveKD kernel memory dump.
fp: In rare occasions administrators might leverage LiveKD to perform live kernel debugging. This should not be allowed on production systems. Investigate and apply additional filters where necessary.
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where FolderPath =~ "C:\\Windows\\livekd.dmp"

t: Load Of RstrtMgr.DLL By A Suspicious Process
de: Detects the load of RstrtMgr DLL (Restart Manager) by a suspicious process. This library has been used during ransomware campaigns to kill processes that would prevent file encryption by locking them (e.g. Conti ransomware, Cactus ransomware). It has also recently been seen used by the BiBi wiper for Windows. It could also be used for anti-analysis purposes by shut downing specific processes.
q:
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\RstrtMgr.dll" or InitiatingProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "RstrtMgr.dll") and ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains ":\\Perflogs\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains ":\\Users\\Public\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\Temporary Internet") or ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains ":\\Users\\" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\Favorites\\") or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains ":\\Users\\" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\Favourites\\") or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains ":\\Users\\" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\Contacts\\")))

de: Detects execution of the legitimate Microsoft binary LockScreenContentServer.exe from outside expected Windows directories. Threat actors associated with the TerminalFix campaign copied the binary alongside a malicious dui70.dll under ProgramData to perform DLL sideloading.
fp: Legitimate administrative or security testing that copies the binary outside default Windows folders
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\LockScreenContentServer.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "LockScreenContentServer.exe") and (not((FolderPath contains ":\\Windows\\System32\\" or FolderPath contains ":\\Windows\\WinSxS\\" or FolderPath contains ":\\Windows\\SystemApps\\")))
pr: #6306 Add rule for LockScreenContentServer.exe execution from uncommon folders

de: Detects a suspicious copy operation that tries to copy a known LOLBIN from system (System32, SysWOW64, WinSxS) directories to another on disk in order to bypass detections based on locations.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" and ProcessCommandLine contains "copy ") or ((FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "copy-item" or ProcessCommandLine contains " copy " or ProcessCommandLine contains "cpi " or ProcessCommandLine contains " cp ")) or ((FolderPath endswith "\\robocopy.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\xcopy.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("robocopy.exe", "XCOPY.EXE")))) and ((ProcessCommandLine contains "\\System32" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\SysWOW64" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\WinSxS") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "\\bitsadmin.exe" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\calc.exe" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\certutil.exe" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\cmdl32.exe" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\cscript.exe" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\mshta.exe" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\rundll32.exe" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\wscript.exe" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\ie4uinit.exe"))

de: Detects setting a custom URL for OneDriveStandaloneUpdater.exe to download a file from the Internet without executing any anomalous executables with suspicious arguments. The downloaded file will be in C:\Users\redacted\AppData\Local\Microsoft\OneDrive\StandaloneUpdaterreSignInSettingsConfig.json
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where RegistryKey contains "\\SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\OneDrive\\UpdateOfficeConfig\\UpdateRingSettingURLFromOC"

au: E.M. Anhaus, Tony Lambert, oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
de: Detects the presence of the keywords "lsass" and ".dmp" in the commandline, which could indicate a potential attempt to dump or create a dump of the lsass process.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessCommandLine contains "lsass.dmp" or ProcessCommandLine contains "lsass.zip" or ProcessCommandLine contains "lsass.rar" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Andrew.dmp" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Coredump.dmp" or ProcessCommandLine contains "NotLSASS.zip" or ProcessCommandLine contains "lsass_2" or ProcessCommandLine contains "lsassdump" or ProcessCommandLine contains "lsassdmp") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "lsass" and ProcessCommandLine contains ".dmp") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "SQLDmpr" and ProcessCommandLine contains ".mdmp") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "nanodump" and ProcessCommandLine contains ".dmp")

t: Lsass Full Dump Request Via DumpType Registry Settings
de: Detects the setting of the "DumpType" registry value to "2" which stands for a "Full Dump". Technique such as LSASS Shtinkering requires this value to be "2" in order to dump LSASS.
fp: Legitimate application that needs to do a full dump of their process
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where (RegistryKey contains "\\SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows\\Windows Error Reporting\\LocalDumps\\DumpType" or RegistryKey contains "\\SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows\\Windows Error Reporting\\LocalDumps\\lsass.exe\\DumpType") and RegistryValueData =~ "DWORD (0x00000002)"

t: LSASS Process Dump Artefact In CrashDumps Folder
de: Detects the presence of an LSASS dump file in the "CrashDumps" folder. This could be a sign of LSASS credential dumping. Techniques such as the LSASS Shtinkering have been seen abusing the Windows Error Reporting to dump said process.
fp: Rare legitimate dump of the process by the operating system due to a crash of lsass
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where FolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\System32\\config\\systemprofile\\AppData\\Local\\CrashDumps\\" and FolderPath contains "lsass.exe." and FolderPath endswith ".dmp"

t: LSASS Process Memory Dump Creation Via Taskmgr.EXE
de: Detects the creation of an "lsass.dmp" file by the taskmgr process. This indicates a manual dumping of the LSASS.exe process memory using Windows Task Manager.
fp: Rare case of troubleshooting by an administrator or support that has to be investigated regardless
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith ":\\Windows\\system32\\taskmgr.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith ":\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\taskmgr.exe") and (FolderPath contains "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\" and FolderPath contains "\\lsass" and FolderPath contains ".DMP")

de: Detects creation of files with names used by different memory dumping tools to create a memory dump of the LSASS process memory, which contains user credentials.
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\Andrew.dmp" or FolderPath endswith "\\Coredump.dmp" or FolderPath endswith "\\lsass.dmp" or FolderPath endswith "\\lsass.rar" or FolderPath endswith "\\lsass.zip" or FolderPath endswith "\\NotLSASS.zip" or FolderPath endswith "\\PPLBlade.dmp" or FolderPath endswith "\\rustive.dmp") or (FolderPath contains "\\lsass_2" or FolderPath contains "\\lsassdmp" or FolderPath contains "\\lsassdump") or (FolderPath contains "\\lsass" and FolderPath contains ".dmp") or (FolderPath contains "SQLDmpr" and FolderPath endswith ".mdmp") or ((FolderPath contains "\\nanodump" or FolderPath contains "\\proc_") and FolderPath endswith ".dmp")

de: Detects creation of files with names used by different memory dumping tools to create a memory dump of the LSASS process memory, which contains user credentials.
q:

de: Detects findstring commands that include the keyword lsass, which indicates recon actviity for the LSASS process PID
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (((FolderPath endswith "\\find.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\findstr.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("FIND.EXE", "FINDSTR.EXE"))) and ProcessCommandLine contains "lsass") or (ProcessCommandLine contains " -i \"lsass" or ProcessCommandLine contains " /i \"lsass" or ProcessCommandLine contains " –i \"lsass" or ProcessCommandLine contains " —i \"lsass" or ProcessCommandLine contains " ―i \"lsass" or ProcessCommandLine contains " -i lsass.exe" or ProcessCommandLine contains " /i lsass.exe" or ProcessCommandLine contains " –i lsass.exe" or ProcessCommandLine contains " —i lsass.exe" or ProcessCommandLine contains " ―i lsass.exe" or ProcessCommandLine contains "findstr \"lsass" or ProcessCommandLine contains "findstr lsass" or ProcessCommandLine contains "findstr.exe \"lsass" or ProcessCommandLine contains "findstr.exe lsass")

de: Detects the terminal stage of a macOS ClickFix chain, in which a shell command the victim pasted themselves fetches a Mach-O into a world-writable directory, strips its extended attributes so Gatekeeper does not evaluate it, marks it executable and runs it. Matching requires the xattr step together with a temporary path, because curl and chmod against /tmp are common in ordinary developer workflows on their own. Observed dropped filenames include helper and update; the sequence is the indicator, not the name.
fp: Build systems and installers that stage binaries under /tmp and clear extended attributes on them
Developers clearing extended attributes on their own build artefacts from a terminal
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "/xattr" and (ProcessCommandLine contains " -c " or ProcessCommandLine contains " -cr " or ProcessCommandLine contains "com.apple.quarantine")) and (ProcessCommandLine contains "/tmp/" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/private/tmp/" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/var/folders/")) and (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/zsh" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/bash" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/sh")
pr: #6205 macOS: cover `xattr -c` in the Gatekeeper bypass rule, add ClickFix stage-3 dropper

t: Macro Enabled In A Potentially Suspicious Document
de: Detects registry changes to Office trust records where the path is located in a potentially suspicious location
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where RegistryKey contains "\\Security\\Trusted Documents\\TrustRecords" and (RegistryKey contains "/AppData/Local/Microsoft/Windows/INetCache/" or RegistryKey contains "/AppData/Local/Temp/" or RegistryKey contains "/PerfLogs/" or RegistryKey contains "C:/Users/Public/" or RegistryKey contains "file:///D:/" or RegistryKey contains "file:///E:/")

t: MacSync Stealer Chunked Upload Via Curl
de: Detects curl command lines associated with the chunked data upload behavior of MacSync Stealer on macOS. The detection combines binary upload arguments with the gate endpoint and upload tracking parameters, without depending on a particular C2 domain, API key value or build token.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "/curl" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "--data-binary" and ProcessCommandLine contains "upload_id=" and ProcessCommandLine contains "chunk_index=" and ProcessCommandLine contains "total_chunks=" and ProcessCommandLine contains "api-key:")) and ProcessCommandLine matches regex "/gate\\?[^ ]*buildtxd="
pr: #6326 feat(macos): detect MacSync Stealer chunked upload

t: Makecab Compression Into Alternate Data Stream
de: Detects usage of "makecab.exe" where the destination cabinet is written into an NTFS Alternate Data Stream (ADS). Adversaries abuse "makecab.exe" to compress a payload into an ADS in order to hide it from directory listings and evade detection.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\makecab.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "makecab.exe") and ProcessCommandLine matches regex "\\\\[^\\\\ ]+:[^\\\\/ ]"
pr: #6092 Add ADS abuse and signed-binary LOLBIN detection rules

t: Mavinject Inject DLL Into Running Process
de: Detects process injection using the signed Windows tool "Mavinject" via the "INJECTRUNNING" flag
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessCommandLine contains " /INJECTRUNNING " and (not(InitiatingProcessFolderPath =~ "C:\\Windows\\System32\\AppVClient.exe"))

t: MCP Server Installed From Non-Approved Registry - Linux
de: Detects installation of Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers via 'claude mcp add', 'mcp install', or npm/pip install of mcp-server-* packages from sources other than the official MCP registry at registry.modelcontextprotocol.io. Untrusted MCP servers run with the same privileges as the calling agent and have direct tool-execution access, making this a high-value supply- chain backdoor vector. Note: local development paths, git URLs, and 'npm link' installs intentionally fire here. Tune via the filter or via private-registry allow-listing.
fp: Internal MCP servers published to a private registry that the SOC has not yet allow-listed
Developers iterating on a local MCP server via 'npm link' or editable installs
Tuning required for orgs using the official MCP packages with version pins (e.g. '@modelcontextprotocol/server-git@0.6.2')
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((ProcessCommandLine contains "claude mcp add" or ProcessCommandLine contains "mcp install") or ((FolderPath endswith "/npm" or FolderPath endswith "/npx" or FolderPath endswith "/yarn" or FolderPath endswith "/pnpm" or FolderPath endswith "/pip" or FolderPath endswith "/pip3" or FolderPath endswith "/uv" or FolderPath endswith "/uvx") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "mcp-server-" or ProcessCommandLine contains "@modelcontextprotocol/server-" or ProcessCommandLine contains "mcp-server@"))) and (not((ProcessCommandLine contains "registry.modelcontextprotocol.io" or (ProcessCommandLine endswith "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "@modelcontextprotocol/server-git" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "@modelcontextprotocol/server-github" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "@modelcontextprotocol/server-postgres" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "@modelcontextprotocol/server-sqlite"))))
pr: #5995 Add 4 detection rules for LLM and MCP attack surface

de: Detects suspicious command line patterns seen being used by MERCURY APT
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessCommandLine contains "-exec bypass -w 1 -enc" and ProcessCommandLine contains "UwB0AGEAcgB0AC0ASgBvAGIAIAAtAFMAYwByAGkAcAB0AEIAbABvAGMAawAgAHsAKABzAGEAcABzACAAKAAiAHAA"

de: Detects use of aspnet_regiis to decrypt Microsoft IIS connection strings. An attacker with Microsoft IIS web server access via a webshell or alike can decrypt and dump any hardcoded connection strings, such as the MSSQL service account password using aspnet_regiis command.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\aspnet_regiis.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "aspnet_regiis.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "connectionStrings" and ProcessCommandLine contains " -pdf")

t: Microsoft IIS Service Account Password Dumped
au: Tim Rauch, Janantha Marasinghe, Elastic (original idea)
de: Detects the Internet Information Services (IIS) command-line tool, AppCmd, being used to list passwords
q:
DeviceProcessEvents

t: Modification Of MCP Or Claude Configuration File - Linux
de: Detects writes to Claude Code or Claude Desktop configuration files where MCP server definitions live. Files include .claude.json, ~/.claude/settings.json, ~/.config/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json, and standalone mcp.json files. An attacker who can write a new MCP server entry into these files gains arbitrary tool execution the next time the agent loads, which is a stealthy persistence and command-and-control vector.
fp: Claude Code itself (runs as a node process) writing settings; covered by the filter but worth tuning per fleet (path of node binary varies)
Configuration management tooling (Ansible, Chef, Puppet) deploying organisation-approved MCP server entries
Backup or sync agents (rclone, restic, Dropbox client) restoring user dotfiles
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "/.claude.json" or FolderPath endswith "/.claude/settings.json" or FolderPath endswith "/.claude/settings.local.json" or FolderPath endswith "/.config/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json" or FolderPath endswith "/mcp.json" or FolderPath endswith "/.cursor/mcp.json" or FolderPath endswith "/.continue/config.json") and (not((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/claude" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/cursor" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/node")))

t: Modify User Shell Folders Startup Value
de: Detect modification of the User Shell Folders registry values for Startup or Common Startup which could indicate persistence attempts. Attackers may modify User Shell Folders registry keys to point to malicious executables or scripts that will be executed during startup. This technique is often used to maintain persistence on a compromised system by ensuring that the malicious payload is executed automatically.
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where ((RegistryKey contains "SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Explorer\\User Shell Folders" or RegistryKey contains "SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Explorer\\Shell Folders") and (RegistryKey endswith "\\Common Startup" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Startup")) and (not((isnull(RegistryValueData) or (RegistryValueData contains "C:\\ProgramData\\Microsoft\\Windows\\Start Menu\\Programs\\Startup" or RegistryValueData contains "%ProgramData%\\Microsoft\\Windows\\Start Menu\\Programs\\Startup") or (RegistryValueData contains "%USERPROFILE%\\AppData\\Roaming\\Microsoft\\Windows\\Start Menu\\Programs\\Startup" or RegistryValueData contains "%%USERPROFILE%%\\AppData\\Roaming\\Microsoft\\Windows\\Start Menu\\Programs\\Startup") or (RegistryValueData contains "C:\\Users\\" and RegistryValueData contains "\\AppData\\Roaming\\Microsoft\\Windows\\Start Menu\\Programs\\Startup"))))

t: msiexec.exe Spawning cmd.exe to Start an LNK File
de: Detects msiexec.exe spawning cmd.exe with the pattern "/d /s /c" plus a ".lnk" target. DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\msiexec.exe" and FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "/d /s /c" and ProcessCommandLine contains ".lnk")

de: Detects a network connection that is initiated by the "notepad.exe" process. This might be a sign of process injection from a beacon process or something similar. Notepad rarely initiates a network communication except when printing documents for example.
fp: Printing documents via notepad might cause communication with the printer via port 9100 or similar.

DeviceNetworkEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\notepad.exe" and (not(RemotePort == 9100))

de: Detects the attempt to create an ActiveScriptEventConsumer via WMIC.EXE. Adversaries often abuse ActiveScriptEventConsumer to maintain persistence on a compromised host by executing a malicious script whenever a specific event occurs.

t: NTLM Hash Leak Via Curl NTLM Authentication
de: Detects the use of curl with NTLM authentication and empty credentials (-u :), which can be abused to leak the currently logged-in user's NTLMv2 challenge-response to an attacker- controlled server, enabling offline cracking or relay attacks. When no credentials are provided, the Microsoft-shipped curl passes a NULL identity to Windows SSPI, which automatically falls back to the current user's logon session credentials stored in LSASS — without requiring a plaintext password. This behavior is exclusive to the curl binary shipped by Microsoft (available since Windows 10 / Windows Server 2019), which is built with SSPI support.
fp: Should be very rare as it's not widely known or used, but could occur in legitimate use cases where curl is used with NTLM authentication and empty credentials, such as in certain scripts or automation tasks.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\curl.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "curl.exe") and ProcessCommandLine contains "--ntlm" and ProcessCommandLine matches regex "(?i)\\s(-u|--user)\\s*:"

t: Obfuscated PowerShell MSI Install via WindowsInstaller COM
de: Detects the execution of obfuscated PowerShell commands that attempt to install MSI packages via the Windows Installer COM object (`WindowsInstaller.Installer`). The technique involves manipulating strings to hide functionality, such as constructing class names using string insertion (e.g., 'indowsInstaller.Installer'.Insert(0,'W')) and correcting malformed URLs (e.g., converting 'htps://' to 'https://') at runtime. This behavior is commonly associated with malware loaders or droppers that aim to bypass static detection by hiding intent in runtime- generated strings and using legitimate tools for code execution. The use of `InstallProduct` and COM object creation, particularly combined with hidden window execution and suppressed UI, indicates an attempt to install software (likely malicious) without user interaction.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\powershell_ise.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("PowerShell_ISE.EXE", "PowerShell.EXE", "pwsh.dll"))) and (ProcessCommandLine contains "-ComObject" and ProcessCommandLine contains "InstallProduct(" and ProcessCommandLine contains ".Insert(" and ProcessCommandLine contains "UILevel")

t: OpenAI Codex Command Runner Child Process Outside Expected Sandbox User Identity
au: Jonathan Johnson, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
de: Detects a child process spawned by the OpenAI Codex command runner (codex-command-runner-*.exe) running under a user account other than the expected sandbox identities (CodexSandboxOffline or CodexSandboxOnline). The command runner operates exclusively as one of the two restricted local sandbox accounts and is expected to inherit that identity to all children it spawns. A child process running under any other user indicates that the restricted token context has been broken — either through token impersonation, a restricted-token bypass, or a local privilege escalation — and the process has escaped the Codex sandbox boundary.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\codex-command-runner-" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith ".exe") and (not((AccountName in~ ("CodexSandboxOffline", "CodexSandboxOnline"))))
pr: #6030 new: OpenAI Codex sandbox abuse detection rules

t: OpenAI Codex Command Runner Execution by Unexpected User
au: Jonathan Johnson, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
de: Detects execution of the OpenAI Codex command runner binary (codex-command-runner-*.exe) under a user account other than the expected dedicated sandbox accounts (CodexSandboxOffline or CodexSandboxOnline). Codex enforces its sandbox boundary by running the command runner exclusively as one of these two restricted local accounts. Execution under any other user may indicate a sandbox escape, token impersonation, or deliberate misuse of the command runner outside its intended security context.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath contains "\\codex-command-runner-" and (not((AccountName in~ ("CodexSandboxOffline", "CodexSandboxOnline"))))
pr: #6030 new: OpenAI Codex sandbox abuse detection rules

t: Osk.exe or ATBroker.exe Modifying Service ImagePath Registry Value
de: Detects potential privilege escalation attempts where osk.exe or ATBroker.exe modifies the ImagePath registry value of a Windows service. This behavior is associated with exploitation of CVE-2026-24291 (RegPwn), where attackers leverage registry symlink redirection to overwrite protected registry keys and escalate privileges to SYSTEM.

q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\ATBroker.exe" and RegistryKey contains "Microsoft\\Windows NT\\CurrentVersion\\Accessibility\\Session" and RegistryKey endswith "ATConfig\\osk\\ImagePath") or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\osk.exe" and RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Services.*$" and RegistryKey endswith "\\ImagePath" and (InitiatingProcessAccountName contains "AUTHORI" or InitiatingProcessAccountName contains "AUTORI"))

t: Outbound Network Connection Initiated By Microsoft Dialer
de: Detects outbound network connection initiated by Microsoft Dialer. The Microsoft Dialer, also known as Phone Dialer, is a built-in utility application included in various versions of the Microsoft Windows operating system. Its primary function is to provide users with a graphical interface for managing phone calls via a modem or a phone line connected to the computer. This is an outdated process in the current conext of it's usage and is a common target for info stealers for process injection, and is used to make C2 connections, common example is "Rhadamanthys"
fp: In Modern Windows systems, unable to see legitimate usage of this process, However, if an organization has legitimate purpose for this there can be false positives.
q:
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith ":\\Windows\\System32\\dialer.exe" and (not((ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "127.0.0.0/8") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "10.0.0.0/8") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "172.16.0.0/12") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "192.168.0.0/16") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "169.254.0.0/16") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "::1/128") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "fe80::/10") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "fc00::/7"))))

de: Detects the use of the "tar" utility with the "--checkpoint-action" or "--to-command" options. These options allow "tar" to execute arbitrary commands and are abused for privilege escalation (e.g. via "sudo tar"), to break out of restricted environments, or through tar wildcard injection where crafted file names are expanded by the shell and interpreted by "tar" as command-line options.
fp: Unlikely. The "--checkpoint-action" and "--to-command" options are rarely used in legitimate automation and should be investigated.
q:

| where FolderPath endswith "/tar" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "--checkpoint-action" or ProcessCommandLine contains "--to-command")

t: Potential Command Execution Via Tcpdump Postrotate Command
de: Detects execution of "tcpdump" with the "-z" (postrotate) option pointing to a shell, a script located in a temporary directory, or combined with "-Z root". The "-z" option runs the specified command after every rotated capture file. When "tcpdump" is executed with elevated privileges (e.g. via "sudo"), this is abused to execute arbitrary commands as root, a well-known Linux privilege-escalation primitive.
fp: Legitimate use of the "-z" option to run a compression utility (e.g. "gzip") on rotated capture files will generally not match, as it lacks the suspicious indicators required by this rule.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "/tcpdump" and ProcessCommandLine contains " -z " and (ProcessCommandLine contains "/tmp/" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/dev/shm/" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/var/tmp/" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/bin/sh" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/bin/bash" or ProcessCommandLine contains " -Z root")

de: Detects the 3CXDesktopApp updater downloading a known compromised version of the 3CXDesktopApp software
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\3CXDesktopApp\\app\\update.exe" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "--update" and ProcessCommandLine contains "http" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/electron/update/win32/18.12")

t: Potential Conti Ransomware Database Dumping Activity Via SQLCmd
de: Detects a command used by conti to dump database
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\sqlcmd.exe" or (ProcessCommandLine contains "sqlcmd " or ProcessCommandLine contains "sqlcmd.exe")) and ProcessCommandLine contains " -S localhost " and (ProcessCommandLine contains "sys.sysprocesses" or ProcessCommandLine contains "master.dbo.sysdatabases" or ProcessCommandLine contains "BACKUP DATABASE")

t: Potential Credential Dumping Attempt Using New NetworkProvider - CLI
de: Detects when an attacker tries to add a new network provider in order to dump clear text credentials, similar to how the NPPSpy tool does it
fp: Other legitimate network providers used and not filtred in this rule
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessCommandLine contains "\\System\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\" and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\NetworkProvider"

de: Detects potential credential dumping via Windows Error Reporting LSASS Shtinkering technique which uses the Windows Error Reporting to dump lsass
fp: Windows Error Reporting might produce similar behavior. In that case, check the PID associated with the "-p" parameter in the CommandLine.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\Werfault.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "WerFault.exe") and ((InitiatingProcessAccountName contains "AUTHORI" or InitiatingProcessAccountName contains "AUTORI") and (AccountName contains "AUTHORI" or AccountName contains "AUTORI") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " -u -p " and ProcessCommandLine contains " -ip " and ProcessCommandLine contains " -s "))) and (not(InitiatingProcessFolderPath =~ "C:\\Windows\\System32\\lsass.exe"))

de: Detects command line parameters or strings often used by crypto miners
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessCommandLine contains " --cpu-priority=" or ProcessCommandLine contains "--donate-level=0" or ProcessCommandLine contains " -o pool." or ProcessCommandLine contains " --nicehash" or ProcessCommandLine contains " --algo=rx/0 " or ProcessCommandLine contains "stratum+tcp://" or ProcessCommandLine contains "stratum+udp://" or ProcessCommandLine contains "LS1kb25hdGUtbGV2ZWw9" or ProcessCommandLine contains "0tZG9uYXRlLWxldmVsP" or ProcessCommandLine contains "tLWRvbmF0ZS1sZXZlbD" or ProcessCommandLine contains "c3RyYXR1bSt0Y3A6Ly" or ProcessCommandLine contains "N0cmF0dW0rdGNwOi8v" or ProcessCommandLine contains "zdHJhdHVtK3RjcDovL" or ProcessCommandLine contains "c3RyYXR1bSt1ZHA6Ly" or ProcessCommandLine contains "N0cmF0dW0rdWRwOi8v" or ProcessCommandLine contains "zdHJhdHVtK3VkcDovL") and (not((ProcessCommandLine contains " pool.c " or ProcessCommandLine contains " pool.o " or ProcessCommandLine contains "gcc -")))

t: Potential CSharp Streamer RAT Loading .NET Executable Image
de: Detects potential CSharp Streamer RAT loading .NET executable image by using the default file name and path associated with the tool.
q:
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where FolderPath matches regex "\\\\AppData\\\\Local\\\\Temp\\\\dat[0-9A-Z]{4}\\.tmp"

de: Detects possible successful exploitation for vulnerability described in CVE-2021-26857 by looking for | abnormal subprocesses spawning by Exchange Server's Unified Messaging service
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\UMWorkerProcess.exe" and (not((FolderPath endswith "wermgr.exe" or FolderPath endswith "WerFault.exe")))

de: Detects potential exploitation of CVE-2021-40444 via suspicious process patterns seen in in-the- wild exploitations
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\control.exe" and (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\winword.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\powerpnt.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\excel.exe")) and (not((ProcessCommandLine endswith "\\control.exe input.dll" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "\\control.exe\" input.dll")))

t: Potential CVE-2021-44228 Exploitation Attempt - VMware Horizon
de: Detects potential initial exploitation attempts against VMware Horizon deployments running a vulnerable versions of Log4j.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\ws_TomcatService.exe" and (not((FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe")))

de: Detects suspicious remote procedure call (RPC) service anomalies based on the spawned sub processes (long shot to detect the exploitation of vulnerabilities like CVE-2022-26809)
fp: Some cases in which the service spawned a werfault.exe process
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath =~ "C:\\Windows\\System32\\svchost.exe" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "-k RPCSS"

de: Detects potential exploitation attempts of CVE-2022-29072, a 7-Zip privilege escalation and command execution vulnerability. 7-Zip version 21.07 and earlier on Windows allows privilege escalation (CVE-2022-29072) and command execution when a file with the .7z extension is dragged to the Help>Contents area. This is caused by misconfiguration of 7z.dll and a heap overflow. The command runs in a child process under the 7zFM.exe process.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\7zFM.exe" and ((FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("Cmd.Exe", "PowerShell.EXE", "pwsh.dll")))) and (not((((ProcessCommandLine contains " /c " or ProcessCommandLine contains " /k " or ProcessCommandLine contains " /r ") or (ProcessCommandLine endswith ".bat" or ProcessCommandLine endswith ".cmd" or ProcessCommandLine endswith ".ps1")) or isnull(ProcessCommandLine))))

de: Detects potential exploitation of CVE-2023-21554 (dubbed QueueJumper)
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\Windows\\System32\\mqsvc.exe" and (FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\cscript.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\mshta.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\regsvr32.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\schtasks.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\wmic.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\wscript.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\wsl.exe")

t: Potential CVE-2023-27363 Exploitation - HTA File Creation By FoxitPDFReader
de: Detects suspicious ".hta" file creation in the startup folder by Foxit Reader. This can be an indication of CVE-2023-27363 exploitation.
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\FoxitPDFReader.exe" and FolderPath contains "\\Microsoft\\Windows\\Start Menu\\Programs\\Startup\\" and FolderPath endswith ".hta"

t: Potential CVE-2023-36874 Exploitation - Fake Wermgr Execution
de: Detects the execution of a renamed "cmd", "powershell" or "powershell_ise" binary. Attackers were seen using these binaries in a renamed form as "wermgr.exe" in exploitation of CVE-2023-36874
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("Cmd.Exe", "powershell_ise.EXE", "powershell.exe")) and FolderPath endswith "\\wermgr.exe"

t: Potential CVE-2023-36874 Exploitation - Fake Wermgr.Exe Creation
de: Detects the creation of a file named "wermgr.exe" being created in an uncommon directory. This could be a sign of potential exploitation of CVE-2023-36874.
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\wermgr.exe" and (not((FolderPath contains ":\\$WINDOWS.~BT\\NewOS\\" or FolderPath contains ":\\$WinREAgent\\" or FolderPath contains ":\\Windows\\servicing\\LCU\\" or FolderPath contains ":\\Windows\\System32\\" or FolderPath contains ":\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\" or FolderPath contains ":\\Windows\\WinSxS\\" or FolderPath contains ":\\WUDownloadCache\\" or FolderPath contains ":\\Windows\\SoftwareDistribution\\Download\\")))

t: Potential CVE-2026-33829 Exploitation - Windows Snipping Tool Remote File Path URI
au: Samir Bousseaden, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
de: Detects potential exploitation of CVE-2026-33829, a vulnerability in the Windows Snipping Tool URI handler (ms-screensketch:). An attacker can abuse the 'filePath' parameter to supply a UNC path or HTTP URL, causing SnippingTool.exe to initiate a connection to a remote resource. When a UNC path is used (e.g. \\attacker.com\share), this triggers an outbound NTLM authentication attempt, allowing the attacker to capture or relay the victim's Net-NTLMv2 hash. HTTP-based paths may result in remote file loading or server-side request forgery (SSRF)-style access. The URI can be delivered via a malicious hyperlink, phishing email, or web page.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\SnippingTool.exe" and ((ProcessCommandLine contains "ms-screensketch:edit" and ProcessCommandLine contains "&filePath=\\") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "ms-screensketch:edit" and ProcessCommandLine contains "&filePath=%%5C") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "ms-screensketch:edit" and ProcessCommandLine contains "&filePath=%5C") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "ms-screensketch:edit" and ProcessCommandLine contains "&filePath=http"))

t: Potential Data Exfiltration Activity Via CommandLine Tools
de: Detects the use of various CLI utilities exfiltrating data via web requests
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (((FolderPath endswith "\\powershell_ise.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "curl " or ProcessCommandLine contains "Invoke-RestMethod" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Invoke-WebRequest" or ProcessCommandLine contains "irm " or ProcessCommandLine contains "iwr " or ProcessCommandLine contains "wget ") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " -ur" and ProcessCommandLine contains " -me" and ProcessCommandLine contains " -b" and ProcessCommandLine contains " POST ")) or ((FolderPath endswith "\\curl.exe" and ProcessCommandLine contains "--ur") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " -d " or ProcessCommandLine contains " --data ")) or (FolderPath endswith "\\wget.exe" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "--post-data" or ProcessCommandLine contains "--post-file"))) and ((ProcessCommandLine matches regex "net\\s+view" or ProcessCommandLine matches regex "sc\\s+query") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "Get-Content" or ProcessCommandLine contains "GetBytes" or ProcessCommandLine contains "hostname" or ProcessCommandLine contains "ifconfig" or ProcessCommandLine contains "ipconfig" or ProcessCommandLine contains "netstat" or ProcessCommandLine contains "nltest" or ProcessCommandLine contains "qprocess" or ProcessCommandLine contains "systeminfo" or ProcessCommandLine contains "tasklist" or ProcessCommandLine contains "ToBase64String" or ProcessCommandLine contains "whoami") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "type " and ProcessCommandLine contains " > " and ProcessCommandLine contains " C:\\"))

t: Potential Data Stealing Via Chromium Headless Debugging
de: Detects chromium based browsers starting in headless and debugging mode and pointing to a user profile. This could be a sign of data stealing or remote control
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessCommandLine contains "--remote-debugging-" and ProcessCommandLine contains "--user-data-dir" and ProcessCommandLine contains "--headless"

t: Potential Defense Evasion Via Rename Of Highly Relevant Binaries
au: Matthew Green - @mgreen27, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), frack113
de: Detects the execution of a renamed binary often used by attackers or malware leveraging new Sysmon OriginalFileName datapoint.
fp: Custom applications use renamed binaries adding slight change to binary name. Typically this is easy to spot and add to whitelist
PsExec installed via Windows Store doesn't contain original filename field (False negative)
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessVersionInfoFileDescription =~ "Execute processes remotely" or ProcessVersionInfoProductName =~ "Sysinternals PsExec" or (ProcessVersionInfoFileDescription startswith "Windows PowerShell" or ProcessVersionInfoFileDescription startswith "pwsh") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("certutil.exe", "cmstp.exe", "cscript.exe", "IE4UINIT.EXE", "finger.exe", "mshta.exe", "msiexec.exe", "msxsl.exe", "powershell_ise.exe", "powershell.exe", "psexec.c", "psexec.exe", "psexesvc.exe", "pwsh.dll", "reg.exe", "regsvr32.exe", "rundll32.exe", "WerMgr", "wmic.exe", "wscript.exe"))) and (not((FolderPath endswith "\\certutil.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\cmstp.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\cscript.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\ie4uinit.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\finger.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\mshta.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\msiexec.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\msxsl.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\powershell_ise.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\psexec.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\psexec64.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\psexec64a.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\PSEXESVC.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\reg.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\regsvr32.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\wermgr.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\wmic.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\wscript.exe")))

t: Potential Defense Evasion Via Right-to-Left Override
au: Micah Babinski, @micahbabinski, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems), Luc Génaux
de: Detects the presence of the "u202+E" character, which causes a terminal, browser, or operating system to render text in a right-to-left sequence. This character is used as an obfuscation and masquerading techniques by adversaries to trick users into opening malicious files.
fp: Commandlines that contains scriptures such as arabic or hebrew might make use of this character
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessCommandLine contains "\\u202e" or ProcessCommandLine contains "[U+202E]" or ProcessCommandLine contains "‮"

de: Detects specific process behavior observed with Devil Bait samples
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\wscript.exe" and FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" and ProcessCommandLine contains ">>%APPDATA%\\Microsoft\\" and (ProcessCommandLine endswith ".xml" or ProcessCommandLine endswith ".txt")) and (ProcessCommandLine matches regex "ipconfig\\s+/all" or (ProcessCommandLine contains "dir" or ProcessCommandLine contains "systeminfo" or ProcessCommandLine contains "tasklist"))

de: Detects the creation of ".xml" and ".txt" files in folders of the "\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft" directory by uncommon processes. This behavior was seen common across different Devil Bait samples and stages as described by the NCSC
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\schtasks.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\wscript.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\mshta.exe") and FolderPath contains "\\AppData\\Roaming\\Microsoft\\" and (FolderPath endswith ".txt" or FolderPath endswith ".xml")

de: Detects potential DLL sideloading using comctl32.dll to obtain system privileges
q:
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where (FolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\System32\\logonUI.exe.local\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\System32\\werFault.exe.local\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\System32\\consent.exe.local\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\System32\\narrator.exe.local\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\windows\\system32\\wermgr.exe.local\\") and FolderPath endswith "\\comctl32.dll"

q:

t: Potential DLL Sideloading Via VMware Xfer
de: Detects loading of a DLL by the VMware Xfer utility from the non-default directory which may be an attempt to sideload arbitrary DLL
q:
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\VMwareXferlogs.exe" and FolderPath endswith "\\glib-2.0.dll") and (not(FolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files\\VMware\\"))

de: Detects potential DLL sideloading of "EACore.dll"
q:
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\EACore.dll" and (not(((InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "C:\\Program Files\\Electronic Arts\\EA Desktop\\" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\EACoreServer.exe") and FolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files\\Electronic Arts\\EA Desktop\\")))

de: Detects potential DLL sideloading of "edputil.dll"
q:
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\edputil.dll" and (not((FolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\System32\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\" or FolderPath startswith "C\\Windows\\WinSxS\\")))

| where ((ProcessCommandLine contains " -e" and ProcessCommandLine contains " PAA") or ProcessCommandLine contains "JABlAG4AdgA6AHUAcwBlAHIAcAByAG8AZgBpAGwAZQ" or ProcessCommandLine contains "QAZQBuAHYAOgB1AHMAZQByAHAAcgBvAGYAaQBsAGUA" or ProcessCommandLine contains "kAGUAbgB2ADoAdQBzAGUAcgBwAHIAbwBmAGkAbABlA" or ProcessCommandLine contains "IgAoACcAKgAnACkAOwAkA" or ProcessCommandLine contains "IAKAAnACoAJwApADsAJA" or ProcessCommandLine contains "iACgAJwAqACcAKQA7ACQA" or ProcessCommandLine contains "JABGAGwAeAByAGgAYwBmAGQ" or ProcessCommandLine contains "PQAkAGUAbgB2ADoAdABlAG0AcAArACgA" or ProcessCommandLine contains "0AJABlAG4AdgA6AHQAZQBtAHAAKwAoA" or ProcessCommandLine contains "9ACQAZQBuAHYAOgB0AGUAbQBwACsAKA") and (not((ProcessCommandLine contains "fAAgAEMAbwBuAHYAZQByAHQAVABvAC0ASgBzAG8AbgAgAC0ARQByAHIAbwByAEEAYwB0AGkAbwBuACAAUwBpAGwAZQBuAHQAbAB5AEMAbwBuAHQAaQBuAHUAZQ" or ProcessCommandLine contains "wAIABDAG8AbgB2AGUAcgB0AFQAbwAtAEoAcwBvAG4AIAAtAEUAcgByAG8AcgBBAGMAdABpAG8AbgAgAFMAaQBsAGUAbgB0AGwAeQBDAG8AbgB0AGkAbgB1AGUA" or ProcessCommandLine contains "8ACAAQwBvAG4AdgBlAHIAdABUAG8ALQBKAHMAbwBuACAALQBFAHIAcgBvAHIAQQBjAHQAaQBvAG4AIABTAGkAbABlAG4AdABsAHkAQwBvAG4AdABpAG4AdQBlA")))

de: Detects potential EmpireMonkey APT activity
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessCommandLine contains "/e:jscript" and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Local\\Temp\\Errors.bat"

de: Detects tampering with EventLog service "file" key. In order to change the default location of an Evtx file. This technique is used to tamper with log collection and alerting
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where (RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\EventLog.*$" and RegistryKey endswith "\\File") and (not(RegistryValueData contains "\\System32\\Winevt\\Logs\\"))

t: Potential Excel.EXE DCOM Lateral Movement Via ActivateMicrosoftApp
de: Detects suspicious child processes of Excel which could be an indicator of lateral movement leveraging the "ActivateMicrosoftApp" Excel DCOM object.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\excel.exe" and ((ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("foxprow.exe", "schdplus.exe", "winproj.exe")) or (FolderPath endswith "\\foxprow.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\schdplus.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\winproj.exe"))

t: Potential Exploitation Attempt From Office Application
de: Detects Office applications executing a child process that includes directory traversal patterns. This could be an attempt to exploit CVE-2022-30190 (MSDT RCE) or CVE-2021-40444 (MSHTML RCE)
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\winword.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\excel.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\powerpnt.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\msaccess.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\mspub.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\eqnedt32.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\visio.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "../../../.." or ProcessCommandLine contains "..\\..\\..\\.." or ProcessCommandLine contains "..//..//..//..")

t: Potential Exploitation Attempt Of Undocumented WindowsServer RCE
de: Detects potential exploitation attempt of undocumented Windows Server Pre Auth Remote Code Execution (RCE)
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\svchost.exe" and FolderPath endswith "\\svchost.exe" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "-k DHCPServer" and ProcessCommandLine contains "-k DHCPServer" and (AccountName contains "NETWORK SERVICE" or AccountName contains "NETZWERKDIENST" or AccountName contains "SERVIZIO DI RETE" or AccountName contains "SERVICIO DE RED")

t: Potential Exploitation of CVE-2024-3094 - Suspicious SSH Child Process
au: Arnim Rupp, Nasreddine Bencherchali, Thomas Patzke
de: Detects potentially suspicious child process of SSH process (sshd) with a specific execution user. This could be a sign of potential exploitation of CVE-2024-3094.
fp: Administrative activity directly with root authentication might trigger this rule if it's unnecessarily prefixed with "sh -c" or "bash -c"
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/sshd" and (ProcessCommandLine startswith "bash -c" or ProcessCommandLine startswith "sh -c") and AccountName =~ "root"

t: Potential Exploitation of CVE-2024-37085 - Suspicious Creation Of ESX Admins Group
de: Detects execution of the "net.exe" command in order to add a group named "ESX Admins". This could indicates a potential exploitation attempt of CVE-2024-37085, which allows an attacker to elevate their privileges to full administrative access on an domain-joined ESXi hypervisor. VMware ESXi hypervisors joined to an Active Directory domain consider any member of a domain group named "ESX Admins" to have full administrative access by default.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (((FolderPath endswith "\\net.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\net1.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("net.exe", "net1.exe"))) and (ProcessCommandLine contains "/add" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/domain" and ProcessCommandLine contains "ESX Admins" and ProcessCommandLine contains "group")) or (((FolderPath endswith "\\PowerShell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("PowerShell.exe", "pwsh.dll"))) and (ProcessCommandLine contains "New-ADGroup" and ProcessCommandLine contains "ESX Admins"))

au: Jonathan Peters (Nextron Systems), Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
de: Detects suspicious filenames that contain a right-to-left override character and a potentially spoofed file extensions.

| where (FolderPath contains "\\u202e" or FolderPath contains "[U+202E]" or FolderPath contains "‮") and (FolderPath contains "3pm." or FolderPath contains "4pm." or FolderPath contains "cod." or FolderPath contains "fdp." or FolderPath contains "ftr." or FolderPath contains "gepj." or FolderPath contains "gnp." or FolderPath contains "gpj." or FolderPath contains "ism." or FolderPath contains "lmth." or FolderPath contains "nls." or FolderPath contains "piz." or FolderPath contains "slx." or FolderPath contains "tdo." or FolderPath contains "vsc." or FolderPath contains "vwm." or FolderPath contains "xcod." or FolderPath contains "xslx." or FolderPath contains "xtpp.")

au: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

t: Potential LSASS Process Dump Via Procdump
de: Detects potential credential harvesting attempts through LSASS memory dumps using ProcDump. This rule identifies suspicious command-line patterns that combine memory dump flags (-ma, -mm, -mp) with LSASS-related process markers. LSASS (Local Security Authority Subsystem Service) contains sensitive authentication data including plaintext passwords, NTLM hashes, and Kerberos tickets in memory. Attackers commonly dump LSASS memory to extract credentials for lateral movement and privilege escalation.
fp: Unlikely, because no one should dump an lsass process memory
Another tool that uses command line flags similar to ProcDump
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessCommandLine contains " -ma " or ProcessCommandLine contains " /ma " or ProcessCommandLine contains " –ma " or ProcessCommandLine contains " —ma " or ProcessCommandLine contains " ―ma " or ProcessCommandLine contains " -mm " or ProcessCommandLine contains " /mm " or ProcessCommandLine contains " –mm " or ProcessCommandLine contains " —mm " or ProcessCommandLine contains " ―mm " or ProcessCommandLine contains " -mp " or ProcessCommandLine contains " /mp " or ProcessCommandLine contains " –mp " or ProcessCommandLine contains " —mp " or ProcessCommandLine contains " ―mp ") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " ls" or ProcessCommandLine contains " keyiso" or ProcessCommandLine contains " samss")

t: Potential Mandatory Profile Persistence Via NTUSER.MAN Creation
de: Detects the creation or modification of an NTUSER.MAN file in a user profile path. NTUSER.MAN is used for mandatory profiles and takes precedence over NTUSER.DAT when Windows loads the user's HKCU hive at logon. Attackers can stage a modified hive as NTUSER.MAN to introduce HKCU persistence without generating registry write telemetry.
fp: Legitimate mandatory profile deployment in kiosk, shared workstation, or roaming profile environments.
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where (FolderPath contains ":\\Users\\" and FolderPath endswith "\\NTUSER.MAN") or (FolderPath startswith "\\" and FolderPath endswith "\\NTUSER.MAN")

t: Potential NTLM Authentication Coercion Tool Execution
de: Detects execution of tools that perform NTLM authentication coercion by abusing Windows RPC interfaces. These tools force a target machine (typically a Domain Controller) to authenticate outbound to an attacker-controlled listener using its machine account credentials, enabling NTLM relay attacks and potential full domain compromise. Covered tools and techniques: - DFSCoerce: abuses the MS-DFSNM (Distributed File System Namespace Management) RPC interface. - ShadowCoerce: abuses the MS-FSRVP (File Server Remote VSS Protocol) RPC interface. - Coercer: a meta-tool by p0dalirius that automates coercion via multiple RPC interfaces (MS-DFSNM, MS-FSRVP, MS-RPRN, MS-EFSRPC, MS-ICPR, and others). - WSPCoerce: abuses the MS-WSP (Windows Search Protocol) RPC interface. This rule detects the *coercion phase* (forcing authentication) and complements existing rules covering the *relay phase* (ntlmrelayx, Responder, Impacket). Note: DFSCoerce and PrinterBug remain unpatched on default Windows Server 2019/2022 configurations as of 2026, as Microsoft does not classify forced authentication as a vulnerability when credentials are required.
fp: Unlikely. These tool names and command patterns have no legitimate use in production environments.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath contains "DFSCoerce" or FolderPath contains "dfscoerce" or FolderPath contains "ShadowCoerce" or FolderPath contains "shadowcoerce" or FolderPath contains "WSPCoerce" or FolderPath contains "wspcoerce") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "DFSCoerce.py" or ProcessCommandLine contains "dfscoerce.py" or ProcessCommandLine contains "ShadowCoerce.py" or ProcessCommandLine contains "shadowcoerce.py" or ProcessCommandLine contains "WSPCoerce.py" or ProcessCommandLine contains "wspcoerce.py") or (FolderPath contains "coercer" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "coercer coerce" or ProcessCommandLine contains "coercer scan" or ProcessCommandLine contains "coercer fuzz" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-m coerce" or ProcessCommandLine contains "from coercer"))
pr: #6111 Add rule: potential NTLM authentication coercion tool execution

t: Potential Persistence Via App Paths Default Property
de: Detects changes to the "Default" property for keys located in the \Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\App Paths\ registry. Which might be used as a method of persistence The entries found under App Paths are used primarily for the following purposes. First, to map an application's executable file name to that file's fully qualified path. Second, to prepend information to the PATH environment variable on a per-application, per-process basis.
fp: Legitimate applications registering their binary from on of the suspicious locations mentioned above (tune it)
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where RegistryKey contains "\\SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\App Paths" and (RegistryKey endswith "(Default)" or RegistryKey endswith "Path") and (RegistryValueData contains "\\Users\\Public" or RegistryValueData contains "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\" or RegistryValueData contains "\\Windows\\Temp\\" or RegistryValueData contains "\\Desktop\\" or RegistryValueData contains "\\Downloads\\" or RegistryValueData contains "%temp%" or RegistryValueData contains "%tmp%" or RegistryValueData contains "iex" or RegistryValueData contains "Invoke-" or RegistryValueData contains "rundll32" or RegistryValueData contains "regsvr32" or RegistryValueData contains "mshta" or RegistryValueData contains "cscript" or RegistryValueData contains "wscript" or RegistryValueData contains ".bat" or RegistryValueData contains ".hta" or RegistryValueData contains ".dll" or RegistryValueData contains ".ps1")
