de: Detects the execution of rundll32 that leads to an external network connection. The malware Pikabot has been seen to use this technique to initiate C2-communication through hard-coded Windows binaries.
q:
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName =~ "rundll32.exe" and (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\SearchFilterHost.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\SearchProtocolHost.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\sndvol.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\wermgr.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\wwahost.exe") and Protocol =~ "tcp"

de: Detects system discovery activity carried out by Pikabot, such as incl. network, user info and domain groups. The malware Pikabot has been seen to use this technique as part of its C2-botnet registration with a short collection time frame (less than 1 minute).
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessParentFileName =~ "rundll32.exe" or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\SearchFilterHost.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\SearchProtocolHost.exe")) and (ProcessCommandLine in~ ("ipconfig.exe /all", "netstat.exe -aon", "whoami.exe /all"))

de: Detects the execution of rundll32 that leads to the invocation of legitimate Windows binaries. The malware Pikabot has been seen to use this technique for process hollowing through hard-coded Windows binaries
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe" and (FolderPath endswith "\\SearchFilterHost.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\SearchProtocolHost.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\sndvol.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\wermgr.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\wwahost.exe")) and (not((FolderPath endswith "\\sndvol.exe" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "mmsys.cpl")))

de: Detects the execution of rundll32 that leads to the invocation of legitimate Windows binaries. The malware Pikabot has been seen to use this technique for process hollowing through hard-coded Windows binaries
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe" and (FolderPath endswith "\\SearchFilterHost.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\SearchProtocolHost.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\sndvol.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\wermgr.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\wwahost.exe")) and (not((FolderPath endswith "\\sndvol.exe" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "mmsys.cpl")))

de: Detects the execution of an executable that is typically used by PlugX for DLL side loading starting from an uncommon location

au: Teymur Kheirkhabarov (idea), Vasiliy Burov (rule), oscd.community, Tim Shelton (fp)
de: Detects the PowerShell command lines with special characters
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (((FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("PowerShell.EXE", "pwsh.dll"))) and (ProcessCommandLine matches regex "\\+.*\\+.*\\+.*\\+.*\\+.*\\+.*\\+.*\\+.*\\+.*\\+.*\\+.*\\+.*\\+.*\\+" or ProcessCommandLine matches regex "\\{.*\\{.*\\{.*\\{.*\\{.*\\{.*\\{.*\\{.*\\{.*\\{" or ProcessCommandLine matches regex "\\^.*\\^.*\\^.*\\^.*\\^" or ProcessCommandLine matches regex "`.*`.*`.*`.*`")) and (not((InitiatingProcessFolderPath =~ "C:\\Program Files\\Amazon\\SSM\\ssm-document-worker.exe" or (ProcessCommandLine contains "new EventSource(\"Microsoft.Windows.Sense.Client.Management\"" or ProcessCommandLine contains "public static extern bool InstallELAMCertificateInfo(SafeFileHandle handle);"))))

de: Detects usage of the "TcpClient" class. Which can be abused to establish remote connections and reverse-shells. As seen used by the Nishang "Invoke-PowerShellTcpOneLine" reverse shell and other.

q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("PowerShell.EXE", "pwsh.dll")) or (FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe")) and (ProcessCommandLine contains " Net.Sockets.TCPClient" and ProcessCommandLine contains ".GetStream(" and ProcessCommandLine contains ".Write(")

t: Potential Print Processor Persistence Via Registry
de: Detects the registration of a new print processor through the "Print Processors" registry key. Print processors are DLLs that are loaded by the print spooler service (spoolsv.exe), which runs as SYSTEM. Adversaries may abuse this mechanism to execute malicious DLLs for persistence and/or privilege escalation.
fp: Legitimate installation of third-party printer software that registers its own print processor
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where (RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\Control\\Print\\Environments.*$" and RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\Print Processors.*$") and (not((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\spoolsv.exe" and RegistryValueData endswith "winprint.dll")))
pr: #6508 Add Windows rules for T1547.012 Print Processors persistence

q:

t: Potential Privilege Escalation Using Symlink Between Osk and Cmd
de: Detects the creation of a symbolic link between "cmd.exe" and the accessibility on-screen keyboard binary (osk.exe) using "mklink". This technique provides an elevated command prompt to the user from the login screen without the need to log in.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "Cmd.Exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "mklink" and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\osk.exe" and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\cmd.exe")

t: Potential Privilege Escalation via Service Permissions Weakness
de: Detect modification of services configuration (ImagePath, FailureCommand and ServiceDLL) in registry by processes with Medium integrity level
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessIntegrityLevel in~ ("Medium", "S-1-16-8192")) and (ProcessCommandLine contains "ControlSet" and ProcessCommandLine contains "services") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "\\ImagePath" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\FailureCommand" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\ServiceDll")

t: Potential Privilege Escalation Via Sudo GTFOBins Shell Escape - Linux
de: Detects a GTFOBins-listed binary spawning a shell as a direct child of sudo. This indicates a low-privileged user with narrow sudo rights on a single binary (via sudoers misconfiguration) escaping to a root shell.
fp: Legitimate administrative use of these binaries under sudo is rare but possible in scripted maintenance tasks — review CommandLine context.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/sudo" and (FolderPath endswith "/find" or FolderPath endswith "/vim" or FolderPath endswith "/vi" or FolderPath endswith "/awk" or FolderPath endswith "/less" or FolderPath endswith "/more" or FolderPath endswith "/python" or FolderPath endswith "/python3" or FolderPath endswith "/perl" or FolderPath endswith "/nmap" or FolderPath endswith "/man" or FolderPath endswith "/gdb" or FolderPath endswith "/ftp") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "/bin/sh" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/bin/bash" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/bin/dash" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/bin/zsh" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-exec" or ProcessCommandLine contains "!bash" or ProcessCommandLine contains "!sh")
pr: #6201 Add rule: Sudo GTFOBins Shell Escape Privilege Escalation - Linux

de: Detects potential process injection via Microsoft Remote Asssistance (Msra.exe) by looking at suspicious child processes spawned from the aforementioned process. It has been a target used by many threat actors and used for discovery and persistence tactics
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\msra.exe" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine endswith "msra.exe" and (FolderPath endswith "\\arp.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\net.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\netstat.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\nslookup.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\route.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\schtasks.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\whoami.exe")

de: Detects potential abuse of the provisioning registry key for indirect command execution through "Provlaunch.exe".
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessCommandLine contains "SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Provisioning\\Commands\\"

t: Potential Provisioning Registry Key Abuse For Binary Proxy Execution - REG
de: Detects potential abuse of the provisioning registry key for indirect command execution through "Provlaunch.exe".
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Provisioning\\Commands.*$"

au: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
de: Detects potential psexec command that initiate execution on a remote systems via common commandline flags used by the utility
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessCommandLine contains "accepteula" and ProcessCommandLine contains " -u " and ProcessCommandLine contains " -p " and ProcessCommandLine contains " \\\\") and (not((ProcessCommandLine contains "\\\\localhost" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\\\127.")))

au: BlackBerry Threat Research and Intelligence Team - @Joseliyo_Jstnk
de: Detects changes to the PSFactory COM InProcServer32 registry. This technique was used by RomCom to create persistence storing a malicious DLL.
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where RegistryKey endswith "\\CLSID\\{c90250f3-4d7d-4991-9b69-a5c5bc1c2ae6}\\InProcServer32\\(Default)" and (not((RegistryValueData in~ ("%windir%\\System32\\ActXPrxy.dll", "C:\\Windows\\System32\\ActXPrxy.dll"))))

de: Detects a registry key used by IceID in a campaign that distributes malicious OneNote files
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where RegistryKey endswith "\\Software\\firm\\soft\\Name"

de: Detects specific process tree behavior of a "rundll32" execution often linked with potential Qakbot activity.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\cscript.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\curl.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\mshta.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\wscript.exe") and FolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe" and (ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\ProgramData\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Users\\Public\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\AppData\\Roaming\\")) and ProcessCommandLine contains ".dll"

t: Potential Radmin DLL Sideloading From User AppData
de: Detects the Radmin executable FamItrfc.exe loading BlkScrDl.dll from a user's local AppData Radmin directory, as observed in a reported supply-chain compromise.
q:
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\AppData\\Local\\Radmin\\FamItrfc.exe" and FolderPath endswith "\\AppData\\Local\\Radmin\\BlkScrDl.dll"
pr: #6502 Add Radmin DLL sideloading detection rule

t: Potential Ransomware Activity Using LegalNotice Message
de: Detect changes to the "LegalNoticeCaption" or "LegalNoticeText" registry values where the message set contains keywords often used in ransomware ransom messages
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where (RegistryKey contains "\\SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Policies\\System\\LegalNoticeCaption" or RegistryKey contains "\\SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Policies\\System\\LegalNoticeText") and (RegistryValueData contains "encrypted" or RegistryValueData contains "Unlock-Password" or RegistryValueData contains "paying")

t: Potential Raspberry Robin CPL Execution Activity
de: Detects the execution of a ".CPL" file located in the user temp directory via the Shell32 DLL "Control_RunDLL" export function. This behavior was observed in multiple Raspberry-Robin variants.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\control.exe") and (FolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "RUNDLL32.EXE") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "shell32.dll" and ProcessCommandLine contains "Control_RunDLL" and ProcessCommandLine contains ".CPL") and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\"

t: Potential Raspberry Robin Dot Ending File
de: Detects commandline containing reference to files ending with a "." This scheme has been seen used by raspberry-robin
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex "\\\\[a-zA-Z0-9]{1,32}\\.[a-zA-Z0-9]{1,6}\\.[ \"']{1}"

de: Detects potential DLL sideloading of rcdll.dll
q:
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\rcdll.dll" and (not((FolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Microsoft Visual Studio\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Windows Kits\\")))

de: Execution of plink to perform data exfiltration and tunneling
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\plink.exe" and ProcessCommandLine contains ":127.0.0.1:3389") or ((FolderPath endswith "\\plink.exe" and ProcessCommandLine contains ":3389") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " -P 443" or ProcessCommandLine contains " -P 22"))

de: Execution of ssh.exe to perform data exfiltration and tunneling through RDP
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\ssh.exe" and ProcessCommandLine contains ":3389"

fp: Legitimate usage by some scripts might trigger this as well
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "driverquery.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "drvqry.exe") and ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\cscript.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\mshta.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\regsvr32.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\wscript.exe") or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\AppData\\Local\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\Users\\Public\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\Windows\\Temp\\"))

fp: Legitimate usage by some scripts might trigger this as well
q:

| where (FolderPath endswith "driverquery.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "drvqry.exe") and ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\cscript.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\mshta.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\regsvr32.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\wscript.exe") or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\AppData\\Local\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\Users\\Public\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\Windows\\Temp\\"))
pr: #6091 Enrich ATT&CK tags (T1654/T1652) and dedupe bcdedit safeboot logic

t: Potential Reconnaissance For Cached Credentials Via Cmdkey.EXE
au: jmallette, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
de: Detects usage of cmdkey to look for cached credentials on the system
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\cmdkey.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "cmdkey.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " -l" or ProcessCommandLine contains " /l" or ProcessCommandLine contains " –l" or ProcessCommandLine contains " —l" or ProcessCommandLine contains " ―l")

t: Potential Registry Persistence Attempt Via Windows Telemetry
de: Detects potential persistence behavior using the windows telemetry registry key. Windows telemetry makes use of the binary CompatTelRunner.exe to run a variety of commands and perform the actual telemetry collections. This binary was created to be easily extensible, and to that end, it relies on the registry to instruct on which commands to run. The problem is, it will run any arbitrary command without restriction of location or type.
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where (RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows NT\\CurrentVersion\\AppCompatFlags\\TelemetryController.*$" and RegistryKey endswith "\\Command" and (RegistryValueData contains ".bat" or RegistryValueData contains ".bin" or RegistryValueData contains ".cmd" or RegistryValueData contains ".dat" or RegistryValueData contains ".dll" or RegistryValueData contains ".exe" or RegistryValueData contains ".hta" or RegistryValueData contains ".jar" or RegistryValueData contains ".js" or RegistryValueData contains ".msi" or RegistryValueData contains ".ps" or RegistryValueData contains ".sh" or RegistryValueData contains ".vb")) and (not((RegistryValueData contains "\\system32\\CompatTelRunner.exe" or RegistryValueData contains "\\system32\\DeviceCensus.exe")))

de: Detects when 'DllRegisterServer' is called in the commandline and the image is not rundll32. This could mean that the 'rundll32' utility has been renamed in order to avoid detection
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessCommandLine contains "DllRegisterServer" and (not(FolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe"))

t: Potential RipZip Attack on Startup Folder
de: Detects a phishing attack which expands a ZIP file containing a malicious shortcut. If the victim expands the ZIP file via the explorer process, then the explorer process expands the malicious ZIP file and drops a malicious shortcut redirected to a backdoor into the Startup folder. Additionally, the file name of the malicious shortcut in Startup folder contains {0AFACED1-E828-11D1-9187-B532F1E9575D} meaning the folder shortcut operation.
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where (FolderPath contains "\\Microsoft\\Windows\\Start Menu\\Programs\\Startup" and FolderPath contains ".lnk.{0AFACED1-E828-11D1-9187-B532F1E9575D}") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\explorer.exe"

t: Potential RjvPlatform.DLL Sideloading From Non-Default Location
de: Detects potential DLL sideloading of "RjvPlatform.dll" by "SystemResetPlatform.exe" located in a non-default location.
q:
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\RjvPlatform.dll" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath =~ "\\SystemResetPlatform.exe") and (not(InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\System32\\SystemResetPlatform\\"))

t: Potential Rundll32 Execution With DLL Stored In ADS
de: Detects execution of rundll32 where the DLL being called is stored in an Alternate Data Stream (ADS).
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "RUNDLL32.EXE") and ProcessCommandLine matches regex "[Rr][Uu][Nn][Dd][Ll][Ll]32(?:\\.[Ee][Xx][Ee])? \\S+?\\w:\\S+?:"

au: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Vasiliy Burov, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
de: Detects Ryuk ransomware activity
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessCommandLine contains "Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run" and ProcessCommandLine contains "C:\\users\\Public\\") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "del /s /f /q c:\\" and ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i).*\.bac" and ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i).*\.bak" and ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i).*\.bkf") or ((FolderPath endswith "\\net.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\net1.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " stop " and ProcessCommandLine contains " /y") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "samss" or ProcessCommandLine contains "audioendpointbuilder" or ProcessCommandLine contains "unistoresvc_" or ProcessCommandLine contains "AcrSch2Svc"))

de: Detects the creation of files that look like exports of the local SAM (Security Account Manager)
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\Temp\\sam" or FolderPath endswith "\\sam.sav" or FolderPath endswith "\\Intel\\sam" or FolderPath endswith "\\sam.hive" or FolderPath endswith "\\Perflogs\\sam" or FolderPath endswith "\\ProgramData\\sam" or FolderPath endswith "\\Users\\Public\\sam" or FolderPath endswith "\\AppData\\Local\\sam" or FolderPath endswith "\\AppData\\Roaming\\sam" or FolderPath endswith "_ShadowSteal.zip" or FolderPath endswith "\\Documents\\SAM.export" or FolderPath endswith ":\\sam") or (FolderPath contains "\\hive_sam_" or FolderPath contains "\\sam.save" or FolderPath contains "\\sam.export" or FolderPath contains "\\~reg_sam.save" or FolderPath contains "\\sam_backup" or FolderPath contains "\\sam.bck" or FolderPath contains "\\sam.backup")

t: Potential Shell Or Command Execution Via GDB
de: Detects the use of the GNU Debugger (gdb) to spawn a shell or execute operating system commands. gdb can run arbitrary commands via its "shell" command, the "!" escape, an inline Python one- liner, or "call system()". When gdb is executed with elevated privileges (e.g. via sudo), this is abused for privilege escalation or to break out of restricted environments.
fp: Legitimate debugging sessions that invoke the "shell" command may occur, but are uncommon in automation and should be reviewed.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "/gdb" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "shell " or ProcessCommandLine contains "!/bin/" or ProcessCommandLine contains "!sh" or ProcessCommandLine contains "!bash" or ProcessCommandLine contains "os.system" or ProcessCommandLine contains "call system" or ProcessCommandLine contains "call (void)system")
pr: #6437 Add Linux rule: Potential Shell Or Command Execution Via GDB

t: Potential Shell Or Command Execution Via Tar
de: Detects the execution of commands or interactive shells using the "tar" utility via flags such as "--checkpoint-action=exec" or "--to-command". This is a GTFOBins technique commonly abused in wildcard injection attacks, sudoers misconfigurations, or restricted shell escapes to execute arbitrary code with elevated privileges.
fp: Highly unlikely in production environments. Reading from archives with "--to-command" or invoking shell execution on checkpoints via "--checkpoint-action=exec" is rarely used in legitimate automation.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "/tar" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "--checkpoint-action=exec" or ProcessCommandLine contains "--checkpoint-action exec" or ProcessCommandLine contains "--checkpoint-action=\"exec" or ProcessCommandLine contains "--checkpoint-action='exec" or ProcessCommandLine contains "--to-command=" or ProcessCommandLine contains "--to-command " or ProcessCommandLine contains "--to-command=\"" or ProcessCommandLine contains "--to-command='")
pr: #6542 Add Linux rule: Potential Shell Or Command Execution Via Tar

t: Potential Shell Or Command Execution Via Xargs
de: Detects the use of "xargs" with the "-a /dev/null" (or "--arg-file=/dev/null") option to execute a command with no input. This is a GTFOBins technique used to spawn a shell or run arbitrary commands, and when "xargs" is executed with elevated privileges (e.g. via sudo) it is abused for privilege escalation or to break out of restricted environments.
fp: Unlikely. Reading arguments from "/dev/null" provides no input and is rarely used in legitimate automation.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "/xargs" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "-a /dev/null" or ProcessCommandLine contains "--arg-file=/dev/null" or ProcessCommandLine contains "--arg-file /dev/null")
pr: #6438 Add Linux rule: Potential Shell Or Command Execution Via Xargs

t: Potential Signing Bypass Via Windows Developer Features
de: Detects when a user enable developer features such as "Developer Mode" or "Application Sideloading". Which allows the user to install untrusted packages.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\SystemSettingsAdminFlows.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "SystemSettingsAdminFlows.EXE") and ProcessCommandLine contains "TurnOnDeveloperFeatures" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "DeveloperUnlock" or ProcessCommandLine contains "EnableSideloading")

t: Potential Signing Bypass Via Windows Developer Features - Registry
de: Detects when the enablement of developer features such as "Developer Mode" or "Application Sideloading". Which allows the user to install untrusted packages.
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where (RegistryKey contains "\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\AppModelUnlock" or RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\Policies\\Microsoft\\Windows\\Appx.*$") and (RegistryKey endswith "\\AllowAllTrustedApps" or RegistryKey endswith "\\AllowDevelopmentWithoutDevLicense") and RegistryValueData =~ "DWORD (0x00000001)"

de: Detects potential DLL sideloading of "SmadHook.dll", a DLL used by SmadAV antivirus
q:
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\SmadHook32c.dll" or FolderPath endswith "\\SmadHook64c.dll") and (not(((InitiatingProcessFolderPath in~ ("C:\\Program Files (x86)\\SMADAV\\SmadavProtect32.exe", "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\SMADAV\\SmadavProtect64.exe", "C:\\Program Files\\SMADAV\\SmadavProtect32.exe", "C:\\Program Files\\SMADAV\\SmadavProtect64.exe")) and (FolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\SMADAV\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files\\SMADAV\\"))))

t: Potential SNAKE Malware Installation Binary Indicator
de: Detects a specific binary name seen used by SNAKE malware during its installation as described by CISA in their report
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\jpsetup.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\jpinst.exe") and (not(((ProcessCommandLine in~ ("jpinst.exe", "jpinst", "jpsetup.exe", "jpsetup")) or ProcessCommandLine =~ "" or isnull(ProcessCommandLine))))

t: Potential SNAKE Malware Installation CLI Arguments Indicator
de: Detects a specific command line arguments sequence seen used by SNAKE malware during its installation as described by CISA in their report
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex "\\s[a-fA-F0-9]{64}\\s[a-fA-F0-9]{16}"

t: Potential SNAKE Malware Persistence Service Execution
de: Detects a specific child/parent process relationship indicative of a "WerFault" process running from the "WinSxS" as a service. This could be indicative of potential SNAKE malware activity as reported by CISA.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\services.exe" and FolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\WinSxS\\" and FolderPath endswith "\\WerFault.exe"

de: Detects specific process characteristics of Snatch ransomware word document droppers
fp: Scripts that shutdown the system immediately and reboot them in safe mode are unlikely
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex "shutdown\\s+/r /f /t 00" or ProcessCommandLine matches regex "net\\s+stop SuperBackupMan"

de: Detects execution of socat with parameters commonly associated with establishing a reverse shell. Socat is a multipurpose relay tool that can be abused to create encrypted or unencrypted reverse shells. This rule covers both plain TCP and SSL/TLS encrypted variants.
fp: Legitimate use of socat for system administration or debugging purposes
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "/socat" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "exec:" or ProcessCommandLine contains "system:") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "bash" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/bin/sh" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/bin/bash" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/bin/zsh" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/bin/ash" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/bin/csh" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/bin/ksh") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "tcp:" or ProcessCommandLine contains "tcp-connect:" or ProcessCommandLine contains "tcp4:" or ProcessCommandLine contains "tcp6:" or ProcessCommandLine contains "ssl:" or ProcessCommandLine contains "ssl-connect:" or ProcessCommandLine contains "openssl:" or ProcessCommandLine contains "openssl-connect:")
pr: #5886 Add Socat Reverse Shell Detection Rule for Linux Process Creation

t: Potential Startup Shortcut Persistence Via PowerShell.EXE
de: Detects PowerShell writing startup shortcuts. This procedure was highlighted in Red Canary Intel Insights Oct. 2021, "We frequently observe adversaries using PowerShell to write malicious .lnk files into the startup directory to establish persistence. Accordingly, this detection opportunity is likely to identify persistence mechanisms in multiple threats. In the context of Yellow Cockatoo, this persistence mechanism eventually launches the command-line script that leads to the installation of a malicious DLL"
fp: Depending on your environment accepted applications may leverage this at times. It is recommended to search for anomalies inidicative of malware.
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe") and FolderPath contains "\\start menu\\programs\\startup\\" and FolderPath endswith ".lnk"

de: Detects uses of the SysInternals ProcDump utility in which ProcDump or its output get renamed, or a dump file is moved or copied to a different name
fp: False positives are expected in cases in which ProcDump just gets copied to a different directory without any renaming
q:
DeviceProcessEvents

t: Potential Third-Party Antivirus Protection Disabled Via Registry
au: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
de: Detects registry modifications that disable antivirus protection or self-defense mechanisms of common third-party security products. Ransomware and targeted attackers commonly disable these protections before deploying their payload to prevent the AV from blocking or removing malicious activity.
fp: Some FP may occur when the feature is disabled by the AV itself, you should always investigate if the action was legitimate

de: Detects execution of the "mofcomp" utility as a child of a suspicious shell or script running utility or by having a suspicious path in the commandline. The "mofcomp" utility parses a file containing MOF statements and adds the classes and class instances defined in the file to the WMI repository. Attackers abuse this utility to install malicious MOF scripts
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\mofcomp.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "mofcomp.exe") and ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\wsl.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\wscript.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\cscript.exe") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Contacts\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Favorites\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Favourites\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Music\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Pictures\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Users\\Public\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Videos\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\WINDOWS\\Temp\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "%appdata%" or ProcessCommandLine contains "%temp%" or ProcessCommandLine contains "%tmp%"))) and (not(((InitiatingProcessFolderPath =~ "C:\\Windows\\System32\\wbem\\WmiPrvSE.exe" and ProcessCommandLine contains "C:\\Windows\\TEMP\\" and ProcessCommandLine endswith ".mof") or (InitiatingProcessCommandLine endswith "\\InstallUtil.exe /Uninstall C:\\Windows\\CCM\\Microsoft.ConfigurationManager.SVProvider.dll" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\InstallUtil.exe" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "C:\\Windows\\TEMP" and ProcessCommandLine contains ".tmp"))))) and (not(isnull(InitiatingProcessCommandLine)))

de: Detects PowerShell download and execution cradles.
fp: Some PowerShell installers were seen using similar combinations. Apply filters accordingly
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessCommandLine contains ".DownloadString(" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".DownloadFile(" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Invoke-WebRequest " or ProcessCommandLine contains "iwr " or ProcessCommandLine contains "Invoke-RestMethod " or ProcessCommandLine contains "irm ") and (ProcessCommandLine contains ";iex $" or ProcessCommandLine contains "| IEX" or ProcessCommandLine contains "|IEX " or ProcessCommandLine contains "I`E`X" or ProcessCommandLine contains "I`EX" or ProcessCommandLine contains "IE`X" or ProcessCommandLine contains "iex " or ProcessCommandLine contains "IEX (" or ProcessCommandLine contains "IEX(" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Invoke-Expression")

t: PowerShell Execution With Potential Decryption Capabilities
de: Detects PowerShell commands that decrypt an ".LNK" "file to drop the next stage of the malware.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe") and (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("PowerShell.EXE", "pwsh.dll"))) and (ProcessCommandLine contains "Get-ChildItem " or ProcessCommandLine contains "dir " or ProcessCommandLine contains "gci " or ProcessCommandLine contains "ls ") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "Get-Content " or ProcessCommandLine contains "gc " or ProcessCommandLine contains "cat " or ProcessCommandLine contains "type " or ProcessCommandLine contains "ReadAllBytes") and ((ProcessCommandLine contains " ^| " and ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i).*\.lnk" and ProcessCommandLine contains "-Recurse" and ProcessCommandLine contains "-Skip ") or (ProcessCommandLine contains " -ExpandProperty " and ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i).*\.lnk" and ProcessCommandLine contains "WriteAllBytes" and ProcessCommandLine contains " .length "))

t: PowerShell Execution With Potential Decryption Capabilities
de: Detects PowerShell commands that decrypt an ".LNK" "file to drop the next stage of the malware.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("PowerShell.EXE", "pwsh.dll"))) and (ProcessCommandLine contains "Get-ChildItem " or ProcessCommandLine contains "dir " or ProcessCommandLine contains "gci " or ProcessCommandLine contains "ls ") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "Get-Content " or ProcessCommandLine contains "gc " or ProcessCommandLine contains "cat " or ProcessCommandLine contains "type " or ProcessCommandLine contains "ReadAllBytes") and ((ProcessCommandLine contains " ^| " and ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i).*\.lnk" and ProcessCommandLine contains "-Recurse" and ProcessCommandLine contains "-Skip ") or (ProcessCommandLine contains " -ExpandProperty " and ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i).*\.lnk" and ProcessCommandLine contains "WriteAllBytes" and ProcessCommandLine contains " .length "))
pr: #6240 Fix renamed PowerShell detection in decryption pattern rule

de: Detects a "Get-Process" cmdlet and it's aliases on lsass process, which is in almost all cases a sign of malicious activity
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessCommandLine contains "Get-Process lsas" or ProcessCommandLine contains "ps lsas" or ProcessCommandLine contains "gps lsas"

t: PowerShell Logging Disabled Via Registry Key Tampering
de: Detects changes to the registry for the currently logged-in user. In order to disable PowerShell module logging, script block logging or transcription and script execution logging
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where (RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\Microsoft\\Windows\\PowerShell.*$" or RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\Microsoft\\PowerShellCore.*$") and (RegistryKey endswith "\\ModuleLogging\\EnableModuleLogging" or RegistryKey endswith "\\ScriptBlockLogging\\EnableScriptBlockLogging" or RegistryKey endswith "\\ScriptBlockLogging\\EnableScriptBlockInvocationLogging" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Transcription\\EnableTranscripting" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Transcription\\EnableInvocationHeader" or RegistryKey endswith "\\EnableScripts") and RegistryValueData =~ "DWORD (0x00000000)"

de: Detects suspicious PowerShell scripts accessing SAM hives
fp: PowerShell scripts fixing HiveNightmare / SeriousSAM ACLs
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessCommandLine contains "\\HarddiskVolumeShadowCopy" and ProcessCommandLine contains "System32\\config\\sam") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "Copy-Item" or ProcessCommandLine contains "cp $_." or ProcessCommandLine contains "cpi $_." or ProcessCommandLine contains "copy $_." or ProcessCommandLine contains ".File]::Copy(")

t: PowerShell Script Change Permission Via Set-Acl
de: Detects PowerShell execution to set the ACL of a file or a folder
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("PowerShell.EXE", "pwsh.dll")) or (FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe")) and (ProcessCommandLine contains "Set-Acl " and ProcessCommandLine contains "-AclObject " and ProcessCommandLine contains "-Path ")

de: Detects PowerShell scripts to set the ACL to a file in the Windows folder
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("PowerShell.EXE", "pwsh.dll")) or (FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe")) and (ProcessCommandLine contains "Set-Acl " and ProcessCommandLine contains "-AclObject ") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "-Path \"C:\\Windows" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-Path 'C:\\Windows" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-Path %windir%" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-Path $env:windir") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "FullControl" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Allow")

de: Detects TOKEN OBFUSCATION technique from Invoke-Obfuscation
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessCommandLine matches regex "\\w+`(?:\\w+|-|.)`[\\w+|\\s]" or ProcessCommandLine matches regex "\"(?:\\{\\d\\})+\"\\s*-f" or ProcessCommandLine matches regex "(?i)\\$\\{`?e`?n`?v`?:`?p`?a`?t`?h`?\\}") and (not(ProcessCommandLine contains "${env:path}"))

t: PowerShell Web Access Feature Enabled Via DISM
de: Detects the use of DISM to enable the PowerShell Web Access feature, which could be used for remote access and potential abuse
fp: Legitimate PowerShell Web Access installations by administrators
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\dism.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "DISM.EXE") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "WindowsPowerShellWebAccess" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/online" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/enable-feature")

de: Detects the deletion of a prefetch file which may indicate an attempt to destroy forensic evidence
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where ActionType =~ "FileDeleted" and ((FolderPath contains ":\\Windows\\Prefetch\\" and FolderPath endswith ".pf") and (not((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith ":\\windows\\system32\\svchost.exe" and (RequestAccountName contains "AUTHORI" or RequestAccountName contains "AUTORI")))))

de: Detects the execution of the LOLBIN PrintBrm.exe, which can be used to create or extract ZIP files. PrintBrm.exe should not be run on a normal workstation.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\PrintBrm.exe" and (ProcessCommandLine contains " -f" and ProcessCommandLine contains ".zip")

t: Privilege Escalation via Named Pipe Impersonation
de: Detects a remote file copy attempt to a hidden network share. This may indicate lateral movement or data staging activity.
fp: Other programs that cause these patterns (please report)
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("Cmd.Exe", "PowerShell.EXE"))) and (ProcessCommandLine contains "echo" and ProcessCommandLine contains ">" and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\\\.\\pipe\\")

t: Privilege Escalation via Named Pipe Impersonation
de: Detects a remote file copy attempt to a hidden network share. This may indicate lateral movement or data staging activity.
fp: Other programs that cause these patterns (please report)
q:

de: Detects a possible process memory dump that uses the white-listed Citrix TrolleyExpress.exe filename as a way to dump the lsass process memory
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessCommandLine contains "\\TrolleyExpress 7" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\TrolleyExpress 8" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\TrolleyExpress 9" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\TrolleyExpress.exe 7" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\TrolleyExpress.exe 8" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\TrolleyExpress.exe 9" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\TrolleyExpress.exe -ma ") or (FolderPath endswith "\\TrolleyExpress.exe" and (not((ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName contains "CtxInstall" or isnull(ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName)))))

t: Process Execution From A Potentially Suspicious Folder
de: Detects a potentially suspicious execution from an uncommon folder.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath contains ":\\Perflogs\\" or FolderPath contains ":\\Users\\All Users\\" or FolderPath contains ":\\Users\\Default\\" or FolderPath contains ":\\Users\\NetworkService\\" or FolderPath contains ":\\Windows\\addins\\" or FolderPath contains ":\\Windows\\debug\\" or FolderPath contains ":\\Windows\\Fonts\\" or FolderPath contains ":\\Windows\\Help\\" or FolderPath contains ":\\Windows\\IME\\" or FolderPath contains ":\\Windows\\Media\\" or FolderPath contains ":\\Windows\\repair\\" or FolderPath contains ":\\Windows\\security\\" or FolderPath contains ":\\Windows\\System32\\Tasks\\" or FolderPath contains ":\\Windows\\Tasks\\" or FolderPath contains "$Recycle.bin" or FolderPath contains "\\config\\systemprofile\\" or FolderPath contains "\\Intel\\Logs\\" or FolderPath contains "\\RSA\\MachineKeys\\") and (not((FolderPath startswith "C:\\Users\\Public\\IBM\\ClientSolutions\\Start_Programs\\" or (FolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\config\\systemprofile\\Citrix\\UpdaterBinaries\\" and FolderPath endswith "\\CitrixReceiverUpdater.exe"))))

t: Process Execution Hijacking Via IFEO Debugger Entry
de: Detects any registry write adding a "Debugger" value under Image File Execution Options (IFEO) for common administrative, security and system binaries. Attackers use this technique to silently redirect to malicious commands when a user attempt to launch a target executable or preventing it from launching at all.
fp: Legitimate debuggers registered for administrative, security or system binaries
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where RegistryKey endswith "\\Image File Execution Options\\calc.exe\\Debugger" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Image File Execution Options\\cleanmgr.exe\\Debugger" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Image File Execution Options\\control.exe\\Debugger" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Image File Execution Options\\msconfig.exe\\Debugger" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Image File Execution Options\\msinfo32.exe\\Debugger" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Image File Execution Options\\mmc.exe\\Debugger" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Image File Execution Options\\mspaint.exe\\Debugger" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Image File Execution Options\\mstsc.exe\\Debugger" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Image File Execution Options\\powershell_ise.exe\\Debugger" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Image File Execution Options\\regedit.exe\\Debugger" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Image File Execution Options\\regedt32.exe\\Debugger" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Image File Execution Options\\SecEdit.exe\\Debugger" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Image File Execution Options\\takeown.exe\\Debugger" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Image File Execution Options\\taskmgr.exe\\Debugger" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Image File Execution Options\\explorer.exe\\Debugger" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Image File Execution Options\\rundll32.exe\\Debugger" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Image File Execution Options\\runonce.exe\\Debugger" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Image File Execution Options\\svchost.exe\\Debugger" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Image File Execution Options\\winlogon.exe\\Debugger" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Image File Execution Options\\SecurityHealthSystray.exe\\Debugger" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Image File Execution Options\\SystemResetPlatform.exe\\Debugger"
pr: #6236 new: closes #4542 - add rules for IFEO Debugger tampering, disabling usb storage and windowsupdate

t: Process Explorer Driver Creation By Non-Sysinternals Binary
de: Detects creation of the Process Explorer drivers by processes other than Process Explorer (procexp) itself. Hack tools or malware may use the Process Explorer driver to elevate privileges, drops it to disk for a few moments, runs a service using that driver and removes it afterwards.
fp: Some false positives may occur with legitimate renamed process explorer binaries
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where (FolderPath contains "\\PROCEXP" and FolderPath endswith ".sys") and (not((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\procexp.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\procexp64.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\procexp64a.exe")))

t: Process Initiated Network Connection To Ngrok Domain
de: Detects an executable initiating a network connection to "ngrok" domains. Attackers were seen using this "ngrok" in order to store their second stage payloads and malware. While communication with such domains can be legitimate, often times is a sign of either data exfiltration by malicious actors or additional download.
fp: Legitimate use of the ngrok service.
q:
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where RemoteUrl endswith ".ngrok-free.app" or RemoteUrl endswith ".ngrok-free.dev" or RemoteUrl endswith ".ngrok.app" or RemoteUrl endswith ".ngrok.dev" or RemoteUrl endswith ".ngrok.io"

au: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Modexp, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
de: Detects a process memory dump via "comsvcs.dll" using rundll32, covering multiple different techniques (ordinal, minidump function, etc.)
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "RUNDLL32.EXE" or ProcessCommandLine contains "rundll32") and ((ProcessCommandLine contains "comsvcs" and ProcessCommandLine contains "full") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "#-" or ProcessCommandLine contains "#+" or ProcessCommandLine contains "#24" or ProcessCommandLine contains "24 " or ProcessCommandLine contains "MiniDump" or ProcessCommandLine contains "#65560"))) or ((ProcessCommandLine contains "24" and ProcessCommandLine contains "comsvcs" and ProcessCommandLine contains "full") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " #" or ProcessCommandLine contains ",#" or ProcessCommandLine contains ", #" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\"#"))

au: Cedric MAURUGEON, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
de: Detects the use of the Microsoft Windows Resource Leak Diagnostic tool "rdrleakdiag.exe" to dump process memory

au: Cedric MAURUGEON, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

q:

de: Detects abuse of the signed Microsoft Copilot Electron binary via the "--gpu-launcher" argument to proxy-execute an arbitrary command. The legitimate value points to the GPU process; attackers set it to a shell command for signed-binary proxy execution.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\mscopilot.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\mscopilot_proxy.exe") and ProcessCommandLine contains "--gpu-launcher=" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "cmd" or ProcessCommandLine contains "powershell" or ProcessCommandLine contains "pwsh" or ProcessCommandLine contains "&&" or ProcessCommandLine contains "rundll32" or ProcessCommandLine contains "regsvr32" or ProcessCommandLine contains "mshta")

au: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research), Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Sreeman, FPT.EagleEye Team
de: Detects the use of the Windows Update Client binary (wuauclt.exe) for proxy execution.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\wuauclt.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "wuauclt.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "UpdateDeploymentProvider" and ProcessCommandLine contains "RunHandlerComServer")) and (not((ProcessCommandLine contains " /UpdateDeploymentProvider UpdateDeploymentProvider.dll " or ProcessCommandLine contains " wuaueng.dll " or (ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Windows\\UUS\\Packages\\Preview\\amd64\\updatedeploy.dll /ClassId" or ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Windows\\UUS\\amd64\\UpdateDeploy.dll /ClassId") or (ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Windows\\WinSxS\\" and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\UpdateDeploy.dll /ClassId "))))

de: Detects renamed SysInternals tool execution with a binary named ps.exe as used by Dragonfly APT group and documented in TA17-293A report
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessCommandLine contains "ps.exe -accepteula" and ProcessCommandLine contains "-s cmd /c netstat"

de: Detects creation of the PSEXEC key file. Which is created anytime a PsExec command is executed. It gets written to the file system and will be recorded in the USN Journal on the target system
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where FolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\PSEXEC-" and FolderPath endswith ".key"

t: PsExec Service Child Process Execution as LOCAL SYSTEM
de: Detects suspicious launch of the PSEXESVC service on this system and a sub process run as LOCAL_SYSTEM (-s), which means that someone remotely started a command on this system running it with highest privileges and not only the privileges of the login user account (e.g. the administrator account)
fp: Users that debug Microsoft Intune issues using the commands mentioned in the official documentation; see https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/mem/intune/apps/intune-management-extension
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath =~ "C:\\Windows\\PSEXESVC.exe" and (AccountName contains "AUTHORI" or AccountName contains "AUTORI")

t: Python Directly Spawning a SUID Binary
de: Detects instances where a Python process directly spawns a SUID binary, which is anomalous and may indicate a privilege-escalation or injection attack. It is intended to catch privilege- escalation attacks where a Python script executes a SUID-root binary directly via subprocess.run() or os.execv() instead of the os.system() path (which inserts an intermediate shell). Caused by direct-exec PoC adaptations of page-cache poisoning exploits: after overwriting the SUID binary's page cache with shellcode, the attacker triggers it through a direct exec call so Python becomes the immediate parent of the SUID binary — bypassing the "sh -c <binary>" intermediate hop that os.system()-based detection relies on. The anomalous Python → SUID binary parent-child relationship is the key indicator, as legitimate Python programs rarely need to exec privileged SUID system tools.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/python" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/python3" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/python3.10" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/python3.11" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/python3.12" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/python3.13") and (FolderPath endswith "/su" or FolderPath endswith "/sudo" or FolderPath endswith "/passwd" or FolderPath endswith "/mount" or FolderPath endswith "/newgrp" or FolderPath endswith "/gpasswd" or FolderPath endswith "/chfn" or FolderPath endswith "/chsh" or FolderPath endswith "/ping" or FolderPath endswith "/newuidmap" or FolderPath endswith "/newgidmap" or FolderPath endswith "/pkexec" or FolderPath endswith "/fusermount" or FolderPath endswith "/expiry" or FolderPath endswith "/fusermount3" or FolderPath endswith "/umount") and (ProcessCommandLine endswith "su" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "sudo" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "passwd" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "mount" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "newgrp" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "gpasswd" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "chfn" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "chsh" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "ping" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "newuidmap" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "newgidmap" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "pkexec" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "fusermount" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "expiry" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "fusermount3" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "umount")

au: Samir Bousseaden, David ANDRE, Roberto Rodriguez @Cyb3rWard0g, Nasreddine Bencherchali
de: Detects tampering of RDP Terminal Service/Server sensitive settings. Such as allowing unauthorized users access to a system via the 'fAllowUnsolicited' or enabling RDP via 'fDenyTSConnections', etc. Below is a list of registry keys/values that are monitored by this rule: - Shadow: Used to enable Remote Desktop shadowing, which allows an administrator to view or control a user's session. - DisableRemoteDesktopAntiAlias: Disables anti-aliasing for remote desktop sessions. - DisableSecuritySettings: Disables certain security settings for Remote Desktop connections. - fAllowUnsolicited: Allows unsolicited remote assistance offers. - fAllowUnsolicitedFullControl: Allows unsolicited remote assistance offers with full control. - InitialProgram: Specifies a program to run automatically when a user logs on to a remote computer. - ServiceDll: Used in RDP hijacking techniques to specify a custom DLL to be loaded by the Terminal Services service. - SecurityLayer: Specifies the security layer used for RDP connections.
fp: Some of the keys mentioned here could be modified by an administrator while setting group policy (it should be investigated either way)
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where (((RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\Control\\Terminal Server.*$" or RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\Windows NT\\Terminal Services.*$") and RegistryKey endswith "\\Shadow" and (RegistryValueData in~ ("DWORD (0x00000001)", "DWORD (0x00000002)", "DWORD (0x00000003)", "DWORD (0x00000004)"))) or ((RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\Control\\Terminal Server.*$" or RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\Windows NT\\Terminal Services.*$") and (RegistryKey endswith "\\DisableRemoteDesktopAntiAlias" or RegistryKey endswith "\\DisableSecuritySettings" or RegistryKey endswith "\\fAllowUnsolicited" or RegistryKey endswith "\\fAllowUnsolicitedFullControl") and RegistryValueData =~ "DWORD (0x00000001)") or (RegistryKey contains "\\Control\\Terminal Server\\InitialProgram" or RegistryKey contains "\\Control\\Terminal Server\\WinStations\\RDP-Tcp\\InitialProgram" or RegistryKey contains "\\services\\TermService\\Parameters\\ServiceDll" or RegistryKey contains "\\Terminal Server\\WinStations\\RDP-Tcp\\SecurityLayer" or RegistryKey contains "\\Windows NT\\Terminal Services\\InitialProgram")) and (not((RegistryKey endswith "\\SecurityLayer" and RegistryValueData =~ "DWORD (0x00000002)")))

t: Redis Server Process Writing To SSH Authorized Keys File
de: Detects the redis-server process writing to a user's SSH authorized_keys file. An unauthenticated Redis instance can be made to write its database to an arbitrary path via CONFIG SET dir and CONFIG SET dbfilename followed by SAVE, which is used to append an attacker- controlled SSH public key and gain persistent shell access. A legitimate Redis deployment does not write to this path.

q:

| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/redis-server" and FolderPath endswith "/.ssh/authorized_keys"

t: Rundll32 Execution of DLL Masquerading as Non-Executable File Type
de: Detects rundll32.exe being invoked either: (a) against a file with a non-DLL/non-executable extension (e.g. .jpg, .png, .pdf, .txt, .ini, .html, .js) followed by an exported function call — a common evasion where a malicious DLL is renamed to a benign extension to bypass extension- based filtering, or (b) from a user-writable staging directory (Temp, AppData, ProgramData, Public, Downloads) — a broader signal since legitimate rundll32 targets are almost always shipped under Program Files/System32, not dropped into user-writable paths at runtime. Excludes cases where the parent process is msiexec.exe, since MSI custom actions legitimately spawn rundll32 against .tmp/.dat staging files during installation.
fp: Other legitimate installers/updaters (e.g. Squirrel-based apps, some ClickOnce deployments) that stage payloads with non-standard extensions before invoking rundll32. Extend filter_parent_msiexec if you identify these in your environment
Some legitimate software (browser components, printer/scanner utilities) loads DLLs from AppData under normal operation, so baseline the staging-module branch before production
Rare legitimate help/media viewer integrations that pass non-.dll files to rundll32
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe" and (ProcessCommandLine matches regex "(?i)rundll32(\\.exe)?\\s.*\\.(jpg|png|gif|ico|pdf|docx|ppt|txt|inf|dat|tmp|ini|html|htm|js)\"?," or ProcessCommandLine matches regex "(?i)rundll32(\\.exe)?\"?\\s+\"?[^,]*\\\\(AppData\\\\Local\\\\Temp|AppData\\\\Roaming|ProgramData|Users\\\\Public|Downloads)\\\\[^,]*,") and (not(InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\msiexec.exe"))
pr: #6319 new: Rundll32 Execution of DLL Masquerading as Non-Executable File Type

t: Safe Mode Boot Configuration Via Bcdedit.EXE
de: Detects the use of "bcdedit.exe" to configure the system to boot into Safe Mode via the "safeboot" option. Adversaries (notably ransomware operators) reboot endpoints into Safe Mode to disable endpoint security products that do not load with the limited Safe Mode driver set, allowing encryption or other actions to proceed unhindered.
fp: Administrators or troubleshooting scripts legitimately configuring Safe Mode boot
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\bcdedit.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "bcdedit.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "set" and ProcessCommandLine contains "safeboot")
pr: #6095 Add cross-platform discovery/collection rules

t: SafeBoot Registry Key Deleted Via Reg.EXE
de: Detects execution of "reg.exe" commands with the "delete" flag on safe boot registry keys. Often used by attacker to prevent safeboot execution of security products
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "reg.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "reg.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " delete " and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\SafeBoot")

t: Scheduled Task Executing Encoded Payload from Registry
au: pH-T (Nextron Systems), @Kostastsale, TheDFIRReport, X__Junior (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
de: Detects the creation of a schtask that potentially executes a base64 encoded payload stored in the Windows Registry using PowerShell.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\schtasks.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "schtasks.exe") and ProcessCommandLine contains "/Create" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "FromBase64String" or ProcessCommandLine contains "encodedcommand") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "Get-ItemProperty" or ProcessCommandLine contains " gp ") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "HKCU:" or ProcessCommandLine contains "HKLM:" or ProcessCommandLine contains "registry::" or ProcessCommandLine contains "HKEY_")

t: Scheduled Task Files Named dllhost or taskhostw Written Outside schtasks.exe
de: Detects creation (or modification) of scheduled task files named "dllhost" or "taskhostw" under C:\Windows\System32\Tasks - names masquerading as the legitimate system binaries dllhost.exe / taskhostw.exe. Observed PavinLoader.BAT persistence dropped such task files. In Sysmon file_event (EID 11) the Image field identifies the process that wrote the file; any writer other than schtasks.exe is suspicious. Note that the Task Scheduler service (svchost.exe) writes task XML natively, so extend the filter if your baseline creates these names through other APIs.
fp: Administrative tooling or configuration management that registers tasks with these exact names through APIs other than schtasks.exe
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\Windows\\System32\\Tasks\\dllhost" or FolderPath endswith "\\Windows\\System32\\Tasks\\taskhostw") and (not(InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\schtasks.exe"))

t: Script Interpreter CommandLine With Reference To Suspicious Directory
au: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
de: Detects script interpreter processes (cscript, wscript, mshta) or processes with suspicious scripting flags whose CommandLine references a suspicious directory such as Temp, Public, or common user profile folders. Note that the suspicious directory check applies to the full CommandLine string and does not distinguish the role of the referenced path. This means the rule may fire when the interpreter or script itself resides in a suspicious location, but can also trigger when such a path appears in any other argument (e.g. an output file or log destination).
fp: Various legitimate software have been observed to use similar techniques for installation or update purposes;thus, it is recommended to review and tune filters for your environment to reduce false positives before deploying to production.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\cscript.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\mshta.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\wscript.exe") or (ProcessCommandLine contains " -ep bypass " or ProcessCommandLine contains " -ExecutionPolicy bypass " or ProcessCommandLine contains " -w hidden " or ProcessCommandLine contains "/e:javascript " or ProcessCommandLine contains "/e:Jscript " or ProcessCommandLine contains "/e:vbscript ") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("cscript.exe", "mshta.exe", "wscript.exe"))) and ((ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Perflogs\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Users\\Public\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\%Public%" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\AppData\\Roaming\\Temp" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Temporary Internet" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Windows\\Temp" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Start Menu\\Programs\\Startup\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "%TEMP%" or ProcessCommandLine contains "%TMP%" or ProcessCommandLine contains "%LocalAppData%\\Temp") or ((ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Users\\" and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Favorites\\") or (ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Users\\" and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Favourites\\") or (ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Users\\" and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Contacts\\") or (ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Users\\" and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Documents\\") or (ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Users\\" and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Music\\") or (ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Users\\" and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Pictures\\") or (ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Users\\" and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Videos\\"))) and (not(((InitiatingProcessFolderPath in~ ("C:\\Windows\\System32\\Msiexec.exe", "C:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\Msiexec.exe")) and FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "-NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command" and ProcessCommandLine contains "AppData\\Local\\Temp\\" and ProcessCommandLine contains "Install-Chocolatey.ps1"))))
pr: #6357 chore: Move Certighost CDC Chase rules to placeholder and fix script interpreter rule metadat

t: Script Interpreter Spawning Credential Scanner - macOS
de: Detects a script interpreter process (like node.js or bun) spawning a known credential scanning tool (e.g., trufflehog, gitleaks). This behavior is indicative of an attempt to find and steal secrets, as seen in the "Shai-Hulud: The Second Coming" campaign.
fp: Legitimate pre-commit hooks or CI/CD pipeline jobs that use a script to run a credential scanner as part of a security check.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/node" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/bun") and ((FolderPath endswith "/trufflehog" or FolderPath endswith "/gitleaks") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "trufflehog" or ProcessCommandLine contains "gitleaks"))
pr: #6162 New rule: Script Interpreter Spawning Credential Scanner - macOS

de: Detects sdiagnhost.exe calling a suspicious child process (e.g. used in exploits for Follina / CVE-2022-30190)
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\sdiagnhost.exe" and (FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\mshta.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\cscript.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\wscript.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\taskkill.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\regsvr32.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\calc.exe")) and (not(((FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" and ProcessCommandLine contains "bits") or (FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" and (ProcessCommandLine endswith "-noprofile -" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "-noprofile")))))

de: Detects a whoami.exe executed with the /priv command line flag instructing the tool to show all current user privileges. This is often used after a privilege escalation attempt.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\whoami.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "whoami.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " /priv" or ProcessCommandLine contains " -priv")

| where (RegistryKey endswith "\\Control\\Lsa\\Security Packages" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Control\\Lsa\\OSConfig\\Security Packages") and (not(((InitiatingProcessFolderPath in~ ("C:\\Windows\\system32\\msiexec.exe", "C:\\Windows\\syswow64\\MsiExec.exe")) or isnull(InitiatingProcessFolderPath))))

t: Self Extracting Package Creation Via Iexpress.EXE From Potentially Suspicious Location
de: Detects the use of iexpress.exe to create binaries via Self Extraction Directive (SED) files located in potentially suspicious locations. This behavior has been observed in-the-wild by different threat actors.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\iexpress.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "IEXPRESS.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " -n " or ProcessCommandLine contains " /n " or ProcessCommandLine contains " –n " or ProcessCommandLine contains " —n " or ProcessCommandLine contains " ―n ") and (ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\ProgramData\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Temp\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Windows\\System32\\Tasks\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Windows\\Tasks\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Windows\\Temp\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\")

t: Sensitive File Access Via Volume Shadow Copy Backup
au: Max Altgelt (Nextron Systems), Tobias Michalski (Nextron Systems)
de: Detects a command that accesses the VolumeShadowCopy in order to extract sensitive files such as the Security or SAM registry hives or the AD database (ntds.dit)
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessCommandLine contains "\\\\?\\GLOBALROOT\\Device\\HarddiskVolumeShadowCopy" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "\\NTDS.dit" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\SYSTEM" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\SECURITY")

de: Detects the abuse of the Print.exe utility for credential harvesting which involves using Print.Exe to copy sensitive files such as ntds.dit, SAM, SECURITY, or SYSTEM from the Windows directory in order to extract credentials, locally or remotely.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\print.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "Print.EXE") and ((ProcessCommandLine contains "-D" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/D" or ProcessCommandLine contains "–D" or ProcessCommandLine contains "—D" or ProcessCommandLine contains "―D") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "\\config\\SAM" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\config\\SECURITY" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\config\\SYSTEM" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\windows\\ntds\\ntds.dit"))

de: Detects the dump of highly sensitive files such as "NTDS.DIT" and "SECURITY" hive. Attackers can leverage the "wbadmin" utility in order to dump sensitive files that might contain credential or sensitive information.
fp: Legitimate backup operation by authorized administrators. Matches must be investigated and allowed on a case by case basis.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\wbadmin.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "WBADMIN.EXE") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "start" or ProcessCommandLine contains "backup") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "\\config\\SAM" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\config\\SECURITY" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\config\\SYSTEM" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Windows\\NTDS\\NTDS.dit")

de: Detects the dump of highly sensitive files such as "NTDS.DIT" and "SECURITY" hive. Attackers can leverage the "wbadmin" utility in order to dump sensitive files that might contain credential or sensitive information.

t: Service StartType Modification by Process Running from Suspicious Directory
de: Detect the modification of a service start type by a process running from a suspicious directory. If the service start type is set to "Automatic" or "System", the service will be started at boot time, which can be used by attackers to maintain persistence. And it could be particularly suspicious if the modification is performed by a process running from a directory that is not commonly used for legitimate software, such as user profile directories, temporary folders, or other non-standard locations.
fp: Software installation or deployment scripts setting a service to start automatically
Management tooling running from a staging directory and changing service start types
Legitimate administrative activity re-configuring service startup. Inspect the writing process and user context to determine intent
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where ((RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\System.*$" and RegistryKey contains "ControlSet" and RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\Services.*$") and RegistryKey endswith "\\Start" and (InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\$Recycle.Bin\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\ADMIN$\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\AppData\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\Desktop\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\Documents\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\Downloads\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\Favorites\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\Favourites\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\Music\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\Perflogs\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\Pictures\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\Temp\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\Users\\Default\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\Users\\Public\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\Videos\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\Windows\\Debug\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\Windows\\Tasks\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\Windows\\Tracing\\") and (RegistryValueData in~ ("DWORD (0x00000000)", "DWORD (0x00000001)", "DWORD (0x00000002)"))) and (not((InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\Common Files\\" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\Temp\\")))

t: Shell Binary Created by Install Outside Standard Paths
de: Detects the 'install' utility writing a shell binary to a location outside standard system binary directories. The 'install' command is commonly abused in privilege escalation postinst scripts to drop a SUID-enabled copy of bash (or another shell) into a writable path such as /tmp or /home, which the attacker then executes with '-p' to obtain a root shell. There is no legitimate reason for 'install' to place a shell binary outside of standard system paths (e.g. /bin, /usr/bin).

t: Shell Command in Git Configuration Value - Linux
de: Detects a Git configuration key set on the command line to a value that invokes a shell or a scripting interpreter. Git runs the values of keys such as core.pager, core.fsmonitor, core.editor, diff.external and sequence.editor as commands during ordinary operations, and treats a credential.helper or alias value beginning with an exclamation mark as a shell snippet, so one "-c key=value" pair turns a routine Git command into command execution. Attacker-supplied Git configuration is a documented remote code execution path, reached either through a crafted command line or through configuration written into a repository that a later Git command reads.
fp: A shell based credential helper set inline, such as the AWS CodeCommit helper, whose value legitimately begins with an exclamation mark.
A Git command whose arguments quote both a configuration key and a shell invocation, such as a commit message that describes this behaviour.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "/git" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "alias." or ProcessCommandLine contains "core.alternateRefsCommand" or ProcessCommandLine contains "core.editor" or ProcessCommandLine contains "core.fsmonitor" or ProcessCommandLine contains "core.pager" or ProcessCommandLine contains "core.sshCommand" or ProcessCommandLine contains "credential.helper" or ProcessCommandLine contains "diff.external" or ProcessCommandLine contains "filter." or ProcessCommandLine contains "pager." or ProcessCommandLine contains "sequence.editor") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "/dev/tcp/" or ProcessCommandLine contains "=!" or ProcessCommandLine contains "nc -e" or ProcessCommandLine contains "perl -e" or ProcessCommandLine contains "python -c" or ProcessCommandLine contains "python3 -c" or ProcessCommandLine contains "ruby -e" or ProcessCommandLine contains "sh -c")
pr: #6218 Add Git configuration command execution rules

t: Shell Command in Git Configuration Value - Windows
de: Detects a Git configuration key set on the command line to a value that invokes a shell or a scripting interpreter. Git runs the values of keys such as core.pager, core.fsmonitor, core.editor, diff.external and sequence.editor as commands during ordinary operations, and treats a credential.helper or alias value beginning with an exclamation mark as a shell snippet, so one "-c key=value" pair turns a routine Git command into command execution. Windows records the command line as a single string, so the quoting around such a value is preserved and is matched here alongside the bare form. Git for Windows also ships a POSIX shell, which is why the Unix interpreter spellings are matched next to the native ones.
fp: A shell based credential helper set inline, such as the AWS CodeCommit helper, whose value legitimately begins with an exclamation mark.
A Git command whose arguments quote both a configuration key and a shell invocation, such as a commit message that describes this behaviour.

t: Sonoma Stealer Loader Execution Chain - macOS
de: Detects process creation activity associated with the Sonoma Stealer (SONOMAC1) loader execution chain on macOS. Sonoma is a macOS infostealer operated by the Crazy Evil cybercrime group, distributed via DMG/ZIP lures impersonating collaboration and Web3 brands such as Zoom, Slack, StreamYard, Brave Talk, DocSend or Toria. The ad-hoc signed launcher strips Gatekeeper quarantine attributes via 'xattr', pipes a second stage script into '/bin/zsh -s', re-signs the payload with 'codesign -fs - --deep' and launches it hidden via 'open -gn'. The staging chain downloads additional components from the C2 under '/tmp/.upd-*', '/tmp/.ldr-*', '/tmp/.pkgunpack-*' or '/tmp/.core-*' paths.
fp: Rare ad-hoc re-signing of unsigned or custom in-house applications via 'codesign -fs -'
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "/xattr" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "-r" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/tmp/")) or (FolderPath endswith "/curl" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "/tmp/.upd-" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/tmp/.ldr-" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/tmp/.pkgunpack-" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/tmp/.core-")) or (FolderPath endswith "/zsh" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "/tmp/.sys-" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/tmp/.appbootstrap" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/tmp/.sn-dropper-")) or (FolderPath endswith "/codesign" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "-fs" and ProcessCommandLine contains " --deep")) or (ProcessCommandLine contains "pkgunpack genkey" or ProcessCommandLine contains "pkgunpack decrypt")
pr: #6320 feat: add Sonoma Stealer (SONOMAC1) macOS detection rules

t: Sonoma Stealer Staging Script Fetch From C2 - macOS

Multiple Gen-2 lures (Brave Talk, CavePay, Crystal Flip) were observed fetching '/agent.zsh' from attacker-controlled Cloudflare-fronted infrastructure ('apple03cloudstore.com' and subdomains) and piping it directly into 'zsh' or saving it under hidden '/tmp' staging paths before execution.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessCommandLine contains "/agent.zsh" or ProcessCommandLine contains "apple03cloudstore"

de: Detects sudo executions of gdb attaching to PID 1 with a command file (i.e., '--command=' or '-x ') located in temporary directories ('/tmp', '/var/tmp', '/dev/shm'). This pattern indicates an attempt to escalate privileges by abusing misconfigured sudoers entries permitting passwordless gdb execution, as observed against Cisco CUCM 15.x where the 'tomcat' user can run 'sudo -n /usr/bin/gdb -pid 1 --command=/tmp/gdb_file'.
fp: Legitimate system administrators debugging PID 1 (rare in production)
Development environments with authorized debugging of the init process
Security or monitoring tooling legitimately attaching debuggers to system processes
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "/sudo" and ProcessCommandLine contains "gdb" and ProcessCommandLine matches regex "(-pid\\s+1|--pid[=\\s]1|-p\\s+1)" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "--command=" or ProcessCommandLine contains "--command " or ProcessCommandLine contains "-x ") and ProcessCommandLine matches regex "/tmp/|/var/tmp/|/dev/shm/") and (not((InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "eclipse" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "vscode" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "intellij")))
pr: #6230 new: silent-call rules
