t: Sudo Spawning a Shell With No Arguments
de: Detects sudo spawning a shell where the parent CommandLine ends with just "sudo" and carries no subcommand or flags. Bare sudo has no legitimate code path that opens a shell — it only prints usage. A shell child under these conditions indicates the process was hijacked, e.g. via shellcode calling execve("/bin/sh", NULL) inside a poisoned SUID binary.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/sudo" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine endswith "sudo" and (FolderPath endswith "/sh" or FolderPath endswith "/dash" or FolderPath endswith "/bash" or FolderPath endswith "/ksh" or FolderPath endswith "/zsh" or FolderPath endswith "/ash" or FolderPath endswith "/tcsh" or FolderPath endswith "/csh")
pr: #5968 new: CVE-2026-31431 Copy Fail Exploit Detection Rules

t: SUID Binary Spawned as Child of Shell Invoked With Command Flag
de: Detects a SUID-root binary spawned as the direct child of a shell that was invoked with "-c <binary>" where the parent shell's CommandLine ends with just the binary name and no flags. This is the artifact of os.system("<binary>") calls used in privilege-escalation exploits that poison the page cache of a SUID binary and trigger its execution via Python's os module.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/sh" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/dash" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/bash" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/ksh" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/zsh" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/ash" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/tcsh" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/csh") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "-c " and (InitiatingProcessCommandLine endswith "su" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine endswith "sudo" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine endswith "passwd" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine endswith "mount" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine endswith "newgrp" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine endswith "gpasswd" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine endswith "chfn" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine endswith "chsh" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine endswith "ping" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine endswith "newuidmap" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine endswith "newgidmap" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine endswith "pkexec" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine endswith "fusermount" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine endswith "fusermount3" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine endswith "expiry") and (FolderPath endswith "/su" or FolderPath endswith "/sudo" or FolderPath endswith "/passwd" or FolderPath endswith "/mount" or FolderPath endswith "/umount" or FolderPath endswith "/newgrp" or FolderPath endswith "/gpasswd" or FolderPath endswith "/chfn" or FolderPath endswith "/chsh" or FolderPath endswith "/newuidmap" or FolderPath endswith "/newgidmap" or FolderPath endswith "/pkexec" or FolderPath endswith "/fusermount" or FolderPath endswith "/fusermount3" or FolderPath endswith "/expiry")

t: Suspicious Active Directory Database Snapshot Via ADExplorer
de: Detects the execution of Sysinternals ADExplorer with the "-snapshot" flag in order to save a local copy of the active directory database to a suspicious directory. This can be used by attackers to extract data for Bloodhound, usernames for password spraying or use the meta data for social engineering. The snapshot doesn't contain password hashes but there have been cases, where administrators put passwords in the comment field.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\ADExp.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\ADExplorer.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\ADExplorer64.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\ADExplorer64a.exe") or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "AdExp" or ProcessVersionInfoFileDescription =~ "Active Directory Editor" or ProcessVersionInfoProductName =~ "Sysinternals ADExplorer") and ProcessCommandLine contains "snapshot" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Downloads\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Users\\Public\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\AppData\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Windows\\Temp\\")

de: Detects ABNotify.exe, running from the standard AOMEI Backupper installation path, spawning any executable located in the html\ rendering hierarchy. | where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\AOMEI\\AOMEI Backupper\\" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\ABNotify.exe") and ((FolderPath contains "\\AOMEI\\AOMEI Backupper\\" and FolderPath contains "\\html\\") and FolderPath endswith ".exe")

de: Detects AnyDesk writing binary files to disk other than "gcapi.dll". According to RedCanary research it is highly abnormal for AnyDesk to write executable files to disk besides gcapi.dll, which is a legitimate DLL that is part of the Google Chrome web browser used to interact with the Google Cloud API. (See reference section for more details)
q:

| where ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\AnyDesk.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\AnyDeskMSI.exe") and (FolderPath endswith ".dll" or FolderPath endswith ".exe")) and (not(FolderPath endswith "\\gcapi.dll"))

de: Detects the execution of the 'bpftool' command to load, attach, or pin eBPF programs and maps. Adversaries and rootkits (e.g., BPFDoor, Symbiote) often leverage eBPF for stealthy persistence and network evasion. While 'bpftool' is a legitimate administrative utility for introspection, unauthorized usage to load or modify eBPF objects outside of known administrative scripts is highly suspicious.
fp: Legitimate execution of bpftool by system administrators for network troubleshooting or observability tool deployments (e.g., Cilium, Datadog).
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "/bpftool" or ProcessCommandLine contains "bpftool ") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " prog load" or ProcessCommandLine contains " prog attach" or ProcessCommandLine contains " prog pin" or ProcessCommandLine contains " map pin" or ProcessCommandLine contains " prog detach")
pr: #6187 new: Suspicious Bpftool State Modification

au: Richard Roy (@unresolvedhost), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
de: Detects suspicious child processes spawned by ConfigurationRemotingServer.exe. Tools such as DSCourier abuse Windows Desired State Configuration (DSC) to execute arbitrary code — once a malicious DSC configuration is processed by ConfigurationRemotingServer.exe, an attacker- controlled PowerShell payload can spawn reconnaissance or post-exploitation tools as child processes.

t: Suspicious Double Extension Executable Launched From User Writable Path

The observed cluster ships as composer.php.exe and composer.dat.exe, imitating a Composer artefact so a developer double-clicking it believes they are opening a PHP or data file.

Developer build output where a toolchain names artefacts after their source file, which is plausible on a build agent or engineering workstation.

DeviceProcessEvents

t: Suspicious Encoded Payload Piped To Shell - macOS
de: Detects a command line that downloads content with curl, decodes it with base64 or gunzip, and pipes the result into a shell interpreter. This chain is used by macOS ClickFix campaigns, where a user is socially engineered into pasting a prepared command into Terminal, and by the MacSync and AMOS infostealer infection chains. The decode step is what separates this from legitimate installer one-liners, which fetch and execute without decoding.
fp: Installation scripts that fetch a compressed archive and pipe it through a shell, which is uncommon but not unheard of in developer tooling
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessCommandLine contains "curl" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "base64 -d" or ProcessCommandLine contains "base64 --decode" or ProcessCommandLine contains "gunzip" or ProcessCommandLine contains "gzip -d" or ProcessCommandLine contains "xxd -r") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "| sh" or ProcessCommandLine contains "|sh" or ProcessCommandLine contains "| bash" or ProcessCommandLine contains "|bash" or ProcessCommandLine contains "| zsh" or ProcessCommandLine contains "|zsh" or ProcessCommandLine contains "| /bin/sh" or ProcessCommandLine contains "| /bin/bash" or ProcessCommandLine contains "| /bin/zsh" or ProcessCommandLine contains "|/bin/sh" or ProcessCommandLine contains "|/bin/bash" or ProcessCommandLine contains "|/bin/zsh")

t: Suspicious Eventlog Clearing or Configuration Change Activity
au: Ecco, Daniil Yugoslavskiy, oscd.community, D3F7A5105, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
de: Detects the clearing or configuration tampering of EventLog using utilities such as "wevtutil", "powershell" and "wmic". This technique were seen used by threat actors and ransomware strains in order to evade defenses.
fp: Scripts and administrative tools used in the monitored environment
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (((FolderPath endswith "\\wevtutil.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "wevtutil.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "clear-log " or ProcessCommandLine contains " cl " or ProcessCommandLine contains "set-log " or ProcessCommandLine contains " sl " or ProcessCommandLine contains "lfn:")) or ((FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\powershell_ise.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe") and ((ProcessCommandLine contains "Clear-EventLog " or ProcessCommandLine contains "Remove-EventLog " or ProcessCommandLine contains "Limit-EventLog " or ProcessCommandLine contains "Clear-WinEvent ") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "Eventing.Reader.EventLogSession" and ProcessCommandLine contains "ClearLog") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "Diagnostics.EventLog" and ProcessCommandLine contains "Clear"))) or ((FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\powershell_ise.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\wmic.exe") and ProcessCommandLine contains "ClearEventLog")) and (not(((InitiatingProcessFolderPath in~ ("C:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\msiexec.exe", "C:\\Windows\\System32\\msiexec.exe")) and ProcessCommandLine contains " sl ")))

t: Suspicious Executable Created In AOMEI Backupper Tmphtml Directory
de: Detects a file creation event for any executable inside the "tmphtml" staging directory beneath the AOMEI Backupper installation path, where the creating process is Backupper.exe. DeviceFileEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\AOMEI\\AOMEI Backupper\\" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\Backupper.exe") and ((FolderPath contains "\\AOMEI\\AOMEI Backupper\\" and FolderPath contains "\\tmphtml\\") and FolderPath endswith ".exe")

DeviceFileEvents

t: Suspicious Invocation of Shell via AWK - Linux
au: Li Ling, Andy Parkidomo, Robert Rakowski, Blake Hartstein (Bloomberg L.P.)
de: Detects the execution of "awk" or it's sibling commands, to invoke a shell using the system() function. This behavior is commonly associated with attempts to execute arbitrary commands or escalate privileges, potentially leading to unauthorized access or further exploitation.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "/awk" or FolderPath endswith "/gawk" or FolderPath endswith "/mawk" or FolderPath endswith "/nawk") and ProcessCommandLine contains "BEGIN {system") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "/bin/bash" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/bin/dash" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/bin/fish" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/bin/sh" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/bin/zsh")

t: Suspicious LiteLLM Python Startup Hook File Creation
de: Detects creation of known Python startup-hook filenames associated with the compromised LiteLLM 1.107.0 package inside "site-packages". The malicious "cook.pth" file contains an executable "import cook" statement that Python processes during ordinary site initialization, allowing the bundled credential collector to run without the victim ever importing LiteLLM directly.
fp: Legitimate packages using sitecustomize.py for environment customization
Unrelated Python packages that happen to contain a file named cook.py
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where FolderPath contains "\\site-packages\\" and (FolderPath endswith "\\cook.pth" or FolderPath endswith "\\cook.py" or FolderPath endswith "\\sitecustomize.py")
pr: #6525 Add detection rules for LiteLLM 1.107.0 cook.pth supply-chain compromise

t: Suspicious Makecab/Diantz File Staging Or Ingress
de: Detects suspicious execution of "makecab.exe" or "diantz.exe" to package sensitive system files (e.g. Active Directory database, registry hives, browser user data, memory dumps) or to perform remote file ingress via UNC/WebDAV paths.
fp: Administrative backups of system hives or Active Directory databases using legacy cabinet packaging utilities like makecab or diantz are exceptionally rare and typically superseded by modern backup mechanisms or PowerShell scripts.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\makecab.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\diantz.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("MakeCab.exe", "diantz.exe"))) and ((ProcessCommandLine contains "\\\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "//") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "\\config\\SAM" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\config\\SYSTEM" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\config\\SECURITY" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\ntds.dit" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Microsoft\\Credentials" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Google\\Chrome\\User Data" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Local State" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".dmp" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".dump"))

t: Suspicious Microsoft Defender Exclusion Added Via WMIC
de: Detects WMIC being used to add or modify a Microsoft Defender exclusion by calling the MSFT_MpPreference class in the root\Microsoft\Windows\Defender namespace. Administrators and vendor installers overwhelmingly use the Add-MpPreference PowerShell cmdlet for this, so the WMIC path is a strong signal of an automated payload carving out a safe staging directory before writing to it.
fp: Endpoint deployment or hardening scripts that apply vendor-recommended antivirus exclusions for database, backup, or virtualisation software. These normally run from a known deployment agent parent process and reference a Program Files path rather than a user-writable one.
Legacy in-house automation that predates the Defender PowerShell module and still shells out to WMIC.
Security product installers that register their own binaries as exclusions during setup.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\wmic.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "wmic.exe") and ProcessCommandLine contains "MSFT_MpPreference" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "ExclusionPath" or ProcessCommandLine contains "ExclusionProcess" or ProcessCommandLine contains "ExclusionExtension" or ProcessCommandLine contains "ExclusionIpAddress")

t: Suspicious Path In Keyboard Layout IME File Registry Value
de: Detects usage of Windows Input Method Editor (IME) keyboard layout feature, which allows an attacker to load a DLL into the process after sending the WM_INPUTLANGCHANGEREQUEST message. Before doing this, the client needs to register the DLL in a special registry key that is assumed to implement this keyboard layout. This registry key should store a value named "Ime File" with a DLL path. IMEs are essential for languages that have more characters than can be represented on a standard keyboard, such as Chinese, Japanese, and Korean.
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where (RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\Control\\Keyboard Layouts.*$" and RegistryKey contains "Ime File") and ((RegistryValueData contains ":\\Perflogs\\" or RegistryValueData contains ":\\Users\\Public\\" or RegistryValueData contains ":\\Windows\\Temp\\" or RegistryValueData contains "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\" or RegistryValueData contains "\\AppData\\Roaming\\" or RegistryValueData contains "\\Temporary Internet") or ((RegistryValueData contains ":\\Users\\" and RegistryValueData contains "\\Favorites\\") or (RegistryValueData contains ":\\Users\\" and RegistryValueData contains "\\Favourites\\") or (RegistryValueData contains ":\\Users\\" and RegistryValueData contains "\\Contacts\\")))

t: Suspicious QoS ThrottleRate Set to Abnormally Low Value
de: Detects suspicious setting of Windows QoS ThrottleRate policies to abnormally low values that would effectively cut off network access for targeted processes. The technique sets a ThrottleRate registry value to an abnormally low value under the QoS Group Policy key, causing TCP/UDP connections for matched processes to time out and cutting off security agent telemetry. Legitimate QoS policies use human-scale bandwidth values; a throttle rate at or below 1KB/s (0-1024 bytes/sec) is too low for any real administrative use and is a strong indicator of deliberate tampering to starve a process of network access - commonly targeting EDR, AV, or other security services to suppress telemetry or block cloud lookups.
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where (RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\Software\\Policies\\Microsoft\\Windows\\QoS.*$" and RegistryKey endswith "\\ThrottleRate") and ((RegistryValueData startswith "QWORD (0x00000000-0x000000" or RegistryValueData startswith "QWORD (0x00000000-0x000001" or RegistryValueData startswith "QWORD (0x00000000-0x000002" or RegistryValueData startswith "QWORD (0x00000000-0x000003") or RegistryValueData =~ "QWORD (0x00000000-0x00000400)")

t: Suspicious Regsvr32 Execution From Remote Share
de: Detects REGSVR32.exe to execute DLL hosted on remote shares. This could be an indicator of threat actor abusing regsvr32 to download and install DLLs located remotely on a network share of threat actor infrastructure.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\regsvr32.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "\\REGSVR32.EXE") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " \\\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains " \"\\\\")
pr: #6122 update: Regsvr32 detection rules tuning and expansion

t: Suspicious Remote Child Process From Outlook

de: Detects the 'remoted' binary, a binary masquerading by living in the Library directory, spawning a shell or osascript in order to execute an AppleScript payload. This technique was reported by TA444 in the BlueNoroff macOS intrusion set.
fp: Legitimate administration scripts shipped by a remoted web server in /Library/WebServer
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "/Library/WebServer" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/remoted") and (FolderPath endswith "/sh" or FolderPath endswith "/bash" or FolderPath endswith "/zsh" or FolderPath endswith "/osascript")

de: Detects execution of system binaries that have been renamed, which is a common technique used by adversaries to evade detection. Attackers often rename legitimate system binaries to bypass security controls and execute malicious payloads without raising suspicion.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("msinfo32.exe", "netsh.exe", "packageinspector.exe", "phoneactivate.exe", "slui.exe")) and (not((FolderPath endswith "\\msinfo32.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\netsh.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\packageinspector.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\phoneactivate.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\slui.exe")))
pr: #5891 new: renamed system binaries execution for dll hijacking attack

t: Suspicious Response File Execution Via Odbcconf.EXE
de: Detects execution of "odbcconf" with the "-f" flag in order to load a response file with a non-".rsp" extension.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\odbcconf.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "odbcconf.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " -f " or ProcessCommandLine contains " /f " or ProcessCommandLine contains " –f " or ProcessCommandLine contains " —f " or ProcessCommandLine contains " ―f ")) and (not((ProcessCommandLine contains ".rsp" or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath =~ "C:\\Windows\\System32\\runonce.exe" and FolderPath =~ "C:\\Windows\\System32\\odbcconf.exe" and ProcessCommandLine contains ".exe /E /F \"C:\\WINDOWS\\system32\\odbcconf.tmp\""))))

t: Suspicious SC.EXE Config Change for Services Vulnerable to Phantom DLL Hijacking

de: Detects the creation of a schtask that executes a file from C:\Users\<USER>\AppData\Local

de: Detects scheduled task creations or modification on a suspicious schedule type

de: Detects a service binary running in a suspicious directory

de: Detects services with a binary path pointing to a suspicious location. Attackers may create or modify services to point to malicious executables in order to maintain persistence on a compromised system. It could be particularly suspicious if the service binary path points to a directory that is not commonly used for legitimate software, such as user profile directories, temporary folders, or other non-standard locations.
fp: Software installation or upgrade staging a service binary in a temporary or user-profile directory before moving it
Backup or deployment tooling running from a staging directory and registering or updating a service
Legitimate administrative activity re-pointing a service ImagePath. Inspect the writing process and user context to determine intent
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where ((RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\System.*$" and RegistryKey contains "ControlSet" and RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\Services.*$") and RegistryKey endswith "\\ImagePath" and (RegistryValueData contains "\\$Recycle.Bin\\" or RegistryValueData contains "\\ADMIN$\\" or RegistryValueData contains "\\Desktop\\" or RegistryValueData contains "\\Documents\\" or RegistryValueData contains "\\Downloads\\" or RegistryValueData contains "\\Favorites\\" or RegistryValueData contains "\\Favourites\\" or RegistryValueData contains "\\Music\\" or RegistryValueData contains "\\Perflogs\\" or RegistryValueData contains "\\Pictures\\" or RegistryValueData contains "\\Temp\\" or RegistryValueData contains "\\Users\\Default\\" or RegistryValueData contains "\\Users\\Public\\" or RegistryValueData contains "\\Videos\\" or RegistryValueData contains "\\Windows\\Debug\\" or RegistryValueData contains "\\Windows\\Tasks\\" or RegistryValueData contains "\\Windows\\Tracing\\" or RegistryValueData contains "%Public%\\" or RegistryValueData contains "%Temp%")) and (not((RegistryKey endswith "\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\MBAMInstallerService\\ImagePath" and RegistryValueData endswith "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\MBAMInstallerService.exe\"" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath =~ "C:\\Windows\\system32\\services.exe")))
pr: #5897 fix: Split Service Binary in Suspicious Folder into two distinct rules

t: Suspicious Service DACL Modification Via Set-Service Cmdlet

| where (FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "pwsh.dll") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "-SecurityDescriptorSddl " or ProcessCommandLine contains "-sd ") and ((ProcessCommandLine contains "Set-Service " and ProcessCommandLine contains "D;;") and (ProcessCommandLine contains ";;;IU" or ProcessCommandLine contains ";;;SU" or ProcessCommandLine contains ";;;BA" or ProcessCommandLine contains ";;;SY" or ProcessCommandLine contains ";;;WD"))

de: Detects suspicious call to the "ShellExec_RunDLL" exported function of SHELL32.DLL through the ordinal number to launch other commands. Adversary might only use the ordinal number in order to bypass existing detection that alert on usage of ShellExec_RunDLL on CommandLine.

au: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
de: Detects the creation of potentially malicious script and executable files in Windows startup folders, which is a common persistence technique used by threat actors. These files (.ps1, .vbs, .js, .bat, etc.) are automatically executed when a user logs in, making the Startup folder an attractive target for attackers. This technique is frequently observed in malvertising campaigns and malware distribution where attackers attempt to maintain long-term access to compromised systems.
fp: Rare legitimate usage of some of the extensions mentioned in the rule
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where FolderPath contains "\\Windows\\Start Menu\\Programs\\Startup\\" and (FolderPath endswith ".bat" or FolderPath endswith ".cmd" or FolderPath endswith ".dll" or FolderPath endswith ".hta" or FolderPath endswith ".jar" or FolderPath endswith ".js" or FolderPath endswith ".jse" or FolderPath endswith ".msi" or FolderPath endswith ".ps1" or FolderPath endswith ".psd1" or FolderPath endswith ".psm1" or FolderPath endswith ".scr" or FolderPath endswith ".url" or FolderPath endswith ".vba" or FolderPath endswith ".vbe" or FolderPath endswith ".vbs" or FolderPath endswith ".wsf")

t: Suspicious SUID Bit Set on Shell Binary via Install Command
de: Detects the use of the GNU 'install' utility to create a SUID-enabled copy of a shell binary (bash, sh, dash, zsh, ksh, fish, etc.). Once a root-owned SUID shell is placed in a writable location, an attacker executes it with '-p' to obtain a shell with the effective UID of root. This technique works with any shell that honours the SUID bit and is used across multiple CVEs and CTF/pentest scenarios. There is no legitimate operational reason to stamp a SUID bit onto a shell binary via the install command.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "/install" and ProcessCommandLine contains "-m") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "bash" or ProcessCommandLine contains " sh" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/sh" or ProcessCommandLine contains "dash" or ProcessCommandLine contains "zsh" or ProcessCommandLine contains "ksh" or ProcessCommandLine contains "mksh" or ProcessCommandLine contains "csh" or ProcessCommandLine contains "tcsh" or ProcessCommandLine contains "fish")) and (ProcessCommandLine matches regex "-m\\s{0,5}0?[4-7]\\d{3}" or ProcessCommandLine contains "+s")

t: Suspicious TamperedChef PDFEditor Run Key Persistence
de: Detects addition of a registry Run key for PDFEditorUpdater, associated with TamperedChef malware persistence via fake PDF editor installers. The observed value data combines 'PDF Editor.exe' with a --cm= argument (e.g. --cm=--fullupdate). Persistence is written to HKCU, though the filter intentionally covers both hives.
fp: Legitimate PDF software auto-update mechanisms (rare with this exact key/value combo; verify via hashes/context or C2 domains if possible)
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where (RegistryKey contains "\\CurrentVersion\\Run" and RegistryKey endswith "\\PDFEditorUpdater") and (RegistryValueData contains "PDF Editor.exe" and RegistryValueData contains "--cm=")

t: Suspicious Volume Shadow Copy VSS_PS.dll Load
de: Detects the image load of vss_ps.dll by uncommon executables. This DLL is used by the Volume Shadow Copy Service (VSS) to manage shadow copies of files and volumes. It is often abused by attackers to delete or manipulate shadow copies, which can hinder forensic investigations and data recovery efforts. The fact that it is loaded by processes that are not typically associated with VSS operations can indicate suspicious activity.

DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\vss_ps.dll" and (not(((InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\" and (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\clussvc.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\dismhost.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\dllhost.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\inetsrv\\appcmd.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\inetsrv\\iissetup.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\msiexec.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\searchindexer.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\srtasks.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\svchost.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\System32\\SystemPropertiesAdvanced.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\taskhostw.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\thor.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\thor64.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\tiworker.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\vssvc.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\vssadmin.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\WmiPrvSE.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\wsmprovhost.exe")) or (InitiatingProcessCommandLine startswith "C:\\$WinREAgent\\Scratch\\" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "\\dismhost.exe {") or isnull(InitiatingProcessFolderPath)))) and (not((InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\")))

t: Suspicious Windows Trace ETW Session Tamper Via Logman.EXE
de: Detects the execution of "logman" utility in order to disable or delete Windows trace sessions
fp: Installer tools that disable services, e.g. before log collection agent installation
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\logman.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "Logman.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "stop " or ProcessCommandLine contains "delete ") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "Circular Kernel Context Logger" or ProcessCommandLine contains "EventLog-" or ProcessCommandLine contains "SYSMON TRACE" or ProcessCommandLine contains "SysmonDnsEtwSession")

t: Suspicious Windows Update Agent Empty Cmdline
de: Detects suspicious Windows Update Agent activity in which a wuauclt.exe process command line doesn't contain any command line flags
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\Wuauclt.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "Wuauclt.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine endswith "Wuauclt" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "Wuauclt.exe")

t: Suspicious WMIC Execution Via Office Process
de: Office application called wmic to proxye execution through a LOLBIN process. This is often used to break suspicious parent-child chain (Office app spawns LOLBin).
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\WINWORD.EXE" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\EXCEL.EXE" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\POWERPNT.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\MSPUB.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\VISIO.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\MSACCESS.EXE" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\EQNEDT32.EXE" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\ONENOTE.EXE" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\wordpad.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\wordview.exe") and (FolderPath endswith "\\wbem\\WMIC.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "wmic.exe") and ((ProcessCommandLine contains "process" and ProcessCommandLine contains "create" and ProcessCommandLine contains "call") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "regsvr32" or ProcessCommandLine contains "rundll32" or ProcessCommandLine contains "msiexec" or ProcessCommandLine contains "mshta" or ProcessCommandLine contains "verclsid" or ProcessCommandLine contains "wscript" or ProcessCommandLine contains "cscript"))

au: Vadim Khrykov (ThreatIntel), Cyb3rEng, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
de: Detects suspicious and uncommon child processes of WmiPrvSE
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\wbem\\WmiPrvSE.exe" and ((FolderPath endswith "\\certutil.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\cscript.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\mshta.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\msiexec.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\regsvr32.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\verclsid.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\wscript.exe") or (FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "cscript" or ProcessCommandLine contains "mshta" or ProcessCommandLine contains "powershell" or ProcessCommandLine contains "pwsh" or ProcessCommandLine contains "regsvr32" or ProcessCommandLine contains "rundll32" or ProcessCommandLine contains "wscript"))) and (not((FolderPath endswith "\\WerFault.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\WmiPrvSE.exe" or (FolderPath endswith "\\msiexec.exe" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/i "))))

au: Vadim Khrykov (ThreatIntel), Cyb3rEng, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

t: Suspicious Word Cab File Write CVE-2021-40444
de: Detects file creation patterns noticeable during the exploitation of CVE-2021-40444
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\winword.exe" and FolderPath contains "\\Windows\\INetCache" and FolderPath endswith ".cab") or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\winword.exe" and (FolderPath contains "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\" and FolderPath contains ".inf"))) and (not((FolderPath startswith "C:\\Users\\" and FolderPath contains "AppData\\Local\\Temp" and FolderPath endswith "\\Content.inf")))

de: Detects suspicious execution of Sysinternals PsSuspend, where the utility is used to suspend critical processes such as AV or EDR to bypass defenses
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "pssuspend.exe" or (FolderPath endswith "\\pssuspend.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pssuspend64.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pssuspend64a.exe")) and ProcessCommandLine contains "msmpeng.exe"

de: Detects handle requests and access operations to specific registry keys to calculate the SysKey
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where RegistryKey endswith "lsa\\JD" or RegistryKey endswith "lsa\\GBG" or RegistryKey endswith "lsa\\Skew1" or RegistryKey endswith "lsa\\Data"

t: Syslog Clearing or Removal Via System Utilities
au: Max Altgelt (Nextron Systems), Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research), MSTIC
de: Detects specific commands commonly used to remove or empty the syslog. Which is a technique often used by attacker as a method to hide their tracks
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessCommandLine contains "/var/log/syslog" and ((FolderPath endswith "/rm" and (ProcessCommandLine contains " -r " or ProcessCommandLine contains " -f " or ProcessCommandLine contains " -rf " or ProcessCommandLine contains "/var/log/syslog")) or FolderPath endswith "/unlink" or FolderPath endswith "/mv" or (FolderPath endswith "/truncate" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "0 " and ProcessCommandLine contains "/var/log/syslog") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "-s " or ProcessCommandLine contains "-c " or ProcessCommandLine contains "--size")) or (FolderPath endswith "/ln" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "/dev/null " and ProcessCommandLine contains "/var/log/syslog") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "-sf " or ProcessCommandLine contains "-sfn " or ProcessCommandLine contains "-sfT ")) or (FolderPath endswith "/cp" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/dev/null") or (FolderPath endswith "/shred" and ProcessCommandLine contains "-u "))) or ((ProcessCommandLine contains " > /var/log/syslog" or ProcessCommandLine contains " >/var/log/syslog" or ProcessCommandLine contains " >| /var/log/syslog" or ProcessCommandLine contains ": > /var/log/syslog" or ProcessCommandLine contains ":> /var/log/syslog" or ProcessCommandLine contains ":>/var/log/syslog" or ProcessCommandLine contains ">|/var/log/syslog") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "journalctl --vacuum" or ProcessCommandLine contains "journalctl --rotate"))

t: Sysmon Discovery Via Default Driver Altitude Using Findstr.EXE
de: Detects usage of "findstr" with the argument "385201". Which could indicate potential discovery of an installed Sysinternals Sysmon service using the default driver altitude (even if the name is changed).
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\find.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\findstr.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("FIND.EXE", "FINDSTR.EXE"))) and ProcessCommandLine contains " 385201"

de: Detects changes in Sysmon driver altitude value. If the Sysmon driver is configured to load at an altitude of another registered service, it will fail to load at boot.
fp: Legitimate driver altitude change to hide sysmon
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\Services.*$" and RegistryKey endswith "\\Instances\\Sysmon Instance\\Altitude"

de: Detects possible Sysmon filter driver unloaded via fltmc.exe
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\fltMC.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "fltMC.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "unload" and ProcessCommandLine contains "sysmon")

t: System Control Panel Item Loaded From Uncommon Location
de: Detects image load events of system control panel items (.cpl) from uncommon or non-system locations that may indicate DLL sideloading or other abuse techniques.
q:
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\appwiz.cpl" or FolderPath endswith "\\bthprops.cpl" or FolderPath endswith "\\hdwwiz.cpl") and (not((FolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\Prefetch\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\System32\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\WinSxS\\")))

| where ((ProcessCommandLine contains "7z.exe a -v500m -mx9 -r0 -p" or ProcessCommandLine contains "7z.exe a -mx9 -r0 -p") and (ProcessCommandLine contains ".zip" and ProcessCommandLine contains ".txt")) or ((ProcessCommandLine contains "7z.exe a -v500m -mx9 -r0 -p" or ProcessCommandLine contains "7z.exe a -mx9 -r0 -p") and (ProcessCommandLine contains ".zip" and ProcessCommandLine contains ".log")) or ((InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "wscript.exe" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains ".vbs") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "rundll32.exe" and ProcessCommandLine contains "C:\\Windows" and ProcessCommandLine contains ".dll,Tk_")) or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe" and (InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "C:\\Windows" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains ".dll") and ProcessCommandLine contains "cmd.exe /C ") or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe" and FolderPath endswith "\\dllhost.exe" and ProcessCommandLine =~ "")

de: Detects file indicators as seen used by UNC4841 during their Barracuda ESG zero day exploitation.
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "/11111.tar" or FolderPath endswith "/aacore.sh" or FolderPath endswith "/appcheck.sh" or FolderPath endswith "/autoins" or FolderPath endswith "/BarracudaMailService" or FolderPath endswith "/etc/cron.daily/core_check.sh" or FolderPath endswith "/etc/cron.daily/core.sh" or FolderPath endswith "/etc/cron.hourly/aacore.sh" or FolderPath endswith "/etc/cron.hourly/appcheck.sh" or FolderPath endswith "/etc/cron.hourly/core.sh" or FolderPath endswith "/get_fs_info.pl" or FolderPath endswith "/imgdata.jpg" or FolderPath endswith "/install_att_v2.tar" or FolderPath endswith "/install_bvp74_auth.tar" or FolderPath endswith "/install_helo.tar" or FolderPath endswith "/install_reuse.tar" or FolderPath endswith "/intent_helo" or FolderPath endswith "/intent_reuse" or FolderPath endswith "/intentbas" or FolderPath endswith "/mod_attachment.lua" or FolderPath endswith "/mod_content.lua" or FolderPath endswith "/mod_require_helo.lua" or FolderPath endswith "/mod_rtf" or FolderPath endswith "/mod_sender.lua" or FolderPath endswith "/mod_udp.so" or FolderPath endswith "/nfsd_stub.ko" or FolderPath endswith "/resize_reisertab" or FolderPath endswith "/resize_risertab" or FolderPath endswith "/resize2fstab" or FolderPath endswith "/rverify" or FolderPath endswith "/saslautchd" or FolderPath endswith "/sendscd" or FolderPath endswith "/snapshot.tar" or FolderPath endswith "/tmp/p" or FolderPath endswith "/tmp/p7" or FolderPath endswith "/tmp/t" or FolderPath endswith "/update_v2.sh" or FolderPath endswith "/update_v31.sh" or FolderPath endswith "/update_v35.sh" or FolderPath endswith "/update_version"

t: UNC4841 - Download Compressed Files From Temp.sh Using Wget
de: Detects execution of "wget" to download a ".zip" or ".rar" files from "temp.sh". As seen used by UNC4841 during their Barracuda ESG zero day exploitation.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "/wget" and ProcessCommandLine contains "https://temp.sh/" and (ProcessCommandLine endswith ".rar" or ProcessCommandLine endswith ".zip")

t: UNC4841 - Download Tar File From Untrusted Direct IP Via Wget
de: Detects execution of "wget" to download a "tar" from an IP address that doesn't have a trusted certificate. As seen used by UNC4841 during their Barracuda ESG zero day exploitation.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "/wget" and ProcessCommandLine matches regex "https://[0-9]{1,3}\\.[0-9]{1,3}\\.[0-9]{1,3}\\.[0-9]{1,3}" and ProcessCommandLine contains "--no-check-certificate" and ProcessCommandLine endswith ".tar") and (not((ProcessCommandLine contains "https://10." or ProcessCommandLine contains "https://192.168." or ProcessCommandLine contains "https://172.16." or ProcessCommandLine contains "https://172.17." or ProcessCommandLine contains "https://172.18." or ProcessCommandLine contains "https://172.19." or ProcessCommandLine contains "https://172.20." or ProcessCommandLine contains "https://172.21." or ProcessCommandLine contains "https://172.22." or ProcessCommandLine contains "https://172.23." or ProcessCommandLine contains "https://172.24." or ProcessCommandLine contains "https://172.25." or ProcessCommandLine contains "https://172.26." or ProcessCommandLine contains "https://172.27." or ProcessCommandLine contains "https://172.28." or ProcessCommandLine contains "https://172.29." or ProcessCommandLine contains "https://172.30." or ProcessCommandLine contains "https://172.31." or ProcessCommandLine contains "https://127." or ProcessCommandLine contains "https://169.254.")))

de: Detects filename pattern of email related data used by UNC4841 for staging and exfiltration
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where FolderPath matches regex "/mail/tmp/[a-zA-Z0-9]{3}[0-9]{3}\\.tar\\.gz"

t: UNC4841 - SSL Certificate Exfiltration Via Openssl
de: Detects the execution of "openssl" to connect to an IP address. This techniques was used by UNC4841 to exfiltrate SSL certificates and as a C2 channel with named pipes. Investigate commands executed in the temporal vicinity of this command.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "/openssl" and ProcessCommandLine matches regex "[0-9]{1,3}\\.[0-9]{1,3}\\.[0-9]{1,3}\\.[0-9]{1,3}" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "s_client" and ProcessCommandLine contains "-quiet" and ProcessCommandLine contains "-connect") and (ProcessCommandLine contains ":443" or ProcessCommandLine contains ":8080")

de: Detects uncommon child process of Setres.EXE. Setres.EXE is a Windows server only process and tool that can be used to set the screen resolution. It can potentially be abused in order to launch any arbitrary file with a name containing the word "choice" from the current execution path.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\setres.exe" and FolderPath contains "\\choice") and (not((FolderPath endswith "C:\\Windows\\System32\\choice.exe" or FolderPath endswith "C:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\choice.exe")))

t: Uncommon Extension In Keyboard Layout IME File Registry Value
de: Detects usage of Windows Input Method Editor (IME) keyboard layout feature, which allows an attacker to load a DLL into the process after sending the WM_INPUTLANGCHANGEREQUEST message. Before doing this, the client needs to register the DLL in a special registry key that is assumed to implement this keyboard layout. This registry key should store a value named "Ime File" with a DLL path. IMEs are essential for languages that have more characters than can be represented on a standard keyboard, such as Chinese, Japanese, and Korean.
fp: IMEs are essential for languages that have more characters than can be represented on a standard keyboard, such as Chinese, Japanese, and Korean.
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where (RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\Control\\Keyboard Layouts.*$" and RegistryKey contains "Ime File") and (not(RegistryValueData endswith ".ime"))

t: Uncommon File Created In Office Startup Folder
de: Detects the creation of a file with an uncommon extension in an Office application startup folder
fp: False positive might stem from rare extensions used by other Office utilities.
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where (((FolderPath contains "\\Microsoft\\Word\\STARTUP" or (FolderPath contains "\\Office" and FolderPath contains "\\Program Files" and FolderPath contains "\\STARTUP")) and (not((FolderPath endswith ".docb" or FolderPath endswith ".docm" or FolderPath endswith ".docx" or FolderPath endswith ".dotm" or FolderPath endswith ".mdb" or FolderPath endswith ".mdw" or FolderPath endswith ".pdf" or FolderPath endswith ".wll" or FolderPath endswith ".wwl")))) or ((FolderPath contains "\\Microsoft\\Excel\\XLSTART" or (FolderPath contains "\\Office" and FolderPath contains "\\Program Files" and FolderPath contains "\\XLSTART")) and (not((FolderPath endswith ".xll" or FolderPath endswith ".xls" or FolderPath endswith ".xlsm" or FolderPath endswith ".xlsx" or FolderPath endswith ".xlt" or FolderPath endswith ".xltm" or FolderPath endswith ".xlw"))))) and (not(((InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains ":\\Program Files\\Common Files\\Microsoft Shared\\ClickToRun\\" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\OfficeClickToRun.exe") or ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains ":\\Program Files\\Microsoft Office\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains ":\\Program Files (x86)\\Microsoft Office\\") and (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\winword.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\excel.exe")))))

t: Uncommon File Creation By Mysql Daemon Process
de: Detects the creation of files with scripting or executable extensions by Mysql daemon. Which could be an indicator of "User Defined Functions" abuse to download malware.
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\mysqld.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\mysqld-nt.exe") and (FolderPath endswith ".bat" or FolderPath endswith ".dat" or FolderPath endswith ".dll" or FolderPath endswith ".exe" or FolderPath endswith ".ps1" or FolderPath endswith ".psm1" or FolderPath endswith ".vbe" or FolderPath endswith ".vbs")

t: Uncommon FileSystem Load Attempt By Format.com
de: Detects the execution of format.com with an uncommon filesystem selection that could indicate a defense evasion activity in which "format.com" is used to load malicious DLL files or other programs.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\format.com" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/fs:") and (not((ProcessCommandLine contains "/fs:exFAT" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/fs:FAT" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/fs:NTFS" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/fs:ReFS" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/fs:UDF")))

t: Uncommon Microsoft Office Trusted Location Added
de: Detects changes to registry keys related to "Trusted Location" of Microsoft Office where the path is set to something uncommon. Attackers might add additional trusted locations to avoid macro security restrictions.
fp: Other unknown legitimate or custom paths need to be filtered to avoid false positives
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where (RegistryKey contains "Security\\Trusted Locations\\Location" and RegistryKey endswith "\\Path") and (not(((InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains ":\\Program Files\\Common Files\\Microsoft Shared\\ClickToRun\\" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\OfficeClickToRun.exe") or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains ":\\Program Files\\Microsoft Office\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains ":\\Program Files (x86)\\Microsoft Office\\")))) and (not((RegistryValueData contains "%APPDATA%\\Microsoft\\Templates" or RegistryValueData contains "%%APPDATA%%\\Microsoft\\Templates" or RegistryValueData contains "%APPDATA%\\Microsoft\\Word\\Startup" or RegistryValueData contains "%%APPDATA%%\\Microsoft\\Word\\Startup" or RegistryValueData contains ":\\Program Files (x86)\\Microsoft Office\\root\\Templates\\" or RegistryValueData contains ":\\Program Files\\Microsoft Office (x86)\\Templates" or RegistryValueData contains ":\\Program Files\\Microsoft Office\\root\\Templates\\" or RegistryValueData contains ":\\Program Files\\Microsoft Office\\Templates\\")))

t: Uncommon One Time Only Scheduled Task At 00:00
de: Detects scheduled task creation events that include suspicious actions, and is run once at 00:00
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath contains "\\schtasks.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "schtasks.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "wscript" or ProcessCommandLine contains "vbscript" or ProcessCommandLine contains "cscript" or ProcessCommandLine contains "wmic " or ProcessCommandLine contains "wmic.exe" or ProcessCommandLine contains "regsvr32.exe" or ProcessCommandLine contains "powershell" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\AppData\\") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "once" and ProcessCommandLine contains "00:00")

de: Detects uncommon "userinit.exe" child processes, which could be a sign of uncommon shells or login scripts used for persistence.
fp: Legitimate logon scripts or custom shells may trigger false positives. Apply additional filters accordingly.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\userinit.exe" and (not(FolderPath endswith ":\\WINDOWS\\explorer.exe")) and (not(((ProcessCommandLine contains "netlogon.bat" or ProcessCommandLine contains "UsrLogon.cmd") or ProcessCommandLine =~ "PowerShell.exe" or (FolderPath endswith ":\\Windows\\System32\\proquota.exe" or FolderPath endswith ":\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\proquota.exe") or (FolderPath endswith ":\\Program Files (x86)\\Citrix\\HDX\\bin\\cmstart.exe" or FolderPath endswith ":\\Program Files (x86)\\Citrix\\HDX\\bin\\icast.exe" or FolderPath endswith ":\\Program Files (x86)\\Citrix\\System32\\icast.exe" or FolderPath endswith ":\\Program Files\\Citrix\\HDX\\bin\\cmstart.exe" or FolderPath endswith ":\\Program Files\\Citrix\\HDX\\bin\\icast.exe" or FolderPath endswith ":\\Program Files\\Citrix\\System32\\icast.exe") or isnull(FolderPath))))

de: Detects uncommon "userinit.exe" child processes, which could be a sign of uncommon shells or login scripts used for persistence.
fp: Legitimate logon scripts or custom shells may trigger false positives. Apply additional filters accordingly.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\userinit.exe" and (not(FolderPath endswith ":\\WINDOWS\\explorer.exe")) and (not(((ProcessCommandLine contains "netlogon.bat" or ProcessCommandLine contains "UsrLogon.cmd") or ProcessCommandLine =~ "PowerShell.exe" or (FolderPath endswith ":\\Windows\\System32\\proquota.exe" or FolderPath endswith ":\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\proquota.exe") or (FolderPath endswith ":\\Program Files (x86)\\Citrix\\HDX\\bin\\cmstart.exe" or FolderPath endswith ":\\Program Files (x86)\\Citrix\\HDX\\bin\\icast.exe" or FolderPath endswith ":\\Program Files (x86)\\Citrix\\System32\\icast.exe" or FolderPath endswith ":\\Program Files\\Citrix\\HDX\\bin\\cmstart.exe" or FolderPath endswith ":\\Program Files\\Citrix\\HDX\\bin\\icast.exe" or FolderPath endswith ":\\Program Files\\Citrix\\System32\\icast.exe") or isnull(FolderPath))))
pr: #6279 🩺 add regression data from evtx-attack-samples

de: Adversaries may disable security tools to avoid possible detection of their tools and activities by uninstalling Crowdstrike Falcon
fp: Administrator might leverage the same command line for debugging or other purposes. However this action must be always investigated
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessCommandLine contains "\\WindowsSensor.exe" and ProcessCommandLine contains " /uninstall" and ProcessCommandLine contains " /quiet"

de: Detects the removal of Sysmon, which could be a potential attempt at defense evasion
fp: Legitimate administrators might use this command to remove Sysmon for debugging purposes
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\Sysmon64.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\Sysmon64a.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\Sysmon.exe") or ProcessVersionInfoFileDescription =~ "System activity monitor") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "-u" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/u" or ProcessCommandLine contains "–u" or ProcessCommandLine contains "—u" or ProcessCommandLine contains "―u")

de: Detects an unexpected process spawning from dns.exe which may indicate activity related to remote code execution or other forms of exploitation as seen in CVE-2020-1350 (SigRed)
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\dns.exe" and (not(FolderPath endswith "\\conhost.exe"))

de: Detects an unexpected file being deleted by dns.exe which my indicate activity related to remote code execution or other forms of exploitation as seen in CVE-2020-1350 (SigRed)
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where ActionType =~ "FileDeleted" and (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\dns.exe" and (not(FolderPath endswith "\\dns.log")))

de: Detects an unexpected file being modified by dns.exe which my indicate activity related to remote code execution or other forms of exploitation as seen in CVE-2020-1350 (SigRed)
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\dns.exe" and (not(FolderPath endswith "\\dns.log"))

de: Detects the redirection of Ursnif discovery commands as part of the initial execution of the malware.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\explorer.exe" and FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "/C " and (ProcessCommandLine contains " >> " and ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\\AppData\\local\\temp.*\.bin"))

t: Usage of Renamed Sysinternals Tools - RegistrySet
de: Detects non-sysinternals tools setting the "accepteula" key which normally is set on sysinternals tool execution
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where ((RegistryKey contains "\\PsExec" or RegistryKey contains "\\ProcDump" or RegistryKey contains "\\Handle" or RegistryKey contains "\\LiveKd" or RegistryKey contains "\\Process Explorer" or RegistryKey contains "\\PsLoglist" or RegistryKey contains "\\PsPasswd" or RegistryKey contains "\\Active Directory Explorer") and RegistryKey endswith "\\EulaAccepted") and (not((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\PsExec.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\PsExec64.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\PsExec64a.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\procdump.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\procdump64.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\procdump64a.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\handle.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\handle64.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\handle64a.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\livekd.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\livekd64.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\procexp.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\procexp64.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\procexp64a.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\psloglist.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\psloglist64.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\psloglist64a.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\pspasswd.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\pspasswd64.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\pspasswd64a.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\ADExplorer.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\ADExplorer64.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\ADExplorer64a.exe"))) and (not(isnull(InitiatingProcessFolderPath)))

de: When configured with suitable command line arguments, w32tm can act as a delay mechanism
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\w32tm.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "w32time.dll") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "/stripchart" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/computer:" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/period:" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/dataonly" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/samples:")

t: User Account Configured With Never Expire Option Via Net.EXE
de: Detects configuration of user accounts with the "never expire" option via net.exe, either during account creation or when modifying an existing account. This is a common technique used by adversaries to maintain persistence on a compromised system.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\net.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\net1.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("net.exe", "net1.exe"))) and (ProcessCommandLine contains "user" and ProcessCommandLine contains "expires:never")
pr: #6107 fix: net user rules coverage and deprecate redundant rule

t: User Added To Highly Privileged Group
de: Detects addition of users to highly privileged groups via "Net" or "Add-LocalGroupMember".
fp: Administrative activity that must be investigated
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((ProcessCommandLine contains "localgroup " and ProcessCommandLine contains " /add") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "Add-LocalGroupMember " and ProcessCommandLine contains " -Group ")) and (ProcessCommandLine contains "Group Policy Creator Owners" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Schema Admins")

t: User Added to Remote Desktop Users Group
de: Detects addition of users to the local Remote Desktop Users group via "Net" or "Add- LocalGroupMember".
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((ProcessCommandLine contains "localgroup " and ProcessCommandLine contains " /add") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "Add-LocalGroupMember " and ProcessCommandLine contains " -Group ")) and (ProcessCommandLine contains "Remote Desktop Users" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Utilisateurs du Bureau à distance" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Usuarios de escritorio remoto")

de: Detects using SettingSyncHost.exe to run hijacked binary
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (not((FolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\System32\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\"))) and (InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "cmd.exe /c" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "RoamDiag.cmd" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "-outputpath")

t: VBA DLL Loaded Via Office Application
de: Detects VB DLL's loaded by an office application. Which could indicate the presence of VBA Macros.
fp: Legitimate macro usage. Add the appropriate filter according to your environment
q:
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\excel.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\mspub.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\onenote.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\onenoteim.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\outlook.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\powerpnt.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\winword.exe") and (FolderPath endswith "\\VBE7.DLL" or FolderPath endswith "\\VBEUI.DLL" or FolderPath endswith "\\VBE7INTL.DLL")

de: Detects VBScript content stored into registry keys as seen being used by UNC2452 group
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where (RegistryKey contains "Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion" and (RegistryValueData contains "vbscript:" or RegistryValueData contains "jscript:" or RegistryValueData contains "mshtml," or RegistryValueData contains "RunHTMLApplication" or RegistryValueData contains "Execute(" or RegistryValueData contains "CreateObject" or RegistryValueData contains "window.close")) and (not((RegistryKey contains "Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run" or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\msiexec.exe" and RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Installer\\UserData.*$" and (RegistryValueData contains "\\Microsoft.NET\\Primary Interop Assemblies\\Microsoft.mshtml.dll" or RegistryValueData contains "<\\Microsoft.mshtml,fileVersion=" or RegistryValueData contains "_mshtml_dll_" or RegistryValueData contains "<\\Microsoft.mshtml,culture=")))))

t: VeeamBackup Database Credentials Dump Via Sqlcmd.EXE
de: Detects dump of credentials in VeeamBackup dbo
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\sqlcmd.exe" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "SELECT" and ProcessCommandLine contains "TOP" and ProcessCommandLine contains "[VeeamBackup].[dbo].[Credentials]")

de: Detects the use of "vim" and it's siblings commands to execute a shell or proxy commands. Such behavior may be associated with privilege escalation, unauthorized command execution, or to break out from restricted environments.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "/rvim" or FolderPath endswith "/vi" or FolderPath endswith "/vim" or FolderPath endswith "/vimdiff") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " --cmd " or ProcessCommandLine contains " -c")) and (ProcessCommandLine contains ":!/" or ProcessCommandLine contains ":!$" or ProcessCommandLine contains ":!.." or ProcessCommandLine contains ":lua " or ProcessCommandLine contains ":py " or ProcessCommandLine contains ":shell" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/bin/bash" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/bin/dash" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/bin/fish" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/bin/sh" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/bin/csh" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/bin/ksh" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/bin/zsh" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/bin/tmux")

t: Visual Basic Command Line Compiler Usage
de: Detects successful code compilation via Visual Basic Command Line Compiler that utilizes Windows Resource to Object Converter.
fp: Utilization of this tool should not be seen in enterprise environment
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\vbc.exe" and FolderPath endswith "\\cvtres.exe"

de: Detects suspicious child process creations of VMware Tools process which may indicate persistence setup
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\vmtoolsd.exe" and ((FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\cscript.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\mshta.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\regsvr32.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\wscript.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("Cmd.Exe", "cscript.exe", "MSHTA.EXE", "PowerShell.EXE", "pwsh.dll", "REGSVR32.EXE", "RUNDLL32.EXE", "wscript.exe")))) and (not(((FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "\\VMware\\VMware Tools\\poweron-vm-default.bat" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\VMware\\VMware Tools\\poweroff-vm-default.bat" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\VMware\\VMware Tools\\resume-vm-default.bat" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\VMware\\VMware Tools\\suspend-vm-default.bat")) or (FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" and ProcessCommandLine =~ "") or (FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" and isnull(ProcessCommandLine)))))

de: Shadow Copies storage symbolic link creation using operating systems utilities
fp: Legitimate administrator working with shadow copies, access for backup purposes
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessCommandLine contains "mklink" and ProcessCommandLine contains "HarddiskVolumeShadowCopy"

t: Wab Execution From Non Default Location
de: Detects execution of wab.exe (Windows Contacts) and Wabmig.exe (Microsoft Address Book Import Tool) from non default locations as seen with bumblebee activity
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\wab.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\wabmig.exe") and (not((FolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\WinSxS\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files\\Windows Mail\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Windows Mail\\")))

t: Wab/Wabmig Unusual Parent Or Child Processes
de: Detects unusual parent or children of the wab.exe (Windows Contacts) and Wabmig.exe (Microsoft Address Book Import Tool) processes as seen being used with bumblebee activity
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\WmiPrvSE.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\svchost.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\dllhost.exe") and (FolderPath endswith "\\wab.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\wabmig.exe")) or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\wab.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\wabmig.exe")

de: Detects potential malicious modification of the property value of IsCredGuardEnabled from HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\WDigest to disable Cred Guard on a system. This is usually used with UseLogonCredential to manipulate the caching credentials.
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where RegistryKey endswith "\\IsCredGuardEnabled"

de: Detects potential malicious modification of the property value of UseLogonCredential from HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\WDigest to enable clear-text credentials
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where RegistryKey endswith "WDigest\\UseLogonCredential" and RegistryValueData =~ "DWORD (0x00000001)"

q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\w3wp.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\php-cgi.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\nginx.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\httpd.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\caddy.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\ws_tomcatservice.exe") or ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\java.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\javaw.exe") and (InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "-tomcat-" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\tomcat")) or ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\java.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\javaw.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "catalina.jar" or ProcessCommandLine contains "CATALINA_HOME"))) and (((ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("net.exe", "net1.exe")) and (ProcessCommandLine contains " user " or ProcessCommandLine contains " use " or ProcessCommandLine contains " group ")) or t: Windows Hypervisor Enforced Code Integrity Disabled
de: Detects changes to the HypervisorEnforcedCodeIntegrity registry key and the "Enabled" value being set to 0 in order to disable the Hypervisor Enforced Code Integrity feature. This allows an attacker to load unsigned and untrusted code to be run in the kernel

q:

| where (RegistryKey endswith "\\Control\\DeviceGuard\\HypervisorEnforcedCodeIntegrity" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Control\\DeviceGuard\\Scenarios\\HypervisorEnforcedCodeIntegrity\\Enabled" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Microsoft\\Windows\\DeviceGuard\\HypervisorEnforcedCodeIntegrity") and RegistryValueData =~ "DWORD (0x00000000)"

t: Windows Script Host Or Scriptlet Runtime Loaded By Explorer
de: Detects explorer.exe loading "wshom.ocx" (WScript.Shell) or "scrobj.dll" (the scriptlet runtime). Explorer has no reason to host script objects. This happens when a COM or TypeLib hijack makes Explorer run a ".sct" scriptlet, which then typically calls WScript.Shell to start the payload.
fp: Third-party shell extensions that host script objects inside Explorer
q:
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\explorer.exe" and (FolderPath endswith "\\scrobj.dll" or FolderPath endswith "\\wshom.ocx")

q:
