au: Matt Anderson, Andrew Schwartz, Caleb Stewart, Huntress
de: This detects file modifications to ASPX and ASHX files within the root of the App_Extensions directory, which is allowed by a ZipSlip vulnerability in versions prior to 23.9.8. This occurs during exploitation of CVE-2024-1708.
fp: This will occur legitimately as well and will result in some benign activity.
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\ScreenConnect.Service.exe" and ((FolderPath contains "ScreenConnect\\App_Extensions\\" and FolderPath contains ".ashx") or (FolderPath contains "ScreenConnect\\App_Extensions\\" and FolderPath contains ".aspx"))) and (not(FolderPath matches regex ".*ScreenConnect\\\\App_Extensions\\\\.*\\\\.*"))

t: CVE-2026-21509 - Malicious RTF File Access and WebDAV Connection
de: Detects suspicious RTF file opening followed by WebDAV network connections, a key indicator of CVE-2026-21509 exploitation. APT28's Operation Neusploit uses weaponized RTF documents that trigger WebDAV connections to download malicious payloads.
fp: Legitimate RTF document creation and editing
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith ".rtf" and (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\WINWORD.EXE" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\outlook.exe")) or (FolderPath contains "BULLETEN" or FolderPath contains "BULLETIN" or FolderPath contains "document.doc" or FolderPath contains "training" or FolderPath contains "military" or FolderPath contains "meteorological")
pr: #5870 CVE-2026-21509 APT28 Office Exploitation Detection Rules

t: DarkGate - Autoit3.EXE File Creation By Uncommon Process
de: Detects the usage of curl.exe, KeyScramblerLogon, or other non-standard/suspicious processes used to create Autoit3.exe. This activity has been associated with DarkGate malware, which uses Autoit3.exe to execute shellcode that performs process injection and connects to the DarkGate command-and-control server. Curl, KeyScramblerLogon, and these other processes consitute non- standard and suspicious ways to retrieve the Autoit3 executable.
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\Autoit3.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\curl.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\ExtExport.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\KeyScramblerLogon.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\wmprph.exe") and FolderPath endswith "\\Autoit3.exe"

t: DarkGate - Drop DarkGate Loader In C:\Temp Directory
de: Detects attackers attempting to save, decrypt and execute the DarkGate Loader in C:\temp folder.
fp: Unlikely legitimate usage of AutoIT in temp folders.
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where (FolderPath contains ":\\temp\\" and (FolderPath endswith ".au3" or FolderPath endswith "\\autoit3.exe")) or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains ":\\temp\\" and (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith ".au3" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\autoit3.exe"))

t: Data Collection From Removable Media Via PowerShell
de: Detects PowerShell commands that enumerate removable/USB drives and recursively search them for documents (e.g. .doc, .xls, .txt, .pdf). Adversaries scan removable media to locate and stage sensitive documents for collection and exfiltration.
fp: Backup or data-management scripts that index documents on removable media
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessCommandLine contains "DriveType -eq 'Removable'" or ProcessCommandLine contains "DriveType -eq \"Removable\"" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Get-Volume") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "Get-ChildItem" or ProcessCommandLine contains "gci " or ProcessCommandLine contains "ls ") and (ProcessCommandLine contains ".doc" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".xls" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".pdf" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".txt")
pr: #6095 Add cross-platform discovery/collection rules

t: Data Export From MSSQL Table Via BCP.EXE
au: Omar Khaled (@beacon_exe), MahirAli Khan (in/mahiralikhan), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
de: Detects the execution of the BCP utility in order to export data from the database. Attackers were seen saving their malware to a database column or table and then later extracting it via "bcp.exe" into a file.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\bcp.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "BCP.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " out " or ProcessCommandLine contains " queryout ")

t: Dbghelp/Dbgcore DLL Loaded By Uncommon/Suspicious Process
de: Detects the load of dbghelp/dbgcore DLL by a potentially uncommon or potentially suspicious process. The Dbghelp and Dbgcore DLLs export functions that allow for the dump of process memory. Tools like ProcessHacker, Task Manager and some attacker tradecraft use the MiniDumpWriteDump API found in dbghelp.dll or dbgcore.dll. As an example, SilentTrynity C2 Framework has a module that leverages this API to dump the contents of Lsass.exe and transfer it over the network back to the attacker's machine. Keep in mind that many legitimate Windows processes and services might load the aforementioned DLLs for debugging or other related purposes. Investigate the CommandLine and the Image location of the process loading the DLL.
fp: Debugging scripts might leverage this DLL in order to dump process memory for further analysis.
q:
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\dbghelp.dll" or FolderPath endswith "\\dbgcore.dll") and (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\bash.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\cscript.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\dnx.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\excel.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\monitoringhost.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\msbuild.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\mshta.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\outlook.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\powerpnt.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\regsvcs.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\sc.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\scriptrunner.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\winword.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\wmic.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\wscript.exe")) and (not(((InitiatingProcessCommandLine startswith "C:\\WINDOWS\\WinSxS\\" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine endswith "\\TiWorker.exe -Embedding") or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\svchost.exe" and (InitiatingProcessCommandLine endswith "-k LocalServiceNetworkRestricted" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine endswith "-k WerSvcGroup")) or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe" and (InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "/d srrstr.dll,ExecuteScheduledSPPCreation" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "aepdu.dll,AePduRunUpdate" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "shell32.dll,OpenAs_RunDL" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "Windows.Storage.ApplicationData.dll,CleanupTemporaryState")))))

de: Detects the deactivation and disabling of the Scheduled defragmentation task as seen by Slingshot APT group
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\schtasks.exe" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "/delete" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/change") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "/TN" and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Microsoft\\Windows\\Defrag\\ScheduledDefrag")

de: Detects usage of the "cipher" built-in utility in order to overwrite deleted data from disk. Adversaries may destroy data and files on specific systems or in large numbers on a network to interrupt availability to systems, services, and network resources. Data destruction is likely to render stored data irrecoverable by forensic techniques through overwriting files or data on local and remote drives
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "CIPHER.EXE" or FolderPath endswith "\\cipher.exe") and ProcessCommandLine contains " /w:"

t: Deno Runtime Spawns Shell Or Scripting Interpreter
de: Detects suspicious child process execution from the Deno runtime, a behavior useful for MuddyWater/Dindoor-inspired hunting.
fp: Developer automation using Deno to orchestrate local shell commands.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\deno.exe" and (FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\wscript.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\cscript.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe")
pr: #6065 Add Deno child process and non-mail IMAP detections

de: Detects unusual processes accessing desktop.ini, which can be leveraged to alter how Explorer displays a folder's content (i.e. renaming files) without changing them on disk.
fp: Operations performed through Windows SCCM or equivalent
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\desktop.ini" and (not(((InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\") or FolderPath startswith "C:\\$WINDOWS.~BT\\NewOS\\"))) and (not(((InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Users\\" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\AppData\\Local\\JetBrains\\Toolbox\\bin\\7z.exe" and FolderPath contains "\\JetBrains\\apps\\") or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Users\\" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\AppData\\Local\\Microsoft\\OneDrive\\"))))

de: Adversaries may attempt to enumerate software for a variety of reasons, such as figuring out what security measures are present or if the compromised system has a version of software that is vulnerable.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\reg.exe" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "query" and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\software\\" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/v" and ProcessCommandLine contains "svcversion")

t: Detection of PowerShell Execution via Sqlps.exe
de: This rule detects execution of a PowerShell code through the sqlps.exe utility, which is included in the standard set of utilities supplied with the MSSQL Server. Script blocks are not logged in this case, so this utility helps to bypass protection mechanisms based on the analysis of these logs.
fp: Direct PS command execution through SQLPS.exe is uncommon, childprocess sqlps.exe spawned by sqlagent.exe is a legitimate action.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\sqlps.exe" or ((FolderPath endswith "\\sqlps.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "sqlps.exe") and (not(InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\sqlagent.exe")))

t: Dev Tunnel Hosting Or Creation Execution
de: Detects execution of the Microsoft "devtunnel" CLI to create or host a Dev Tunnel, which exposes a local port or endpoint to the internet through Microsoft infrastructure (*.devtunnels.ms). Adversaries abuse Dev Tunnels for command-and-control, reverse shells and persistent remote access that blends in with trusted Microsoft domains. This rule complements existing network and DNS detections by catching the on-host tunnel setup.
fp: Legitimate use of Microsoft Dev Tunnels by developers exposing local services for testing.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\devtunnel.exe" and (ProcessCommandLine contains " host" or ProcessCommandLine contains " create" or ProcessCommandLine contains " port forward")
pr: #6089 rules/windows: add Dev Tunnel hosting or creation process_creation rule

de: Detects the execution of DeviceCredentialDeployment to hide a process from view.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\DeviceCredentialDeployment.exe"

t: Dfsvc.EXE Network Connection To Non-Local IPs
de: Detects network connections from "dfsvc.exe" used to handled ClickOnce applications to non-local IPs
fp: False positives are expected from ClickOnce manifests hosted on public IPs and domains. Apply additional filters for the accepted IPs in your environement as necessary
q:
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\dfsvc.exe" and (not((ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "127.0.0.0/8") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "10.0.0.0/8") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "169.254.0.0/16") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "172.16.0.0/12") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "192.168.0.0/16") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "::1/128") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "fe80::/10") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "fc00::/7"))))

t: DinDoor Backdoor Deno Remote JavaScript Execution From PowerShell
de: Detects Deno launched from PowerShell with full permissions to execute remote JavaScript as observed in DinDoor Backdoor MSI installer chains.
fp: Legitimate PowerShell automation using Deno with full permissions to execute remote JavaScript.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\deno.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "deno.exe") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "-A" or ProcessCommandLine contains "--allow-all") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "http:" or ProcessCommandLine contains "https:")
pr: #6083 new: Dindoor Backdoor Malware rule

au: Victor Sergeev, Daniil Yugoslavskiy, oscd.community, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
de: Detects direct modification of autostart extensibility point (ASEP) in registry using reg.exe.
fp: Legitimate software automatically (mostly, during installation) sets up autorun keys for legitimate reasons.
Legitimate administrator sets up autorun keys for legitimate reasons.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\reg.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "reg.exe") and ProcessCommandLine contains "add" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "\\software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\software\\WOW6432Node\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Policies\\Explorer\\Run" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\software\\Microsoft\\Windows NT\\CurrentVersion\\Winlogon\\Userinit" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\software\\Microsoft\\Windows NT\\CurrentVersion\\Winlogon\\Shell" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\software\\Microsoft\\Windows NT\\CurrentVersion\\Windows" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\system\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\SafeBoot\\AlternateShell")

au: Victor Sergeev, Daniil Yugoslavskiy, oscd.community, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
de: Detects direct modification of autostart extensibility point (ASEP) in registry using reg.exe.

Legitimate administrator sets up autorun keys for legitimate reasons.

t: Disable Administrative Share Creation at Startup
de: Administrative shares are hidden network shares created by Microsoft Windows NT operating systems that grant system administrators remote access to every disk volume on a network- connected system
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\Services\\LanmanServer\\Parameters.*$" and (RegistryKey endswith "\\AutoShareWks" or RegistryKey endswith "\\AutoShareServer") and RegistryValueData =~ "DWORD (0x00000000)"

t: Disable Exploit Guard Network Protection on Windows Defender
de: Detects disabling Windows Defender Exploit Guard Network Protection
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where RegistryKey contains "SOFTWARE\\Policies\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender Security Center\\App and Browser protection\\DisallowExploitProtectionOverride" and RegistryValueData =~ "DWORD (00000001)"

t: Disable Exploit Guard Network Protection on Windows Defender
de: Detects disabling Windows Defender Exploit Guard Network Protection
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where RegistryKey contains "SOFTWARE\\Policies\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender Security Center\\App and Browser protection\\DisallowExploitProtectionOverride" and RegistryValueData =~ "DWORD (0x00000001)"
pr: #6560 fix: Disable Exploit Guard Network Protection on Windows Defender - add the 0x prefix to the DWORD value

"SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Policies\\Explorer\\HideSCAHealth" or RegistryKey endswith "SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Policies\\Explorer\\HideSCANetwork" or t: Disable Microsoft Defender Firewall via Registry
de: Adversaries may disable or modify system firewalls in order to bypass controls limiting network usage
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\Services\\SharedAccess\\Parameters\\FirewallPolicy.*$" and RegistryKey endswith "\\EnableFirewall" and RegistryValueData =~ "DWORD (0x00000000)"

de: Detects the usage of utilities such as 'systemctl', 'service'...etc to stop or disable tools and services on Linux systems. Attackers may stop or disable security tools and services to evade detection, maintain persistence, or disrupt system operations.
fp: Some false positives are to be expected. Apply additional filters as needed before pushing to production.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "/service" or FolderPath endswith "/systemctl" or FolderPath endswith "/chkconfig") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " stop " or ProcessCommandLine contains " disable ")) and (not(((FolderPath endswith "/systemctl" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "--no-reload disable snap-snapd-" or ProcessCommandLine contains " stop snap-snapd-")) or (FolderPath endswith "/systemctl" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "tmp.ci/preinst upgrade" and (ProcessCommandLine contains " stop " and ProcessCommandLine contains "ssh.")) or (InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "/dpkg/info/ubuntu-pro-client.prerm upgrade" and FolderPath endswith "/systemctl")))) and (not((FolderPath endswith "/systemctl" and ProcessCommandLine endswith "snap.amazon-ssm-agent.amazon-ssm-agent.service")))

t: Disable Privacy Settings Experience in Registry
de: Detects registry modifications that disable Privacy Settings Experience
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where RegistryKey endswith "\\SOFTWARE\\Policies\\Microsoft\\Windows\\OOBE\\DisablePrivacyExperience" and RegistryValueData =~ "DWORD (0x00000000)"

de: Detects disabling security tools
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath =~ "/bin/launchctl" and ProcessCommandLine contains "unload") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "com.objective-see.lulu.plist" or ProcessCommandLine contains "com.objective-see.blockblock.plist" or ProcessCommandLine contains "com.google.santad.plist" or ProcessCommandLine contains "com.carbonblack.defense.daemon.plist" or ProcessCommandLine contains "com.carbonblack.daemon.plist" or ProcessCommandLine contains "at.obdev.littlesnitchd.plist" or ProcessCommandLine contains "com.tenablesecurity.nessusagent.plist" or ProcessCommandLine contains "com.opendns.osx.RoamingClientConfigUpdater.plist" or ProcessCommandLine contains "com.crowdstrike.falcond.plist" or ProcessCommandLine contains "com.crowdstrike.userdaemon.plist" or ProcessCommandLine contains "osquery" or ProcessCommandLine contains "filebeat" or ProcessCommandLine contains "auditbeat" or ProcessCommandLine contains "packetbeat" or ProcessCommandLine contains "td-agent")) or (FolderPath =~ "/usr/sbin/spctl" and ProcessCommandLine contains "disable")

t: Disable Tamper Protection on Windows Defender
de: Detects disabling Windows Defender Tamper Protection
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where (RegistryKey contains "\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender\\Features\\TamperProtection" and RegistryValueData =~ "DWORD (0x00000000)") and (not(((InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\ProgramData\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender\\Platform\\" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\MsMpEng.exe") or InitiatingProcessFolderPath =~ "C:\\Program Files\\Windows Defender\\MsMpEng.exe")))

de: Detect set EnableFirewall to 0 to disable the Windows firewall
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where (RegistryKey endswith "\\SOFTWARE\\Policies\\Microsoft\\WindowsFirewall\\StandardProfile\\EnableFirewall" or RegistryKey endswith "\\SOFTWARE\\Policies\\Microsoft\\WindowsFirewall\\DomainProfile\\EnableFirewall") and RegistryValueData =~ "DWORD (0x00000000)"

de: Detect set UseActionCenterExperience to 0 to disable the Windows security center notification
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where RegistryKey endswith "Windows\\CurrentVersion\\ImmersiveShell\\UseActionCenterExperience" and RegistryValueData =~ "DWORD (0x00000000)"

de: Detects disabling security tools
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "/service" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "iptables" and ProcessCommandLine contains "stop")) or (FolderPath endswith "/service" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "ip6tables" and ProcessCommandLine contains "stop")) or (FolderPath endswith "/chkconfig" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "iptables" and ProcessCommandLine contains "stop")) or (FolderPath endswith "/chkconfig" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "ip6tables" and ProcessCommandLine contains "stop")) or (FolderPath endswith "/systemctl" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "firewalld" and ProcessCommandLine contains "stop")) or (FolderPath endswith "/systemctl" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "firewalld" and ProcessCommandLine contains "disable")) or (FolderPath endswith "/service" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "cbdaemon" and ProcessCommandLine contains "stop")) or (FolderPath endswith "/chkconfig" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "cbdaemon" and ProcessCommandLine contains "off")) or (FolderPath endswith "/systemctl" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "cbdaemon" and ProcessCommandLine contains "stop")) or (FolderPath endswith "/systemctl" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "cbdaemon" and ProcessCommandLine contains "disable")) or (FolderPath endswith "/setenforce" and ProcessCommandLine contains "0") or (FolderPath endswith "/systemctl" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "stop" and ProcessCommandLine contains "falcon-sensor")) or (FolderPath endswith "/systemctl" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "disable" and ProcessCommandLine contains "falcon-sensor"))

t: Disk Image Creation Via Hdiutil - MacOS
de: Detects the execution of the hdiutil utility in order to create a disk image.
fp: Legitimate usage of hdiutil by administrators and users.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "/hdiutil" and ProcessCommandLine contains "create"

t: Disk Image Mounting Via Hdiutil - MacOS
de: Detects the execution of the hdiutil utility in order to mount disk images.
fp: Legitimate usage of hdiutil by administrators and users.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "/hdiutil" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "attach " or ProcessCommandLine contains "mount ")

de: Detects any child process spawning from "Diskshadow.exe". This could be due to executing Diskshadow in interpreter mode or script mode and using the "exec" flag to launch other applications.
fp: Likely from legitimate usage of Diskshadow in Interpreter mode.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\diskshadow.exe" and (not(FolderPath endswith ":\\Windows\\System32\\WerFault.exe"))

t: Diskshadow Script Mode - Execution From Potential Suspicious Location
de: Detects execution of "Diskshadow.exe" in script mode using the "/s" flag where the script is located in a potentially suspicious location.
fp: False positives may occur if you execute the script from one of the paths mentioned in the rule. Apply additional filters that fits your org needs.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "diskshadow.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\diskshadow.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "-s " or ProcessCommandLine contains "/s " or ProcessCommandLine contains "–s " or ProcessCommandLine contains "—s " or ProcessCommandLine contains "―s ") and (ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Temp\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Windows\\Temp\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\AppData\\Local\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\AppData\\Roaming\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\ProgramData\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Users\\Public\\")

t: Diskshadow Script Mode - Uncommon Script Extension Execution
de: Detects execution of "Diskshadow.exe" in script mode to execute an script with a potentially uncommon extension. Initial baselining of the allowed extension list is required.
fp: False postitve might occur with legitimate or uncommon extensions used internally. Initial baseline is required.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "diskshadow.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\diskshadow.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "-s " or ProcessCommandLine contains "/s " or ProcessCommandLine contains "–s " or ProcessCommandLine contains "—s " or ProcessCommandLine contains "―s ")) and (not(ProcessCommandLine contains ".txt"))

de: Detects execution of "Diskshadow.exe" in script mode using the "/s" flag. Attackers often abuse "diskshadow" to execute scripts that deleted the shadow copies on the systems. Investigate the content of the scripts and its location.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "diskshadow.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\diskshadow.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "-s " or ProcessCommandLine contains "/s " or ProcessCommandLine contains "–s " or ProcessCommandLine contains "—s " or ProcessCommandLine contains "―s ")

de: Deployment Image Servicing and Management tool. DISM is used to enumerate, install, uninstall, configure, and update features and packages in Windows images
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\DismHost.exe" and (InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "/Online" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "/Disable-Feature")) or (FolderPath endswith "\\Dism.exe" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "/Online" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/Disable-Feature"))

de: Detects modifications to the "Hidden" and "ShowSuperHidden" explorer registry values in order to disable showing of hidden files and system files. This technique is abused by several malware families to hide their files from normal users.
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where (RegistryKey endswith "\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Explorer\\Advanced\\ShowSuperHidden" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Explorer\\Advanced\\Hidden") and RegistryValueData =~ "DWORD (0x00000000)"

t: DLL Call by Ordinal Via Rundll32.EXE
de: Detects calls of DLLs exports by ordinal numbers via rundll32.dll.
fp: False positives depend on scripts and administrative tools used in the monitored environment.

t: Execution Of Script Located In Potentially Suspicious Directory

t: Execution of Suspicious File Type Extension
de: Detects whether the image specified in a process creation event doesn't refer to an ".exe" (or other known executable extension) file. q:

q:

q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\certutil.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "CertUtil.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "-encode" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/encode" or ProcessCommandLine contains "–encode" or ProcessCommandLine contains "—encode" or ProcessCommandLine contains "―encode")

t: Git Pack or Proxy Program Override - Linux
de: Detects Git being told to run a caller-supplied program in place of one of the helpers it normally starts for itself. The "--upload-pack" and "--receive-pack" options, their "remote.<name>.uploadpack" and "remote.<name>.receivepack" configuration equivalents, "uploadpack.packObjectsHook" and "core.gitProxy" each name a program that Git executes while moving objects to or from a repository. Against a local path or a local clone that program runs on the host issuing the command, which turns an otherwise ordinary looking Git invocation into command execution.
fp: Connecting to a server that keeps Git outside the default path, which is the documented reason to pass "--upload-pack" or "--receive-pack".
A proxy program configured for the deprecated "git://" protocol in an environment that still restricts direct outbound connections.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "/git" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "--receive-pack" or ProcessCommandLine contains "--upload-pack" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".receivepack" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".uploadpack" or ProcessCommandLine contains "core.gitProxy" or ProcessCommandLine contains "uploadpack.packObjectsHook")

de: Detects GitHub self-hosted runners executing workflows on local infrastructure that could be abused for persistence and code execution. Shai-Hulud is an npm supply chain worm targeting CI/CD environments. It installs runners on compromised systems to maintain access after credential theft, leveraging their access to secrets and internal networks.
fp: Legitimate GitHub self-hosted runner installations on designated CI/CD infrastructure
Authorized runner deployments by DevOps/Platform teams following change management
Scheduled runner updates or reconfigurations on existing build agents
Self-hosted runners that follow expected/known naming patterns
Installation via expected/known configuration management tools (reflected mostly as parent process name)
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\Runner.Worker.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "Runner.Worker.dll") and ProcessCommandLine contains "spawnclient") or ((FolderPath endswith "\\Runner.Listener.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "Runner.Listener.dll") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "run" or ProcessCommandLine contains "configure"))

de: Detects the use of the OpenSSH "scp.exe" client to execute commands indirectly, either via the "-S" option (which specifies the program to use for the encrypted connection) or via a "ProxyCommand". Both mechanisms allow a threat actor to abuse the trusted "scp.exe" binary as a proxy to launch arbitrary programs while evading detection. This completes coverage of the OpenSSH client LOLBin family alongside the existing "sftp.exe" and "ssh.exe" rules.
fp: Legitimate use of scp with a custom transport program or proxy command. This is rare and mostly seen in constrained network or administration scenarios.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\scp.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "scp.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " -S " or ProcessCommandLine contains "ProxyCommand=")
pr: #6104 Add rule: indirect command execution via scp.exe

t: Indirect Inline Command Execution Via Bash.EXE
de: Detects execution of Microsoft bash launcher with the "-c" flag. This can be used to potentially bypass defenses and execute Linux or Windows-based binaries directly via bash.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith ":\\Windows\\System32\\bash.exe" or FolderPath endswith ":\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\bash.exe") or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "Bash.exe") and ProcessCommandLine contains " -c "

de: Executes SCT script using scrobj.dll from a command in entered into a specially prepared INF file.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessCommandLine contains "InfDefaultInstall.exe " and ProcessCommandLine contains ".inf"

de: Detects execution of "curl.exe" with the "insecure" flag over proxy or DOH.
fp: Access to badly maintained internal or development systems
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\curl.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "curl.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "--doh-insecure" or ProcessCommandLine contains "--proxy-insecure")

de: Detects execution of "curl.exe" with the "--insecure" flag.
fp: Access to badly maintained internal or development systems
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\curl.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "curl.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine matches regex "\\s-k\\s" or ProcessCommandLine contains "--insecure")

t: Install New Package Via Winget Local Manifest
de: Detects usage of winget to install applications via manifest file. Adversaries can abuse winget to download payloads remotely and execute them. The manifest option enables you to install an application by passing in a YAML file directly to the client. Winget can be used to download and install exe, msi or msix files later.
fp: Some false positives are expected in some environment that may use this functionality to install and test their custom applications
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\winget.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "winget.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "install" or ProcessCommandLine contains " add ") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "-m " or ProcessCommandLine contains "--manifest")

de: TeamViewer_Desktop.exe is create during install
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\TeamViewer_Desktop.exe"

de: Detects suspicious interactive bash as a parent to rather uncommon child processes
fp: Legitimate software that uses these patterns
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine =~ "bash -i" and ((ProcessCommandLine contains "-c import " or ProcessCommandLine contains "base64" or ProcessCommandLine contains "pty.spawn") or (FolderPath endswith "whoami" or FolderPath endswith "iptables" or FolderPath endswith "/ncat" or FolderPath endswith "/nc" or FolderPath endswith "/netcat"))

au: Victor Sergeev, Daniil Yugoslavskiy, Gleb Sukhodolskiy, Timur Zinniatullin, oscd.community, Tim Shelton, frack113 (split)
de: Detects modification of autostart extensibility point (ASEP) in registry.
fp: Legitimate software automatically (mostly, during installation) sets up autorun keys for legitimate reason
Legitimate administrator sets up autorun keys for legitimate reason
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where (RegistryKey contains "\\Software\\Wow6432Node\\Microsoft\\Internet Explorer" or RegistryKey contains "\\Software\\Microsoft\\Internet Explorer") and (RegistryKey contains "\\Toolbar" or RegistryKey contains "\\Extensions" or RegistryKey contains "\\Explorer Bars") and (not((RegistryValueData =~ "(Empty)" or (RegistryKey contains "\\Extensions\\{2670000A-7350-4f3c-8081-5663EE0C6C49}" or RegistryKey contains "\\Extensions\\{31D09BA0-12F5-4CCE-BE8A-2923E76605DA}" or RegistryKey contains "\\Extensions\\{789FE86F-6FC4-46A1-9849-EDE0DB0C95CA}" or RegistryKey contains "\\Extensions\\{A95fe080-8f5d-11d2-a20b-00aa003c157a}") or (RegistryKey endswith "\\Toolbar\\ShellBrowser\\ITBar7Layout" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Toolbar\\ShowDiscussionButton" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Toolbar\\Locked"))))

de: Detects changes to the Internet Explorer "DisableFirstRunCustomize" value, which prevents Internet Explorer from running the first run wizard the first time a user starts the browser after installing Internet Explorer or Windows.
fp: As this is controlled by group policy as well as user settings. Some false positives may occur.
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where (RegistryKey endswith "\\Microsoft\\Internet Explorer\\Main\\DisableFirstRunCustomize" and (RegistryValueData in~ ("DWORD (0x00000001)", "DWORD (0x00000002)"))) and (not((InitiatingProcessFolderPath in~ ("C:\\Windows\\explorer.exe", "C:\\Windows\\System32\\ie4uinit.exe")))) and (not((((InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\Temp\\" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\.cr\\avira_") and RegistryValueData contains "DWORD (0x00000001)") or ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath in~ ("C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Foxit Software\\Foxit PDF Reader\\FoxitPDFReader.exe", "C:\\Program Files\\Foxit Software\\Foxit PDF Reader\\FoxitPDFReader.exe")) and RegistryValueData contains "DWORD (0x00000001)"))))

t: Invocation of Active Directory Diagnostic Tool (ntdsutil.exe)
de: Detects execution of ntdsutil.exe, which can be used for various attacks against the NTDS database (NTDS.DIT)
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\ntdsutil.exe"

t: Invocation Of Crypto-Classes From The "Cryptography" PowerShell Namespace
de: Detects the invocation of PowerShell commands with references to classes from the "System.Security.Cryptography" namespace. The PowerShell namespace "System.Security.Cryptography" provides classes for on-the-fly encryption and decryption. These can be used for example in decrypting malicious payload for defense evasion.
fp: Classes are legitimately used, but less so when e.g. parents with low prevalence or decryption of content in temporary folders.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("PowerShell.EXE", "pwsh.dll"))) and ProcessCommandLine contains "System.Security.Cryptography." and (ProcessCommandLine contains ".AesCryptoServiceProvider" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".DESCryptoServiceProvider" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".DSACryptoServiceProvider" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".RC2CryptoServiceProvider" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".Rijndael" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".RSACryptoServiceProvider" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".TripleDESCryptoServiceProvider")

de: Detects Obfuscated Powershell via COMPRESS OBFUSCATION
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessCommandLine contains "new-object" and ProcessCommandLine contains "text.encoding]::ascii") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "system.io.compression.deflatestream" or ProcessCommandLine contains "system.io.streamreader" or ProcessCommandLine contains "readtoend(")

t: ISO or Image Mount Indicator in Recent Files
de: Detects the creation of recent element file that points to an .ISO, .IMG, .VHD or .VHDX file as often used in phishing attacks. This can be a false positive on server systems but on workstations users should rarely mount .iso or .img files.
fp: Cases in which a user mounts an image file for legitimate reasons
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith ".iso.lnk" or FolderPath endswith ".img.lnk" or FolderPath endswith ".vhd.lnk" or FolderPath endswith ".vhdx.lnk") and FolderPath contains "\\Microsoft\\Windows\\Recent\\"

t: JAMF MDM Potential Suspicious Child Process
de: Detects potential suspicious child processes of "jamf". Could be a sign of potential abuse of Jamf as a C2 server as seen by Typhon MythicAgent.
fp: Legitimate execution of custom scripts or commands by Jamf administrators. Apply additional filters accordingly
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/jamf" and (FolderPath endswith "/bash" or FolderPath endswith "/sh")

de: Detects a JAVA process running with remote debugging allowing more than just localhost to connect
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessCommandLine contains "transport=dt_socket,address=" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "jre1." or ProcessCommandLine contains "jdk1.")) and (not((ProcessCommandLine contains "address=127.0.0.1" or ProcessCommandLine contains "address=localhost")))

de: Detects registry set activity of a value called "Seed" stored in the "\Cryptography\Providers\" registry key. The Kapeka backdoor leverages this location to register a new SIP provider for backdoor configuration persistence.
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where (RegistryKey contains "\\SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Cryptography\\Providers\\{" and RegistryKey endswith "\\Seed") and (not(RegistryValueData contains "(Empty)"))

de: Detects the execution of programs as Launch Agents or Launch Daemons using launchctl on macOS.
fp: Legitimate administration activities is expected to trigger false positives. Investigate the command line being passed to determine if the service or launch agent are suspicious.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "/launchctl" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "submit" or ProcessCommandLine contains "load" or ProcessCommandLine contains "start")

de: Detects the execution of programs as Launch Agents or Launch Daemons using launchctl on macOS.
fp: Legitimate administration activities is expected to trigger false positives. Investigate the command line being passed to determine if the service or launch agent are suspicious.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "/launchctl" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "submit" or ProcessCommandLine contains "load" or ProcessCommandLine contains "start" or ProcessCommandLine contains "bootstrap")
pr: #6209 macOS: cover `launchctl bootstrap`, add AMOS LaunchDaemon install and wallet replacement rules

de: Detects the execution of programs as Launch Agents or Launch Daemons using launchctl on macOS.
fp: Legitimate administration activities is expected to trigger false positives. Investigate the command line being passed to determine if the service or launch agent are suspicious.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "/launchctl" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "bootstrap" or ProcessCommandLine contains "submit" or ProcessCommandLine contains "load" or ProcessCommandLine contains "start")
pr: #6543 Update macOS launchctl rule to cover the bootstrap verb

de: Detects the use of the 'Launch-VsDevShell.ps1' Microsoft signed script to execute commands.
fp: Legitimate usage of the script by a developer
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessCommandLine contains "Launch-VsDevShell.ps1" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "VsWherePath " or ProcessCommandLine contains "VsInstallationPath ")

t: Linux Base64 Encoded Pipe to Shell
de: Detects suspicious process command line that uses base64 encoded input for execution with a shell
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessCommandLine contains "base64 " and ((ProcessCommandLine contains "| bash " or ProcessCommandLine contains "| sh " or ProcessCommandLine contains "|bash " or ProcessCommandLine contains "|sh ") or (ProcessCommandLine endswith " |sh" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "| bash" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "| sh" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "|bash"))

t: Linux Base64 Encoded Shebang In CLI
de: Detects the presence of a base64 version of the shebang in the commandline, which could indicate a malicious payload about to be decoded
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessCommandLine contains "IyEvYmluL2Jhc2" or ProcessCommandLine contains "IyEvYmluL2Rhc2" or ProcessCommandLine contains "IyEvYmluL3pza" or ProcessCommandLine contains "IyEvYmluL2Zpc2" or ProcessCommandLine contains "IyEvYmluL3No"

de: Detects the creation of doas.conf file in linux host platform.
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "/etc/doas.conf"

t: Linux Kernel Ring Buffer Cleared via Dmesg
de: Detects the use of 'dmesg' to clear the kernel ring buffer, which removes kernel log messages that could contain evidence of exploitation, privilege escalation, or hardware errors. Threat actors use this technique to destroy forensic artifacts after gaining access to a system.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "/dmesg" and ((ProcessCommandLine contains " -C " or ProcessCommandLine contains "-clear") or ProcessCommandLine endswith " -C")
pr: #6242 update: linux anti forensics rules

de: Detects logs clearing attempts on Linux systems via utilities such as 'rm', 'rmdir', 'shred', and 'unlink' targeting log files and directories. Adversaries often try to clear logs to cover their tracks after performing malicious activities.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "/rm" or FolderPath endswith "/rmdir" or FolderPath endswith "/shred" or FolderPath endswith "/unlink") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "/var/log" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/var/spool/mail")) and (not(((FolderPath endswith "/rm" and ProcessCommandLine startswith "rm -f /var/log/sysstat/") or (FolderPath endswith "/rm" and ProcessCommandLine startswith "rm -f -- /var/log//dmesg"))))

t: Linux Security Capability Set via Setfattr Utility
de: Detects the use of the 'setfattr' utility to modify security capabilities of a file. The capability feature in Linux allows executable files to obtain specific permissions without needing traditional root privileges, which can be exploited for unauthorized access, privileges escalation, or to bypass security controls. Unlike the standard 'setcap' utility, the use of 'setfattr' to modify security capabilities is not common in normal operations and could indicate stealthy and suspicious activity.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "/setfattr" and ProcessCommandLine contains "security.capability"
pr: #5800 add: Linux Security Capability Set Via Setfattr Utility

de: Detects suspicious process command line that starts with a shell that executes something and finally gets piped into another shell
fp: Legitimate software that uses these patterns
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessCommandLine startswith "sh -c " or ProcessCommandLine startswith "bash -c ") and ((ProcessCommandLine contains "| bash " or ProcessCommandLine contains "| sh " or ProcessCommandLine contains "|bash " or ProcessCommandLine contains "|sh ") or (ProcessCommandLine endswith "| bash" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "| sh" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "|bash" or ProcessCommandLine endswith " |sh"))

t: Linux Suspicious Setcap Use with All Capabilities
de: Detects the use of the 'setcap' utility with parameters that assign all Linux capabilities to a binary file. This action can be exploited by adversaries to create a completely backdoored binary, enabling unauthorized access, privilege escalation, or the circumvention of security controls.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "/setcap" and (ProcessCommandLine contains " all=" or ProcessCommandLine contains " =e" or ProcessCommandLine contains " =i" or ProcessCommandLine contains " =p")
pr: #5878 add: Linux Suspicious Setcap Use with All Capabilities

de: Detects the creation of the LiveKD driver, which is used for live kernel debugging
fp: Legitimate usage of LiveKD for debugging purposes will also trigger this
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where FolderPath =~ "C:\\Windows\\System32\\drivers\\LiveKdD.SYS" and (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\livekd.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\livek64.exe")

de: Detects the enumeration of a specific DLL or EXE being used by a binary via "tasklist.exe". This is often used by attackers in order to find the specific process identifier (PID) that is using the DLL in question. In order to dump the process memory or perform other nefarious actions.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\tasklist.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "tasklist.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "-m" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/m" or ProcessCommandLine contains "–m" or ProcessCommandLine contains "—m" or ProcessCommandLine contains "―m") and ProcessCommandLine contains "rdpcorets.dll"

t: Local And Domain Account Discovery Via Net.EXE
de: Detects the use of net.exe to enumerate local or domain user accounts. This covers listing all accounts, querying a specific account's details, or enumerating domain users via the /domain flag.
fp: Administrators querying account status as part of routine checks or scripts
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (((FolderPath endswith "\\net.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\net1.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("net.exe", "net1.exe"))) and ProcessCommandLine contains " user ") and (not((ProcessCommandLine contains "/active" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/add" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/delete" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/expires" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/fullname" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/comment" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/homedir" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/passwordreq" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/passwordchg" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/logonpasswordchg" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/times" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/workstations" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/scriptpath")))
pr: #6107 fix: net user rules coverage and deprecate redundant rule

de: Detects execution of "curl.exe" with the "file://" protocol handler in order to read local files.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\curl.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "curl.exe") and ProcessCommandLine contains "file:///"

t: Local Network Connection Initiated By Script Interpreter
de: Detects a script interpreter (Wscript/Cscript) initiating a local network connection to download or execute a script hosted on a shared folder.
q:
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\wscript.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\cscript.exe") and (ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "127.0.0.0/8") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "10.0.0.0/8") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "172.16.0.0/12") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "192.168.0.0/16") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "169.254.0.0/16") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "::1/128") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "fe80::/10") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "fc00::/7"))

t: Logged-On User Password Change Via Ksetup.EXE
de: Detects password change for the logged-on user's via "ksetup.exe"
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\ksetup.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "ksetup.exe") and ProcessCommandLine contains " /ChangePassword "

de: Detects when a user performs data exfiltration by using DataSvcUtil.exe
fp: DataSvcUtil.exe being used may be performed by a system administrator.
Verify whether the user identity, user agent, and/or hostname should be making changes in your environment.
DataSvcUtil.exe being executed from unfamiliar users should be investigated. If known behavior is causing false positives, it can be exempted from the rule.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessCommandLine contains "/in:" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/out:" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/uri:") and (FolderPath endswith "\\DataSvcUtil.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "DataSvcUtil.exe")

t: LOLBIN Or Encoded PowerShell Spawned By Node.js Package Manager
de: Detects a Node.js runtime or JavaScript package manager (node.exe / bun.exe, the executors behind npm, pnpm and yarn) spawning a download/execution LOLBIN or an obfuscated PowerShell command, either directly or through a "cmd /c" lifecycle-script shell. This behaviour is characteristic of install-time "lifecycle hook" (preinstall/postinstall) abuse used in modern npm supply-chain compromises (e.g. Shai-Hulud, the @tanstack "Mini Shai-Hulud" and the axios "plain-crypto-js" campaigns), where a trojanised dependency executes attacker code the moment it is installed on a developer or CI host. Unlike campaign-specific indicator rules, this is a generic behavioural hunt intended to surface the next compromise before its IOCs are published.
fp: Legitimate package "preinstall"/"postinstall" scripts that fetch prebuilt native binaries or invoke the Windows Script Host (some node-gyp / prebuild-install flows). Baseline per project and allowlist known-good packages.
Developer or CI setup tooling that intentionally shells out to PowerShell for provisioning tasks.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\node.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\bun.exe") and (FolderPath endswith "\\bitsadmin.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\certutil.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\cscript.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\mshta.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\regsvr32.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\wscript.exe")) or ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\node.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\bun.exe") and (FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "bitsadmin" or ProcessCommandLine contains "certutil" or ProcessCommandLine contains "DownloadFile" or ProcessCommandLine contains "DownloadString" or ProcessCommandLine contains "FromBase64String" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Invoke-WebRequest" or ProcessCommandLine contains "iwr " or ProcessCommandLine contains "mshta" or ProcessCommandLine contains "regsvr32" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Start-BitsTransfer" or ProcessCommandLine contains " -enc" or ProcessCommandLine contains " -windowstyle hidden" or ProcessCommandLine contains " -w hidden"))
pr: #6130 new: Node.js Package Manager Supply-Chain Execution Hunts (Windows/Linux/macOS)

de: Detect usage of the "runexehelper.exe" binary as a proxy to launch other programs
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\runexehelper.exe"

de: Detect usage of the "unregmp2.exe" binary as a proxy to launch a custom version of "wmpnscfg.exe"
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\unregmp2.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "unregmp2.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " -HideWMP" or ProcessCommandLine contains " /HideWMP" or ProcessCommandLine contains " –HideWMP" or ProcessCommandLine contains " —HideWMP" or ProcessCommandLine contains " ―HideWMP")

t: LSA PPL Protection Setting Modification via CommandLine
au: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
de: Detects modification of LSA PPL protection settings via CommandLine. It may indicate an attempt to disable protection and enable credential dumping tools to access LSASS process memory.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\reg.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("reg.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.dll"))) and ((ProcessCommandLine contains "ControlSet" and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Control\\Lsa") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "Set-ItemProperty" or ProcessCommandLine contains "New-ItemProperty" or ProcessCommandLine contains " add ")) and (ProcessCommandLine contains "IsPplAutoEnabled" or ProcessCommandLine contains "RunAsPPL" or ProcessCommandLine contains "RunAsPPLBoot")

de: Detects additions to the Emond Launch Daemon that adversaries may use to gain persistence and elevate privileges.
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where (FolderPath contains "/etc/emond.d/rules/" and FolderPath endswith ".plist") or FolderPath contains "/private/var/db/emondClients/"

de: Detects execution of AppleScript of the macOS scripting language AppleScript.
fp: Application installers might contain scripts as part of the installation process.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "/osascript" and (ProcessCommandLine contains " -e " or ProcessCommandLine contains ".scpt" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".js")) and (not((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "opencode" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "osascript" and ProcessCommandLine contains " -e " and ProcessCommandLine contains "set imageData to the clipboard" and ProcessCommandLine contains "set fileRef"))))

t: Malicious PE Execution by Microsoft Visual Studio Debugger
de: There is an option for a MS VS Just-In-Time Debugger "vsjitdebugger.exe" to launch specified executable and attach a debugger. This option may be used adversaries to execute malicious code by signed verified binary. The debugger is installed alongside with Microsoft Visual Studio package.
fp: The process spawned by vsjitdebugger.exe is uncommon.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\vsjitdebugger.exe" and (not(((FolderPath contains "\\vsimmersiveactivatehelper" and FolderPath contains ".exe") or FolderPath endswith "\\devenv.exe")))

t: Manual Execution of Script Inside of a Compressed File
de: This is a threat-hunting query to collect information related to the interactive execution of a script from inside a compressed file (zip/rar). Windows will automatically run the script using scripting interpreters such as wscript and cscript binaries. From the query below, the child process is the script interpreter that will execute the script. The script extension is also a set of standard extensions that Windows OS recognizes. Selections 1-3 contain three different execution scenarios. 1. Compressed file opened using 7zip. 2. Compressed file opened using WinRar. 3. Compressed file opened using native windows File Explorer capabilities. When the malicious script is double-clicked, it will be extracted to the respected directories as signified by the CommandLine on each of the three Selections. It will then be executed using the relevant script interpreter."
fp: Batch files may produce a lot of noise, as many applications appear to bundle them as part of their installation process. You should baseline your environment and generate a new query excluding the noisy and expected activity. Some false positives may come up depending on your environment. All results should be investigated thoroughly before filtering out results.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath matches regex ".*\\\\7z.*\\.exe" and ProcessCommandLine matches regex ".*\\\\AppData\\\\local\\\\temp\\\\7z.*\\\\.*") or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\winrar.exe" and ProcessCommandLine matches regex ".*\\\\AppData\\\\local\\\\temp\\\\rar.*\\\\.*") or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\explorer.exe" and (ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\\AppData\\local\\temp.*\.rar\\" or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\\AppData\\local\\temp.*\.zip\\"))) and ((FolderPath endswith "\\cscript.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\mshta.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\wscript.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine endswith ".hta" or ProcessCommandLine endswith ".js" or ProcessCommandLine endswith ".jse" or ProcessCommandLine endswith ".ps1" or ProcessCommandLine endswith ".vbe" or ProcessCommandLine endswith ".vbs" or ProcessCommandLine endswith ".wsf" or ProcessCommandLine endswith ".wsh"))

t: MCP Server Execution Attempt Via NPX Or UVX
de: Detects Node.EXE or UV launching an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server via "npx" or "uvx". MCP servers run with the privileges of the user and often expose local tools, files, or credentials to an AI agent. Attackers can persist or execute untrusted code by adding an "npx -y" or "uvx" MCP server entry to an agent config (Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code). Analysts should verify the package name, source, and parent process. Tune this rule based on whether MCP servers are allowed in your environment. In environments where AI agent tooling is authorized, this detection may reflect normal activity and the alert level should be adjusted accordingly.
fp: Legitimate MCP server startup from approved AI agent configurations (Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code).
Developers installing or testing official MCP packages.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\node.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "node.exe") and ProcessCommandLine contains "npx-cli.js" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "mcp-server" or ProcessCommandLine contains "@modelcontextprotocol/")) or (((FolderPath endswith "\\uvx.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\uv.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("uvx.exe", "uv.exe"))) and (ProcessCommandLine contains "mcp-server" or ProcessCommandLine contains "@modelcontextprotocol/"))
pr: #6304 new: detect MCP servers launched via npx or uvx

t: MFA Bypass Via Windows Hello PIN Or Credential Provider Registry Tampering
de: Detects registry modifications that disable domain PIN sign-in (AllowDomainPINLogon) or disable a Credential Provider, both of which can be used to weaken or bypass multi-factor authentication enforcement on a Windows host.
fp: Administrators deliberately disabling convenience PIN sign-in or a specific credential provider as part of a hardening baseline
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where (RegistryKey endswith "\\Policies\\Microsoft\\Windows\\System\\AllowDomainPINLogon" and RegistryValueData =~ "DWORD (0x00000000)") or (RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Authentication\\Credential Providers.*$" and RegistryKey endswith "\\Disabled" and RegistryValueData =~ "DWORD (0x00000001)")
pr: #6212 new: MFA Bypass via registry tampering and PowerShell requirement tam

t: Microsoft Excel Add-In Loaded From Uncommon Location
de: Detects Microsoft Excel loading an Add-In (.xll) file from an uncommon location
fp: Some tuning might be required to allow or remove certain locations used by the rule if you consider them as safe locations
q:
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\excel.exe" and (FolderPath contains "\\Desktop\\" or FolderPath contains "\\Downloads\\" or FolderPath contains "\\Perflogs\\" or FolderPath contains "\\Temp\\" or FolderPath contains "\\Users\\Public\\" or FolderPath contains "\\Windows\\Tasks\\") and FolderPath endswith ".xll"

de: Detects changes to the registry keys related to "Trusted Location" of Microsoft Office. Attackers might add additional trusted locations to avoid macro security restrictions.

t: New Agent Skills Installation Attempt Via Node - Linux
de: Detects the attempt to install new skills for AI agents using the "npx skills" command on Linux systems. Agent skills enhance AI agents with new capabilities, but attackers may abuse this mechanism to inject malicious commands executed by the agent on behalf of the user. The "npx skills" command can install skills for various agents (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor, and others). Analysts should review any installed skills to verify their legitimacy. Note: Tune this rule based on whether AI agent tooling is allowed in your environment. In environments where such tooling is authorized, this detection may reflect normal activity and the alert level should be adjusted accordingly. In environments where AI agent tooling is not permitted, this activity is likely suspicious and may require immediate investigation.
fp: This rule will be triggered when a new agent skill is installed regardless if it is benign or malicious.
High false positive rate expected in environments where AI agent tooling is authorized and commonly used, such as developer workstations or CI/CD build agents.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "/node" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "npx-cli.js" and ProcessCommandLine contains "skills " and ProcessCommandLine contains " add ")
pr: #6163 New Agent Skills Installation Attempt Via Node - Linux

de: Detects execution of "certmgr" with the "add" flag in order to install a new certificate on the system. Adversaries may install a root certificate on a compromised system to avoid warnings when connecting to adversary controlled web servers.

q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\CertMgr.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "CERTMGT.EXE") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "/add" and ProcessCommandLine contains "root")

t: New Root Certificate Installed Via Certutil.EXE

fp: Help Desk or IT may need to manually add a corporate Root CA on occasion. Need to test if GPO push doesn't trigger FP
q:

| where (FolderPath endswith "\\certutil.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "CertUtil.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "-addstore" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/addstore" or ProcessCommandLine contains "–addstore" or ProcessCommandLine contains "—addstore" or ProcessCommandLine contains "―addstore") and ProcessCommandLine contains "root"

t: New Root or CA or AuthRoot Certificate to Store

t: New Self Extracting Package Created Via IExpress.EXE

t: Node.js Package Manager Spawning Download Or Reverse Shell - Linux
de: Detects a Node.js runtime or JavaScript package manager (node / bun, the executors behind npm, pnpm and yarn) spawning a shell that downloads-and-executes payloads or opens a reverse shell, or invoking a scripting interpreter with a network download cradle. This behaviour is characteristic of install-time "lifecycle hook" (preinstall/postinstall) abuse used in modern npm supply-chain compromises (e.g. Shai-Hulud, the @tanstack "Mini Shai-Hulud" and the axios "plain-crypto-js" campaigns), which increasingly target Linux developer workstations and CI runners. Unlike campaign-specific indicator rules, this is a generic behavioural hunt intended to surface the next compromise before its IOCs are published.
fp: Legitimate "preinstall"/"postinstall" scripts that fetch prebuilt native binaries via curl/wget. Baseline per project and allowlist known-good packages.
Build tooling that invokes Python/Perl/Ruby for setup tasks.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/node" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/bun") and (FolderPath endswith "/bash" or FolderPath endswith "/dash" or FolderPath endswith "/ksh" or FolderPath endswith "/sh" or FolderPath endswith "/zsh") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "base64 -d" or ProcessCommandLine contains "base64 --decode" or ProcessCommandLine contains "chmod +x" or ProcessCommandLine contains "curl " or ProcessCommandLine contains "/dev/tcp/" or ProcessCommandLine contains "nohup " or ProcessCommandLine contains "| bash" or ProcessCommandLine contains "|bash" or ProcessCommandLine contains "| sh" or ProcessCommandLine contains "|sh" or ProcessCommandLine contains "wget ")) or ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/node" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/bun") and (FolderPath endswith "/perl" or FolderPath endswith "/php" or FolderPath endswith "/python" or FolderPath endswith "/python3" or FolderPath endswith "/ruby") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "b64decode" or ProcessCommandLine contains "base64" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/dev/tcp/" or ProcessCommandLine contains "socket" or ProcessCommandLine contains "urllib"))
pr: #6130 new: Node.js Package Manager Supply-Chain Execution Hunts (Windows/Linux/macOS)

t: OneNote Attachment File Dropped In Suspicious Location

| where ((FolderPath contains "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\" or FolderPath contains "\\Users\\Public\\" or FolderPath contains "\\Windows\\Temp\\" or FolderPath contains ":\\Temp\\") and (FolderPath endswith ".one" or FolderPath endswith ".onepkg")) and (not((InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains ":\\Program Files\\Microsoft Office\\" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\ONENOTE.EXE")))

t: OpenAI Codex CLI Approval and Sandbox Bypass Mode
de: Detects execution of the OpenAI Codex CLI with command-line options that bypass approval prompts and sandbox restrictions. The "--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox" option skips confirmation prompts and executes commands without sandboxing. The "--yolo" option is an alias for the same behavior. This mode is intended for environments that provide an external isolation boundary.
fp: Legitimate use in isolated development, testing, or automation environments where approval and sandbox bypass behavior is explicitly intended.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\codex.exe" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox" or ProcessCommandLine contains "--yolo")
pr: #6335 Add OpenAI Codex CLI approval and sandbox bypass detection

t: OpenAI Codex Command Runner Spawned By Unexpected Parent Process
au: Jonathan Johnson, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
de: Detects the OpenAI Codex command runner binary (codex-command-runner-*.exe) being spawned by a process other than codex.exe. The legitimate execution chain is strictly: codex.exe -> codex- command-runner-<version>.exe. Execution via any other parent process may indicate abuse of the command runner binary for sandbox escape, lateral movement, or persistence by an attacker who has obtained access to the Codex installation directory.
fp: Security tooling or EDR agents that wrap process creation may alter the observed parent
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath contains "\\codex-command-runner-" and (not(InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\codex.exe"))
pr: #6030 new: OpenAI Codex sandbox abuse detection rules

t: OpenAI Codex Sandbox Configuration Files Modified By Unexpected Process
au: Jonathan Johnson, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
de: Detects modification of sensitive OpenAI Codex sandbox configuration files under the .codex directory by a process other than the legitimate Codex binaries. The .codex directory contains the sandbox setup marker, encrypted sandbox user credentials (.sandbox- secrets\sandbox_users.json), capability SIDs (cap_sid), and the command runner binary itself. Tampering with these files by an unrelated process may indicate credential harvesting of the DPAPI-encrypted sandbox credentials, persistence via replacement, or attempts to manipulate the capability SID file to weaken workspace isolation. Note: Codex does not remove these artifacts on uninstall, so they may be present on systems where Codex has been previously installed.
fp: Backup software that creates temporary copies of files for backup purposes following similar file directory patterns
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where (FolderPath contains "\\.codex\\" and (FolderPath endswith "\\sandbox_users.json" or FolderPath endswith "\\setup_marker.json" or FolderPath endswith "\\cap_sid" or FolderPath endswith "\\sandbox.log")) and (not(((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\codex.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\codex-command-runner-")))
pr: #6030 new: OpenAI Codex sandbox abuse detection rules

t: Osacompile Execution By Potentially Suspicious Applet/Osascript

q:

| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/applet" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/osascript") and ProcessCommandLine contains "osacompile"

t: Outbound Network Connection To Public IP Via Winlogon
de: Detects a "winlogon.exe" process that initiate network communications with public IP addresses
fp: Communication to other corporate systems that use IP addresses from public address spaces
q:
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\winlogon.exe" and (not((ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "127.0.0.0/8") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "10.0.0.0/8") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "172.16.0.0/12") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "192.168.0.0/16") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "169.254.0.0/16") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "::1/128") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "fe80::/10") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "fc00::/7"))))

de: Detects changes to the registry values related to outlook security settings
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where (RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Office.*$" and RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\Outlook\\Security.*$") and (not(((InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files\\Microsoft Office\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Microsoft Office\\") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\OUTLOOK.EXE")))

t: Password Provided In Command Line Of Net.EXE

de: Detects value modification of registry key containing path to binary used as screensaver.

t: Payload Decoded and Decrypted via Built-in Utilities
de: Detects when a built-in utility is used to decode and decrypt a payload after a macOS disk image (DMG) is executed. Malware authors may attempt to evade detection and trick users into executing malicious code by encoding and encrypting their payload and placing it in a disk image file. This behavior is consistent with adware or malware families such as Bundlore and Shlayer.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "/openssl" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "/Volumes/" and ProcessCommandLine contains "enc" and ProcessCommandLine contains "-base64" and ProcessCommandLine contains " -d ")

t: PDQ Deploy Remote Adminstartion Tool Execution
de: Detect use of PDQ Deploy remote admin tool
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessVersionInfoFileDescription =~ "PDQ Deploy Console" or ProcessVersionInfoProductName =~ "PDQ Deploy" or ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName =~ "PDQ.com" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "PDQDeployConsole.exe"

t: Periodic Backup For System Registry Hives Enabled
de: Detects the enabling of the "EnablePeriodicBackup" registry value. Once enabled, The OS will backup System registry hives on restarts to the "C:\Windows\System32\config\RegBack" folder. Windows creates a "RegIdleBackup" task to manage subsequent backups. Registry backup was a default behavior on Windows and was disabled as of "Windows 10, version 1803".
fp: Legitimate need for RegBack feature by administrators.
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where RegistryKey endswith "\\Control\\Session Manager\\Configuration Manager\\EnablePeriodicBackup" and RegistryValueData =~ "DWORD (0x00000001)"

de: Detects execution of perl using the "-e"/"-E" flags. This is could be used as a way to launch a reverse shell or execute live perl code.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\perl.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "perl.exe") and ProcessCommandLine contains " -e"

au: Teymur Kheirkhabarov (idea), Mangatas Tondang, oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
de: Detects the usage of the "Accesschk" utility, an access and privilege audit tool developed by SysInternal and often being abused by attacker to verify process privileges
q:

| where (ProcessVersionInfoProductName endswith "AccessChk" or ProcessVersionInfoFileDescription contains "Reports effective permissions" or (FolderPath endswith "\\accesschk.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\accesschk64.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\accesschk64a.exe") or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "accesschk.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "uwcqv " or ProcessCommandLine contains "kwsu " or ProcessCommandLine contains "qwsu " or ProcessCommandLine contains "uwdqs ")

de: Detects usage of findstr with the "EVERYONE" or "BUILTIN" keywords. This was seen being used in combination with "icacls" and other utilities to spot misconfigured files or folders permissions.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (((FolderPath endswith "\\find.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\findstr.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("FIND.EXE", "FINDSTR.EXE"))) and (ProcessCommandLine contains "\"Everyone\"" or ProcessCommandLine contains "'Everyone'" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\"BUILTIN\\\"" or ProcessCommandLine contains "'BUILTIN\\'")) or (ProcessCommandLine contains "icacls " and ProcessCommandLine contains "findstr " and ProcessCommandLine contains "Everyone")

t: Persistence Via Disk Cleanup Handler - Autorun
de: Detects when an attacker modifies values of the Disk Cleanup Handler in the registry to achieve persistence via autorun. The disk cleanup manager is part of the operating system. It displays the dialog box […] The user has the option of enabling or disabling individual handlers by selecting or clearing their check box in the disk cleanup manager's UI. Although Windows comes with a number of disk cleanup handlers, they aren't designed to handle files produced by other applications. Instead, the disk cleanup manager is designed to be flexible and extensible by enabling any developer to implement and register their own disk cleanup handler. Any developer can extend the available disk cleanup services by implementing and registering a disk cleanup handler.
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents

de: Detects modification addition to the 'TypedPaths' key in the user or admin registry via the commandline. Which might indicate persistence attempt

de: Detects command line patterns associated with the use of Pnscan for sending and receiving binary data across the network. | where RegistryKey endswith "\\DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS"

de: Detects the execution of Dnx.EXE. The Dnx utility allows for the execution of C# code. Attackers might abuse this in order to bypass application whitelisting.

t: Potential Arbitrary Command Execution Via Git Config Override
de: Detects execution of "git.exe" with an inline configuration override ("-c") that points a code- execution configuration directive (such as "core.sshCommand", "core.fsmonitor", "core.pager", "core.editor" or "diff.external") at a command interpreter, as well as the use of the "ext::" transport. Git executes the value of several configuration directives as external programs. This allows a threat actor to abuse the trusted "git.exe" binary as a proxy to run arbitrary commands and evade detection (indirect command execution). Note that the closely related abuse where the payload is stored inside a repository's ".git/config" file (e.g. "core.fsmonitor") and triggered when an editor or IDE automatically runs "git status" is not observable on the "git.exe" command line and is therefore out of scope for this command-line based rule.
fp: Rare legitimate use of a git configuration directive that points to a scripting interpreter (e.g. a custom pager or editor wrapper). Baseline before enabling.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\git.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "git.exe") and (((ProcessCommandLine contains "core.sshCommand=" or ProcessCommandLine contains "core.fsmonitor=" or ProcessCommandLine contains "core.pager=" or ProcessCommandLine contains "core.editor=" or ProcessCommandLine contains "sequence.editor=" or ProcessCommandLine contains "diff.external=") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "cmd " or ProcessCommandLine contains "cmd.exe" or ProcessCommandLine contains "cmd /" or ProcessCommandLine contains "powershell" or ProcessCommandLine contains "pwsh" or ProcessCommandLine contains "mshta" or ProcessCommandLine contains "rundll32" or ProcessCommandLine contains "regsvr32" or ProcessCommandLine contains "wscript" or ProcessCommandLine contains "cscript" or ProcessCommandLine contains "bitsadmin" or ProcessCommandLine contains "certutil" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".bat" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".cmd" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".ps1" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".vbs" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".hta")) or ProcessCommandLine contains "ext::")
pr: #6103 Add rule: arbitrary command execution via git config override

q:
