t: Potential Arbitrary File Download Via Cmdl32.EXE
de: Detects execution of Cmdl32 with the "/vpn" and "/lan" flags. Attackers can abuse this utility in order to download arbitrary files via a configuration file. Inspect the location and the content of the file passed as an argument in order to determine if it is suspicious.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\cmdl32.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "CMDL32.EXE") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "/vpn" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/lan")

t: Potential Autonomous AI Agent NPM Install
de: Detects an npm install command whose arguments name a package in the OpenClaw agent family or its copycat ecosystem. The npm-cli.js invocation is observed as a child of the user shell with a CommandLine that contains both 'npm-cli.js install' and one of the package names. Catches the install moment, before the workspace is materialized, so it pairs with the working-directory and file-event sister rules for layered coverage.
fp: Sanctioned developer install of any of these packages. Apply a per-host or per-user allowlist filter.
Unrelated package whose name contains a substring collision. Tighten the package list to exact-token matches if seen in practice.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessCommandLine contains "npm-cli.js" and ProcessCommandLine contains " install " and (ProcessCommandLine contains "openclaw" or ProcessCommandLine contains "moltbot" or ProcessCommandLine contains "moltbook" or ProcessCommandLine contains "clawdbot" or ProcessCommandLine contains "clawbot" or ProcessCommandLine contains "nanobot" or ProcessCommandLine contains "nanoclaw" or ProcessCommandLine contains "picoclaw" or ProcessCommandLine contains "zeroclaw" or ProcessCommandLine contains "moltis" or ProcessCommandLine contains "agentzero")
pr: #6017 new: OpenClaw AI agent family detection rules

t: Potential Autonomous AI Agent Workspace File Creation
de: Detects FileCreate events under the dot-folder used by the OpenClaw agent family and its copycat ecosystem. Catches initial workspace bootstrap, credential and session state writes, and ongoing tool I/O. Sister rule to proc_creation_win_openclaw_agent_workdir.yml. Fires even when the writing process is not itself running with its CurrentDirectory under the folder, for example a setup script that absolute-paths into the workspace.
fp: Sanctioned developer or operator use of these agents. Apply a per-host or per-user allowlist filter.

Apple Hermes JavaScript engine bytecode cache (Meta React Native, present in Slack, Discord, Messenger, Electron apps). The .hermes folder is intentionally NOT covered by this rule to avoid that false positive.
Backup or sync software touching the user profile that happens to traverse one of these folders.
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where FolderPath contains "\\.openclaw\\" or FolderPath contains "\\.moltbot\\" or FolderPath contains "\\.moltbook\\" or FolderPath contains "\\.clawdbot\\" or FolderPath contains "\\.clawd\\" or FolderPath contains "\\.clawbot\\" or FolderPath contains "\\.nanobot\\" or FolderPath contains "\\.nanoclaw\\" or FolderPath contains "\\.picoclaw\\" or FolderPath contains "\\.zeroclaw\\" or FolderPath contains "\\.moltis\\" or FolderPath contains "\\.agentzero\\"
pr: #6017 new: OpenClaw AI agent family detection rules

t: Potential BigDiskBuster-Like Buster-File Creation in TEMP
de: Detects the creation of GUID-braced files in user TEMP directories. This corresponds to the buster-file stage of the BigDiskBuster technique, where hidden files sized to all free disk space are created to cause Windows Defender platform and signature updates to fail due to disk exhaustion.

Developer test suites creating GUID-named temporary fixtures

DeviceFileEvents
| where FolderPath matches regex "\\\\AppData\\\\Local\\\\Temp\\\\\\{[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{12}\\}$" and (not((InitiatingProcessFolderPath in~ ("C:\\Windows\\System32\\taskhost.exe", "C:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\taskhost.exe")))) and (not(((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\TeamViewer\\tv_x64.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\TeamViewer\\tv_w32.exe") or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\.vscode\\extensions\\" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\cpptools.exe") or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Users\\" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\target.exe"))))

t: Potential Browser Cache Smuggling Payload Extraction
de: Detects a process reading, searching, or extracting content directly out of a web browser's on- disk cache directory (Chromium "Cache_Data", Firefox "cache2\entries", or the legacy/WebView2/Outlook "INetCache"). In the "cache smuggling" / "Living off the Browser" technique, a phishing page (commonly a ClickFix or FileFix lure) serves an executable payload disguised with an "image/jpeg" Content-Type so the browser silently caches it with no download prompt and no Mark-of-the-Web. The victim is then social-engineered into pasting a benign- looking command that carves the payload out of the cache file (often between two marker strings via regex), writes it to a writable/executable location, and runs it. Because no second network request is made, network/proxy controls and download/MotW-based detections are evaded. This rule targets the local extraction step rather than the (invisible) delivery step.
fp: Browser cache maintenance, backup, or DLP/AV tools that read cache contents. Tune via the Image / ParentImage of approved tooling.
Forensic or IR tooling (e.g. cache parsers) run by analysts. Filter on known investigator hosts/accounts.
Developers debugging browser cache behavior with PowerShell.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Cache_Data" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\cache2\\entries" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Windows\\INetCache") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "Get-ChildItem" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Get-Content" or ProcessCommandLine contains "[IO.File]::ReadAllBytes" or ProcessCommandLine contains "[System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes" or ProcessCommandLine contains "ReadAllText" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Select-String" or ProcessCommandLine contains "findstr" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-match" or ProcessCommandLine contains "[regex]" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".Matches(" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Copy-Item" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Move-Item" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Expand-Archive" or ProcessCommandLine contains "FromBase64String" or ProcessCommandLine contains "certutil" or ProcessCommandLine contains "tar " or ProcessCommandLine contains "expand ")) and (not((FolderPath endswith "\\ccleaner.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\ccleaner64.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\bleachbit.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\bleachbit_console.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\cleanmgr.exe")))

t: Potential Container Escape Via Docker Socket Or Host Namespace Access
de: Detects the start of a container that shares the host PID namespace, mounts the Docker socket or the host root filesystem, or is granted the SYS_ADMIN capability. Each of these options removes a part of the isolation between the container and the host and is a well-known path to escape from a container to the host. An attacker with access to the Docker CLI or API can use these options to gain root privileges on the host. Some monitoring agents, reverse proxies and container management tools legitimately require these options. It is recommended to baseline those and filter them by image name.
fp: Monitoring agents, reverse proxies and container management tools that require access to the Docker socket
Administrators debugging the host from a container
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "/docker" or FolderPath endswith "/nerdctl" or FolderPath endswith "/podman") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " create " or ProcessCommandLine contains " run ") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "--cap-add SYS_ADMIN" or ProcessCommandLine contains "--cap-add=SYS_ADMIN" or ProcessCommandLine contains "--pid host" or ProcessCommandLine contains "--pid=host" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-v /:/" or ProcessCommandLine contains "--volume /:/" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/var/run/docker.sock:" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/run/docker.sock:")

de: Detects potential exploitation attempt of CVE-2022-22954, a remote code execution vulnerability in VMware Workspace ONE Access and Identity Manager. As reported by Morphisec, part of the attack chain, threat actors used PowerShell commands that executed as a child processes of the legitimate Tomcat "prunsrv.exe" process application.
fp: Some false positives are possible as part of a custom script implementation from admins executed with cmd.exe as the child process.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\prunsrv.exe" and (FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or (FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/c powershell"))

t: Potential CVE-2023-36874 Exploitation - Uncommon Report.Wer Location
de: Detects the creation of a "Report.wer" file in an uncommon folder structure. This could be a sign of potential exploitation of CVE-2023-36874.
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where (FolderPath contains ":\\ProgramData\\Microsoft\\Windows\\WER\\ReportArchive\\" and FolderPath endswith "\\Report.wer") and (not((FolderPath contains "\\ReportArchive\\AppCrash_" or FolderPath contains "\\ReportArchive\\AppHang_" or FolderPath contains "\\ReportArchive\\Critical_" or FolderPath contains "\\ReportArchive\\Kernel_" or FolderPath contains "\\ReportArchive\\NonCritical_")))

de: Detects a specific file being created in the recent folder of Office. These files have been seen being dropped during potential exploitations of CVE-2023-36884
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where FolderPath startswith "C:\\Users\\" and FolderPath contains "\\AppData\\Roaming\\Microsoft\\Office\\Recent\\" and FolderPath endswith "\\file001.url"

t: Potential CVE-2024-3400 Exploitation - Palo Alto GlobalProtect OS Command Injection - File Creation
de: Detects suspicious file creations in the Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS' parent telemetry folder, which are processed by the vulnerable 'dt_curl' script if device telemetry is enabled. As said script overrides the shell-subprocess restriction, arbitrary command execution may occur by carefully crafting filenames that are escaped through this function.
fp: The PAN-OS device telemetry function does not enforce a standard filename convention, but observations are unlikely.
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where (FolderPath contains "{IFS}" or FolderPath contains "base64" or FolderPath contains "bash" or FolderPath contains "curl" or FolderPath contains "http") and FolderPath startswith "/opt/panlogs/tmp/device_telemetry/"

de: Detects the execution of the "curl" process with "upload" flags. Which might indicate potential data exfiltration
fp: Scripts created by developers and admins
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\curl.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoProductName =~ "The curl executable") and ((ProcessCommandLine contains " --form" or ProcessCommandLine contains " --upload-file " or ProcessCommandLine contains " --data " or ProcessCommandLine contains " --data-") or ProcessCommandLine matches regex "\\s-[FTd]\\s")) and (not((ProcessCommandLine contains "://localhost" or ProcessCommandLine contains "://127.0.0.1")))

de: Detects child processes spawned by DbgSrv.exe, a Microsoft debugging process server that can be abused to execute arbitrary processes through a trusted developer utility.
fp: Legitimate use of DbgSrv.exe to create processes during debugging sessions
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\dbgsrv.exe"
pr: #6285 Add DbgSrv.exe child process detection

t: Potential Defense Evasion Via Binary Rename
au: Matthew Green @mgreen27, Ecco, James Pemberton @4A616D6573, oscd.community, Andreas Hunkeler (@Karneades)
de: Detects the execution of a renamed binary often used by attackers or malware leveraging new Sysmon OriginalFileName datapoint.
fp: Custom applications use renamed binaries adding slight change to binary name. Typically this is easy to spot and add to whitelist
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("Cmd.Exe", "CONHOST.EXE", "7z.exe", "7za.exe", "7zr.exe", "WinRAR.exe", "wevtutil.exe", "net.exe", "net1.exe", "netsh.exe", "InstallUtil.exe")) and (not((FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\conhost.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\7z.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\7za.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\7zr.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\WinRAR.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\wevtutil.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\net.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\net1.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\netsh.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\InstallUtil.exe")))

t: Potential Discovery Activity Using Find - Linux
de: Detects usage of "find" binary in a suspicious manner to perform discovery
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "/find" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "-perm -4000" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-perm -2000" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-perm 0777" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-perm -222" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-perm -o w" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-perm -o x" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-perm -u=s" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-perm -g=s")

de: Detects usage of "find" binary in a suspicious manner to perform discovery
q:

| where FolderPath endswith "/find" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "-perm -4000" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-perm -2000" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-perm 0777" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-perm -222" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-perm -o w" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-perm -o x" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-perm -u=s" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-perm -g=s")

de: Detects an attempt to leverage dnscmd.exe to enumerate the DNS zones of a domain. DNS zones used to host the DNS records for a particular domain.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\dnscmd.exe" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "/enumrecords" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/enumzones" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/ZonePrint" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/info")

t: Potential DLL Execution Via OpenSSH PKCS11Provider
de: Detects the use of the OpenSSH PKCS11Provider option with SSH or SCP. This option can be abused to load a DLL from a local path or remote SMB share into a trusted OpenSSH process.
fp: Legitimate use of smart cards, hardware security modules, or other PKCS#11 providers with OpenSSH
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\ssh.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\scp.exe") and ProcessCommandLine contains "PKCS11Provider="
pr: #6308 Add OpenSSH PKCS11Provider DLL load detection

t: Potential DLL File Download Via PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest
de: Detects potential DLL files being downloaded using the PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest or Invoke- RestMethod cmdlets.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessCommandLine contains "Invoke-RestMethod " or ProcessCommandLine contains "Invoke-WebRequest " or ProcessCommandLine contains "IRM " or ProcessCommandLine contains "IWR ") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "http" and ProcessCommandLine contains "OutFile" and ProcessCommandLine contains ".dll")

t: Potential DLL Injection Or Execution Using Tracker.exe
de: Detects potential DLL injection and execution using "Tracker.exe"
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\tracker.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoFileDescription =~ "Tracker") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " /d " or ProcessCommandLine contains " /c ")) and (not((ProcessCommandLine contains " /ERRORREPORT:PROMPT " or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\Msbuild\\Current\\Bin\\MSBuild.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\Msbuild\\Current\\Bin\\amd64\\MSBuild.exe"))))

de: Detects the execution "AccCheckConsole" a command-line tool for verifying the accessibility implementation of an application's UI. One of the tests that this checker can run are called "verification routine", which tests for things like Consistency, Navigation, etc. The tool allows a user to provide a DLL that can contain a custom "verification routine". An attacker can build such DLLs and pass it via the CLI, which would then be loaded in the context of the "AccCheckConsole" utility.
fp: Legitimate use of the UI Accessibility Checker
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\AccCheckConsole.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "AccCheckConsole.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " -hwnd" or ProcessCommandLine contains " -process " or ProcessCommandLine contains " -window ")

t: Potential DLL Sideloading Activity Via ExtExport.EXE
de: Detects the execution of "Extexport.exe".A utility that is part of the Internet Explorer browser and is used to export and import various settings and data, particularly when switching between Internet Explorer and other web browsers like Firefox. It allows users to transfer bookmarks, browsing history, and other preferences from Internet Explorer to Firefox or vice versa. It can be abused as a tool to side load any DLL. If a folder is provided in the command line it'll load any DLL with one of the following names "mozcrt19.dll", "mozsqlite3.dll", or "sqlite.dll". Arbitrary DLLs can also be loaded if a specific number of flags was provided.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\Extexport.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "extexport.exe"

au: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Wietze Beukema (project and research)
de: Detects DLL sideloading of "dbgcore.dll"
fp: Legitimate applications loading their own versions of the DLL mentioned in this rule
q:
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\dbgcore.dll" and (not((FolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\SoftwareDistribution\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\System32\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\SystemTemp\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\WinSxS\\"))) and (not((FolderPath endswith "\\Steam\\bin\\cef\\cef.win7x64\\dbgcore.dll" or (FolderPath contains "opera\\Opera Installer Temp\\opera_package" and FolderPath endswith "\\assistant\\dbgcore.dll"))))

au: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Wietze Beukema (project and research)
de: Detects potential DLL sideloading of "dbghelp.dll"
fp: Legitimate applications loading their own versions of the DLL mentioned in this rule
q:

| where FolderPath endswith "\\dbghelp.dll" and (not((FolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\SoftwareDistribution\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\System32\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\SystemTemp\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\WinSxS\\"))) and (not(((FolderPath endswith "\\Anaconda3\\Lib\\site-packages\\vtrace\\platforms\\windll\\amd64\\dbghelp.dll" or FolderPath endswith "\\Anaconda3\\Lib\\site-packages\\vtrace\\platforms\\windll\\i386\\dbghelp.dll") or (FolderPath endswith "\\Epic Games\\Launcher\\Engine\\Binaries\\ThirdParty\\DbgHelp\\dbghelp.dll" or FolderPath endswith "\\Epic Games\\MagicLegends\\x86\\dbghelp.dll") or (FolderPath contains "opera\\Opera Installer Temp\\opera_package" and FolderPath endswith "\\assistant\\dbghelp.dll"))))

de: Detects potential DLL sideloading of "DbgModel.dll"
fp: Legitimate applications loading their own versions of the DLL mentioned in this rule

t: Potential DLL Sideloading Of Libcurl.DLL Via GUP.EXE
de: Detects potential DLL sideloading of "libcurl.dll" by the "gup.exe" process from an uncommon location
q:

| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\gup.exe" and FolderPath endswith "\\libcurl.dll") and (not(InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\Notepad++\\updater\\GUP.exe"))

fp: Legitimate applications loading their own versions of the DLL mentioned in this rule.
q:

de: Detects potential DLL sideloading of "mscorsvc.dll".
fp: Legitimate applications loading their own versions of the DLL mentioned in this rule.
q:

| where FolderPath endswith "\\mscorsvc.dll" and (not((FolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\Microsoft.NET\\Framework\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\Microsoft.NET\\Framework64\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\Microsoft.NET\\FrameworkArm\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\Microsoft.NET\\FrameworkArm64\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\WinSxS\\")))

de: Detects potential DLL sideloading of SPPC.dll by identifying instances where the DLL is loaded from a directory other than the legitimate Windows system directories.
fp: Legitimate software that may load SPPC.dll from non-standard locations, baselining and further investigation required.
q:
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\sppc.dll" and (not((FolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\System32\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\WinSxS\\")))
pr: #5891 new: renamed system binaries execution for dll hijacking attack

de: Detect usage of the "coregen.exe" (Microsoft CoreCLR Native Image Generator) binary to sideload arbitrary DLLs.
q:
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\coregen.exe" and (not((FolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Microsoft Silverlight\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files\\Microsoft Silverlight\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\System32\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\")))

de: Detects "AccCheckConsole.exe" (UI Accessibility Checker, a signed Microsoft binary) loading a DLL from a user-writable / non-system location. The utility accepts a user-supplied DLL containing a custom verification routine, which is then loaded into the trusted process context. Adversaries abuse this to proxy execution of an attacker-controlled DLL and bypass application whitelisting.
fp: Legitimate use of the UI Accessibility Checker with verification routine DLLs stored in user directories
q:
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\AccCheckConsole.exe" and FolderPath endswith ".dll") and (not((FolderPath contains "C:\\Windows\\System32\\" or FolderPath contains "C:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\" or FolderPath contains "C:\\Windows\\WinSxS\\" or FolderPath contains "C:\\Windows\\Microsoft.NET\\" or FolderPath contains "C:\\Program Files\\" or FolderPath contains "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\")))
pr: #6094 Add Sysinternals tooling and driver/UAC detection rules

de: Detects potential DLL sideloading using ClassicExplorer32.dll from the Classic Shell software
q:
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\ClassicExplorer32.dll" and (not(FolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files\\Classic Shell\\"))

de: Detects the use of the PhoneDeepLink parameter to potentially sideload a DLL file that does not exist. This non-existent DLL file is named "ShellChromeAPI.dll". Adversaries can drop their own renamed DLL and execute it via DeviceEnroller.exe using this parameter
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\deviceenroller.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "deviceenroller.exe") and ProcessCommandLine contains "/PhoneDeepLink"

de: Detects potential DLL sideloading using JUSTSYSTEMS Japanese word processor
q:
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\JSESPR.dll" and (not(FolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files\\Common Files\\Justsystem\\JsSchHlp\\"))

de: Detects possible payload obfuscation via the commandline
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessCommandLine contains "^^" or ProcessCommandLine contains "^|^" or ProcessCommandLine contains ",;," or ProcessCommandLine contains ";;;;" or ProcessCommandLine contains ";; ;;" or ProcessCommandLine contains "(,(," or ProcessCommandLine contains "%COMSPEC:~" or ProcessCommandLine contains " c^m^d" or ProcessCommandLine contains "^c^m^d" or ProcessCommandLine contains " c^md" or ProcessCommandLine contains " cm^d" or ProcessCommandLine contains "^cm^d" or ProcessCommandLine contains " s^et " or ProcessCommandLine contains " s^e^t " or ProcessCommandLine contains " se^t "

t: Potential Download/Upload Activity Using Type Command
de: Detects usage of the "type" command to download/upload data from WebDAV server
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessCommandLine contains "type " and ProcessCommandLine contains " > \\\\") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "type \\\\" and ProcessCommandLine contains " > ")

t: Potential Dropper Script Execution Via WScript/CScript/MSHTA
au: Margaritis Dimitrios (idea), Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Dave Johnson
de: Detects wscript/cscript/mshta executions of scripts located in user directories
fp: Some installers might generate a similar behavior. An initial baseline is required
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\wscript.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\cscript.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\mshta.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Perflogs\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Temp\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Tmp\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Users\\Public\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Windows\\Temp\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\AppData\\Roaming\\Temp\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Start Menu\\Programs\\Startup\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Temporary Internet" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Windows\\Temp" or ProcessCommandLine contains "%LocalAppData%\\Temp\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "%TEMP%" or ProcessCommandLine contains "%TMP%") and (ProcessCommandLine contains ".hta" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".js" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".jse" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".vba" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".vbe" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".vbs" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".wsf" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".wsh")

t: Potential Encrypted Registry Blob Related To SNAKE Malware
de: Detects the creation of a registry value in the ".wav\OpenWithProgIds" key with an uncommon name. This could be related to SNAKE Malware as reported by CISA
fp: Some additional tuning might be required to tune out legitimate processes that write to this key by default
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\SOFTWARE\\Classes\\\.wav\\OpenWithProgIds.*$" and (not((RegistryKey endswith ".AssocFile.WAV" or RegistryKey contains ".wav.")))

t: Potential Execution Or Persistence Via Systemd-Run
de: Detects potentially suspicious execution of the "systemd-run" utility. Attackers can abuse "systemd-run" to launch commands, scripts or reverse shells as a transient service, scope or timer. This allows the payload to run under a trusted system process, detach from the current session, evade process-tree based monitoring and establish persistence via transient timers.
fp: Legitimate administrators or automation tools using "systemd-run" to launch scheduled or transient services and scripts.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "/systemd-run" and ((ProcessCommandLine contains "--on-active" or ProcessCommandLine contains "--on-boot" or ProcessCommandLine contains "--on-calendar" or ProcessCommandLine contains "--on-startup" or ProcessCommandLine contains "--on-unit-active" or ProcessCommandLine contains "--on-unit-inactive" or ProcessCommandLine contains "--timer-property") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "/dev/shm/" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/tmp/" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/var/tmp/" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/bin/bash" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/bin/sh" or ProcessCommandLine contains "bash -c" or ProcessCommandLine contains "sh -c" or ProcessCommandLine contains "--remain-after-exit"))
pr: #6434 Add Linux rule: Potential Execution Or Persistence Via Systemd-Run

t: Potential Fake Instance Of Hxtsr.EXE Executed
de: HxTsr.exe is a Microsoft compressed executable file called Microsoft Outlook Communications. HxTsr.exe is part of Outlook apps, because it resides in a hidden "WindowsApps" subfolder of "C:\Program Files". Any instances of hxtsr.exe not in this folder may be malware camouflaging itself as HxTsr.exe
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\hxtsr.exe" and (not((FolderPath contains ":\\program files\\windowsapps\\microsoft.windowscommunicationsapps_" and FolderPath endswith "\\hxtsr.exe")))

t: Potential File Download Via MS-AppInstaller Protocol Handler
au: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel
de: Detects usage of the "ms-appinstaller" protocol handler via command line to potentially download arbitrary files via AppInstaller.EXE The downloaded files are temporarly stored in ":\Users\%use rname%\AppData\Local\Packages\Microsoft.DesktopAppInstaller_8wekyb3d8bbwe\AC\INetCache\<RANDOM- 8-CHAR-DIRECTORY>"
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessCommandLine contains "ms-appinstaller://" and ProcessCommandLine contains "source=") and ProcessCommandLine contains "http"

t: Potential Fileless Execution Via Windows Sandbox CLI Inline LogonCommand
de: Detects use of wsb.exe (Windows Sandbox CLI, available on Windows 11 24H2 and later) to launch a sandbox from an inline XML configuration that contains an embedded <LogonCommand>.
fp: Developers or QA pipelines that spawn ad-hoc sandboxes from inline XML configurations for build verification
Power users who script Sandbox usage to avoid maintaining .wsb files
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\wsb.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "wsb.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "--config" and ProcessCommandLine contains "<LogonCommand>")
pr: #6168 add sigma rules for Windows Sandbox

de: Detects potential DLL sideloading of "goopdate.dll", a DLL used by googleupdate.exe
fp: False positives are expected from Google Chrome installations running from user locations (AppData) and other custom locations. Apply additional filters accordingly.
Other third party chromium browsers located in AppData
q:
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\goopdate.dll" and (not((FolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files\\"))) and (not((((InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\GUM" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains ".tmp\\Dropbox") and (FolderPath contains "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\GUM" and FolderPath contains ".tmp\\goopdate.dll")) or ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\GUM" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains ":\\Windows\\SystemTemp\\GUM") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith ".tmp\\GoogleUpdate.exe" and (FolderPath contains "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\GUM" or FolderPath contains ":\\Windows\\SystemTemp\\GUM")))))

t: Potential Hidden Directory Creation Via NTFS INDEX_ALLOCATION Stream
de: Detects the creation of hidden file/folder with the "::$index_allocation" stream. Which can be used as a technique to prevent access to folder and files from tooling such as "explorer.exe" and "powershell.exe"
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where FolderPath contains "::$index_allocation"

t: Potential Hidden Directory Creation Via NTFS INDEX_ALLOCATION Stream - CLI
de: Detects command line containing reference to the "::$index_allocation" stream, which can be used as a technique to prevent access to folders or files from tooling such as "explorer.exe" or "powershell.exe"
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessCommandLine contains "::$index_allocation"

t: Potential Hidden Executable Run From Shared
de: Detects the execution of a hidden file (name starting with a dot) located in the /Users/Shared directory. Masquerading an executable as a dot-file in a shared location is a technique observed in the BlueNoroff macOS intrusion set (TA444) and reduces its visibility in a casual listing.
fp: Legitimate scripts or installers that hide files in /Users/Shared
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath matches regex "^/Users/Shared/\\.[a-zA-Z0-9._-]{1,255}$"
pr: #5700 macOS process create detections related to Bluenoroff macOS intrusion

t: Potential Homoglyph Attack Using Lookalike Characters
de: Detects the presence of unicode characters which are homoglyphs, or identical in appearance, to ASCII letter characters. This is used as an obfuscation and masquerading techniques. Only "perfect" homoglyphs are included; these are characters that are indistinguishable from ASCII characters and thus may make excellent candidates for homoglyph attack characters.
fp: Commandlines with legitimate Cyrillic text; will likely require tuning (or not be usable) in countries where these alphabets are in use.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessCommandLine contains "А" or ProcessCommandLine contains "В" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Е" or ProcessCommandLine contains "К" or ProcessCommandLine contains "М" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Н" or ProcessCommandLine contains "О" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Р" or ProcessCommandLine contains "С" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Т" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Х" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Ѕ" or ProcessCommandLine contains "І" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Ј" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Ү" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Ӏ" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Ԍ" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Ԛ" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Ԝ" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Α" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Β" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Ε" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Ζ" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Η" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Ι" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Κ" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Μ" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Ν" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Ο" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Ρ" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Τ" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Υ" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Χ") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "а" or ProcessCommandLine contains "е" or ProcessCommandLine contains "о" or ProcessCommandLine contains "р" or ProcessCommandLine contains "с" or ProcessCommandLine contains "х" or ProcessCommandLine contains "ѕ" or ProcessCommandLine contains "і" or ProcessCommandLine contains "ӏ" or ProcessCommandLine contains "ј" or ProcessCommandLine contains "һ" or ProcessCommandLine contains "ԁ" or ProcessCommandLine contains "ԛ" or ProcessCommandLine contains "ԝ" or ProcessCommandLine contains "ο")

t: Potential Homoglyph Attack Using Lookalike Characters in Filename
de: Detects the presence of unicode characters which are homoglyphs, or identical in appearance, to ASCII letter characters. This is used as an obfuscation and masquerading techniques. Only "perfect" homoglyphs are included; these are characters that are indistinguishable from ASCII characters and thus may make excellent candidates for homoglyph attack characters.
fp: File names with legitimate Cyrillic text. Will likely require tuning (or not be usable) in countries where these alphabets are in use.

t: Potential In-Memory Download And Compile Of Payloads
de: Detects potential in-memory downloading and compiling of applets using curl and osacompile as seen used by XCSSET malware
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessCommandLine contains "osacompile" and ProcessCommandLine contains "curl"

t: Potential Indirect Command Execution Via XBootMgr.EXE
de: Detects execution of "xbootmgr.exe" (Windows Performance Toolkit boot/trace tool) with the "-callBack" or "-preTraceCmd" arguments, which cause it to launch an arbitrary executable before or after a performance trace completes. This can be abused as a way to execute a payload through a legitimate, signed Microsoft binary.
fp: Legitimate performance-trace automation scripts that use the "-callBack" or "-preTraceCmd" parameters
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\xbootmgr.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "xbootmgr.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "-callBack" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-preTraceCmd")
pr: #6264 New Rule: Potential Indirect Command Execution Via XBootMgr.EXE

t: Potential Ingress Tool Transfer Via ECMangen.EXE
de: Detects execution of "ECMangen.exe" with a remote URL on the command line. ECMangen.exe is a utility that ships with the Windows SDK and with Microsoft Exchange Server. It does not take a URL as part of its normal usage. When given a URL, it downloads the remote content and stores it in the INetCache folder, which attackers can abuse to transfer tools onto a host.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\ECMangen.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "ECMangen.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "http://" or ProcessCommandLine contains "https://")
pr: #6538 New Rule: Potential Ingress Tool Transfer Via ECMangen.EXE

t: Potential Initial Access via DLL Search Order Hijacking
de: Detects attempts to create a DLL file to a known desktop application dependencies folder such as Slack, Teams or OneDrive and by an unusual process. This may indicate an attempt to load a malicious module via DLL search order hijacking.
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\winword.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\excel.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\powerpnt.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\MSACCESS.EXE" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\MSPUB.EXE" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\fltldr.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\certutil.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\mshta.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\cscript.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\wscript.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\curl.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe") and FolderPath endswith ".dll" and (FolderPath contains "\\Users\\" and FolderPath contains "\\AppData\\") and (FolderPath contains "\\Microsoft\\OneDrive\\" or FolderPath contains "\\Microsoft OneDrive\\" or FolderPath contains "\\Microsoft\\Teams\\" or FolderPath contains "\\Local\\slack\\app-" or FolderPath contains "\\Local\\Programs\\Microsoft VS Code\\")) and (not((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" and (FolderPath contains "\\Users\\" and FolderPath contains "\\AppData\\" and FolderPath contains "\\Microsoft\\OneDrive\\" and FolderPath contains "\\api-ms-win-core-"))))

t: Potential KamiKakaBot Activity - Lure Document Execution
de: Detects the execution of a Word document via the WinWord Start Menu shortcut. This behavior was observed being used by KamiKakaBot samples in order to initiate the 2nd stage of the infection.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "/c " and ProcessCommandLine contains ".lnk ~" and ProcessCommandLine contains "Start Menu\\Programs\\Word") and ProcessCommandLine endswith ".doc"

t: Potential KamiKakaBot Activity - Shutdown Schedule Task Creation
de: Detects the creation of a schedule task that runs weekly and execute the "shutdown /l /f" command. This behavior was observed being used by KamiKakaBot samples in order to achieve persistence on a system.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\schtasks.exe" and (ProcessCommandLine contains " /create " and ProcessCommandLine contains "shutdown /l /f" and ProcessCommandLine contains "WEEKLY")) and (not((AccountName contains "AUTHORI" or AccountName contains "AUTORI")))

t: Potential Launch Agent/Daemon Masquerading As Apple
de: Detects the creation of a launch agent or launch daemon property list named after Apple ("com.apple.*") outside of "/System/Library". macOS ships its own launch agents and daemons in "/System/Library", so a "com.apple.*" plist written to "/Library/LaunchAgents", "/Library/LaunchDaemons" or a user's "~/Library/LaunchAgents" is likely a program hiding behind Apple's name to persist. EvilQuest installed "com.apple.questd.plist" in both "/Library/LaunchDaemons" and "~/Library/LaunchAgents", and CookieMiner installed "com.apple.rig2.plist" in "~/Library/LaunchAgents".
fp: Apple software installed outside of macOS that ships its own launch agents or daemons
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where ((FolderPath contains "/Library/LaunchAgents/com.apple." or FolderPath contains "/Library/LaunchDaemons/com.apple.") and FolderPath endswith ".plist") and (not((FolderPath in~ ("/Library/LaunchDaemons/com.apple.installer.cleanupinstaller.plist") or FolderPath startswith "/System/Library/")))
pr: #6456 new: Potential Launch Agent/Daemon Masquerading As Apple

de: Detects potential DLL sideloading of "libvlc.dll", a DLL that is legitimately used by "VLC.exe"
fp: False positives are expected if VLC is installed in non-default locations
q:
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\libvlc.dll" and (not((FolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\VideoLAN\\VLC\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files\\VideoLAN\\VLC\\")))

t: Potential Linux Amazon SSM Agent Hijacking
de: Detects potential Amazon SSM agent hijack attempts as outlined in the Mitiga research report.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "/amazon-ssm-agent" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "-register " and ProcessCommandLine contains "-code " and ProcessCommandLine contains "-id " and ProcessCommandLine contains "-region ")

t: Potential Linux Process Code Injection Via DD Utility
de: Detects the injection of code by overwriting the memory map of a Linux process using the "dd" Linux command.
q:

| where FolderPath endswith "/dd" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "of=" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/proc/" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/mem")

t: Potential Local Credential Testing Via Dscl Authonly
de: Detects execution of the macOS "dscl" (Directory Service command line) utility with the "-authonly" flag, which validates local user credentials without creating a full authenticated session. Repeated or unexpected use of this flag can indicate credential validation/brute-force attempts against local accounts, outside of normal administrative activity.
fp: Legitimate administrative credential checks or password-reset tooling using dscl
Automated MDM/config-management scripts validating local account credentials
IT helpdesk scripts run as root during account troubleshooting
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "/dscl" and ProcessCommandLine contains "-authonly") and (not(AccountName =~ "root"))
pr: #6317 new: Potential Local Credential Testing via dscl -authonly

t: Potential Malicious Extension Loading via Chromium Flag on Linux
de: Detects the use of the '--load-extension' Chromium flag on any process on Linux. This parameter exists in all Chromium-based applications including browsers (Chrome, Edge, Brave, etc.), Electron apps (Discord, Slack, VS Code, Teams, etc.), and CEF framework applications. Adversaries may abuse this feature to load malicious extensions for persistence, credential theft, cookie stealing, or browser session hijacking.
fp: Automated testing frameworks such as Selenium, Cypress, or Playwright
Electron app development using remote debugging or custom extensions
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessCommandLine contains "--load-extension="
pr: #5949 new: Chromium --load-extension Detection for Linux and macOS

t: Potential Malicious Extension Loading via Chromium Flag on macOS
de: Detects the use of the '--load-extension' Chromium flag on any process on macOS. This parameter exists in all Chromium-based applications including browsers (Chrome, Edge, Brave, etc.), Electron apps (Discord, Slack, VS Code, Teams, etc.), and CEF framework applications. Threat actors abuse this to load malicious extensions for cookie theft, session hijacking, or persistence.
fp: Automated testing frameworks such as Selenium, Cypress, or Playwright
Electron app development using remote debugging or custom extensions
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessCommandLine contains "--load-extension="
pr: #5949 new: Chromium --load-extension Detection for Linux and macOS

t: Potential Memory Dumping Activity Via LiveKD
de: Detects execution of LiveKD based on PE metadata or image name
fp: Administration and debugging activity (must be investigated)
q:

| where (FolderPath endswith "\\livekd.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\livekd64.exe") or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "livekd.exe"

de: Detects potential DLL sideloading of "mfdetours.dll". While using "mftrace.exe" it can be abused to attach to an arbitrary process and force load any DLL named "mfdetours.dll" from the current directory of execution.
q:

| where FolderPath endswith "\\mfdetours.dll" and (not(FolderPath contains ":\\Program Files (x86)\\Windows Kits\\10\\bin\\"))

de: Detects child processes of the "Trace log generation tool for Media Foundation Tools" (Mftrace.exe) which can abused to execute arbitrary binaries.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\mftrace.exe"

t: Potential MOVEit Transfer CVE-2023-34362 Exploitation - Dynamic Compilation Via Csc.EXE
de: Detects the execution of "csc.exe" via "w3wp.exe" process. MOVEit affected hosts execute "csc.exe" via the "w3wp.exe" process to dynamically compile malicious DLL files. MOVEit is affected by a critical vulnerability. Exploited hosts show evidence of dynamically compiling a DLL and writing it under C:\\Windows\\Microsoft\.NET\\Framework64\\v4\.0\.30319\\Temporary ASP\.NET Files\\root\\([a-z0-9]{5,12})\\([a-z0-9]{5,12})\\App_Web_[a-z0-9]{5,12}\.dll. Hunting Opportunity Events from IIS dynamically compiling binaries via the csc.exe on behalf of the MOVEit application, especially since May 27th should be investigated.
fp: Initial software installation and software updates.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\w3wp.exe" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "moveitdmz pool" and FolderPath endswith "\\csc.exe"

t: Potential Network Sniffing Activity Using Network Tools
au: Timur Zinniatullin, oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
de: Detects potential network sniffing via use of network tools such as "tshark", "windump". Network sniffing refers to using the network interface on a system to monitor or capture information sent over a wired or wireless connection. An adversary may place a network interface into promiscuous mode to passively access data in transit over the network, or use span ports to capture a larger amount of data.
fp: Legitimate administration activity to troubleshoot network issues
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\tshark.exe" and ProcessCommandLine contains "-i") or FolderPath endswith "\\windump.exe"

t: Potential NtLoadDriver Syscall Abuse to Load Suspicious Kernel Driver Service
de: Detects a service Type registry value being set to 1 (kernel driver) by potentially suspicious non-legitimate processes. Calls the undocumented NtLoadDriver syscall, this bypasses SCM, meaning Event ID 7045 will not trigger. Threat actors can abuse this to load a malicious or vulnerable kernel driver in order to disable security products, achieve persistence, or perform arbitrary kernel operations.
fp: Third-party driver installers writing service keys directly via registry API
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where ((RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Services.*$" or (RegistryKey contains "\\SYSTEM\\ControlSet" and RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\Services.*$")) and (RegistryKey endswith "\\Type" and RegistryValueData =~ "DWORD (0x00000001)")) and (not((InitiatingProcessFolderPath =~ "SYSTEM" or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\Installer\\" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith ".tmp") or ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\system32\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\WinSxS\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\uus\\") and (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\drvinst.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\loginui.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\loginw32.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\msiexec.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\ntoskrnl.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\poqexec.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\services.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\silsvc.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\TiWorker.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\waasmedicagent.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\wininit.exe")) or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\ProgramData\\")))) and (not(((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\procexp.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\procexp64.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\procexp64a.exe") and RegistryKey contains "\\Services\\PROCEXP")))
pr: #6255 new: BTR Reforged Exploit

t: Potential Obfuscated Ordinal Call Via Rundll32
au: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
de: Detects execution of "rundll32" with potential obfuscated ordinal calls
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "RUNDLL32.EXE" or ProcessCommandLine contains "rundll32") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "#+" or ProcessCommandLine contains "#-" or ProcessCommandLine contains "#0" or ProcessCommandLine contains "#655" or ProcessCommandLine contains "#656")

t: Potential PaperCut NG/MF Tapestry Page Webshell Plant
de: Detects file write events targeting Tapestry page files (.page, .html) within the PaperCut NG/MF webapp directory tree on Windows. Attackers exploiting CVE-2026-81578 and CVE-2026-82078 gain unauthenticated file-write access to the PaperCut webapp via the Tapestry ConfigEditor component. Planting arbitrary Tapestry pages in WEB-INF or the webapp root enables embedding OGNL expressions that execute server-side on the next HTTP request, resulting in OS command execution as the PaperCut service account. Affected: PaperCut NG/MF <= 25.0.11 build 75758. Fixed in 25.0.12 build 76510.
fp: PaperCut upgrade or installation that legitimately writes Tapestry page files into the webapp directory
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where (FolderPath contains "\\PaperCut MF\\" or FolderPath contains "\\PaperCut NG\\" or FolderPath contains "\\papercut\\") and (FolderPath contains "\\WEB-INF\\" or FolderPath contains "\\server\\tmp\\webapp-") and (FolderPath endswith ".page" or FolderPath endswith ".html")
pr: #6444 new: papercut exploitation rules for CVE-2026-81578 and CVE-2026-82078

fp: PaperCut upgrade or installation that legitimately writes Tapestry page files into the webapp directory

pr: #6444 new: papercut exploitation rules for CVE-2026-81578 and CVE-2026-82078

de: Detects possible password spraying attempts using Dsacls

q:

| where (FolderPath endswith "\\dsacls.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "DSACLS.EXE") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "/user:" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/passwd:")

t: Potential PavinLoader MSBuild Execution from User-Writable Path via cmd.exe
de: Detects MSBuild.exe running from a user-writable directory (for example %LOCALAPPDATA% or %TEMP%) with cmd.exe as the parent process. Observed in the PavinLoader incident: a fake .NET solution ("CatalogIngestor" / "Ingestion Labs") ships a bundled MSBuild.exe (255,904 bytes, 4.8.9032.0, Authenticode HashMismatch) that build.cmd invokes from %LOCALAPPDATA% after setting MSBUILDENABLEALLPROPERTYFUNCTIONS=1. In-memory assembly loading follows via Internal.targets property functions.
fp: Developer workstations or CI agents that intentionally run portable MSBuild copies from user-writable directories
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" and FolderPath endswith "\\MSBuild.exe" and (FolderPath contains "\\AppData\\Local\\" or FolderPath contains "\\AppData\\Roaming\\" or FolderPath contains "\\Users\\Public\\" or FolderPath contains "\\ProgramData\\")
pr: #6540 Sigma: PavinLoader fake-driver MSI campaign (MSBuild from %LOCALAPPDATA%, MSBUILDENABLEALLPROPERTYFUNCTIONS, fake dllhost/taskhostw tasks, m

de: Detect changes to the "PendingFileRenameOperations" registry key from uncommon or suspicious images locations to stage currently used files for rename or deletion after reboot.
fp: Installers and updaters may set currently in use files for rename or deletion after a reboot.
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where RegistryKey contains "\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\Session Manager\\PendingFileRenameOperations" and (InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\Users\\Public\\" or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\reg.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\regedit.exe"))

de: Detects creation of a file named "ErrorHandler.cmd" in the "C:\WINDOWS\Setup\Scripts\" directory which could be used as a method of persistence The content of C:\WINDOWS\Setup\Scripts\ErrorHandler.cmd is read whenever some tools under C:\WINDOWS\System32\oobe\ (e.g. Setup.exe) fail to run for any reason.
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\WINDOWS\\Setup\\Scripts\\ErrorHandler.cmd"

de: Detects the modification of an existing service in order to execute an arbitrary payload when the service is started or killed as a potential method for persistence.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((ProcessCommandLine contains "sc " and ProcessCommandLine contains "config " and ProcessCommandLine contains "binpath=") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "sc " and ProcessCommandLine contains "failure" and ProcessCommandLine contains "command=")) or (((ProcessCommandLine contains "reg " and ProcessCommandLine contains "add " and ProcessCommandLine contains "FailureCommand") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "reg " and ProcessCommandLine contains "add " and ProcessCommandLine contains "ImagePath")) and (ProcessCommandLine contains ".sh" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".exe" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".dll" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".bin$" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".bat" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".cmd" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".js" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".msh$" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".reg$" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".scr" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".ps" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".vb" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".jar" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".pl"))

t: Potential Persistence Attempt Via Run Keys Using Reg.EXE
au: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
de: Detects suspicious command line reg.exe tool adding key to RUN key in Registry
fp: Legitimate software automatically (mostly, during installation) sets up autorun keys for legitimate reasons.
Legitimate administrator sets up autorun keys for legitimate reasons.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\reg.exe" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "reg" and ProcessCommandLine contains " add ") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Software\\WOW6432Node\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Policies\\Explorer\\Run")

de: Detects potential persistence using Appx DebugPath
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where (RegistryKey contains "Classes\\ActivatableClasses\\Package\\Microsoft." and RegistryKey endswith "\\DebugPath") or (RegistryKey contains "\\Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\PackagedAppXDebug\\Microsoft." and RegistryKey endswith "\\(Default)")

t: Potential Persistence Via AppCompat RegisterAppRestart Layer
de: Detects the setting of the REGISTERAPPRESTART compatibility layer on an application. This compatibility layer allows an application to register for restart using the "RegisterApplicationRestart" API. This can be potentially abused as a persistence mechanism.
fp: Legitimate applications making use of this feature for compatibility reasons
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows NT\\CurrentVersion\\AppCompatFlags\\Layers.*$" and RegistryValueData contains "REGISTERAPPRESTART"

t: Potential Persistence Via Custom Protocol Handler
de: Detects potential persistence activity via the registering of a new custom protocole handlers. While legitimate applications register protocole handlers often times during installation. And attacker can abuse this by setting a custom handler to be used as a persistence mechanism.
fp: Many legitimate applications can register a new custom protocol handler. Additional filters needs to applied according to your environment.
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where (RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)^HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\\CLASSES.*$" and RegistryValueData startswith "URL:") and (not((RegistryValueData startswith "URL:ms-" or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files (x86)" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\System32\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\"))))

t: Potential Persistence Via Disk Cleanup Handler - Registry
de: Detects when an attacker modifies values of the Disk Cleanup Handler in the registry to achieve persistence. The disk cleanup manager is part of the operating system. It displays the dialog box […] The user has the option of enabling or disabling individual handlers by selecting or clearing their check box in the disk cleanup manager's UI. Although Windows comes with a number of disk cleanup handlers, they aren't designed to handle files produced by other applications. Instead, the disk cleanup manager is designed to be flexible and extensible by enabling any developer to implement and register their own disk cleanup handler. Any developer can extend the available disk cleanup services by implementing and registering a disk cleanup handler.
fp: Legitimate new entry added by windows
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where (ActionType =~ "RegistryKeyCreated" and RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Explorer\\VolumeCaches.*$") and (not((RegistryKey endswith "\\Active Setup Temp Folders" or RegistryKey endswith "\\BranchCache" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Content Indexer Cleaner" or RegistryKey endswith "\\D3D Shader Cache" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Delivery Optimization Files" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Device Driver Packages" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Diagnostic Data Viewer database files" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Downloaded Program Files" or RegistryKey endswith "\\DownloadsFolder" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Feedback Hub Archive log files" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Internet Cache Files" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Language Pack" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Microsoft Office Temp Files" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Offline Pages Files" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Old ChkDsk Files" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Previous Installations" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Recycle Bin" or RegistryKey endswith "\\RetailDemo Offline Content" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Setup Log Files" or RegistryKey endswith "\\System error memory dump files" or RegistryKey endswith "\\System error minidump files" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Temporary Files" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Temporary Setup Files" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Temporary Sync Files" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Thumbnail Cache" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Update Cleanup" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Upgrade Discarded Files" or RegistryKey endswith "\\User file versions" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Windows Defender" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Windows Error Reporting Files" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Windows ESD installation files" or RegistryKey endswith "\\Windows Upgrade Log Files")))

t: Potential Persistence Via Event Viewer Events.asp
de: Detects potential registry persistence technique using the Event Viewer "Events.asp" technique
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where (RegistryKey contains "\\Microsoft\\Windows NT\\CurrentVersion\\Event Viewer\\MicrosoftRedirectionProgram" or RegistryKey contains "\\Microsoft\\Windows NT\\CurrentVersion\\Event Viewer\\MicrosoftRedirectionURL") and (not(((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "C:\\WINDOWS\\system32\\svchost.exe" and RegistryKey endswith "\\Microsoft\\Windows NT\\CurrentVersion\\Event Viewer\\MicrosoftRedirectionProgram" and RegistryValueData =~ "%%SystemRoot%%\\PCHealth\\HelpCtr\\Binaries\\HelpCtr.exe") or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "C:\\WINDOWS\\system32\\svchost.exe" and RegistryKey endswith "\\Microsoft\\Windows NT\\CurrentVersion\\Event Viewer\\MicrosoftRedirectionProgramCommandLineParameters" and RegistryValueData matches regex "-url hcp://services/centers/support.topic=%%s") or RegistryValueData =~ "http://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/events.asp" or RegistryValueData =~ "(Empty)")))

t: Potential Persistence Via Logon Scripts - Registry

t: Potential Persistence Via Netsh Helper DLL
de: Detects the execution of netsh with "add helper" flag in order to add a custom helper DLL. This technique can be abused to add a malicious helper DLL that can be used as a persistence proxy that gets called when netsh.exe is executed.

| where (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "netsh.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\netsh.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "add" and ProcessCommandLine contains "helper")

t: Potential Persistence Via Netsh Helper DLL
de: Detects the execution of netsh with "add helper" flag in order to add a custom helper DLL. This technique can be abused to add a malicious helper DLL that can be used as a persistence proxy that gets called when netsh.exe is executed.

t: Potential Persistence Via New AMSI Providers - Registry
de: Detects when an attacker adds a new AMSI provider via the Windows Registry to bypass AMSI (Antimalware Scan Interface) protections. Attackers may add custom AMSI providers to persist on the system and evade detection by security software that relies on AMSI for scanning scripts and other content. This technique is often used in conjunction with fileless malware and script- based attacks to maintain persistence while avoiding detection.
fp: Legitimate security products adding their own AMSI providers. Filter these according to your environment.
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where (RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\AMSI\\Providers.*$" or RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\SOFTWARE\\WOW6432Node\\Microsoft\\AMSI\\Providers.*$") and (not((((InitiatingProcessFolderPath in~ ("C:\\Program Files\\Avast Software\\Avast\\RegSvr.exe", "C:\\Program Files\\Avast Software\\Avast\\x86\\RegSvr.exe")) and RegistryKey contains "\\{FB904E4E-D2C7-4C8D-8492-B620BB9896B1}") or ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath in~ ("C:\\Program Files\\AVG\\Antivirus\\RegSvr.exe", "C:\\Program Files\\AVG\\Antivirus\\x86\\RegSvr.exe")) and RegistryKey contains "\\{FB904E4E-D2C7-4C8D-8492-B620BB9896B1}") or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath =~ "C:\\Program Files\\Avira\\Endpoint Protection SDK\\endpointprotection.exe" and RegistryKey contains "\\{00000001-3DCC-4B48-A82E-E2071FE58E05}"))))

t: Potential Pikabot Infection - Suspicious Command Combinations Via Cmd.EXE
de: Detects the execution of concatenated commands via "cmd.exe". Pikabot often executes a combination of multiple commands via the command handler "cmd /c" in order to download and execute additional payloads. Commands such as "curl", "wget" in order to download extra payloads. "ping" and "timeout" are abused to introduce delays in the command execution and "Rundll32" is also used to execute malicious DLL files. In the observed Pikabot infections, a combination of the commands described above are used to orchestrate the download and execution of malicious DLL files.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessCommandLine contains "cmd" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/c") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " & " or ProcessCommandLine contains " || ") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " curl" or ProcessCommandLine contains " wget" or ProcessCommandLine contains " timeout " or ProcessCommandLine contains " ping ") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " rundll32" or ProcessCommandLine contains " mkdir ")

t: Potential PyArmor Obfuscated PyInstaller Payload Extraction
de: Detects the PyArmor runtime extension being written into a PyInstaller one-file extraction directory. PyInstaller unpacks to a _MEI prefixed folder at runtime, and the presence of pyarmor_runtime inside that folder means the bundled Python bytecode was deliberately obfuscated before packaging. The combination is common in commodity Python malware and rare in software an enterprise buys or builds.
fp: Commercial or internal Python applications distributed as PyInstaller bundles with PyArmor licence protection applied. This is the main expected source of noise and is most likely on developer and engineering estates.
Security or automation tooling packaged by a third party using the same build chain.
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where FolderPath contains "\\_MEI" and FolderPath contains "pyarmor_runtime"

de: Detects regsvr32 invocations where the "/i" (DllInstall) flag is used without "/n" (skip DllRegisterServer/DllUnregisterServer). Legitimate use of "/i" is normally paired with "/n" since DllInstall is meant as an alternative to the standard registration path. When "/n" is absent, regsvr32 both registers the DLL and runs DllInstall, which is an unusual combination outside of abuse scenarios.
fp: Administrator typo might cause some false positives
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\regsvr32.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "REGSVR32.EXE") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " -i" or ProcessCommandLine contains " /i" or ProcessCommandLine contains " –i" or ProcessCommandLine contains " —i" or ProcessCommandLine contains " ―i")) and (not(ProcessCommandLine contains " -n " or ProcessCommandLine contains " /n " or ProcessCommandLine contains " –n " or ProcessCommandLine contains " —n " or ProcessCommandLine contains " ―n "))
