| where (FolderPath endswith "\\setspn.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "setspn.exe" or (ProcessVersionInfoFileDescription contains "Query or reset the computer" and ProcessVersionInfoFileDescription contains "SPN attribute")) and (ProcessCommandLine contains " -q " or ProcessCommandLine contains " /q ")

de: Detects potential suspicious behaviour using secedit.exe. Such as exporting or modifying the security policy
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\secedit.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "SeCEdit") and ((ProcessCommandLine contains "/export" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/cfg") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "/configure" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/db"))

t: Potential Suspicious Browser Extension Force Install via Policy on Linux
de: Detects the creation or modification of browser policy JSON files on Linux that can force- install extensions. The ExtensionInstallForcelist and ExtensionSettings policies silently install extensions that users cannot disable or remove. Adversaries may abuse these to persist malicious browser extensions without user interaction.
fp: Enterprise IT administrators deploying browser extensions via policy files
Package managers installing browser policy packages
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where (FolderPath contains "/etc/opt/chrome/policies/managed/" or FolderPath contains "/etc/opt/chrome/policies/recommended/") or (FolderPath contains "/etc/chromium/policies/managed/" or FolderPath contains "/etc/chromium/policies/recommended/") or FolderPath contains "/etc/opt/edge/policies/managed/"
pr: #5957 new: Browser Extension Force Install via Policy Detection (Windows, macOS, Linux)

t: Potential Suspicious Browser Extension Force Install via Policy on Windows
de: Detects the creation of browser extension force-install policy entries in the Windows registry. The ExtensionInstallForcelist policy silently installs extensions that users cannot disable or remove. ExtensionSettings allows configuring force-installed extensions with auto-granted permissions. Adversaries may abuse these to persist malicious browser extensions across reboots without user interaction.
fp: Enterprise IT administrators deploying browser extensions via Group Policy
MDM tools managing browser extensions in corporate environments
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where (RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\Policies\\Google\\Chrome\\ExtensionInstallForcelist.*$" or RegistryKey contains "\\Policies\\Google\\Chrome\\ExtensionSettings") or (RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\Policies\\Microsoft\\Edge\\ExtensionInstallForcelist.*$" or RegistryKey contains "\\Policies\\Microsoft\\Edge\\ExtensionSettings") or (RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\Policies\\Chromium\\ExtensionInstallForcelist.*$" or RegistryKey contains "\\Policies\\Chromium\\ExtensionSettings")
pr: #5957 new: Browser Extension Force Install via Policy Detection (Windows, macOS, Linux)

t: Potential Suspicious Browser Extension Force Install via Policy Plist on macOS
de: Detects the creation of browser policy plist files on macOS that can force-install extensions. The ExtensionInstallForcelist policy silently installs extensions that users cannot disable or remove. Adversaries may abuse these to persist malicious browser extensions across reboots without user interaction.
fp: Enterprise IT administrators deploying browser extensions via policy plist
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "/Library/Preferences/com.google.Chrome.plist" or FolderPath endswith "/Library/Preferences/com.microsoft.Edge.plist"
pr: #5957 new: Browser Extension Force Install via Policy Detection (Windows, macOS, Linux)

t: Potential Suspicious Browser External Extension File Creation on Linux
de: Detects the creation of External Extensions JSON files in browser-specific directories on Linux. External extensions can be installed from external update URLs or local CRX files without user interaction. Supported by Chrome, Chromium, and Edge. Adversaries may abuse this to silently install malicious browser extensions.
fp: Legitimate software installers registering browser extensions
Package managers installing browser extension packages
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where FolderPath contains "/usr/share/google-chrome/extensions/" or FolderPath contains "/.config/google-chrome/External Extensions/" or FolderPath contains "/usr/share/chromium/extensions/" or FolderPath contains "/.config/chromium/External Extensions/" or FolderPath contains "/usr/share/microsoft-edge/extensions/" or FolderPath contains "/.config/microsoft-edge/External Extensions/"
pr: #5958 new: Browser External Extensions Silent Install Detection (Windows, macOS, Linux)

t: Potential Suspicious Browser External Extension File Creation on macOS
de: Detects the creation of External Extensions JSON files in browser-specific directories on macOS. External extensions can be installed from external update URLs without user interaction. Supported by Chrome, Chromium, and Edge. Adversaries may abuse this to silently install malicious browser extensions.
fp: Legitimate software installers registering browser extensions
Enterprise IT administrators deploying browser extensions via External Extensions
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where FolderPath contains "/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/External Extensions/" or FolderPath contains "/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/External Extensions/" or FolderPath contains "/Library/Application Support/Chromium/External Extensions/" or FolderPath contains "/Library/Application Support/Microsoft/Edge/External Extensions/" or FolderPath contains "/Library/Application Support/Microsoft Edge/External Extensions/"
pr: #5958 new: Browser External Extensions Silent Install Detection (Windows, macOS, Linux)

t: Potential Suspicious Browser External Extension Registration on Windows
de: Detects the creation of registry entries used to register external browser extensions on Windows. External extensions can be installed from external update URLs without user interaction by writing to the Extensions registry key with an update_url value. Adversaries may abuse this to silently install malicious browser extensions across reboots.
fp: Legitimate software installers registering browser extensions (password managers, screen readers, etc.)
Enterprise IT administrators deploying browser extensions
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where (RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\Software\\Google\\Chrome\\Extensions.*$" and RegistryKey endswith "\\update_url") or (RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\Software\\Microsoft\\Edge\\Extensions.*$" and RegistryKey endswith "\\update_url")
pr: #5958 new: Browser External Extensions Silent Install Detection (Windows, macOS, Linux)

t: Potential Suspicious Browser Launch From Document Reader Process
de: Detects when a browser process or browser tab is launched from an application that handles document files such as Adobe, Microsoft Office, etc. And connects to a web application over http(s), this could indicate a possible phishing attempt.
fp: Unlikely in most cases, further investigation should be done in the commandline of the browser process to determine the context of the URL accessed.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "Acrobat Reader" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "Microsoft Office" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "PDF Reader") and (FolderPath endswith "\\brave.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\chrome.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\firefox.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\msedge.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\opera.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\maxthon.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\seamonkey.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\vivaldi.exe") and ProcessCommandLine contains "http") and (not(ProcessCommandLine contains "https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/")) and (not(((ProcessCommandLine contains "http://ad.foxitsoftware.com/adlog.php") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "https://globe-map.foxitservice.com/go.php" and ProcessCommandLine contains "do=redirect"))))

t: Potential Suspicious Browser Native Messaging Host File Creation on Linux
de: Detects the creation of native messaging host manifest files in browser-specific directories on Linux. Native messaging allows browser extensions to communicate with local binaries via stdin/stdout, which can be abused to execute arbitrary commands and escape the browser sandbox.
fp: Legitimate browser extensions installing native messaging hosts (password managers, screen readers, etc.)
Package managers (apt, yum, dnf) installing browser extension packages
Browser updates that register new native messaging hosts
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where FolderPath contains "/etc/opt/chrome/native-messaging-hosts/" or FolderPath contains "/.config/google-chrome/NativeMessagingHosts/" or FolderPath contains "/etc/chromium/native-messaging-hosts/" or FolderPath contains "/.config/chromium/NativeMessagingHosts/" or FolderPath contains "/etc/opt/edge/native-messaging-hosts/" or FolderPath contains "/.config/microsoft-edge/NativeMessagingHosts/" or (FolderPath contains "/usr/lib/mozilla/native-messaging-hosts/" or FolderPath contains "/usr/lib64/mozilla/native-messaging-hosts/") or FolderPath contains "/.mozilla/native-messaging-hosts/"
pr: #5956 new: Native Messaging Host Registration Detection for Windows, macOS and Linux

t: Potential Suspicious Browser Native Messaging Host File Creation on macOS
de: Detects the creation of native messaging host manifest files in browser-specific directories on macOS. Native messaging allows browser extensions to communicate with local binaries via stdin/stdout, which can be abused to execute arbitrary commands and escape the browser sandbox.
fp: Legitimate browser extensions installing native messaging hosts (password managers, screen readers, etc.)
Enterprise MDM tools deploying browser extensions
Browser updates that register new native messaging hosts
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where FolderPath contains "/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/NativeMessagingHosts/" or FolderPath contains "/Library/Application Support/Microsoft Edge/NativeMessagingHosts/" or FolderPath contains "/Library/Application Support/Mozilla/NativeMessagingHosts/"
pr: #5956 new: Native Messaging Host Registration Detection for Windows, macOS and Linux

t: Potential Suspicious Browser Native Messaging Host Registration
de: Detects the creation of a native messaging host registration via the Windows registry. Native messaging allows browser extensions to communicate with local binaries via stdin/stdout, which can be abused to execute arbitrary commands and escape the browser sandbox. Adversaries such as ChromeAlone (DEF CON 33) register native messaging hosts to achieve shell execution from a malicious extension.
fp: Legitimate browser extensions installing native messaging hosts (password managers, screen readers, etc.)
Enterprise software deployment tools installing browser extensions
Browser updates that register new native messaging hosts
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\NativeMessagingHosts.*$"
pr: #5956 new: Native Messaging Host Registration Detection for Windows, macOS and Linux

t: Potential Suspicious Change To Sensitive/Critical Files
de: Detects changes of sensitive and critical files. Monitors files that you don't expect to change without planning on Linux system. These files include, but are not limited to, system configuration files, authentication files, and critical application files. Attackers often target these files to maintain persistence, escalate privileges, or disrupt system operations.
fp: Some false positives are to be expected on user or administrator machines. Apply additional filters as needed.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (((FolderPath endswith "/cat" or FolderPath endswith "/echo" or FolderPath endswith "/grep" or FolderPath endswith "/head" or FolderPath endswith "/more" or FolderPath endswith "/tail") and ProcessCommandLine contains ">") or (FolderPath endswith "/emacs" or FolderPath endswith "/nano" or FolderPath endswith "/sed" or FolderPath endswith "/vi" or FolderPath endswith "/vim")) and (ProcessCommandLine contains "/bin/login" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/bin/passwd" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/boot/" or (ProcessCommandLine contains "/etc/" and ProcessCommandLine contains ".conf") or ProcessCommandLine contains "/etc/cron." or ProcessCommandLine contains "/etc/crontab" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/etc/hosts" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/etc/init.d" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/etc/sudoers" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/opt/bin/" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/sbin" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/usr/bin/" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/usr/local/bin/") and (not((FolderPath endswith "/bin/sed" and (ProcessCommandLine startswith "sed -i /^" or ProcessCommandLine startswith "sed -ne s/^") and ProcessCommandLine endswith "/etc/mdadm/mdadm.conf")))

t: Potential Suspicious PowerShell Module File Created
de: Detects the creation of a new PowerShell module in the first folder of the module directory structure "\WindowsPowerShell\Modules\malware\malware.psm1". This is somewhat an uncommon practice as legitimate modules often includes a version folder.
fp: False positive rate will vary depending on the environments. Additional filters might be required to make this logic usable in production.
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where (FolderPath contains "\\WindowsPowerShell\\Modules\\" and FolderPath contains "\\.ps") or (FolderPath contains "\\WindowsPowerShell\\Modules\\" and FolderPath contains "\\.dll")

t: Potential Suspicious Registry File Imported Via Reg.EXE
de: Detects the import of '.reg' files from suspicious paths using the 'reg.exe' utility
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\reg.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "reg.exe") and ProcessCommandLine contains " import " and (ProcessCommandLine contains "C:\\Users\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "%temp%" or ProcessCommandLine contains "%tmp%" or ProcessCommandLine contains "%appdata%" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "C:\\Windows\\Temp\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "C:\\ProgramData\\")

t: Potential Suspicious Windows Feature Enabled - ProcCreation
de: Detects usage of the built-in PowerShell cmdlet "Enable-WindowsOptionalFeature" used as a Deployment Image Servicing and Management tool. Similar to DISM.exe, this cmdlet is used to enumerate, install, uninstall, configure, and update features and packages in Windows images
fp: Legitimate usage of the features listed in the rule.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessCommandLine contains "Enable-WindowsOptionalFeature" and ProcessCommandLine contains "-Online" and ProcessCommandLine contains "-FeatureName") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "TelnetServer" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Internet-Explorer-Optional-amd64" or ProcessCommandLine contains "TFTP" or ProcessCommandLine contains "SMB1Protocol" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Client-ProjFS" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Microsoft-Windows-Subsystem-Linux")

t: Potential Tampering of Service Privileges in Registry
de: Detects potentially suspicious modifications to the Windows Registry that add suspicious privileges to services, potentially indicating preparation for EDR bypass or kernel driver loading. These elevated privileges enable loading kernel drivers, which can bypass or disable Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) tools on the compromised system. If privileges like 'SeLoadDriverPrivilege' or 'SeDebugPrivilege' are added to a service, it may indicate malicious intent to escalate privileges or evade security measures.
fp: Legitimate service configuration changes by administrators or authorized software.
Some binaries may be used by installers or system management tools, therefore, use baselining to reduce false positives before pushing to production.
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\reg.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\wscript.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\cscript.exe") and RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Services.*$" and RegistryKey endswith "\\RequiredPrivileges" and RegistryValueData =~ "Binary Data"
pr: #5643 feat: susp service priv esc and phantom hijack rules

de: A General detection for sdclt being spawned as an elevated process. This could be an indicator of sdclt being used for bypass UAC techniques.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "sdclt.exe" and (ProcessIntegrityLevel in~ ("High", "S-1-16-12288"))

de: A General detection for sdclt being spawned as an elevated process. This could be an indicator of sdclt being used for bypass UAC techniques.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "sdclt.exe" and (ProcessIntegrityLevel in~ ("High", "S-1-16-12288"))
pr: #6279 🩺 add regression data from evtx-attack-samples

t: Potential Unquoted Service Path Reconnaissance Via Wmic.EXE
de: Detects known WMI recon method to look for unquoted service paths using wmic. Often used by pentester and attacker enumeration scripts
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "wmic.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\WMIC.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " service get " and ProcessCommandLine contains "name,displayname,pathname,startmode")

t: Potential Use of BrowserCore.exe for PRT Extraction
de: Detects suspicious execution of BrowserCore.exe potentially used to extract Primary Refresh Tokens (PRTs) for Azure AD SSO abuse. Legitimate executions are typically spawned by a browser (like Chrome or Edge) via cmd.exe using named pipes for inter-process communication. An attacker can execute BrowserCore.exe directly to request a Primary Refresh Token (PRT) cookie as part of an Azure AD SSO abuse attack.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\BrowserCore.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "BrowserCore.exe") and ProcessCommandLine contains "chrome-extension://ppnbnpeolgkicgegkbkbjmhlideopiji/") and (not((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "\\.\\pipe\\")))
pr: #5676 add detection rule for suspicious use of BrowserCore.exe in PRT extra…

t: Potential Veeam PostgreSQL Credential Table Query Via Psql.EXE
de: Detects the PostgreSQL psql client executing a SELECT query against the credentials table in the VeeamBackup database. Similar credential access was documented in an Akira ransomware intrusion. Legitimate Veeam credential recovery procedures may also produce this activity.
fp: Authorized Veeam credential recovery or database troubleshooting, as described in Veeam KB4349.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\psql.exe" and ProcessCommandLine matches regex "(?i)\\s(?:-d\\s+|--dbname(?:=|\\s+))\"?VeeamBackup\"?(?:\\s|$)" and ProcessCommandLine matches regex "(?i)select\\s" and ProcessCommandLine matches regex "(?i)from\\s+(?:(?:[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*|\"[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*\")\\.)?\"?credentials\"?(?:\\s|[,;)\"]|$)"
pr: #6464 feat(windows): detect potential Veeam credential access via psql.exe

t: Potential Virtualization/Sandbox Evasion Via WMI Or Registry Recon
de: Detects processes querying well-known WMI classes or registry values used to fingerprint virtual machines and sandboxes (BIOS/board manufacturer strings, thermal zone presence, disk/video controller identifiers). This is commonly done by malware and loaders before deciding whether to detonate their real payload, in order to avoid analysis environments. The only existing Sigma coverage for this sub-technique targets PowerShell Script Block Logging exclusively; this rule instead relies on Process Creation, which is far more commonly enabled, and additionally covers reg.exe invocations.
fp: Legitimate IT asset inventory, hardware/software audit, and RMM (Remote Monitoring and Management) tooling routinely queries the same WMI classes and registry values as part of normal hardware discovery. Baseline and, where possible, filter by known-good parent processes or scheduled tasks in your environment.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\reg.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "reg.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "HARDWARE\\DESCRIPTION\\System" or ProcessCommandLine contains "HARDWARE\\DESCRIPTION\\System\\CentralProcessor") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "SystemBiosVersion" or ProcessCommandLine contains "VideoBiosVersion" or ProcessCommandLine contains "SystemManufacturer" or ProcessCommandLine contains "SystemProductName" or ProcessCommandLine contains "BaseBoardManufacturer" or ProcessCommandLine contains "BaseBoardProduct" or ProcessCommandLine contains "ProcessorNameString" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Identifier")) or (((FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("PowerShell.EXE", "pwsh.dll"))) and (ProcessCommandLine contains "Get-WmiObject" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Get-CimInstance" or ProcessCommandLine contains "gwmi" or ProcessCommandLine contains "gcim") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "Win32_ComputerSystem" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Win32_BIOS" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Win32_DiskDrive" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Win32_VideoController" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Win32_PnPEntity" or ProcessCommandLine contains "MSAcpi_ThermalZoneTemperature" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Win32_Fan"))
pr: #6258 New rule: Potential Virtualization/Sandbox Evasion Via WMI Or Registry Recon

de: Detects potential DLL sideloading of "vivaldi_elf.dll"
q:
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\vivaldi_elf.dll" and (not((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\Vivaldi\\Application\\vivaldi.exe" and FolderPath contains "\\Vivaldi\\Application\\")))

t: Potential Wazuh Security Platform DLL Sideloading
de: Detects potential DLL side loading of DLLs that are part of the Wazuh security platform
fp: Many legitimate applications leverage this DLL. (Visual Studio, JetBrains, Ruby, Anaconda, GithubDesktop, etc.)
q:
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\libwazuhshared.dll" or FolderPath endswith "\\libwinpthread-1.dll") and (not((FolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\"))) and (not(((FolderPath contains "\\AppData\\Local\\" or FolderPath contains "\\ProgramData\\") and FolderPath endswith "\\mingw64\\bin\\libwinpthread-1.dll")))

t: Potential Webshell Creation On Static Website
au: Beyu Denis, oscd.community, Tim Shelton, Thurein Oo
de: Detects the creation of files with certain extensions on a static web site. This can be indicative of potential uploads of a web shell.
fp: Legitimate administrator or developer creating legitimate executable files in a web application folder
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where ((FolderPath contains "\\inetpub\\wwwroot\\" and (FolderPath contains ".ashx" or FolderPath contains ".asp" or FolderPath contains ".ph" or FolderPath contains ".soap")) or ((FolderPath contains "\\www\\" or FolderPath contains "\\htdocs\\" or FolderPath contains "\\html\\") and FolderPath contains ".ph")) and (not(((FolderPath contains "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\" or FolderPath contains "\\Windows\\Temp\\") or InitiatingProcessFolderPath =~ "System" or FolderPath contains "\\xampp")))

t: Potential WinGet Proxy Execution via DSC Engine
de: Detects WindowsPackageManagerServer.exe (WinGet) spawning ConfigurationRemotingServer.exe with PowerShell in the command line. HackTools such as DSCourier abuse WinGet's ability to apply DSC configurations to proxy code execution — a malicious DSC YAML causes WinGet to invoke ConfigurationRemotingServer.exe, which runs PowerShell to process and execute the configuration payload.
fp: Legitimate DSC configurations executed via WinGet
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\WindowsPackageManagerServer.exe" and FolderPath endswith "\\ConfigurationRemotingServer.exe" and ProcessCommandLine contains "pwsh"
pr: #5944 NEWRULE: ProxyExecution with ConfigurationRemotingServer (DSCourier)

t: Potential WMI Lateral Movement WmiPrvSE Spawned PowerShell
de: Detects Powershell as a child of the WmiPrvSE process. Which could be a sign of lateral movement via WMI.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\WmiPrvSE.exe" and ((FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("PowerShell.EXE", "pwsh.dll")))

de: Detects potential DLL sideloading of "wwlib.dll"
q:
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\wwlib.dll" and (not(((InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Microsoft Office\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files\\Microsoft Office\\") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\winword.exe" and (FolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Microsoft Office\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files\\Microsoft Office\\"))))

de: Detects potential DLL sideloading of "wwlib.dll"
q:
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\wwlib.dll" and (not(((InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Microsoft Office\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files\\Microsoft Office\\") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\winword.exe" and (FolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Microsoft Office\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files\\Microsoft Office\\"))))
pr: #6279 🩺 add regression data from evtx-attack-samples

de: Identifies the execution traces of the XCSSET malware. XCSSET is a macOS trojan that primarily spreads via Xcode projects and maliciously modifies applications. Infected users are also vulnerable to having their credentials, accounts, and other vital data stolen.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/bash" and FolderPath endswith "/curl" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "/sys/log.php" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/sys/prepod.php" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/sys/bin/Pods")) and ProcessCommandLine contains "https://") or ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/bash" and FolderPath endswith "/osacompile" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "/Users/" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/Library/Group Containers/")) or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/bash" and FolderPath endswith "/plutil" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "LSUIElement" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/Users/" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/Library/Group Containers/")) or (FolderPath endswith "/zip" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "-r" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/Users/" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/Library/Group Containers/")))

de: Detects usage of "xterm" as a potential reverse shell tunnel
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath contains "xterm" and ProcessCommandLine contains "-display" and ProcessCommandLine endswith ":1"

t: Potentially Over Permissive Permissions Granted Using Dsacls.EXE
de: Detects usage of Dsacls to grant over permissive permissions
fp: Legitimate administrators granting over permissive permissions to users
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\dsacls.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "DSACLS.EXE") and ProcessCommandLine contains " /G " and (ProcessCommandLine contains "GR" or ProcessCommandLine contains "GE" or ProcessCommandLine contains "GW" or ProcessCommandLine contains "GA" or ProcessCommandLine contains "WP" or ProcessCommandLine contains "WD")

t: Potentially Suspicious Azure Front Door Connection
de: Detects connections with Azure Front Door (known legitimate service that can be leveraged for C2) that fall outside of known benign behavioral baseline (not using common apps or common azurefd.net endpoints)
fp: Results are not inherently suspicious, but should be investigated during threat hunting for potential cloud C2.
q:
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where RemoteUrl contains "azurefd.net" and (not(((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "brave.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "chrome.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "chromium.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "firefox.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "msedge.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "msedgewebview2.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "opera.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "vivaldi.exe") or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "searchapp.exe" or (RemoteUrl contains "afdxtest.z01.azurefd.net" or RemoteUrl contains "fp-afd.azurefd.net" or RemoteUrl contains "fp-afdx-bpdee4gtg6frejfd.z01.azurefd.net" or RemoteUrl contains "roxy.azurefd.net" or RemoteUrl contains "powershellinfraartifacts-gkhedzdeaghdezhr.z01.azurefd.net" or RemoteUrl contains "storage-explorer-publishing-feapcgfgbzc2cjek.b01.azurefd.net" or RemoteUrl contains "graph.azurefd.net"))))

de: Detects the expansion or decompression of cabinet files from potentially suspicious or uncommon locations, e.g. seen in Iranian MeteorExpress related attacks
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\expand.exe" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "-F:" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/F:" or ProcessCommandLine contains "–F:" or ProcessCommandLine contains "—F:" or ProcessCommandLine contains "―F:")) and ((ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Perflogs\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\ProgramData" or ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Users\\Public\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Windows\\Temp\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Admin$\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\AppData\\Roaming\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\C$\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Temporary Internet") or ((ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Users\\" and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Favorites\\") or (ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Users\\" and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Favourites\\") or (ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Users\\" and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Contacts\\"))) and (not((InitiatingProcessFolderPath =~ "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Dell\\UpdateService\\ServiceShell.exe" and ProcessCommandLine contains "C:\\ProgramData\\Dell\\UpdateService\\Temp\\")))

t: Potentially Suspicious Child Process Of ClickOnce Application
de: Detects potentially suspicious child processes of a ClickOnce deployment application
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\AppData\\Local\\Apps\\2.0\\" and (FolderPath endswith "\\calc.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\cscript.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\explorer.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\mshta.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\net.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\net1.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\nltest.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\notepad.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\reg.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\regsvr32.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\schtasks.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\werfault.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\wscript.exe")

t: Potentially Suspicious Child Process Of DiskShadow.EXE
de: Detects potentially suspicious child processes of "Diskshadow.exe". This could be an attempt to bypass parent/child relationship detection or application whitelisting rules.
fp: False postitve can occur in cases where admin scripts levreage the "exec" flag to execute applications
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\diskshadow.exe" and (FolderPath endswith "\\certutil.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\cscript.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\mshta.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\regsvr32.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\wscript.exe")

t: Potentially Suspicious Child Process of KeyScrambler.exe
de: Detects potentially suspicious child processes of KeyScrambler.exe
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\KeyScrambler.exe" and ((FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\cscript.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\mshta.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\regsvr32.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\wscript.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("Cmd.Exe", "cscript.exe", "mshta.exe", "PowerShell.EXE", "pwsh.dll", "regsvr32.exe", "RUNDLL32.EXE", "wscript.exe")))

t: Potentially Suspicious Child Process Of TextTransform
de: Detects potentially suspicious child processes spawned by Microsoft Visual Studio Text Transformation utilities. T4 text templates can contain C# code that is compiled and executed during transformation and could be abused to proxy execution through a trusted developer utility.
fp: Legitimate T4 templates or development and build automation that intentionally launch external command or script interpreters
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\TextTransform.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\TextTransformCore.exe") and (FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\cscript.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\mshta.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\regsvr32.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\wscript.exe")
pr: #6418 Detection texttransform suspicious child

t: Potentially Suspicious Child Process Of VsCode
de: Detects uncommon or suspicious child processes spawning from a VsCode "code.exe" process. This could indicate an attempt of persistence via VsCode tasks or terminal profiles.
fp: In development environment where VsCode is used heavily. False positives may occur when developers use task to compile or execute different types of code. Remove or add processes accordingly
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\code.exe" and ((FolderPath endswith "\\calc.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\regsvr32.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\cscript.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\wscript.exe") or ((FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "Invoke-Expressions" or ProcessCommandLine contains "IEX" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Invoke-Command" or ProcessCommandLine contains "ICM" or ProcessCommandLine contains "DownloadString" or ProcessCommandLine contains "rundll32" or ProcessCommandLine contains "regsvr32" or ProcessCommandLine contains "wscript" or ProcessCommandLine contains "cscript")) or (FolderPath contains ":\\Users\\Public\\" or FolderPath contains ":\\Windows\\Temp\\" or FolderPath contains ":\\Temp\\"))

t: Potentially Suspicious Child Process Of VSLaunchBrowser
de: Detects potentially suspicious command and script interpreters spawned by the Microsoft Visual Studio VSLaunchBrowser utility. VSLaunchBrowser can open local or remote resources through their associated file handlers and could be abused to proxy execution through a trusted developer utility.
fp: Legitimate Visual Studio development or debugging workflows that intentionally open command or script files through VSLaunchBrowser
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\VSLaunchBrowser.exe" and (FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\cscript.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\mshta.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\msiexec.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\regsvr32.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\wscript.exe")
pr: #6422 New Rule: Potentially Suspicious Child Process Of VSLaunchBrowser

t: Potentially Suspicious Child Process Of WinRAR.EXE
de: Detects potentially suspicious child processes of WinRAR.exe.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\WinRAR.exe" and ((FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\cscript.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\mshta.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\regsvr32.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\wscript.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("Cmd.Exe", "cscript.exe", "mshta.exe", "PowerShell.EXE", "pwsh.dll", "regsvr32.exe", "RUNDLL32.EXE", "wscript.exe")))

t: Potentially Suspicious CMD Shell Output Redirect
de: Detects inline Windows shell commands redirecting output via the ">" symbol to a suspicious location. This technique is sometimes used by malicious actors in order to redirect the output of reconnaissance commands such as "hostname" and "dir" to files for future exfiltration.
fp: Legitimate admin or third party scripts used for diagnostic collection might generate some false positives
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "Cmd.Exe") and (((ProcessCommandLine contains ">" and ProcessCommandLine contains "%APPDATA%\\") or (ProcessCommandLine contains ">" and ProcessCommandLine contains "%TEMP%\\") or (ProcessCommandLine contains ">" and ProcessCommandLine contains "%TMP%\\") or (ProcessCommandLine contains ">" and ProcessCommandLine contains "%USERPROFILE%\\") or (ProcessCommandLine contains ">" and ProcessCommandLine contains "C:\\ProgramData\\") or (ProcessCommandLine contains ">" and ProcessCommandLine contains "C:\\Temp\\") or (ProcessCommandLine contains ">" and ProcessCommandLine contains "C:\\Users\\Public\\") or (ProcessCommandLine contains ">" and ProcessCommandLine contains "C:\\Windows\\Temp\\")) or ((ProcessCommandLine contains " >" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\">" or ProcessCommandLine contains "'>") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "C:\\Users\\" and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\AppData\\Local\\")))

t: Potentially Suspicious Command Targeting Teams Sensitive Files
de: Detects a commandline containing references to the Microsoft Teams database or cookies files from a process other than Teams. The database might contain authentication tokens and other sensitive information about the logged in accounts.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Microsoft\\Teams\\Cookies" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Microsoft\\Teams\\Local Storage\\leveldb") and (not(FolderPath endswith "\\Microsoft\\Teams\\current\\Teams.exe"))

de: Detects potentially suspicious command line arguments of common data compression tools
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (((ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName contains "7z" and ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName contains ".exe") or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName endswith "rar.exe" or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName contains "Command" and ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName contains "Line" and ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName contains "RAR")) and (ProcessCommandLine contains " -p" or ProcessCommandLine contains " -ta" or ProcessCommandLine contains " -tb" or ProcessCommandLine contains " -sdel" or ProcessCommandLine contains " -dw" or ProcessCommandLine contains " -hp")) and (not((InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains ":\\Program Files\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains ":\\Program Files (x86)\\")))

t: Potentially Suspicious Desktop Background Change Using Reg.EXE
de: Detects the execution of "reg.exe" to alter registry keys that would replace the user's desktop background. This is a common technique used by malware to change the desktop background to a ransom note or other image.
fp: Administrative scripts that change the desktop background to a company logo or other image.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\reg.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "reg.exe") and ProcessCommandLine contains "add") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "Control Panel\\Desktop" or ProcessCommandLine contains "CurrentVersion\\Policies\\ActiveDesktop" or ProcessCommandLine contains "CurrentVersion\\Policies\\System") and ((ProcessCommandLine contains "/v NoChangingWallpaper" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/d 1") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "/v Wallpaper" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/t REG_SZ") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "/v WallpaperStyle" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/d 2"))

t: Potentially Suspicious Desktop Background Change Via Registry
de: Detects registry value settings that would replace the user's desktop background. This is a common technique used by malware to change the desktop background to a ransom note or other image.
fp: Administrative scripts that change the desktop background to a company logo or other image.
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where (RegistryKey contains "Control Panel\\Desktop" or RegistryKey contains "CurrentVersion\\Policies\\ActiveDesktop" or RegistryKey contains "CurrentVersion\\Policies\\System") and ((RegistryKey endswith "NoChangingWallpaper" and RegistryValueData =~ "DWORD (0x00000001)") or RegistryKey endswith "\\Wallpaper" or (RegistryKey endswith "\\WallpaperStyle" and RegistryValueData =~ "2")) and (not((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\svchost.exe" or (RegistryKey endswith "\\Control Panel\\Desktop\\Wallpaper" and RegistryValueData =~ "(Empty)") or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "C:\\Windows\\Explorer.EXE"))) and (not(((InitiatingProcessFolderPath in~ ("C:\\Program Files\\Amazon\\EC2Launch\\EC2Launch.exe", "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Amazon\\EC2Launch\\EC2Launch.exe")) and RegistryKey endswith "\\Control Panel\\Desktop\\Wallpaper")))

de: Detects the creation of a file with the ".dmp"/".hdmp" extension by a shell or scripting application such as "cmd", "powershell", etc. Often created by software during a crash. Memory dumps can sometimes contain sensitive information such as credentials. It's best to determine the source of the crash.
fp: Some administrative PowerShell or VB scripts might have the ability to collect dumps and move them to other folders which might trigger a false positive.
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\cscript.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\mshta.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\wscript.exe") and (FolderPath endswith ".dmp" or FolderPath endswith ".dump" or FolderPath endswith ".hdmp")

de: Detects potentially suspicious CommandLine of electron apps (teams, discord, slack, etc.). This could be a sign of abuse to proxy execution through a signed binary.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\chrome.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\code.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\discord.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\GitHubDesktop.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\keybase.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\msedge_proxy.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\msedge.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\msedgewebview2.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\msteams.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\slack.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\Teams.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("chrome.exe", "code.exe", "discord.exe", "GitHubDesktop.exe", "keybase.exe", "msedge_proxy.exe", "msedge.exe", "msedgewebview2.exe", "msteams.exe", "slack.exe", "Teams.exe"))) and (ProcessCommandLine contains "--browser-subprocess-path" or ProcessCommandLine contains "--gpu-launcher" or ProcessCommandLine contains "--renderer-cmd-prefix" or ProcessCommandLine contains "--utility-cmd-prefix")

t: Potentially Suspicious EventLog Recon Activity Using Log Query Utilities
de: Detects execution of different log query utilities and commands to search and dump the content of specific event logs or look for specific event IDs. This technique is used by threat actors in order to extract sensitive information from events logs such as usernames, IP addresses, hostnames, etc.
fp: Legitimate usage of the utility by administrators to query the event log
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((ProcessCommandLine contains "Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Microsoft-Windows-Security-Auditing" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Microsoft-Windows-TerminalServices-LocalSessionManager" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Microsoft-Windows-TerminalServices-RemoteConnectionManager" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Microsoft-Windows-Windows Defender" or ProcessCommandLine contains "PowerShellCore" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Security" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Windows PowerShell") or ((ProcessCommandLine contains "-InstanceId 462") or (ProcessCommandLine contains ".eventid -eq 462") or (ProcessCommandLine contains ".ID -eq 462") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "EventCode=" and ProcessCommandLine contains "462") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "EventIdentifier=" and ProcessCommandLine contains "462") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "System[EventID=462" and ProcessCommandLine contains "]") or ProcessCommandLine contains "-InstanceId 4778" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".eventid -eq 4778" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".ID -eq 4778" or (ProcessCommandLine contains "EventCode=" and ProcessCommandLine contains "4778") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "EventIdentifier=" and ProcessCommandLine contains "4778") or ProcessCommandLine contains "System[EventID=4778]" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-InstanceId 25" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".eventid -eq 25" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".ID -eq 25" or (ProcessCommandLine contains "EventCode=" and ProcessCommandLine contains "25") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "EventIdentifier=" and ProcessCommandLine contains "25") or ProcessCommandLine contains "System[EventID=25]" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-InstanceId 1149" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".eventid -eq 1149" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".ID -eq 1149" or (ProcessCommandLine contains "EventCode=" and ProcessCommandLine contains "1149") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "EventIdentifier=" and ProcessCommandLine contains "1149") or ProcessCommandLine contains "System[EventID=1149]" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-InstanceId 21" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".eventid -eq 21" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".ID -eq 21" or (ProcessCommandLine contains "EventCode=" and ProcessCommandLine contains "21") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "EventIdentifier=" and ProcessCommandLine contains "21") or ProcessCommandLine contains "System[EventID=21]" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-InstanceId 22" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".eventid -eq 22" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".ID -eq 22" or (ProcessCommandLine contains "EventCode=" and ProcessCommandLine contains "22") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "EventIdentifier=" and ProcessCommandLine contains "22") or ProcessCommandLine contains "System[EventID=22]")) and ((ProcessCommandLine contains "Select" and ProcessCommandLine contains "Win32_NTLogEvent") or ((FolderPath endswith "\\wevtutil.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "wevtutil.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " qe " or ProcessCommandLine contains " query-events ")) or ((FolderPath endswith "\\wmic.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "wmic.exe") and ProcessCommandLine contains " ntevent") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "Get-WinEvent " or ProcessCommandLine contains "get-eventlog "))

t: Potentially Suspicious Execution From Tmp Folder
de: Detects a potentially suspicious execution of a process located in the '/tmp/' folder
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath startswith "/tmp/" and (not(FolderPath endswith "/usr/bin/nextcloud"))

de: Detects suspicious execution of "PDQDeployRunner" which is part of the PDQDeploy service stack that is responsible for executing commands and packages on a remote machines
fp: Legitimate use of the PDQDeploy tool to execute these commands
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\PDQDeployRunner-" and ((FolderPath endswith "\\bash.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\certutil.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\csc.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\cscript.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\dllhost.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\mshta.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\msiexec.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\regsvr32.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\scriptrunner.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\wmic.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\wscript.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\wsl.exe") or (FolderPath contains ":\\ProgramData\\" or FolderPath contains ":\\Users\\Public\\" or FolderPath contains ":\\Windows\\TEMP\\" or FolderPath contains "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp") or (ProcessCommandLine contains " -decode " or ProcessCommandLine contains " -enc " or ProcessCommandLine contains " -encodedcommand " or ProcessCommandLine contains " -w hidden" or ProcessCommandLine contains "DownloadString" or ProcessCommandLine contains "FromBase64String" or ProcessCommandLine contains "http" or ProcessCommandLine contains "iex " or ProcessCommandLine contains "Invoke-"))

t: Potentially Suspicious Execution Of Regasm/Regsvcs From Uncommon Location
de: Detects potentially suspicious execution of the Regasm/Regsvcs utilities from a potentially suspicious location
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\Regsvcs.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\Regasm.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("RegSvcs.exe", "RegAsm.exe"))) and (ProcessCommandLine contains "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Microsoft\\Windows\\Start Menu\\Programs\\Startup\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\PerfLogs\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Users\\Public\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Windows\\Temp\\")

t: Potentially Suspicious Execution Of Regasm/Regsvcs With Uncommon Extension
de: Detects potentially suspicious execution of the Regasm/Regsvcs utilities with an uncommon extension.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\Regsvcs.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\Regasm.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("RegSvcs.exe", "RegAsm.exe"))) and (ProcessCommandLine contains ".dat" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".gif" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".jpeg" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".jpg" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".png" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".txt")

t: Potentially Suspicious JWT Token Search Via CLI
de: Detects potentially suspicious search for JWT tokens via CLI by looking for the string "eyJ0eX" or "eyJhbG". JWT tokens are often used for access-tokens across various applications and services like Microsoft 365, Azure, AWS, Google Cloud, and others. Threat actors may search for these tokens to steal them for lateral movement or privilege escalation.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessCommandLine contains "find " or ProcessCommandLine contains "find.exe" or ProcessCommandLine contains "findstr" or ProcessCommandLine contains "select-string " or ProcessCommandLine contains "strings") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "eyJ0eXAiOi" or ProcessCommandLine contains "eyJhbGciOi" or ProcessCommandLine contains " eyJ0eX" or ProcessCommandLine contains " \"eyJ0eX\"" or ProcessCommandLine contains " 'eyJ0eX'" or ProcessCommandLine contains " eyJhbG" or ProcessCommandLine contains " \"eyJhbG\"" or ProcessCommandLine contains " 'eyJhbG'")

t: Potentially Suspicious Named Pipe Created Via Mkfifo
de: Detects the creation of a new named pipe using the "mkfifo" utility in a potentially suspicious location
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "/mkfifo" and ProcessCommandLine contains " /tmp/"

t: Potentially Suspicious NTFS Symlink Behavior Modification
de: Detects the modification of NTFS symbolic link behavior using fsutil, which could be used to enable remote to local or remote to remote symlinks for potential attacks.
fp: Legitimate usage, investigate the parent process and context to determine if benign.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("Cmd.Exe", "PowerShell.EXE", "pwsh.dll"))) and (ProcessCommandLine contains "fsutil" and ProcessCommandLine contains "behavior" and ProcessCommandLine contains "set" and ProcessCommandLine contains "SymlinkEvaluation") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "R2L:1" or ProcessCommandLine contains "R2R:1" or ProcessCommandLine contains "L2L:1")

de: Detects uncommon and potentially suspicious one-liner command containing both "ping" and "copy" at the same time, which is usually used by malware.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "Cmd.Exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "ping" and ProcessCommandLine contains "copy ") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " -n " or ProcessCommandLine contains " /n " or ProcessCommandLine contains " –n " or ProcessCommandLine contains " —n " or ProcessCommandLine contains " ―n ") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " -y " or ProcessCommandLine contains " /y " or ProcessCommandLine contains " –y " or ProcessCommandLine contains " —y " or ProcessCommandLine contains " ―y ")

de: Detects potentially suspicious child processes spawned by PowerShell. Use this rule to hunt for potential anomalies initiating from PowerShell scripts and commands.
fp: False positives are to be expected from PowerShell scripts that might make use of additional binaries such as "mshta", "bitsadmin", etc. Apply additional filters for those scripts.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\powershell_ise.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe") and (FolderPath endswith "\\bash.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\bitsadmin.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\certutil.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\cscript.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\forfiles.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\hh.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\mshta.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\regsvr32.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\schtasks.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\scrcons.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\scriptrunner.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\sh.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\wmic.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\wscript.exe")) and (not(((FolderPath endswith "\\certutil.exe" and ProcessCommandLine contains "-verifystore ") or (FolderPath endswith "\\wmic.exe" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "qfe list" or ProcessCommandLine contains "diskdrive " or ProcessCommandLine contains "csproduct " or ProcessCommandLine contains "computersystem " or ProcessCommandLine contains " os " or ProcessCommandLine startswith ""))))) and (not((InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "\\Program Files\\Amazon\\WorkspacesConfig\\Scripts\\" and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Program Files\\Amazon\\WorkspacesConfig\\Scripts\\")))

t: Potentially Suspicious Powershell Script Execution From Temp Folder
au: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Max Altgelt (Nextron Systems), Tim Shelton
de: Detects a potentially suspicious powershell script executions from temporary folder
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Windows\\Temp" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Temporary Internet" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\AppData\\Roaming\\Temp" or ProcessCommandLine contains "%TEMP%" or ProcessCommandLine contains "%TMP%" or ProcessCommandLine contains "%LocalAppData%\\Temp")) and (not((ProcessCommandLine contains "-WindowStyle hidden -Verb runAs" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Windows\\system32\\config\\systemprofile\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\Amazon\\EC2-Windows\\" or (ProcessCommandLine contains " >" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Out-File" or ProcessCommandLine contains "ConvertTo-Json") or ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath in~ ("C:\\Windows\\System32\\Msiexec.exe", "C:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\Msiexec.exe")) and FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "-NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command" and ProcessCommandLine contains "AppData\\Local\\Temp\\" and ProcessCommandLine contains "Install-Chocolatey.ps1")))))

de: Detects regsvr32 execution to download/install/register new DLLs that are hosted on Web or FTP servers.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\regsvr32.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "REGSVR32.EXE") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " /i" or ProcessCommandLine contains " -i") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "ftp" or ProcessCommandLine contains "http")

de: Detects regsvr32 execution to download/install/register new DLLs that are hosted on Web or FTP servers.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\regsvr32.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "REGSVR32.EXE") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " /i" or ProcessCommandLine contains " -i") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "ftp" or ProcessCommandLine contains "http")
pr: #6279 🩺 add regression data from evtx-attack-samples

de: Detects regsvr32 execution to load/register DLLs from remote locations via HTTP, HTTPS, or FTP protocols. This is a common technique used by attackers to bypass application whitelisting and execute malicious code.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\regsvr32.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "REGSVR32.EXE") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " -i" or ProcessCommandLine contains " /i" or ProcessCommandLine contains " –i" or ProcessCommandLine contains " —i" or ProcessCommandLine contains " ―i" or ProcessCommandLine contains " -s" or ProcessCommandLine contains " /s" or ProcessCommandLine contains " –s" or ProcessCommandLine contains " —s" or ProcessCommandLine contains " ―s") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "ftp://" or ProcessCommandLine contains "http://" or ProcessCommandLine contains "https://")
pr: #6122 update: Regsvr32 detection rules tuning and expansion

au: juju4, Jonhnathan Ribeiro, oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
de: Detects suspicious execution of rundll32, with specific calls to some DLLs with known LOLBIN functionalities
fp: False positives depend on scripts and administrative tools used in the monitored environment
q:

| where ((ProcessCommandLine contains "javascript:" and ProcessCommandLine contains ".RegisterXLL") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "url.dll" and ProcessCommandLine contains "OpenURL") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "url.dll" and ProcessCommandLine contains "OpenURLA") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "url.dll" and ProcessCommandLine contains "FileProtocolHandler") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "zipfldr.dll" and ProcessCommandLine contains "RouteTheCall") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "shell32.dll" and ProcessCommandLine contains "Control_RunDLL") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "shell32.dll" and ProcessCommandLine contains "ShellExec_RunDLL") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "mshtml.dll" and ProcessCommandLine contains "PrintHTML") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "advpack.dll" and ProcessCommandLine contains "LaunchINFSection") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "advpack.dll" and ProcessCommandLine contains "RegisterOCX") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "ieadvpack.dll" and ProcessCommandLine contains "LaunchINFSection") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "ieadvpack.dll" and ProcessCommandLine contains "RegisterOCX") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "ieframe.dll" and ProcessCommandLine contains "OpenURL") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "shdocvw.dll" and ProcessCommandLine contains "OpenURL") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "syssetup.dll" and ProcessCommandLine contains "SetupInfObjectInstallAction") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "setupapi.dll" and ProcessCommandLine contains "InstallHinfSection") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "pcwutl.dll" and ProcessCommandLine contains "LaunchApplication") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "dfshim.dll" and ProcessCommandLine contains "ShOpenVerbApplication") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "dfshim.dll" and ProcessCommandLine contains "ShOpenVerbShortcut") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "scrobj.dll" and ProcessCommandLine contains "GenerateTypeLib" and ProcessCommandLine contains "http") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "shimgvw.dll" and ProcessCommandLine contains "ImageView_Fullscreen" and ProcessCommandLine contains "http") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "comsvcs.dll" and ProcessCommandLine contains "MiniDump")) and (not((ProcessCommandLine contains "shell32.dll,Control_RunDLL desk.cpl,screensaver,@screensaver" or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath =~ "C:\\Windows\\System32\\control.exe" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains ".cpl" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "Shell32.dll" and ProcessCommandLine contains "Control_RunDLL" and ProcessCommandLine contains ".cpl")) or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath =~ "C:\\Windows\\System32\\control.exe" and ProcessCommandLine startswith "\"C:\\Windows\\system32\\rundll32.exe\" Shell32.dll,Control_RunDLL \"C:\\Windows\\System32\\" and ProcessCommandLine endswith ".cpl\","))))

t: Potentially Suspicious Rundll32.EXE Execution of UDL File
de: Detects the execution of rundll32.exe with the oledb32.dll library to open a UDL file. Threat actors can abuse this technique as a phishing vector to capture authentication credentials or other sensitive data.
fp: UDL files serve as a convenient and flexible tool for managing and testing database connections in various development and administrative scenarios.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\explorer.exe" and (FolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "RUNDLL32.EXE") and ((ProcessCommandLine contains "oledb32.dll" and ProcessCommandLine contains ",OpenDSLFile " and (ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Users\\" and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Downloads\\")) and ProcessCommandLine endswith ".udl")

t: Potentially Suspicious TestWindowRemoteAgent Execution From Uncommon Location
de: Detects the Microsoft Visual Studio Test Window Remote Agent executing from outside expected Visual Studio installation directories in outbound client mode. The binary is listed by LOLBAS and can be abused for attacker-controlled network activity such as DNS-based exfiltration.
fp: Developers or administrators who intentionally copy the Visual Studio remote agent to a non-default location and use it for legitimate remote testing.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\TestWindowRemoteAgent.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "TestWindowRemoteAgent.dll") and ProcessCommandLine contains " start " and (ProcessCommandLine contains " -h " or ProcessCommandLine contains " --hostname ") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " -p " or ProcessCommandLine contains " --port ")) and (not((FolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files\\Microsoft Visual Studio\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Microsoft Visual Studio\\")))
pr: #6419 Detection testwindowremoteagent uncommon location

de: Detects potentially suspicious execution of the Qemu utility in a Windows environment. Threat actors have leveraged this utility and this technique for achieving network access as reported by Kaspersky.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((ProcessCommandLine contains "-m 1M" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-m 2M" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-m 3M") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "restrict=off" and ProcessCommandLine contains "-netdev " and ProcessCommandLine contains "connect=" and ProcessCommandLine contains "-nographic")) and (not((ProcessCommandLine contains " -cdrom " or ProcessCommandLine contains " type=virt " or ProcessCommandLine contains " -blockdev ")))

t: Potentially Suspicious Volume Shadow Copy Vsstrace.dll Load
de: Detects the image load of VSS DLL by uncommon executables
q:
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\vsstrace.dll" and (not((((InitiatingProcessFolderPath in~ ("C:\\Windows\\explorer.exe", "C:\\Windows\\ImmersiveControlPanel\\SystemSettings.exe", "C:\\Windows\\servicing\\TrustedInstaller.exe")) or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\System32\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\Temp\\{" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\WinSxS\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\ProgramData\\Package Cache\\{")) or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\") or isnull(InitiatingProcessFolderPath)))) and (not((InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\$WinREAgent\\Scratch\\" or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\temp\\is-" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\avira_system_speedup.tmp"))))

de: Detects possible execution via LNK file accessed on a WebDAV server.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\explorer.exe" and (FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\cscript.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\mshta.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\wscript.exe") and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\DavWWWRoot\\"

de: Detects potentially suspicious child process of applications launched from inside the WindowsApps directory. This could be a sign of a rogue ".appx" package installation/execution
fp: Legitimate packages that make use of external binaries such as Windows Terminal
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "C:\\Program Files\\WindowsApps\\" and ((FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\cscript.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\mshta.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\powershell_ise.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\regsvr32.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\wscript.exe") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "cmd /c" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Invoke-" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Base64")) and (not(((InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains ":\\Program Files\\WindowsApps\\Microsoft.WindowsTerminal" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\WindowsTerminal.exe" and (FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe")) or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files\\WindowsApps\\Microsoft.SysinternalsSuite" and FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe"))))

t: Potentially Suspicious WSLC Host Directory Mount With Shell
de: Detects Microsoft WSL container CLI execution that bind mounts a sensitive Windows host directory into a Linux container and invokes an inline Unix shell. This may allow a threat actor to access or modify host files with Linux tooling while the inner Linux process is not represented as a Windows child process.
fp: Legitimate container development or administrative workflows that intentionally bind mount Windows user or system directories and invoke an inline shell
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\wslc.exe" or FolderPath =~ "C:\\Program Files\\WSL\\container.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "wslc.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " run " or ProcessCommandLine contains " container run ") and ((ProcessCommandLine contains " -v " or ProcessCommandLine contains " --volume ") or (ProcessCommandLine contains " --mount " and ProcessCommandLine contains "type=bind")) and (ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Users\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Windows\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\ProgramData\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Temp\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\inetpub\\") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " sh " or ProcessCommandLine contains " bash " or ProcessCommandLine contains " ash " or ProcessCommandLine contains " dash " or ProcessCommandLine contains " zsh " or ProcessCommandLine contains "/bin/sh" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/bin/bash" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/bin/ash" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/bin/dash" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/bin/zsh") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " -c " or ProcessCommandLine contains " -lc ")
pr: #6358 Detection wslc host mount shell

de: Detects the use of the Windows Update Client binary (wuauclt.exe) to proxy execute code and making network connections. One could easily make the DLL spawn a new process and inject to it to proxy the network connection and bypass this rule.
q:
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "wuauclt" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains " /RunHandlerComServer") and (not(((ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "127.0.0.0/8") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "10.0.0.0/8") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "169.254.0.0/16") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "172.16.0.0/12") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "192.168.0.0/16") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "::1/128") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "fe80::/10") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "fc00::/7")) or (ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "20.184.0.0/13") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "20.192.0.0/10") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "23.79.0.0/16") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "51.10.0.0/15") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "51.103.0.0/16") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "51.104.0.0/15") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "52.224.0.0/11")) or (InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Windows\\UUS\\Packages\\Preview\\amd64\\updatedeploy.dll /ClassId" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Windows\\UUS\\amd64\\UpdateDeploy.dll /ClassId") or (InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Windows\\WinSxS\\" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "\\UpdateDeploy.dll /ClassId ") or isnull(InitiatingProcessCommandLine) or InitiatingProcessCommandLine =~ "")))

de: Detects the deletion of the PowerShell console History logs which may indicate an attempt to destroy forensic evidence
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where ActionType =~ "FileDeleted" and FolderPath endswith "\\PSReadLine\\ConsoleHost_history.txt"

t: PowerShell Core DLL Loaded By Non PowerShell Process

de: Detects loading of essential DLLs used by PowerShell by non-PowerShell process. Detects behavior similar to meterpreter's "load powershell" extension.
fp: Used by some .NET binaries, minimal on user workstation.
Used by Microsoft SQL Server Management Studio
q:

| where (InitiatingProcessVersionInfoFileDescription =~ "System.Management.Automation" or InitiatingProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "System.Management.Automation.dll" or (FolderPath endswith "C:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\WindowsPowerShell\\v1.0\\powershell_ise.exe", "C:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\WindowsPowerShell\\v1.0\\powershell.exe")) or ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "C:\\Program Files\\WindowsApps\\Microsoft.PowerShellPreview" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\AppData\\Local\\Microsoft\\WindowsApps\\Microsoft.PowerShellPreview") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe") or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath in~ ("C:\\Windows\\System32\\dsac.exe", "C:\\WINDOWS\\System32\\RemoteFXvGPUDisablement.exe", "C:\\Windows\\System32\\runscripthelper.exe", "C:\\WINDOWS\\System32\\sdiagnhost.exe", "C:\\Windows\\System32\\ServerManager.exe", "C:\\Windows\\System32\\SyncAppvPublishingServer.exe", "C:\\Windows\\System32\\winrshost.exe", "C:\\Windows\\Microsoft.NET\\FrameworkArm64\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\Microsoft.NET\\Framework64\\") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\mscorsvw.exe")))) and (not(((InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files\\WindowsApps\\Microsoft.GetHelp_" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\GetHelp.exe") or ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Microsoft SQL Server Management Studio" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files\\Microsoft SQL Server Management Studio") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\IDE\\Ssms.exe") or ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Microsoft SQL Server\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files\\Microsoft SQL Server\\") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\Tools\\Binn\\SQLPS.exe") or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\Citrix\\ConfigSync\\ConfigSyncRun.exe" or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Microsoft Visual Studio\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files\\Microsoft Visual Studio\\") or InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith
