t: PowerShell Core DLL Loaded Via Office Application
de: Detects PowerShell core DLL being loaded by an Office Product
q:
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\excel.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\mspub.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\outlook.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\onenote.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\onenoteim.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\powerpnt.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\winword.exe") and (FolderPath contains "\\System.Management.Automation.Dll" or FolderPath contains "\\System.Management.Automation.ni.Dll")

t: Powershell Create Scheduled Task via CommandLine
de: Detects PowerShell invocations that create scheduled tasks via the command line. Covers native PowerShell cmdlets (e.g. Register-ScheduledTask), the WMI/CIM method, and the Schedule.Service COM object (which bypasses schtasks.exe-based detections).
fp: Legitimate administrative scripts passed inline on the command line
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.dll"))) and ((ProcessCommandLine contains "New-ScheduledTaskAction" or ProcessCommandLine contains "New-ScheduledTaskTrigger" or ProcessCommandLine contains "New-ScheduledTaskPrincipal" or ProcessCommandLine contains "New-ScheduledTaskSettingsSet" or ProcessCommandLine contains "New-ScheduledTask" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Register-ScheduledTask") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "Invoke-CimMethod" and ProcessCommandLine contains "-ClassName" and ProcessCommandLine contains "PS_ScheduledTask" and ProcessCommandLine contains "-NameSpace" and ProcessCommandLine contains "Root\\Microsoft\\Windows\\TaskScheduler") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "-ComObject" and ProcessCommandLine contains "Schedule.Service" and ProcessCommandLine contains "RegisterTaskDefinition"))
pr: #6262 new: add coverage for schtasks creation via Schedule.Service ComObject

de: Detects requests to exclude files, folders or processes from Antivirus scanning using PowerShell cmdlets
fp: Other Cmdlets that may use the same parameters
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessCommandLine contains "Add-MpPreference " or ProcessCommandLine contains "Set-MpPreference ") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " -ExclusionPath " or ProcessCommandLine contains " -ExclusionExtension " or ProcessCommandLine contains " -ExclusionProcess " or ProcessCommandLine contains " -ExclusionIpAddress ")

au: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), oscd.community, Jonhnathan Ribeiro
de: Detects a Powershell process that contains download commands in its command line string
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\powershell_ise.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("PowerShell_ISE.EXE", "PowerShell.EXE", "pwsh.dll"))) and ((ProcessCommandLine contains "new-object" and ProcessCommandLine contains "net.webclient)." and ProcessCommandLine contains "download") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "string(" or ProcessCommandLine contains "file("))

t: Powershell Executed From Headless ConHost Process
de: Detects the use of powershell commands from headless ConHost window. The "--headless" flag hides the windows from the user upon execution.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\conhost.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "CONHOST.EXE") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "--headless" and ProcessCommandLine contains "powershell")

de: Detects usage of the 'Get-Clipboard' cmdlet via CLI
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessCommandLine contains "Get-Clipboard"

t: Powershell Inline Execution From A File
de: Detects inline execution of PowerShell code from a file
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessCommandLine contains "iex " or ProcessCommandLine contains "Invoke-Expression " or ProcessCommandLine contains "Invoke-Command " or ProcessCommandLine contains "icm ") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "cat " or ProcessCommandLine contains "get-content " or ProcessCommandLine contains "type ") and ProcessCommandLine contains " -raw"

t: PowerShell Module File Created By Non-PowerShell Process
de: Detects the creation of a new PowerShell module ".psm1", ".psd1", ".dll", ".ps1", etc. by a non- PowerShell process
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where (FolderPath contains "\\WindowsPowerShell\\Modules\\" or FolderPath contains "\\PowerShell\\7\\Modules\\") and (not(((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith ":\\Program Files\\PowerShell\\7-preview\\pwsh.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith ":\\Program Files\\PowerShell\\7\\pwsh.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith ":\\Windows\\System32\\poqexec.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith ":\\Windows\\System32\\WindowsPowerShell\\v1.0\\powershell_ise.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith ":\\Windows\\System32\\WindowsPowerShell\\v1.0\\powershell.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith ":\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\poqexec.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith ":\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\WindowsPowerShell\\v1.0\\powershell_ise.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith ":\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\WindowsPowerShell\\v1.0\\powershell.exe") or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath in~ ("C:\\Windows\\System32\\msiexec.exe", "C:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\msiexec.exe")))))

t: PowerShell MSI Install via WindowsInstaller COM From Remote Location
de: Detects the execution of PowerShell commands that attempt to install MSI packages via the Windows Installer COM object (`WindowsInstaller.Installer`) hosted remotely. This could be an indication of malicious software deployment or lateral movement attempts using Windows Installer functionality. The usage of WindowsInstaller COM object rather than msiexec could be an attempt to bypass the detection.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (((FolderPath endswith "\\powershell_ise.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("PowerShell_ISE.EXE", "PowerShell.EXE", "pwsh.dll"))) and (ProcessCommandLine contains "-ComObject" and ProcessCommandLine contains "InstallProduct(") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "http" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\\\")) and (not((ProcessCommandLine contains "://127.0.0.1" or ProcessCommandLine contains "://localhost")))
pr: #5548 update: windowsInstaller com object related rules

de: Detects the creation or modification of a powershell profile which could indicate suspicious activity as the profile can be used as a mean of persistence
fp: System administrator creating Powershell profile manually
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\Microsoft.PowerShell_profile.ps1" or FolderPath endswith "\\PowerShell\\profile.ps1" or FolderPath endswith "\\Program Files\\PowerShell\\7-preview\\profile.ps1" or FolderPath endswith "\\Program Files\\PowerShell\\7\\profile.ps1" or FolderPath endswith "\\Windows\\System32\\WindowsPowerShell\\v1.0\\profile.ps1" or FolderPath endswith "\\WindowsPowerShell\\profile.ps1"

au: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Jonhnathan Ribeiro, oscd.community
de: Detects a suspicious command line execution that invokes PowerShell with reference to an AppData folder
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessCommandLine contains "powershell.exe" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\powershell" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\pwsh" or ProcessCommandLine contains "pwsh.exe") and ((ProcessCommandLine contains "/c " and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\AppData\\") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "Local\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Roaming\\"))

de: Detects events in which someone prints the contents of history files to the commandline or redirects it to a file for reconnaissance
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "/cat" or FolderPath endswith "/head" or FolderPath endswith "/tail" or FolderPath endswith "/more") and ((ProcessCommandLine contains "/.bash_history" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/.zsh_history") or (ProcessCommandLine endswith "_history" or ProcessCommandLine endswith ".history" or ProcessCommandLine endswith "zhistory"))

t: Private Keys Reconnaissance Via CommandLine Tools
de: Adversaries may search for private key certificate files on compromised systems for insecurely stored credential
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessCommandLine contains ".key" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".pgp" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".gpg" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".ppk" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".p12" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".pem" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".pfx" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".cer" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".p7b" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".asc") and (((FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "Cmd.Exe") and ProcessCommandLine contains "dir ") or (((FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("PowerShell.EXE", "pwsh.dll"))) and ProcessCommandLine contains "Get-ChildItem ") or (FolderPath endswith "\\findstr.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "FINDSTR.EXE"))

de: Detects usage of the SysInternals Procdump utility
fp: Legitimate use of procdump by a developer or administrator
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\procdump.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\procdump64.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\procdump64a.exe"

au: Michael Haag, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), juju4, oscd.community
de: Detects the attempt to create a process via "wmic" with the "process call create" flag, which might indicate an attempt to execute a malicious process on the compromised host. Adversaries may use wmic to execute a process on the compromised host as part of their attack. This event is triggered on on attempt and process creation can be either successful or unsuccessful.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\wmic.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "wmic.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "process" and ProcessCommandLine contains "call" and ProcessCommandLine contains "create")

de: Detects process creation events that use the Sysnative folder (common for CobaltStrike spawns)
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Windows\\Sysnative\\" or FolderPath contains ":\\Windows\\Sysnative\\") and (not(((FolderPath contains "C:\\Windows\\Microsoft.NET\\Framework64\\v" or FolderPath contains "C:\\Windows\\Microsoft.NET\\Framework\\v" or FolderPath contains "C:\\Windows\\Microsoft.NET\\FrameworkArm\\v" or FolderPath contains "C:\\Windows\\Microsoft.NET\\FrameworkArm64\\v") and FolderPath endswith "\\ngen.exe" and ProcessCommandLine contains "install"))) and (not((ProcessCommandLine contains "\"C:\\Windows\\sysnative\\cmd.exe\"" and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\xampp\\" and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\catalina_start.bat")))

de: Detect the use of processes with no name (".exe"), which can be used to evade Image-based detections.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\.exe"

de: Detects the execution of "dotnet-dump" with the "collect" flag. The execution could indicate potential process dumping of critical processes such as LSASS.
fp: Process dumping is the expected behavior of the tool. So false positives are expected in legitimate usage. The PID/Process Name of the process being dumped needs to be investigated
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\dotnet-dump.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "dotnet-dump.dll") and ProcessCommandLine contains "collect"

t: Process Monitor Driver Creation By Non-Sysinternals Binary
de: Detects creation of the Process Monitor driver by processes other than Process Monitor (procmon) itself.
fp: Some false positives may occur with legitimate renamed process monitor binaries
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where (FolderPath contains "\\procmon" and FolderPath endswith ".sys") and (not((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\procmon.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\procmon64.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\procmon64a.exe")))

au: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Karneades / Markus Neis, Jonhnathan Ribeiro, oscd.community
de: Detects the usage of the "Squirrel.exe" binary to execute arbitrary processes. This binary is part of multiple Electron based software installations (Slack, Teams, Discord, etc.)
fp: Expected FP with some Electron based applications such as (1Clipboard, Beaker Browser, Caret, Discord, GitHub Desktop, etc.)
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\squirrel.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\update.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "--processStart" or ProcessCommandLine contains "--processStartAndWait" or ProcessCommandLine contains "--createShortcut")) and (not((((ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Users\\" and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\AppData\\Local\\Discord\\Update.exe" and ProcessCommandLine contains "Discord.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "--createShortcut" or ProcessCommandLine contains "--processStart")) or ((ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Users\\" and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\AppData\\Local\\GitHubDesktop\\Update.exe" and ProcessCommandLine contains "GitHubDesktop.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "--createShortcut" or ProcessCommandLine contains "--processStartAndWait")) or ((ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Users\\" and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\AppData\\Local\\Microsoft\\Teams\\Update.exe" and ProcessCommandLine contains "Teams.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "--processStart" or ProcessCommandLine contains "--createShortcut")) or ((ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Users\\" and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\AppData\\Local\\yammerdesktop\\Update.exe" and ProcessCommandLine contains "Yammer.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "--processStart" or ProcessCommandLine contains "--createShortcut")))))

t: Processes Accessing the Microphone and Webcam
de: Potential adversaries accessing the microphone and webcam in an endpoint.
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where RegistryKey contains "\\SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\CapabilityAccessManager\\ConsentStore\\microphone\\NonPackaged" or RegistryKey contains "\\SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\CapabilityAccessManager\\ConsentStore\\webcam\\NonPackaged"

de: Detects the invocation of vshadow.exe with the -exec parameter that executes a specified script or command after the shadow copies are created but before the VShadow tool exits. VShadow is a command-line tool that you can use to create and manage volume shadow copies. While legitimate backup or administrative scripts may use this flag, attackers can leverage this parameter to proxy the execution of malware.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\vshadow.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "vshadow.exe") and ProcessCommandLine contains "-exec"
pr: #6279 🩺 add regression data from evtx-attack-samples

de: Detects user accept agreement execution in psexec commandline
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\psexec.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "psexec.c"

au: Thomas Patzke, Romaissa Adjailia, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
de: Detects launch of the PSEXESVC service, which means that this system was the target of a psexec remote execution
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath =~ "C:\\Windows\\PSEXESVC.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "psexesvc.exe"

au: Thomas Patzke, Romaissa Adjailia, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
de: Detects launch of the PSEXESVC service, which means that this system was the target of a psexec remote execution
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath =~ "C:\\Windows\\PSEXESVC.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "psexesvc.exe"
pr: #6279 🩺 add regression data from evtx-attack-samples

de: Detects the creation of the "PSScriptPolicyTest" PowerShell script by an uncommon process. This file is usually generated by Microsoft Powershell to test against Applocker.
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where FolderPath contains "__PSScriptPolicyTest_" and (not(((InitiatingProcessFolderPath in~ ("C:\\Program Files\\PowerShell\\7-preview\\pwsh.exe", "C:\\Program Files\\PowerShell\\7\\pwsh.exe", "C:\\Windows\\System32\\WindowsPowerShell\\v1.0\\powershell_ise.exe", "C:\\Windows\\System32\\WindowsPowerShell\\v1.0\\powershell.exe", "C:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\WindowsPowerShell\\v1.0\\powershell_ise.exe", "C:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\WindowsPowerShell\\v1.0\\powershell.exe")) or ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "C:\\Program Files\\WindowsApps\\Microsoft.PowerShellPreview" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\AppData\\Local\\Microsoft\\WindowsApps\\Microsoft.PowerShellPreview") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe") or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath in~ ("C:\\Windows\\System32\\dsac.exe", "C:\\Windows\\System32\\sdiagnhost.exe", "C:\\Windows\\System32\\ServerManager.exe", "C:\\Windows\\System32\\wsmprovhost.exe", "C:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\sdiagnhost.exe"))))) and (not(((InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files\\WindowsApps\\Microsoft.GetHelp_" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\GetHelp.exe") or ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files\\Citrix\\ConfigSync\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Citrix\\ConfigSync\\") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\ConfigSyncRun.exe"))))

de: Detects the use of Advanced IP Scanner. Seems to be a popular tool for ransomware groups.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath contains "\\advanced_ip_scanner" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName contains "advanced_ip_scanner" or ProcessVersionInfoFileDescription contains "Advanced IP Scanner") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "/portable" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/lng")

de: Detects the use of Advanced Port Scanner.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath contains "\\advanced_port_scanner" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName contains "advanced_port_scanner" or ProcessVersionInfoFileDescription contains "Advanced Port Scanner") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "/portable" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/lng")

de: Detects the execution of AdvancedRun utility
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "AdvancedRun.exe" or (ProcessCommandLine contains " /EXEFilename " and ProcessCommandLine contains " /Run") or (ProcessCommandLine contains " /WindowState 0" and ProcessCommandLine contains " /RunAs " and ProcessCommandLine contains " /CommandLine ")

de: In Kaspersky's 2020 Incident Response Analyst Report they listed legitimate tool "Mouse Lock" as being used for both credential access and collection in security incidents.
fp: Legitimate uses of Mouse Lock software
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessVersionInfoProductName contains "Mouse Lock" or ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName contains "Misc314" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Mouse Lock_"

au: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
de: Detects the use of NirCmd tool for command execution, which could be the result of legitimate administrative activity
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\NirCmd.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "NirCmd.exe") or (ProcessCommandLine contains " execmd " or ProcessCommandLine contains ".exe script " or ProcessCommandLine contains ".exe shexec " or ProcessCommandLine contains " runinteractive ")) or ((ProcessCommandLine contains " exec " or ProcessCommandLine contains " exec2 ") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " show " or ProcessCommandLine contains " hide "))

de: Detects usage of namp/zenmap. Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of services running on remote hosts, including those that may be vulnerable to remote software exploitation
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\nmap.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\zennmap.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("nmap.exe", "zennmap.exe"))

de: Detects execution of PUA 'NSSM' (the Non-Sucking Service Manager) which is a legitimate tool for managing Windows services, but is often abused by threat actors to maintain persistence by installing malicious payloads as system services.
fp: NSSM is legitimately used by several applications
Administrators using NSSM for legitimate service management
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\nssm.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoFileDescription =~ "The non-sucking service manager" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "nssm.exe") and (not((FolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\")))
pr: #5810 PUA - NSSM Execution

t: PUA - Potential PE Metadata Tamper Using Rcedit
de: Detects the use of rcedit to potentially alter executable PE metadata properties, which could conceal efforts to rename system utilities for defense evasion.
fp: Legitimate use of the tool by administrators or users to update metadata of a binary
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\rcedit-x64.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\rcedit-x86.exe") or ProcessVersionInfoFileDescription =~ "Edit resources of exe" or ProcessVersionInfoProductName =~ "rcedit") and ProcessCommandLine contains "--set-" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "OriginalFileName" or ProcessCommandLine contains "CompanyName" or ProcessCommandLine contains "FileDescription" or ProcessCommandLine contains "ProductName" or ProcessCommandLine contains "ProductVersion" or ProcessCommandLine contains "LegalCopyright")

de: Detects the execution of Process Hacker based on binary metadata information (Image, Hash, Imphash, etc). Process Hacker is a tool to view and manipulate processes, kernel options and other low level options. Threat actors abused older vulnerable versions to manipulate system processes.
fp: While sometimes 'Process Hacker is used by legitimate administrators, the execution of Process Hacker must be investigated and allowed on a case by case basis
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath contains "\\ProcessHacker_" or FolderPath endswith "\\ProcessHacker.exe" or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("ProcessHacker.exe", "Process Hacker")) or ProcessVersionInfoFileDescription =~ "Process Hacker" or ProcessVersionInfoProductName =~ "Process Hacker" or ((MD5 startswith "68F9B52895F4D34E74112F3129B3B00D" or MD5 startswith "B365AF317AE730A67C936F21432B9C71") or (SHA1 startswith "A0BDFAC3CE1880B32FF9B696458327CE352E3B1D" or SHA1 startswith "C5E2018BF7C0F314FED4FD7FE7E69FA2E648359E") or (SHA256 startswith "D4A0FE56316A2C45B9BA9AC1005363309A3EDC7ACF9E4DF64D326A0FF273E80F" or SHA256 startswith "BD2C2CF0631D881ED382817AFCCE2B093F4E412FFB170A719E2762F250ABFEA4"))

de: Detects the execution of Radmin which can be abused by an adversary to remotely control Windows machines
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessVersionInfoFileDescription =~ "Radmin Viewer" or ProcessVersionInfoProductName =~ "Radmin Viewer" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "Radmin.exe"

de: Detects usage of SoftPerfect's "netscan.exe". An application for scanning networks. It is actively used in-the-wild by threat actors to inspect and understand the network architecture of a victim.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\netscan.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoProductName =~ "Network Scanner" or ProcessVersionInfoFileDescription =~ "Application for scanning networks"

de: Detects the execution of some potentially unwanted tools such as PsExec, Procdump, etc. (part of the Sysinternals suite) via the creation of the "accepteula" registry key.
fp: Legitimate use of SysInternals tools. Filter the legitimate paths used in your environment
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where (RegistryKey contains "\\Active Directory Explorer" or RegistryKey contains "\\Handle" or RegistryKey contains "\\LiveKd" or RegistryKey contains "\\Process Explorer" or RegistryKey contains "\\ProcDump" or RegistryKey contains "\\PsExec" or RegistryKey contains "\\PsLoglist" or RegistryKey contains "\\PsPasswd" or RegistryKey contains "\\SDelete" or RegistryKey contains "\\Sysinternals") and RegistryKey endswith "\\EulaAccepted"

de: Detects the execution of System Informer, a task manager tool to view and manipulate processes, kernel options and other low level operations
fp: System Informer is regularly used legitimately by system administrators or developers. Apply additional filters accordingly
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\SystemInformer.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "SystemInformer.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoFileDescription =~ "System Informer" or ProcessVersionInfoProductName =~ "System Informer" or (MD5 startswith "19426363A37C03C3ED6FEDF57B6696EC" or SHA1 startswith "8B12C6DA8FAC0D5E8AB999C31E5EA04AF32D53DC" or SHA256 startswith "8EE9D84DE50803545937A63C686822388A3338497CDDB660D5D69CF68B68F287")

de: Detects execution of TruffleHog, a tool used to search for secrets in different platforms like Git, Jira, Slack, SharePoint, etc. that could be used maliciously. While it is a legitimate tool, intended for use in CI pipelines and security assessments, It was observed in the Shai- Hulud malware campaign targeting npm packages to steal sensitive information.
fp: Legitimate use of TruffleHog by security teams or developers.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "/trufflehog" or ((ProcessCommandLine contains " docker --image " or ProcessCommandLine contains " Git " or ProcessCommandLine contains " GitHub " or ProcessCommandLine contains " Jira " or ProcessCommandLine contains " Slack " or ProcessCommandLine contains " Confluence " or ProcessCommandLine contains " SharePoint " or ProcessCommandLine contains " s3 " or ProcessCommandLine contains " gcs ") and ProcessCommandLine contains " --results=verified")
pr: #6166 feat: Add PUA - TruffleHog Execution macOS rule

de: Detects the execution of WebBrowserPassView.exe. A password recovery tool that reveals the passwords stored by the following Web browsers, Internet Explorer (Version 4.0 - 11.0), Mozilla Firefox (All Versions), Google Chrome, Safari, and Opera
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessVersionInfoFileDescription =~ "Web Browser Password Viewer" or FolderPath endswith "\\WebBrowserPassView.exe"

t: Publisher Attachment File Dropped In Suspicious Location
de: Detects creation of files with the ".pub" extension in suspicious or uncommon locations. This could be a sign of attackers abusing Publisher documents
fp: Legitimate usage of ".pub" files from those locations
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where (FolderPath contains "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\" or FolderPath contains "\\Users\\Public\\" or FolderPath contains "\\Windows\\Temp\\" or FolderPath contains "C:\\Temp\\") and FolderPath endswith ".pub"

de: Detects the use of the 'Pubprn.vbs' Microsoft signed script to execute commands.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessCommandLine contains "\\pubprn.vbs" and ProcessCommandLine contains "script:"

de: Detects a Python process initiating a network connection. While this often relates to package installation, it can also indicate a potential malicious script communicating with a C&C server.
fp: Legitimate python scripts using the socket library or similar will trigger this. Apply additional filters and perform an initial baseline before deploying.
q:
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\python" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains ".exe") and (not(((RemoteIP =~ "127.0.0.1" and LocalIP =~ "127.0.0.1") or (InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "pip.exe" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "install")))) and (not(((InitiatingProcessParentFileName =~ "conda.exe" and (InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains ":\\ProgramData\\Anaconda3\\Scripts\\conda-script.py" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "update")) or (InitiatingProcessParentFileName =~ "python.exe" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "C:\\ProgramData\\Anaconda3\\Scripts\\jupyter-notebook-script.py"))))

de: Detects execution of python using the "-c" flag. This is could be used as a way to launch a reverse shell or execute live python code.
fp: Python libraries that use a flag starting with "-c". Filter according to your environment
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "python.exe" or (FolderPath endswith "python.exe" or FolderPath endswith "python3.exe" or FolderPath endswith "python2.exe")) and ProcessCommandLine contains " -c") and (not((((InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files\\Python" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Python") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\python.exe" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "-E -s -m ensurepip -U --default-pip") or ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files\\Python" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Python") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "-W ignore::DeprecationWarning" and ProcessCommandLine contains "['install', '--no-cache-dir', '--no-index', '--find-links'," and ProcessCommandLine contains "'--upgrade', 'pip'"))))) and (not(((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\AppData\\Local\\Programs\\Microsoft VS Code\\Code.exe" or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath in~ ("C:\\Program Files\\Microsoft VS Code\\Code.exe", "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Microsoft VS Code\\Code.exe"))) or (ProcessCommandLine contains "<pip-setuptools-caller>" and ProcessCommandLine contains "exec(compile("))))

t: Python Path Configuration File Creation - Linux
de: Detects creation of a Python path configuration file (.pth) in Python library folders, which can be maliciously abused for code execution and persistence. Modules referenced by these files are run at every Python startup (v3.5+), regardless of whether the module is imported by the calling script. Default paths are '\lib\site-packages\*.pth' (Windows) and '/lib/pythonX.Y/site- packages/*.pth' (Unix and macOS).
fp: Although .pth files are discouraged due to potential security implications, these are legitimate files by specification.
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where FolderPath matches regex "(?i)/lib/python3\\.([5-9]|[0-9]{2})/site-packages/" and FolderPath endswith ".pth"

t: Python Path Configuration File Creation - MacOS
de: Detects creation of a Python path configuration file (.pth) in Python library folders, which can be maliciously abused for code execution and persistence. Modules referenced by these files are run at every Python startup (v3.5+), regardless of whether the module is imported by the calling script. Default paths are '\lib\site-packages\*.pth' (Windows) and '/lib/pythonX.Y/site- packages/*.pth' (Unix and macOS).
fp: Although .pth files are discouraged due to potential security implications, these are legitimate files by specification.
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where FolderPath matches regex "(?i)/lib/python3\\.([5-9]|[0-9]{2})/site-packages/" and FolderPath endswith ".pth"

t: Python Path Configuration File Creation - Windows
de: Detects creation of a Python path configuration file (.pth) in Python library folders, which can be maliciously abused for code execution and persistence. Modules referenced by these files are run at every Python startup (v3.5+), regardless of whether the module is imported by the calling script. Default paths are '\lib\site-packages\*.pth' (Windows) and '/lib/pythonX.Y/site- packages/*.pth' (Unix and macOS).
fp: Although .pth files are discouraged due to potential security implications, these are legitimate files by specification.
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where (FolderPath matches regex "(?i)\\\\(venv|python(.+)?)\\\\lib\\\\site-packages\\\\" and FolderPath endswith ".pth") and (not((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\python.exe" and (FolderPath endswith "\\pywin32.pth" or FolderPath endswith "\\distutils-precedence.pth"))))

t: Python Process Spawning Windows Discovery Utilities
de: Detects Python launching Windows system or network discovery utilities. Observed in the LiteLLM 1.107.0 supply-chain compromise, where a malicious "cook.pth" startup hook caused the Python interpreter to import a credential collector that invokes these utilities during interpreter startup, independent of the script being executed.
fp: Network automation or inventory tooling written in Python
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\python.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\pythonw.exe") and (FolderPath endswith "\\systeminfo.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\ipconfig.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\route.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\arp.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\netstat.exe")
pr: #6525 Add detection rules for LiteLLM 1.107.0 cook.pth supply-chain compromise

t: Python Spawning Pretty TTY Via PTY Module
de: Detects a python process calling to the PTY module in order to spawn a pretty tty which could be indicative of potential reverse shell activity.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "/python" or FolderPath endswith "/python2" or FolderPath endswith "/python3") or (FolderPath contains "/python2." or FolderPath contains "/python3.")) and (ProcessCommandLine contains "import pty" or ProcessCommandLine contains "from pty ") and ProcessCommandLine contains "spawn"

t: QoS ThrottleRate Policy Set via PowerShell CommandLine
de: Detects PowerShell invoking New-NetQosPolicy or Set-NetQosPolicy with a ThrottleRateActionBitsPerSecond parameter to potentially set abnormal bandwidth limits on targeted processes. ThrottleRateActionBitsPerSecond is a QoS policy setting that can be used to limit the bandwidth of targeted processes. Tools such as EDRChoker use this to throttle network bandwidth of targeted processes (e.g. EDR agents) to near-zero, silencing telemetry without terminating the process.
fp: Legitimate QoS bandwidth policy management by administrators
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("PowerShell.EXE", "pwsh.dll"))) and (ProcessCommandLine contains "New-NetQosPolicy" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Set-NetQosPolicy") and ProcessCommandLine contains "ThrottleRateActionBitsPerSecond"
pr: #6063 new: edrchoker qos throttle rate modification rules

de: Detects when a Quality of Service (QoS) Throttle Rate policy is created/updated by the Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) provider service (wmiprvse.exe). Threat actors use WMI to remotely script or automate changes. They abuse this feature to choke outbound EDR connection, ultimately bypassing EDR, slow down data leaks to bypass filters, or cause intentional denial- of-service conditions on critical communication apps.
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\wmiprvse.exe" and (RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\Software\\Policies\\Microsoft\\Windows\\QoS.*$" and RegistryKey contains "ThrottleRate")
pr: #6062 new: EDRChoker QoS ThrottleRate Set by WMI

de: Detects usage of "query.exe" a system binary to exfil information such as "sessions" and "processes" for later use
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith ":\\Windows\\System32\\query.exe" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "session >" or ProcessCommandLine contains "process >")

de: Detects Rclone config files being created
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where FolderPath contains ":\\Users\\" and FolderPath contains "\\.config\\rclone\\"

t: RDP Sensitive Settings Changed to Zero
au: Samir Bousseaden, David ANDRE, Roberto Rodriguez @Cyb3rWard0g, Nasreddine Bencherchali
de: Detects tampering of RDP Terminal Service/Server sensitive settings. Such as allowing unauthorized users access to a system via the 'fAllowUnsolicited' or enabling RDP via 'fDenyTSConnections', etc.
fp: Some of the keys mentioned here could be modified by an administrator while setting group policy (it should be investigated either way)
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where (RegistryKey endswith "\\fDenyTSConnections" or RegistryKey endswith "\\fSingleSessionPerUser" or RegistryKey endswith "\\UserAuthentication") and RegistryValueData =~ "DWORD (0x00000000)"

t: Read Contents From Stdin Via Cmd.EXE
de: Detect the use of "<" to read and potentially execute a file via cmd.exe
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "Cmd.Exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe") and ProcessCommandLine contains "<"

t: Rebuild Performance Counter Values Via Lodctr.EXE
de: Detects the execution of "lodctr.exe" to rebuild the performance counter registry values. This can be abused by attackers by providing a malicious config file to overwrite performance counter configuration to confuse and evade monitoring and security solutions.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\lodctr.exe" and ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "LODCTR.EXE") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " -r" or ProcessCommandLine contains " /r" or ProcessCommandLine contains " –r" or ProcessCommandLine contains " —r" or ProcessCommandLine contains " ―r")

t: Recon Command Output Piped To Findstr.EXE
de: Detects the execution of a potential recon command where the results are piped to "findstr". This is meant to trigger on inline calls of "cmd.exe" via the "/c" or "/k" for example. Attackers often time use this technique to extract specific information they require in their reconnaissance phase.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((ProcessCommandLine contains "ipconfig" and ProcessCommandLine contains "|" and ProcessCommandLine contains "find") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "net" and ProcessCommandLine contains "|" and ProcessCommandLine contains "find") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "netstat" and ProcessCommandLine contains "|" and ProcessCommandLine contains "find") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "ping" and ProcessCommandLine contains "|" and ProcessCommandLine contains "find") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "systeminfo" and ProcessCommandLine contains "|" and ProcessCommandLine contains "find") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "tasklist" and ProcessCommandLine contains "|" and ProcessCommandLine contains "find") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "whoami" and ProcessCommandLine contains "|" and ProcessCommandLine contains "find")) and (not((ProcessCommandLine contains "cmd.exe /c TASKLIST /V |" and ProcessCommandLine contains "FIND /I" and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\xampp\\" and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\catalina_start.bat")))

t: Recon Information for Export with Command Prompt
de: Once established within a system or network, an adversary may use automated techniques for collecting internal data.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\tree.com" or FolderPath endswith "\\WMIC.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\doskey.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\sc.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("wmic.exe", "DOSKEY.EXE", "sc.exe"))) and (InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains " > %TEMP%\\" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains " > %TMP%\\")

t: RegAsm.EXE Initiating Network Connection To Public IP
de: Detects "RegAsm.exe" initiating a network connection to public IP adresses
q:
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\regasm.exe" and (not((ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "127.0.0.0/8") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "10.0.0.0/8") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "172.16.0.0/12") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "192.168.0.0/16") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "169.254.0.0/16") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "::1/128") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "fe80::/10") or ipv4_is_in_range(RemoteIP, "fc00::/7"))))

de: Detects the use of a Microsoft signed script 'REGISTER_APP.VBS' to register a VSS/VDS Provider as a COM+ application.
fp: Legitimate usage of the script. Always investigate what's being registered to confirm if it's benign
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessCommandLine contains "\\register_app.vbs" and ProcessCommandLine contains "-register"

de: Detects registry modifications that hide internal tools or functions from the user (malware like Agent Tesla, Hermetic Wiper uses this technique)
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where ((RegistryKey endswith "SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Policies\\Explorer\\HideClock" or RegistryKey endswith "SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Policies\\Explorer\\HideSCAHealth" or RegistryKey endswith "SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Policies\\Explorer\\HideSCANetwork" or RegistryKey endswith "SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Policies\\Explorer\\HideSCAPower" or RegistryKey endswith "SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Policies\\Explorer\\HideSCAVolume") and RegistryValueData =~ "DWORD (0x00000001)") or ((RegistryKey endswith "SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Explorer\\Advanced\\ShowInfoTip" or RegistryKey endswith "SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Explorer\\Advanced\\ShowCompColor") and RegistryValueData =~ "DWORD (0x00000000)")

t: Registry Modification of MS-settings Protocol Handler
de: Detects registry modifications to the 'ms-settings' protocol handler, which is frequently targeted for UAC bypass or persistence. Attackers can modify this registry to execute malicious code with elevated privileges by hijacking the command execution path.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (((FolderPath endswith "\\reg.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "reg.exe") and ProcessCommandLine contains "add") or (((FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.dll"))) and (ProcessCommandLine contains "New-ItemProperty" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Set-ItemProperty" or ProcessCommandLine contains "ni " or ProcessCommandLine contains "sp "))) and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\ms-settings\\shell\\open\\command"

t: Registry Modification to Hidden File Extension
de: Hides the file extension through modification of the registry
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where (RegistryKey endswith "\\SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Explorer\\Advanced\\HideFileExt" and RegistryValueData =~ "DWORD (0x00000001)") or (RegistryKey endswith "\\SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Explorer\\Advanced\\Hidden" and RegistryValueData =~ "DWORD (0x00000002)")

t: Registry Modification to Hidden File Extension
de: Hides the file extension through modification of the registry

| where (RegistryKey endswith "\\SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Explorer\\Advanced\\HideFileExt" and RegistryValueData =~ "DWORD (0x00000001)") or (RegistryKey endswith "\\SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Explorer\\Advanced\\Hidden" and RegistryValueData =~ "DWORD (0x00000002)")
pr: #6279 🩺 add regression data from evtx-attack-samples

t: Registry Set With Crypto-Classes From The "Cryptography" PowerShell Namespace
de: Detects the setting of a registry inside the "\Shell\Open\Command" value with PowerShell classes from the "System.Security.Cryptography" namespace. The PowerShell namespace "System.Security.Cryptography" provides classes for on-the-fly encryption and decryption. These can be used for example in decrypting malicious payload for defense evasion.
fp: Classes are legitimately used, but less so when e.g. parents with low prevalence or decryption of content in temporary folders.
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where RegistryKey contains "\\Shell\\Open\\Command" and (RegistryValueData contains "powershell" or RegistryValueData contains "pwsh") and RegistryValueData contains "System.Security.Cryptography." and (RegistryValueData contains ".AesCryptoServiceProvider" or RegistryValueData contains ".DESCryptoServiceProvider" or RegistryValueData contains ".DSACryptoServiceProvider" or RegistryValueData contains ".RC2CryptoServiceProvider" or RegistryValueData contains ".Rijndael" or RegistryValueData contains ".RSACryptoServiceProvider" or RegistryValueData contains ".TripleDESCryptoServiceProvider")

t: Regsvr32 DLL Execution With Uncommon Extension
de: Detects a "regsvr32" execution where the DLL doesn't contain a common file extension.
fp: Other legitimate extensions currently not in the list either from third party or specific Windows components.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\regsvr32.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "REGSVR32.EXE") and (not(((ProcessCommandLine contains ".ax" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".cpl" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".dll" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".ocx") or isnull(ProcessCommandLine) or ProcessCommandLine =~ ""))) and (not((ProcessCommandLine contains ".ppl" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".bav")))

t: Regsvr32 DLL Execution With Uncommon Extension
de: Detects a "regsvr32" execution where the DLL doesn't contain a common file extension. Threat actors often rename their malicious DLLs to often benign file extensions to avoid detection.
fp: Other legitimate extensions currently not in the list either from third party or specific Windows components.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\regsvr32.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "REGSVR32.EXE") and (not(((ProcessCommandLine contains ".ax" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".cpl" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".dll" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".ocx") or isnull(ProcessCommandLine) or ProcessCommandLine =~ "" or (ProcessCommandLine in~ ("\"C:\\WINDOWS\\system32\\regsvr32.exe\"", "\"C:\\WINDOWS\\SysWOW64\\regsvr32.exe\""))))) and (not((ProcessCommandLine contains ".ppl" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".bav")))

t: Regsvr32 Execution From Potential Suspicious Location
au: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
de: Detects execution of regsvr32 where the DLL is located in a potentially suspicious location.
fp: Some installers might execute "regsvr32" with DLLs located in %TEMP% or in %PROGRAMDATA%. Apply additional filters if necessary.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\regsvr32.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "REGSVR32.EXE") and (ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\ProgramData\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Temp\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Users\\Public\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Windows\\Temp\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\AppData\\Roaming\\")

de: Detects default RemCom service filename which indicates RemCom service installation and execution
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\RemComSvc.exe"

t: Remote Access Tool - Action1 Arbitrary Code Execution and Remote Sessions
de: Detects the execution of Action1 in order to execute arbitrary code or establish a remote session. Action1 is a powerful Remote Monitoring and Management tool that enables users to execute commands, scripts, and binaries. Through the web interface of action1, the administrator must create a new policy or an app to establish remote execution and then points that the agent is installed. Hunting Opportunity 1- Weed Out The Noise When threat actors execute a script, a command, or a binary through these new policies and apps, the names of these become visible in the command line during the execution process. Below is an example of the command line that contains the deployment of a binary through a policy with name "test_app_1": ParentCommandLine: "C:\WINDOWS\Action1\action1_agent.exe schedule:Deploy_App__test_app_1_1681327673425 runaction:0" After establishing a baseline, we can split the command to extract the policy name and group all the policy names and inspect the results with a list of frequency occurrences. Hunting Opportunity 2 - Remote Sessions On Out Of Office Hours If you have admins within your environment using remote sessions to administer endpoints, you can create a threat-hunting query and modify the time of the initiated sessions looking for abnormal activity.
fp: If Action1 is among the approved software in your environment, you might find that this is a noisy query. See description for ideas on how to alter this query and start looking for suspicious activities.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\action1_agent.exe" and FolderPath contains "\\Windows\\Action1\\package_downloads\\") or ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe") and (InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "\\Action1\\scripts\\Run_Command_" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "\\Action1\\scripts\\Run_PowerShell_")) or FolderPath endswith "\\agent1_remote.exe"

t: Remote Access Tool - Ammy Admin Agent Execution
de: Detects the execution of the Ammy Admin RMM agent for remote management.
fp: Legitimate use of Ammy Admin RMM agent for remote management by admins.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe" and ProcessCommandLine contains "AMMYY\\aa_nts.dll\",run"

de: An adversary may use legitimate desktop support and remote access software, such as Team Viewer, Go2Assist, LogMein, AmmyyAdmin, etc, to establish an interactive command and control channel to target systems within networks. These services are commonly used as legitimate technical support software, and may be allowed by application control within a target environment. Remote access tools like VNC, Ammyy, and Teamviewer are used frequently when compared with other legitimate software commonly used by adversaries. (Citation: Symantec Living off the Land)
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\AnyDesk.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\AnyDeskMSI.exe") or ProcessVersionInfoFileDescription =~ "AnyDesk" or ProcessVersionInfoProductName =~ "AnyDesk" or ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName =~ "AnyDesk Software GmbH"

t: Remote Access Tool - AnyDesk Execution With Known Revoked Signing Certificate
au: Sai Prashanth Pulisetti, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
de: Detects the execution of an AnyDesk binary with a version prior to 8.0.8. Prior to version 8.0.8, the Anydesk application used a signing certificate that got compromised by threat actors. Use this rule to detect instances of older versions of Anydesk using the compromised certificate This is recommended in order to avoid attackers leveraging the certificate and signing their binaries to bypass detections.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\AnyDesk.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoFileDescription =~ "AnyDesk" or ProcessVersionInfoProductName =~ "AnyDesk" or ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName =~ "AnyDesk Software GmbH") and (ProcessVersionInfoProductVersion startswith "7.0." or ProcessVersionInfoProductVersion startswith "7.1." or ProcessVersionInfoProductVersion startswith "8.0.1" or ProcessVersionInfoProductVersion startswith "8.0.2" or ProcessVersionInfoProductVersion startswith "8.0.3" or ProcessVersionInfoProductVersion startswith "8.0.4" or ProcessVersionInfoProductVersion startswith "8.0.5" or ProcessVersionInfoProductVersion startswith "8.0.6" or ProcessVersionInfoProductVersion startswith "8.0.7")) and (not((ProcessCommandLine contains " --remove" or ProcessCommandLine contains " --uninstall")))

t: Remote Access Tool - AnyDesk Piped Password Via CLI
de: Detects piping the password to an anydesk instance via CMD and the '--set-password' flag.
fp: Legitimate piping of the password to anydesk
Some FP could occur with similar tools that uses the same command line '--set-password'
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessCommandLine contains "/c " and ProcessCommandLine contains "echo " and ProcessCommandLine contains ".exe --set-password"

t: Remote Access Tool - Cmd.EXE Execution via AnyViewer
de: Detects execution of "cmd.exe" via the AnyViewer RMM agent on a remote management sessions.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\AVCore.exe" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "AVCore.exe\" -d" and FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe"

Remote access tools like VNC, Ammyy, and Teamviewer are used frequently when compared with other legitimate software commonly used by adversaries. (Citation: Symantec Living off the Land)

t: Remote Access Tool - MeshAgent Command Execution via MeshCentral
de: Detects the use of MeshAgent to execute commands on the target host, particularly when threat actors might abuse it to execute commands directly. fp: False positives can be found in environments using MeshAgent for remote management, analysis should prioritize the grandparent process, MeshAgent.exe, and scrutinize the resulting child processes triggered by any suspicious interactive commands directed at the target host.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\meshagent.exe" and (FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe")

t: Remote Management Tool - Ninite Execution From Suspicious Context
de: Detects execution of the Ninite / Ninite Pro software deployment tool from a suspicious parent (browser, mail client, msiexec or script host) or from a user-writable path. fp: Authorized use of Ninite for patch management, especially when launched by an RMM agent or a scheduled task. Baseline its normal parents and paths before deploying broadly.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\NiniteOne.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\NinitePro.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\NiniteAgent.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\Ninite.exe") and ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\chrome.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\msedge.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\firefox.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\outlook.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\msiexec.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\wscript.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\cscript.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe") or (FolderPath contains "\\Users\\" or FolderPath contains "\\AppData\\" or FolderPath contains "\\Downloads\\" or FolderPath contains "\\Temp\\"))

| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\explorer.exe" and (FolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "RUNDLL32.EXE")) and (not((ProcessCommandLine contains " C:\\Windows\\System32\\" or ProcessCommandLine endswith " -localserver 22d8c27b-47a1-48d1-ad08-7da7abd79617")))

t: Rundll32.EXE Calling DllRegisterServer Export Function Explicitly
de: Detects when the DLL export function 'DllRegisterServer' is called in the commandline by Rundll32 explicitly where the DLL is located in a non-standard path.
fp: Legitimate usage as part of application installation, but less likely from e.g. temporary paths.
Not every instance is considered malicious, but this rule will capture the malicious usages.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "RUNDLL32.EXE") and ProcessCommandLine contains "DllRegisterServer") and (not((ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Program Files (x86)" or ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Program Files\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Windows\\System32\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\")))

t: Runtime Read-Write Host-Folder Sharing Via Windows Sandbox CLI
de: Detects use of the wsb.exe share subcommand with --allow-write, which dynamically maps a host folder into a running Windows Sandbox with sandbox-to-host write permissions.
fp: Interactive Sandbox users adding folders to a running sandbox via the wsb.exe CLI as documented Microsoft workflow
Automation that intentionally grants write-back access to a sandbox for output collection
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\wsb.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "wsb.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " share " and ProcessCommandLine contains "--allow-write")

au: Entroprism (Beijing Yijun Foreign Trade Co., Ltd.)
de: Detects attempts to identify virtualization or sandbox environments via VM artifact queries or macOS hardware model probing.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessCommandLine contains "VMware" or ProcessCommandLine contains "VBoxService" or ProcessCommandLine contains "vbox" or ProcessCommandLine contains "qemu-ga") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "sysctl hw.model" or ProcessCommandLine contains "ioreg -l")

t: Schedule Task Creation From Env Variable Or Potentially Suspicious Path Via Schtasks.EXE
de: Detects Schtask creations that point to a suspicious folder or an environment variable often used by malware
fp: Benign scheduled tasks creations or executions that happen often during software installations
Software that uses the AppData folder and scheduled tasks to update the software in the AppData folders
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (((FolderPath endswith "\\schtasks.exe" and (ProcessCommandLine contains " -create " or ProcessCommandLine contains " /create " or ProcessCommandLine contains " –create " or ProcessCommandLine contains " —create " or ProcessCommandLine contains " ―create ")) and (ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Perflogs" or ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Users\\All Users\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Users\\Default\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Users\\Public" or ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Windows\\Temp" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\AppData\\Local\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\AppData\\Roaming\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "%AppData%" or ProcessCommandLine contains "%Public%")) or (InitiatingProcessCommandLine endswith "\\svchost.exe -k netsvcs -p -s Schedule" and (ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Perflogs" or ProcessCommandLine contains ":\\Windows\\Temp" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Users\\Public" or ProcessCommandLine contains "%Public%"))) and (not(((InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "unattended.ini" or ProcessCommandLine contains "update_task.xml") or ProcessCommandLine contains "/Create /TN TVInstallRestore /TR" or (ProcessCommandLine contains "/Create /Xml " and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Temp\\.CR." and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Avira_Security_Installation.xml") or ((ProcessCommandLine contains "/Create /F /TN" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/Xml " and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Temp\\" and ProcessCommandLine contains "Avira_") and (ProcessCommandLine contains ".tmp\\UpdateFallbackTask.xml" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".tmp\\WatchdogServiceControlManagerTimeout.xml" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".tmp\\SystrayAutostart.xml" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".tmp\\MaintenanceTask.xml")) or (ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Temp\\" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/Create /TN \"klcp_update\" /XML " and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\klcp_update_task.xml"))))

de: Detects Schtask creations that point to a suspicious folder or an environment variable often used by malware

q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "/crontab" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/tmp/"

t: Scheduled Task Creation From Potential Suspicious Parent Location
de: Detects the execution of "schtasks.exe" from a parent that is located in a potentially suspicious location. Multiple malware strains were seen exhibiting a similar behavior in order to achieve persistence.
fp: Software installers that run from temporary folders and also install scheduled tasks
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains ":\\Temp\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\AppData\\Local\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\AppData\\Roaming\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\Temporary Internet" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\Users\\Public\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\Windows\\Temp\\") and FolderPath endswith "\\schtasks.exe" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/Create ") and (not((ProcessCommandLine contains "update_task.xml" or ProcessCommandLine contains "unattended.ini")))

t: Scheduled Task Executing Payload from Registry
de: Detects the creation of a schtasks that potentially executes a payload stored in the Windows Registry using PowerShell.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\schtasks.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "schtasks.exe") and ProcessCommandLine contains "/Create" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "Get-ItemProperty" or ProcessCommandLine contains " gp ") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "HKCU:" or ProcessCommandLine contains "HKLM:" or ProcessCommandLine contains "registry::" or ProcessCommandLine contains "HKEY_")) and (not((ProcessCommandLine contains "FromBase64String" or ProcessCommandLine contains "encodedcommand")))

de: Detects the creation of screensaver files (.scr) outside of system folders. Attackers may execute an application as an ".SCR" file using "rundll32.exe desk.cpl,InstallScreenSaver" for example.
fp: The installation of new screen savers by third party software
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where FolderPath endswith ".scr" and (not((FolderPath contains ":\\$WINDOWS.~BT\\NewOS\\" or FolderPath contains ":\\Windows\\System32\\" or FolderPath contains ":\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\" or FolderPath contains ":\\Windows\\WinSxS\\" or FolderPath contains ":\\WUDownloadCache\\")))

de: Detects execution of Windows Problem Steps Recorder (psr.exe), a utility used to record the user screen and clicks.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\Psr.exe" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "/start" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-start")

de: An adversary may use legitimate desktop support and remote access software, such as Team Viewer, Go2Assist, LogMein, AmmyyAdmin, etc, to establish an interactive command and control channel to target systems within networks. These services are commonly used as legitimate technical support software, and may be allowed by application control within a target environment. Remote access tools like VNC, Ammyy, and Teamviewer are used frequently when compared with other legitimate software commonly used by adversaries. (Citation: Symantec Living off the Land)
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where FolderPath contains "\\Bin\\ScreenConnect."

au: Matt Anderson, Andrew Schwartz, Caleb Stewart, Huntress
de: Detects file modifications to the temporary xml user database file indicating local user modification in the ScreenConnect server. This will occur during exploitation of the ScreenConnect Authentication Bypass vulnerability (CVE-2024-1709) in versions <23.9.8, but may also be observed when making legitimate modifications to local users or permissions.
fp: This will occur legitimately as well and will result in some benign activity.
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where FolderPath endswith ".xml" and (FolderPath contains "Temp" and FolderPath contains "ScreenConnect") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\ScreenConnect.Service.exe"

de: Detects registry key established after masqueraded .scr file execution using Rundll32 through desk.cpl
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe" and (RegistryKey contains "\\Control Panel\\Desktop\\SCRNSAVE.EXE" and RegistryValueData endswith ".scr") and (not((RegistryValueData contains "C:\\Windows\\System32\\" or RegistryValueData contains "C:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\")))

t: Scripted Diagnostics Turn Off Check Enabled - Registry
de: Detects enabling TurnOffCheck which can be used to bypass defense of MSDT Follina vulnerability
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where RegistryKey endswith "\\Policies\\Microsoft\\Windows\\ScriptedDiagnostics\\TurnOffCheck" and RegistryValueData =~ "DWORD (0x00000001)"

au: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
de: Detects various command line and scripting engines/processes such as "PowerShell", "Wscript", "Cmd", etc. spawning a "regsvr32" instance.
fp: Legitimate ".bat", ".hta", ".ps1" or ".vbs" scripts leverage legitimately often. Apply additional filter and exclusions as necessary
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\cscript.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\mshta.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\powershell_ise.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\wscript.exe") and FolderPath endswith "\\regsvr32.exe") and (not((InitiatingProcessFolderPath =~ "C:\\Windows\\System32\\cmd.exe" and ProcessCommandLine endswith " /s C:\\Windows\\System32\\RpcProxy\\RpcProxy.dll")))

au: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
de: Detects various command line and scripting engines/processes such as "PowerShell", "Wscript", "Cmd", etc. spawning a "regsvr32" instance.

de: A General detection for sdclt spawning new processes. This could be an indicator of sdclt being used for bypass UAC techniques.
