DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\sdclt.exe"

de: Detects usage of system utilities (only grep for now) to discover security software discovery
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath =~ "/usr/bin/grep" and ((ProcessCommandLine contains "nessusd" or ProcessCommandLine contains "santad" or ProcessCommandLine contains "CbDefense" or ProcessCommandLine contains "falcond" or ProcessCommandLine contains "td-agent" or ProcessCommandLine contains "packetbeat" or ProcessCommandLine contains "filebeat" or ProcessCommandLine contains "auditbeat" or ProcessCommandLine contains "osqueryd" or ProcessCommandLine contains "BlockBlock" or ProcessCommandLine contains "LuLu") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "Little" and ProcessCommandLine contains "Snitch"))

t: Security Tools Keyword Lookup Via Findstr.EXE
de: Detects execution of "findstr" to search for common names of security tools. Attackers often pipe the results of recon commands such as "tasklist" or "whoami" to "findstr" in order to filter out the results. This detection focuses on the keywords that the attacker might use as a filter.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\find.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\findstr.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("FIND.EXE", "FINDSTR.EXE"))) and (ProcessCommandLine endswith " avira" or ProcessCommandLine endswith " avira\"" or ProcessCommandLine endswith " cb" or ProcessCommandLine endswith " cb\"" or ProcessCommandLine endswith " cylance" or ProcessCommandLine endswith " cylance\"" or ProcessCommandLine endswith " defender" or ProcessCommandLine endswith " defender\"" or ProcessCommandLine endswith " kaspersky" or ProcessCommandLine endswith " kaspersky\"" or ProcessCommandLine endswith " kes" or ProcessCommandLine endswith " kes\"" or ProcessCommandLine endswith " mc" or ProcessCommandLine endswith " mc\"" or ProcessCommandLine endswith " sec" or ProcessCommandLine endswith " sec\"" or ProcessCommandLine endswith " sentinel" or ProcessCommandLine endswith " sentinel\"" or ProcessCommandLine endswith " symantec" or ProcessCommandLine endswith " symantec\"" or ProcessCommandLine endswith " virus" or ProcessCommandLine endswith " virus\"")

t: Self Extraction Directive File Created In Potentially Suspicious Location
de: Detects the creation of Self Extraction Directive files (.sed) in a potentially suspicious location. These files are used by the "iexpress.exe" utility in order to create self extracting packages. Attackers were seen abusing this utility and creating PE files with embedded ".sed" entries.
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where (FolderPath contains ":\\ProgramData\\" or FolderPath contains ":\\Temp\\" or FolderPath contains ":\\Windows\\System32\\Tasks\\" or FolderPath contains ":\\Windows\\Tasks\\" or FolderPath contains ":\\Windows\\Temp\\" or FolderPath contains "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\") and FolderPath endswith ".sed"

t: Sensitive Data Archived Via Ditto - MacOS
de: Detects the "ditto" utility archiving a path that holds credentials, browser secrets or cryptocurrency wallet data. "ditto" is Apple's own copy and archive tool and preserves resource forks and extended attributes, which is why macOS infostealers use it to stage collected data into a single archive before exfiltration. AMOS collects Keychain files, browser credentials and wallet data and compresses them with "ditto" into an archive in "/tmp" prior to upload.
fp: Backup or migration tooling that archives the Keychain directory or SSH keys on a schedule
A user archiving their own SSH keys or browser profile before moving to another machine
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "/ditto" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "/Library/Keychains" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/.ssh" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Login Data" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/Cookies" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Extension Settings" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/Exodus" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/Electrum" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/Ledger Live")
pr: #6234 Add macOS rule for sensitive data archived via ditto

t: Service Binary in User Controlled Folder
au: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
de: Detects the setting of the "ImagePath" value of a service registry key to a path controlled by a non-administrator user such as "\AppData\" or "\ProgramData\". Attackers often use such directories for staging purposes. This rule might also trigger on badly written software, where if an attacker controls an auto starting service, they might achieve persistence or privilege escalation. Note that while ProgramData is a user controlled folder, software might apply strict ACLs which makes them only accessible to admin users. Remove such folders via filters if you experience a lot of noise.
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where ((RegistryKey contains "ControlSet" and RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\Services.*$") and RegistryKey endswith "\\ImagePath" and (RegistryValueData contains ":\\ProgramData\\" or RegistryValueData contains "\\AppData\\Local\\" or RegistryValueData contains "\\AppData\\Roaming\\")) and (not(((RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\Services\\WinDefend.*$" or RegistryKey contains "\\Services\\MpKs") and RegistryValueData contains "C:\\ProgramData\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender\\"))) and (not(((RegistryKey contains "\\Services\\ZoomCptService" and RegistryValueData contains "C:\\Program Files\\Common Files\\Zoom\\Support\\CptService.exe") or (RegistryKey contains "\\Services\\MBAMInstallerService" and (RegistryValueData contains "C:\\Users\\" and RegistryValueData contains "AppData\\Local\\Temp\\MBAMInstallerService.exe")))))

de: An adversary might use WMI to check if a certain remote service is running on a remote device. When the test completes, a service information will be displayed on the screen if it exists. A common feedback message is that "No instance(s) Available" if the service queried is not running. A common error message is "Node - (provided IP or default) ERROR Description =The RPC server is unavailable" if the provided remote host is unreachable
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\WMIC.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "wmic.exe") and ProcessCommandLine contains "service") and (not(((ProcessCommandLine contains "stopservice" or ProcessCommandLine contains "startservice") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "Change" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Create" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Delete" or ProcessCommandLine contains "PauseService" or ProcessCommandLine contains "ResumeService" or ProcessCommandLine contains "SetSecurityDescriptor" or ProcessCommandLine contains "StartService" or ProcessCommandLine contains "StopService" or ProcessCommandLine contains "UserControlService"))))

t: Service Security Descriptor Tampering Via Sc.EXE
de: Detection of sc.exe utility adding a new service with special permission which hides that service.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\sc.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "sc.exe") and ProcessCommandLine contains "sdset"

de: Detects usage of wmic to start or stop a service
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "wmic.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\WMIC.exe") and ((ProcessCommandLine contains " service " and ProcessCommandLine contains " call ") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "stopservice" or ProcessCommandLine contains "startservice"))

t: Service StartupType Change Via PowerShell Set-Service
de: Detects the use of the PowerShell "Set-Service" cmdlet to change the startup type of a service to "disabled" or "manual"
fp: False positives may occur with troubleshooting scripts
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "PowerShell.EXE") and ((ProcessCommandLine contains "Set-Service" and ProcessCommandLine contains "-StartupType") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "Disabled" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Manual"))

de: Detect the use of "sc.exe" to change the startup type of a service to "disabled" or "demand"
fp: False positives may occur with troubleshooting scripts
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\sc.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "sc.exe") and ((ProcessCommandLine contains " config " and ProcessCommandLine contains "start") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "disabled" or ProcessCommandLine contains "demand"))

de: Detects changes to the "ServiceDLL" value related to a service in the registry. This is often used as a method of persistence.
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where ((RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\System.*$" and RegistryKey contains "ControlSet" and RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\Services.*$") and RegistryKey endswith "\\Parameters\\ServiceDll") and (not((RegistryValueData =~ "C:\\Windows\\system32\\spool\\drivers\\x64\\3\\PrintConfig.dll" or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\regsvr32.exe" and RegistryKey endswith "\\Services\\PrintNotify\\Parameters\\ServiceDll" and RegistryValueData startswith "C:\\WINDOWS\\System32\\DriverStore\\FileRepository\\" and RegistryValueData endswith "\\arm64\\PrintConfig.dll") or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath =~ "C:\\Windows\\system32\\lsass.exe" and RegistryKey endswith "\\Services\\NTDS\\Parameters\\ServiceDll" and RegistryValueData =~ "%%systemroot%%\\system32\\ntdsa.dll") or InitiatingProcessFolderPath =~ "C:\\Windows\\System32\\poqexec.exe"))) and (not((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\regsvr32.exe" and RegistryValueData =~ "C:\\Windows\\System32\\STAgent.dll")))

de: Detects changes to the "ServiceDLL" value related to a service in the registry. This is often used as a method of persistence.
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where ((RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\System.*$" and RegistryKey contains "ControlSet" and RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\Services.*$") and RegistryKey endswith "\\Parameters\\ServiceDll") and (not((RegistryValueData =~ "C:\\Windows\\system32\\spool\\drivers\\x64\\3\\PrintConfig.dll" or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\regsvr32.exe" and RegistryKey endswith "\\Services\\PrintNotify\\Parameters\\ServiceDll" and RegistryValueData startswith "C:\\WINDOWS\\System32\\DriverStore\\FileRepository\\" and RegistryValueData endswith "\\arm64\\PrintConfig.dll") or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath =~ "C:\\Windows\\system32\\lsass.exe" and RegistryKey endswith "\\Services\\NTDS\\Parameters\\ServiceDll" and RegistryValueData =~ "%%systemroot%%\\system32\\ntdsa.dll") or InitiatingProcessFolderPath =~ "C:\\Windows\\System32\\poqexec.exe"))) and (not((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\regsvr32.exe" and RegistryValueData =~ "C:\\Windows\\System32\\STAgent.dll")))
pr: #6279 🩺 add regression data from evtx-attack-samples

au: Victor Sergeev, Daniil Yugoslavskiy, Gleb Sukhodolskiy, Timur Zinniatullin, oscd.community, Tim Shelton, frack113 (split)
de: Detects modification of autostart extensibility point (ASEP) in registry.
fp: Legitimate software automatically (mostly, during installation) sets up autorun keys for legitimate reason
Legitimate administrator sets up autorun keys for legitimate reason
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where RegistryKey contains "\\System\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\Session Manager" and (RegistryKey contains "\\SetupExecute" or RegistryKey contains "\\S0InitialCommand" or RegistryKey contains "\\KnownDlls" or RegistryKey contains "\\Execute" or RegistryKey contains "\\BootExecute" or RegistryKey contains "\\AppCertDlls") and (not(RegistryValueData =~ "(Empty)"))

de: Detects the execution of "Setup16.EXE" and old installation utility with a custom ".lst" file. These ".lst" file can contain references to external program that "Setup16.EXE" will execute. Attackers and adversaries might leverage this as a living of the land utility.
fp: On modern Windows system, the "Setup16" utility is practically never used, hence false positive should be very rare.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath =~ "C:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\setup16.exe" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains " -m ") and (not(FolderPath startswith "C:\\~MSSETUP.T\\"))

t: Shadow Copies Creation Using Operating Systems Utilities
de: Shadow Copies creation using operating systems utilities, possible credential access
fp: Legitimate administrator working with shadow copies, access for backup purposes
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\wmic.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\vssadmin.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("PowerShell.EXE", "pwsh.dll", "wmic.exe", "VSSADMIN.EXE"))) and (ProcessCommandLine contains "shadow" and ProcessCommandLine contains "create")

t: Shell Binary Created Outside Standard Binary Paths
de: Detects creation of shell binary files (bash, sh, dash, zsh, ksh, fish, etc.) in paths outside standard system binary directories. Dropping a shell binary into a writable location such as /tmp, /home, or /dev/shm is a common step in privilege escalation chains — for example, an exploit postinst script creating a SUID bash copy (CVE-2026-41651) or an attacker staging a shell for later execution. This complements the corresponding process_creation rule by catching the file drop before execution occurs.
fp: Package managers installing shells to custom prefixes (e.g. /opt, /snap, /nix)
Container image builds writing shell binaries to overlay mounts
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "/bash" or FolderPath endswith "/sh" or FolderPath endswith "/dash" or FolderPath endswith "/zsh" or FolderPath endswith "/ksh" or FolderPath endswith "/mksh" or FolderPath endswith "/csh" or FolderPath endswith "/tcsh" or FolderPath endswith "/fish") and (not((FolderPath startswith "/bin/" or FolderPath startswith "/usr/bin/" or FolderPath startswith "/sbin/" or FolderPath startswith "/usr/sbin/" or FolderPath startswith "/usr/local/bin/" or FolderPath startswith "/usr/local/sbin/" or FolderPath startswith "/mnt/")))
pr: #5960 new: CVE-2026-41651 Pack2TheRoot detection rules and generic Linux LPE coverage

de: Detects the use of the "apt" and "apt-get" commands to execute a shell or proxy commands. Such behavior may be associated with privilege escalation, unauthorized command execution, or to break out from restricted environments.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "/apt" or FolderPath endswith "/apt-get") and ProcessCommandLine contains "APT::Update::Pre-Invoke::="

t: Shell Process Executed Outside Standard Binary Paths
de: Detects shell processes (bash, sh, dash, zsh, ksh, fish, etc.) executed from paths outside standard system binary directories. Legitimate shells reside under /bin, /usr/bin, or /usr/local/bin or some mounted overlay of those paths. Execution from writable locations such as /tmp, /home, /dev/shm, or /var is a strong indicator of a dropped SUID shell, a staged payload, or a container/namespace escape technique.
fp: Custom shell installations in non-standard prefix paths (e.g. /opt, /snap, /nix)
Container runtimes with overlayfs mounts that remap /bin
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "/bash" or FolderPath endswith "/sh" or FolderPath endswith "/dash" or FolderPath endswith "/zsh" or FolderPath endswith "/ksh" or FolderPath endswith "/mksh" or FolderPath endswith "/csh" or FolderPath endswith "/tcsh" or FolderPath endswith "/fish") and (not((FolderPath startswith "/bin/" or FolderPath startswith "/usr/bin/" or FolderPath startswith "/sbin/" or FolderPath startswith "/usr/sbin/" or FolderPath startswith "/usr/local/bin/" or FolderPath startswith "/usr/local/sbin/" or FolderPath startswith "/mnt/")))
pr: #5960 new: CVE-2026-41651 Pack2TheRoot detection rules and generic Linux LPE coverage

de: Detects shell spawned from Java host process, which could be a sign of exploitation (e.g. log4j exploitation)
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\java.exe" and (FolderPath endswith "\\bash.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe")) and (not((InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "build" and ProcessCommandLine contains "build")))

t: Shred with Zero-Fill Flag Used to Conceal Deletion
de: Detects use of shred with the -z (--zero) flag, which adds a final zero-fill pass after random overwrites to hide the fact that shred was used at all. Without this flag, the random-pattern overwrite can be identified forensically as evidence of shred execution. The -z flag is a deliberate attempt to obscure anti-forensic activity, making it a stronger indicator of malicious intent than shred alone.
fp: Authorized secure data sanitization in regulated environments
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "/shred" and ProcessCommandLine matches regex "\\s(-[A-ya-y]{0,2}z|--zero)"
pr: #6242 update: linux anti forensics rules

de: Detects the mounting of Windows SMB shares over QUIC, which can be an unexpected event in some enterprise environments.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\net.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\net1.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("net.exe", "net1.exe"))) and ProcessCommandLine contains "/TRANSPORT:QUIC"

t: SQL Client Tools PowerShell Session Detection
de: This rule detects execution of a PowerShell code through the sqltoolsps.exe utility, which is included in the standard set of utilities supplied with the Microsoft SQL Server Management studio. Script blocks are not logged in this case, so this utility helps to bypass protection mechanisms based on the analysis of these logs.
fp: Direct PS command execution through SQLToolsPS.exe is uncommon, childprocess sqltoolsps.exe spawned by smss.exe is a legitimate action.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\sqltoolsps.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\sqltoolsps.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "sqltoolsps.exe") and (not(InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\smss.exe"))

de: Detects use of the chattr utility to add immutable or append-only attributes to an SSH authorized_keys file. Threat actors may use this after planting a public key to make their persistence harder to remove.
fp: Administrators intentionally protecting approved SSH authorized_keys files
Configuration-management or hardening tools applying immutable file attributes
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "/chattr" or ProcessCommandLine contains "chattr ") and ProcessCommandLine contains "/.ssh/authorized_keys" and (ProcessCommandLine contains " +i" or ProcessCommandLine contains " +a")
pr: #6229 new: SSH Authorized Keys Made Immutable

de: Detects the creation or modification of the 'authorized_keys' file on Linux systems. Attackers often modify this file to maintain persistence by adding their own public key to a user's authorized_keys file.
fp: Configuration management tools (Ansible, Chef, Puppet) managing SSH keys
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "/.ssh/authorized_keys" and (not(InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/sshd"))
pr: #6186 new: SSH Authorized Keys Modification

t: SSH Tunneling via SSH Client on Windows
de: Detects the use of SSH clients on Windows (PuTTY, OpenSSH) to create SSH tunnels, a technique commonly abused to relay traffic into a network, expose internal services to a remote host, or pivot into an otherwise unreachable segment.
fp: Legitimate SSH tunneling by system administrators or developers
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\putty.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\plink.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " -L" or ProcessCommandLine contains " -R" or ProcessCommandLine contains " -D")) or (FolderPath endswith "\\ssh.exe" and (ProcessCommandLine contains " -L" or ProcessCommandLine contains " -R" or ProcessCommandLine contains " -D"))
pr: #5747 3 New rules

t: Start of NT Virtual DOS Machine
de: Ntvdm.exe allows the execution of 16-bit Windows applications on 32-bit Windows operating systems, as well as the execution of both 16-bit and 32-bit DOS applications
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\ntvdm.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\csrstub.exe"

de: A General detection for files being created in the Windows startup directory. This could be an indicator of persistence.
fp: FP could be caused by legitimate application writing shortcuts for example. This folder should always be inspected to make sure that all the files in there are legitimate
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where FolderPath contains "\\Microsoft\\Windows\\Start Menu\\Programs\\StartUp" and (not(((InitiatingProcessFolderPath in~ ("C:\\Windows\\System32\\wuauclt.exe", "C:\\Windows\\uus\\ARM64\\wuaucltcore.exe")) or (FolderPath startswith "C:\\$WINDOWS.~BT\\NewOS\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\$WinREAgent\\Scratch\\Mount\\")))) and (not((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\ONENOTE.EXE" and FolderPath endswith "\\Send to OneNote.lnk")))

de: A General detection for files being created in the Windows startup directory. This could be an indicator of persistence.
fp: FP could be caused by legitimate application writing shortcuts for example. This folder should always be inspected to make sure that all the files in there are legitimate
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where FolderPath contains "\\Microsoft\\Windows\\Start Menu\\Programs\\StartUp" and (not(((InitiatingProcessFolderPath in~ ("C:\\Windows\\System32\\wuauclt.exe", "C:\\Windows\\uus\\ARM64\\wuaucltcore.exe")) or (FolderPath startswith "C:\\$WINDOWS.~BT\\NewOS\\" or FolderPath startswith "C:\\$WinREAgent\\Scratch\\Mount\\")))) and (not((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\ONENOTE.EXE" and FolderPath endswith "\\Send to OneNote.lnk")))
pr: #6279 🩺 add regression data from evtx-attack-samples

t: Startup Items Enumeration Via CommandLine Utility
de: Detects enumeration of startup items on Windows via WMIC or PowerShell WMI/CIM cmdlets. Startup items are programs configured to run automatically at boot. Attackers may enumerate them during reconnaissance or to verify their own persistence mechanisms have been added successfully.
fp: Legitimate administration and endpoint management activity (SCCM, Intune, inventory scripts).
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\wmic.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "wmic.exe") and ProcessCommandLine contains " startup " and (ProcessCommandLine contains " get " or ProcessCommandLine contains " list ")) or (((FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("PowerShell.EXE", "pwsh.dll"))) and (ProcessCommandLine contains "Get-CimInstance" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Get-WmiObject" or ProcessCommandLine contains "gwmi " or ProcessCommandLine contains "gcim ") and ProcessCommandLine contains "Win32_StartupCommand")
pr: #6040 new: windows discovery rules

de: Detects file renames where the target filename uses an uncommon double extension. Could indicate potential ransomware activity renaming files and adding a custom extension to the encrypted files, such as ".jpg.crypted", ".docx.locky", etc.
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where ((PreviousFileName endswith ".doc" or PreviousFileName endswith ".docx" or PreviousFileName endswith ".jpeg" or PreviousFileName endswith ".jpg" or PreviousFileName endswith ".lnk" or PreviousFileName endswith ".pdf" or PreviousFileName endswith ".png" or PreviousFileName endswith ".pst" or PreviousFileName endswith ".rtf" or PreviousFileName endswith ".xls" or PreviousFileName endswith ".xlsx") and (FolderPath contains ".doc." or FolderPath contains ".docx." or FolderPath contains ".jpeg." or FolderPath contains ".jpg." or FolderPath contains ".lnk." or FolderPath contains ".pdf." or FolderPath contains ".png." or FolderPath contains ".pst." or FolderPath contains ".rtf." or FolderPath contains ".xls." or FolderPath contains ".xlsx.")) and (not((FolderPath endswith ".backup" or FolderPath endswith ".bak" or FolderPath endswith ".old" or FolderPath endswith ".orig" or FolderPath endswith ".temp" or FolderPath endswith ".tmp"))) and (not((FolderPath contains ":\\ProgramData\\Anaconda3\\" and FolderPath endswith ".c~")))

de: Detects suspicious child processes spawned from browsers. This could be a result of a potential web browser exploitation.
fp: Legitimate browser install, update and recovery scripts
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "com.apple.WebKit.WebContent" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "firefox" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "Google Chrome Helper" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "Google Chrome" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "Microsoft Edge" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "Opera" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "Safari" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "Tor Browser") and (FolderPath endswith "/bash" or FolderPath endswith "/curl" or FolderPath endswith "/dash" or FolderPath endswith "/ksh" or FolderPath endswith "/osascript" or FolderPath endswith "/perl" or FolderPath endswith "/php" or FolderPath endswith "/pwsh" or FolderPath endswith "/python" or FolderPath endswith "/sh" or FolderPath endswith "/tcsh" or FolderPath endswith "/wget" or FolderPath endswith "/zsh")) and (not((ProcessCommandLine contains "--defaults-torrc" or ProcessCommandLine matches regex ".*/Library/Application Support/Microsoft/MAU.*/Microsoft AutoUpdate\\.app/Contents/MacOS/msupdate.*" or ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "Google Chrome Helper" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "Google Chrome") and ((ProcessCommandLine contains "/Volumes/Google Chrome/Google Chrome.app/Contents/Frameworks/" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/Resources/install.sh") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/Frameworks/Google Chrome Framework.framework/" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/Resources/keystone_promote_preflight.sh") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/Frameworks/Google Chrome Framework.framework/" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/Resources/keystone_promote_postflight.sh"))) or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "Microsoft Edge" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "IOPlatformExpertDevice" or ProcessCommandLine contains "hw.model")) or ((InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "Google Chrome Helper" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "Google Chrome") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "/Users/" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/recovery/" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/ChromeRecovery"))))) and (not((isnull(ProcessCommandLine) or ProcessCommandLine =~ "")))

t: Suspicious Cabinet File Execution Via Msdt.EXE
de: Detects execution of msdt.exe using the "cab" flag which could indicates suspicious diagcab files with embedded answer files leveraging CVE-2022-30190
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\msdt.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "msdt.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " -cab " or ProcessCommandLine contains " /cab " or ProcessCommandLine contains " –cab " or ProcessCommandLine contains " —cab " or ProcessCommandLine contains " ―cab ")

de: Detects "ntsd.exe" (Microsoft NT Symbolic Debugger) spawning a shell or a common LOLBIN as a child process. Attackers can abuse this signed debugger to proxy execution of arbitrary commands, for example via the "-g" flag.
fp: Developers debugging scripts or command-line tools with ntsd
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\ntsd.exe" and ((FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\cscript.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\mshta.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\regsvr32.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\wscript.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("Cmd.Exe", "cscript.exe", "MSHTA.EXE", "PowerShell.EXE", "pwsh.dll", "REGSVR32.EXE", "RUNDLL32.EXE", "wscript.exe")))
pr: #6530 Add rules for proxy execution via Ntsd, PIX and UE-V AppLauncher

t: Suspicious Child Process Of PIX Engine Host
de: Detects "WinPixEngineHost.exe", the launcher component of Microsoft PIX on Windows, spawning a shell or a common LOLBIN as a child process. Attackers can abuse "pixtool.exe launch" to proxy execution of arbitrary binaries through this signed developer tool. The target process is started by "WinPixEngineHost.exe" rather than by "pixtool.exe" itself, so this rule monitors the engine host as the parent.
fp: Developers using PIX to capture a script host or shell-launched application
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\WinPixEngineHost.exe" and ((FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\cscript.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\mshta.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\regsvr32.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\wscript.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("Cmd.Exe", "cscript.exe", "MSHTA.EXE", "PowerShell.EXE", "pwsh.dll", "REGSVR32.EXE", "RUNDLL32.EXE", "wscript.exe")))
pr: #6530 Add rules for proxy execution via Ntsd, PIX and UE-V AppLauncher

t: Suspicious Child Process Of UE-V AppLauncher
de: Detects "AppLauncher.exe", part of the Microsoft User Experience Virtualization (UE-V) Template Generator in the Windows ADK, spawning a shell or a common LOLBIN as a child process. Attackers can abuse this signed tool to proxy execution of arbitrary binaries.
fp: Administrators generating UE-V settings location templates for a script host or shell-based application
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\Microsoft User Experience Virtualization\\Management\\AppLauncher.exe" and ((FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\cscript.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\mshta.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\regsvr32.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\wscript.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("Cmd.Exe", "cscript.exe", "MSHTA.EXE", "PowerShell.EXE", "pwsh.dll", "REGSVR32.EXE", "RUNDLL32.EXE", "wscript.exe")))
pr: #6530 Add rules for proxy execution via Ntsd, PIX and UE-V AppLauncher

t: Suspicious Child Process Spawned By IntelliTrace.EXE
de: Detects suspicious command and script interpreters spawned by the Microsoft Visual Studio IntelliTrace utility. IntelliTrace supports launching an arbitrary executable for diagnostic tracing and may be abused to proxy execution through a Microsoft-signed developer utility.
fp: Legitimate Visual Studio diagnostic workflows that intentionally trace command or script interpreters
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\IntelliTrace.exe" and (FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\cscript.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\mshta.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\wscript.exe")
pr: #6426 New Rule: Suspicious Child Process Spawned By IntelliTrace.EXE

au: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Jonhnathan Ribeiro, oscd.community
de: Detects a code page switch in command line or batch scripts to a rare language
fp: Administrative activity (adjust code pages according to your organization's region)
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\chcp.com" and (ProcessCommandLine endswith " 936" or ProcessCommandLine endswith " 1258")

t: Suspicious Copy From or To System Directory
au: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Markus Neis, Tim Shelton (HAWK.IO), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
de: Detects a suspicious copy operation that tries to copy a program from system (System32, SysWOW64, WinSxS) directories to another on disk. Often used to move LOLBINs such as 'certutil' or 'desktopimgdownldr' to a different location with a different name in order to bypass detections based on locations.
fp: Depend on scripts and administrative tools used in the monitored environment (For example an admin scripts like https://www.itexperience.net/sccm-batch-files-and-32-bits-processes-on-64-bits-os/)
When cmd.exe and xcopy.exe are called directly
When the command contains the keywords but not in the correct order
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" and ProcessCommandLine contains "copy ") or ((FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "copy-item" or ProcessCommandLine contains " copy " or ProcessCommandLine contains "cpi " or ProcessCommandLine contains " cp ")) or ((FolderPath endswith "\\robocopy.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\xcopy.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("robocopy.exe", "XCOPY.EXE")))) and ProcessCommandLine matches regex "(?i)\\s['\"]?C:\\\\Windows\\\\(?:System32|SysWOW64|WinSxS)" and (not((FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "/c copy" and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\Temp\\" and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\avira_system_speedup.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "C:\\Program Files\\Avira\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Avira\\"))))

au: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Markus Neis, Tim Shelton (HAWK.IO), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

When cmd.exe and xcopy.exe are called directly
When the command contains the keywords but not in the correct order

t: Suspicious Creation TXT File in User Desktop
de: Detects creation of .txt files in user desktop folders via cmd.exe. This behavior may indicate ransomware deploying ransom notes, but can also occur during legitimate administrative tasks. Analysts should investigate for suspicious filenames (e.g., "RANSOM", "DECRYPT", "READ_ME"), bulk file creation patterns, or concurrent encryption activity to determine if this is part of a ransomware attack.
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" and (FolderPath contains "\\Users\\" and FolderPath contains "\\Desktop\\") and FolderPath endswith ".txt"

de: Csi.exe is a signed binary from Microsoft that comes with Visual Studio and provides C# interactive capabilities. It can be used to run C# code from a file passed as a parameter in command line. Early version of this utility provided with Microsoft “Roslyn” Community Technology Preview was named 'rcsi.exe'
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\csi.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\rcsi.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("csi.exe", "rcsi.exe"))) and ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName =~ "Microsoft Corporation"

t: Suspicious Curl Change User Agents - Linux
de: Detects a suspicious curl process start on linux with set useragent options
fp: Scripts created by developers and admins
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "/curl" and (ProcessCommandLine contains " -A " or ProcessCommandLine contains " --user-agent ")

de: Detects a suspicious curl process start the adds a file to a web request
fp: Scripts created by developers and admins
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "/curl" and ((ProcessCommandLine contains " --form" or ProcessCommandLine contains " --upload-file " or ProcessCommandLine contains " --data " or ProcessCommandLine contains " --data-") or ProcessCommandLine matches regex "\\s-[FTd]\\s")) and (not((ProcessCommandLine contains "://localhost" or ProcessCommandLine contains "://127.0.0.1")))

t: Suspicious Diantz Alternate Data Stream Execution
de: Compress target file into a cab file stored in the Alternate Data Stream (ADS) of the target file.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessCommandLine contains "diantz.exe" and ProcessCommandLine contains ".cab") and ProcessCommandLine matches regex ":[^\\\\]"

t: Suspicious Diantz Download and Compress Into a CAB File
de: Download and compress a remote file and store it in a cab file on local machine.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessCommandLine contains "diantz.exe" and ProcessCommandLine contains " \\\\" and ProcessCommandLine contains ".cab"

au: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Jonhnathan Ribeiro, oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
de: Detects the execution of certutil with certain flags that allow the utility to download files.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\certutil.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "CertUtil.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "urlcache " or ProcessCommandLine contains "verifyctl " or ProcessCommandLine contains "URL ") and ProcessCommandLine contains "http"

au: Hai Vaknin @LuxNoBulIshit, Avihay eldad  @aloneliassaf, Austin Songer @austinsonger
de: Detects when a possible suspicious driver is being installed via pnputil.exe lolbin
fp: Pnputil.exe being used may be performed by a system administrator.
Verify whether the user identity, user agent, and/or hostname should be making changes in your environment.
Pnputil.exe being executed from unfamiliar users should be investigated. If known behavior is causing false positives, it can be exempted from the rule.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessCommandLine contains "-i" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/install" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-a" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/add-driver" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".inf") and FolderPath endswith "\\pnputil.exe"

t: Suspicious Driver or Device Removal via PnPUtil
de: Detects when a driver is deleted/uninstalled or a device is disabled/removed using the built-in Plug and Play Utility (pnputil.exe). This behavior is often observed when threat actors attempt to disable security product drivers (defense evasion) or uninstall drivers after exploiting them (BYOVD clean-up).
fp: System administrators or deployment scripts updating drivers by removing old versions.
Antivirus or hardware OEM software updates (e.g. Dell, Lenovo, HP update managers).
VMware Tools, VirtualBox Guest Additions, or other VM guest integration agent updates.
Device drivers uninstallation during legitimate system maintenance.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\pnputil.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "pnputil.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "delete-driver" or ProcessCommandLine contains "disable-device" or ProcessCommandLine contains "remove-device")
pr: #6099 Add detection for PnPUtil driver and device removal activity

de: Detects suspicious child processes of electron apps (teams, discord, slack, etc.). This could be a potential sign of ".asar" file tampering (See reference section for more information) or binary execution proxy through specific CLI arguments (see related rule)
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\chrome.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\discord.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\GitHubDesktop.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\keybase.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\msedge.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\msedgewebview2.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\msteams.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\slack.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\teams.exe") and ((FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\cscript.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\mshta.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\regsvr32.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\whoami.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\wscript.exe") or (FolderPath contains ":\\ProgramData\\" or FolderPath contains ":\\Temp\\" or FolderPath contains "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\" or FolderPath contains "\\Users\\Public\\" or FolderPath contains "\\Windows\\Temp\\")) and (not((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\Discord.exe" and FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" and ProcessCommandLine contains "\\NVSMI\\nvidia-smi.exe")))

t: Suspicious Execution of InstallUtil Without Log
de: Uses the .NET InstallUtil.exe application in order to execute image without log
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\InstallUtil.exe" and FolderPath contains "Microsoft.NET\\Framework" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "/logfile= " and ProcessCommandLine contains "/LogToConsole=false")

t: Suspicious Execution of Powershell with Base64
de: Commandline to launch powershell with a base64 payload
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains " -e " or ProcessCommandLine contains " -en " or ProcessCommandLine contains " -enc " or ProcessCommandLine contains " -enco" or ProcessCommandLine contains " -ec ")) and (not((ProcessCommandLine contains " -Encoding " or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "C:\\Packages\\Plugins\\Microsoft.GuestConfiguration.ConfigurationforWindows\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\gc_worker.exe"))))

de: Use of the commandline to shutdown or reboot windows
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\shutdown.exe" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "/r " or ProcessCommandLine contains "/s ")

t: Suspicious Execution of Shutdown to Log Out
de: Detects the rare use of the command line tool shutdown to logoff a user
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\shutdown.exe" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/l"

t: Suspicious Execution via macOS Script Editor
de: Detects when the macOS Script Editor utility spawns an unusual child process.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/Script Editor" and ((FolderPath endswith "/curl" or FolderPath endswith "/bash" or FolderPath endswith "/sh" or FolderPath endswith "/zsh" or FolderPath endswith "/dash" or FolderPath endswith "/fish" or FolderPath endswith "/osascript" or FolderPath endswith "/mktemp" or FolderPath endswith "/chmod" or FolderPath endswith "/php" or FolderPath endswith "/nohup" or FolderPath endswith "/openssl" or FolderPath endswith "/plutil" or FolderPath endswith "/PlistBuddy" or FolderPath endswith "/xattr" or FolderPath endswith "/sqlite" or FolderPath endswith "/funzip" or FolderPath endswith "/popen") or (FolderPath contains "python" or FolderPath contains "perl"))

t: Suspicious Extrac32 Alternate Data Stream Execution
de: Extract data from cab file and hide it in an alternate data stream
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessCommandLine contains "extrac32.exe" and ProcessCommandLine contains ".cab") and ProcessCommandLine matches regex ":[^\\\\]"

de: Download or Copy file with Extrac32
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessCommandLine contains "extrac32.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\extrac32.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "extrac32.exe") and ProcessCommandLine contains ".cab" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "/C" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/Y" or ProcessCommandLine contains " \\\\")

t: Suspicious File Characteristics Due to Missing Fields
de: Detects Executables in the Downloads folder without FileVersion,Description,Product,Company likely created with py2exe
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((ProcessVersionInfoFileDescription =~ "?" and ProcessVersionInfoProductVersion =~ "?") or (ProcessVersionInfoFileDescription =~ "?" and ProcessVersionInfoProductName =~ "?") or (ProcessVersionInfoFileDescription =~ "?" and ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName =~ "?")) and FolderPath contains "\\Downloads\\"

t: Suspicious File Characteristics Due to Missing Fields
de: Detects Executables in the Downloads folder without FileVersion,Description,Product,Company likely created with py2exe
fp: Rarely there are benign executables that have no VERSION INFORMATION that need to be base lined
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((ProcessVersionInfoFileDescription =~ "?" and ProcessVersionInfoProductVersion =~ "?") or (ProcessVersionInfoFileDescription =~ "?" and ProcessVersionInfoProductName =~ "?") or (ProcessVersionInfoFileDescription =~ "?" and ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName =~ "?") or (ProcessVersionInfoFileDescription =~ "" and ProcessVersionInfoProductVersion =~ "" and ProcessVersionInfoProductName =~ "" and ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName =~ "") or (isnull(ProcessVersionInfoFileDescription) and isnull(ProcessVersionInfoProductVersion) and isnull(ProcessVersionInfoProductName) and isnull(ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName))) and FolderPath contains "\\Downloads\\"

t: Suspicious File Characteristics Due to Missing Fields

| where ((ProcessVersionInfoFileDescription =~ "?" and ProcessVersionInfoProductVersion =~ "?") or (ProcessVersionInfoFileDescription =~ "?" and ProcessVersionInfoProductName =~ "?") or (ProcessVersionInfoFileDescription =~ "?" and ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName =~ "?")) and FolderPath contains "\\Downloads\\"

t: Suspicious Group And Account Reconnaissance Activity Using Net.EXE
au: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), omkar72, @svch0st, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
de: Detects suspicious reconnaissance command line activity on Windows systems using Net.EXE Check if the user that executed the commands is suspicious (e.g. service accounts, LOCAL_SYSTEM)
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\net.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\net1.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("net.exe", "net1.exe"))) and ((((ProcessCommandLine contains " group " or ProcessCommandLine contains " localgroup ") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "domain admins" or ProcessCommandLine contains " administrator" or ProcessCommandLine contains " administrateur" or ProcessCommandLine contains "enterprise admins" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Exchange Trusted Subsystem" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Remote Desktop Users" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Utilisateurs du Bureau à distance" or ProcessCommandLine contains "Usuarios de escritorio remoto" or ProcessCommandLine contains " /do")) and (not(ProcessCommandLine contains " /add"))) or (ProcessCommandLine contains " accounts " and ProcessCommandLine contains " /do"))

t: Suspicious IIS URL GlobalRules Rewrite Via AppCmd
de: Detects usage of "appcmd" to create new global URL rewrite rules. This behaviour has been observed being used by threat actors to add new rules so they can access their webshells.
fp: Legitimate usage of appcmd to add new URL rewrite rules
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\appcmd.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "appcmd.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "set" and ProcessCommandLine contains "config" and ProcessCommandLine contains "section:system.webServer/rewrite/globalRules" and ProcessCommandLine contains "commit:")

de: Detects the execution of suspicious child processes from macOS installer package parent process. This includes osascript, JXA, curl and wget amongst other interpreters
fp: Legitimate software uses the scripts (preinstall, postinstall)

| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/package_script_service" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/installer") and (FolderPath endswith "/sh" or FolderPath endswith "/bash" or FolderPath endswith "/dash" or FolderPath endswith "/python" or FolderPath endswith "/ruby" or FolderPath endswith "/perl" or FolderPath endswith "/php" or FolderPath endswith "/javascript" or FolderPath endswith "/osascript" or FolderPath endswith "/tclsh" or FolderPath endswith "/curl" or FolderPath endswith "/wget") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "preinstall" or ProcessCommandLine contains "postinstall")

de: Detects the keyboard preload installation with a suspicious keyboard layout, e.g. Chinese, Iranian or Vietnamese layout load in user session on systems maintained by US staff only
fp: Administrators or users that actually use the selected keyboard layouts (heavily depends on the organisation's user base)
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where (RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\Keyboard Layout\\Preload.*$" or RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\Keyboard Layout\\Substitutes.*$") and (RegistryValueData contains "00000429" or RegistryValueData contains "00050429" or RegistryValueData contains "0000042a")

t: Suspicious LNK Double Extension File Created
de: Detects the creation of files with an "LNK" as a second extension. This is sometimes used by malware as a method to abuse the fact that Windows hides the "LNK" extension by default.
fp: Some tuning is required for other general purpose directories of third party apps
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith ".lnk" and (FolderPath contains ".doc." or FolderPath contains ".docx." or FolderPath contains ".jpg." or FolderPath contains ".pdf." or FolderPath contains ".ppt." or FolderPath contains ".pptx." or FolderPath contains ".xls." or FolderPath contains ".xlsx.")) and (not(FolderPath contains "\\AppData\\Roaming\\Microsoft\\Windows\\Recent\\")) and (not((((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\excel.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\powerpnt.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\winword.exe") and FolderPath contains "\\AppData\\Roaming\\Microsoft\\Office\\Recent\\") or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\excel.exe" and FolderPath contains "\\AppData\\Roaming\\Microsoft\\Excel") or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\powerpnt.exe" and FolderPath contains "\\AppData\\Roaming\\Microsoft\\PowerPoint") or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\winword.exe" and FolderPath contains "\\AppData\\Roaming\\Microsoft\\Word"))))

t: Suspicious New Instance Of An Office COM Object
de: Detects an svchost process spawning an instance of an office application. This happens when the initial word application creates an instance of one of the Office COM objects such as 'Word.Application', 'Excel.Application', etc. This can be used by malicious actors to create malicious Office documents with macros on the fly. (See vba2clr project in the references)

DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\svchost.exe" and (FolderPath endswith "\\eqnedt32.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\excel.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\msaccess.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\mspub.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\powerpnt.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\visio.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\winword.exe")

t: Suspicious PaperCut Class File Drop in Server Lib - Linux
de: Detects the creation of potentially unexpected .class files into the server/lib directory on Linux, indicative of exploitation via CVE-2026-82078. The vulnerability allows an attacker to abuse unsafe dynamic class-loading in PaperCut's database connection utilities. After gaining unauthenticated config-write access (CVE-2026-81578), the attacker plants arbitrary Java bytecode as .class files under server/lib/, which the JVM loads and executes within the PaperCut process context.
fp: PaperCut upgrade or installation that legitimately drops class files into server/lib
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where (FolderPath contains "/PaperCut MF/" or FolderPath contains "/PaperCut NG/" or FolderPath contains "/papercut/") and FolderPath contains "/server/lib/" and FolderPath endswith ".class"
pr: #6444 new: papercut exploitation rules for CVE-2026-81578 and CVE-2026-82078

t: Suspicious PaperCut Class File Drop in Server Lib - Windows
de: Detects the creation of potentially malicious .class files into the server/lib directory, indicative of exploitation via CVE-2026-82078. The vulnerability allows an attacker to abuse unsafe dynamic class-loading in PaperCut's database connection utilities. After gaining unauthenticated config-write access (CVE-2026-81578), the attacker plants arbitrary Java bytecode as .class files under server/lib/, which the JVM loads and executes within the PaperCut process context. Active exploitation has been observed on Windows with random-named class files (e.g. Udydn.class, Moo97.class) and the Derby memory URI jdbc:derby:memory:pwn.
fp: PaperCut upgrade or installation that legitimately drops class files into server/lib
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where (FolderPath contains "\\PaperCut MF\\" or FolderPath contains "\\papercut\\" or FolderPath contains "\\PaperCut NG\\") and FolderPath contains "\\server\\lib\\" and FolderPath endswith ".class"
pr: #6444 new: papercut exploitation rules for CVE-2026-81578 and CVE-2026-82078

t: Suspicious PROCEXP152.sys File Created In TMP
de: Detects the creation of the PROCEXP152.sys file in the application-data local temporary folder. This driver is used by Sysinternals Process Explorer but also by KDU (https://github.com/hfiref0x/KDU) or Ghost-In-The-Logs (https://github.com/bats3c/Ghost-In-The- Logs), which uses KDU.
fp: Other legimate tools using this driver and filename (like Sysinternals). Note - Clever attackers may easily bypass this detection by just renaming the driver filename. Therefore just Medium-level and don't rely on it.
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where (FolderPath contains "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\" and FolderPath endswith "PROCEXP152.sys") and (not((InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\procexp64.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\procexp64a.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\procexp.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\procmon64.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\procmon64a.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\procmon.exe")))

fp: Legitimate software automatically (mostly, during installation) sets up autorun keys for legitimate reason
Legitimate administrator sets up autorun keys for legitimate reason
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where RegistryKey contains "\\Software\\Policies\\Microsoft\\Windows\\System\\Scripts" and (RegistryKey contains "\\Startup" or RegistryKey contains "\\Shutdown" or RegistryKey contains "\\Logon" or RegistryKey contains "\\Logoff") and (not(RegistryValueData =~ "(Empty)"))

de: Detects the creation of files in systemd generator directories. Systemd executes generators very early during boot and on configuration reload to dynamically generate unit files, symlinks, or drop-ins. An adversary can create a malicious generator to execute arbitrary code before regular services start and maintain persistence. System generators run as root, while user generators run with the privileges of the user session.
fp: Legitimate systemd package upgrades or custom generators deployed by administrators
Package managers or configuration management tools creating generator files
Temporary editor files created in generator directories
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where (FolderPath startswith "/etc/systemd/system-generators/" or FolderPath startswith "/etc/systemd/user-generators/" or FolderPath startswith "/lib/systemd/system-generators/" or FolderPath startswith "/lib/systemd/user-generators/" or FolderPath startswith "/run/systemd/system-generators/" or FolderPath startswith "/run/systemd/user-generators/" or FolderPath startswith "/usr/lib/systemd/system-generators/" or FolderPath startswith "/usr/lib/systemd/user-generators/" or FolderPath startswith "/usr/local/lib/systemd/system-generators/" or FolderPath startswith "/usr/local/lib/systemd/user-generators/") and (not(((InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/apk" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/apt" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/apt-get" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/dnf" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/dnf-automatic" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/dpkg" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/dpkg-divert" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/microdnf" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/pacman" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/packagekitd" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/rpm" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/snapd" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/yum" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/zypper") or (FolderPath endswith ".dpkg-new" or FolderPath endswith ".dpkg-remove" or FolderPath endswith ".swp" or FolderPath endswith ".swpx" or FolderPath endswith ".swx"))))
pr: #6519 new: Systemd Generator Created

de: Detects the use of tccutil to reset Transparency, Consent, and Control (TCC) permissions for AppleEvents or for all services. macOS infostealers such as Banshee reset AppleEvents permissions to clear previous consent decisions and re-trigger automation prompts that let them control other applications. Investigate the parent process, as legitimate resets are usually performed by administrators or MDM tooling.
fp: Administrators or MDM solutions (e.g. Jamf, Kandji) resetting TCC permissions during troubleshooting
q:

| where FolderPath endswith "/tccutil" and ProcessCommandLine contains " reset " and (ProcessCommandLine contains " AppleEvents" or ProcessCommandLine contains " All")

de: Detects when an attacker tries to disable User Account Control (UAC) notification by tampering with the "UACDisableNotify" value. UAC is a critical security feature in Windows that prevents unauthorized changes to the operating system. It prompts the user for permission or an administrator password before allowing actions that could affect the system's operation or change settings that affect other users. When "UACDisableNotify" is set to 1, UAC prompts are suppressed.
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where RegistryKey contains "\\Microsoft\\Security Center\\UACDisableNotify" and RegistryValueData =~ "DWORD (0x00000001)"

de: Detects when an attacker tries to change User Account Control (UAC) elevation request destination via the "PromptOnSecureDesktop" value. The "PromptOnSecureDesktop" setting specifically determines whether UAC prompts are displayed on the secure desktop. The secure desktop is a separate desktop environment that's isolated from other processes running on the system. It's designed to prevent malicious software from intercepting or tampering with UAC prompts. When "PromptOnSecureDesktop" is set to 0, UAC prompts are displayed on the user's current desktop instead of the secure desktop. This reduces the level of security because it potentially exposes the prompts to manipulation by malicious software.
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where RegistryKey contains "\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Policies\\System\\PromptOnSecureDesktop" and RegistryValueData =~ "DWORD (0x00000000)"

de: Detects attempts to disable the Uncomplicated Firewall (UFW) on Linux systems. UFW is a popular firewall management tool that provides an easy-to-use interface for configuring firewall rules. Disabling UFW can leave a system vulnerable to attacks, as it may allow unauthorized access to network services and resources.
fp: Legitimate actions by system administrators to disable UFW.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "/ufw-init" and (ProcessCommandLine contains " force-stop" or ProcessCommandLine contains " stop" or ProcessCommandLine contains " flush")) or (ProcessCommandLine contains "ufw " and ProcessCommandLine contains "disable")

t: Uncommon Connection to Active Directory Web Services
de: Detects uncommon network connections to the Active Directory Web Services (ADWS) from processes not typically associated with ADWS management.
fp: ADWS is used by a number of legitimate applications that need to interact with Active Directory. These applications should be added to the allow-listing to avoid false positives.

DeviceNetworkEvents
| where RemotePort == 9389 and (not((InitiatingProcessFolderPath =~ "C:\\Windows\\system32\\dsac.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath =~ "C:\\Program Files\\Microsoft Monitoring Agent\\" or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files\\PowerShell\\7\\pwsh.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files\\PowerShell\\7-preview\\pwsh.ex" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\System32\\WindowsPowerShell\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\WindowsPowerShell\\"))))

de: Detects an uncommon parent process of "LINK.EXE". Link.EXE in Microsoft incremental linker. Its a utility usually bundled with Visual Studio installation. Multiple utilities often found in the same folder (editbin.exe, dumpbin.exe, lib.exe, etc) have a hardcode call to the "LINK.EXE" binary without checking its validity. This would allow an attacker to sideload any binary with the name "link.exe" if one of the aforementioned tools get executed from a different location. By filtering the known locations of such utilities we can spot uncommon parent process of LINK.EXE that might be suspicious or malicious.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\link.exe" and ProcessCommandLine contains "LINK /") and (not(((InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files\\Microsoft Visual Studio\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Microsoft Visual Studio\\") and (InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\VC\\bin\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\VC\\Tools\\"))))

t: Uncommon System Information Discovery Via Wmic.EXE

t: USB Storage Service Disabled Via Registry
de: Detects when the USBSTOR service is disabled via the registry by setting its Start value to 4 (disabled). Malware uses this to prevent USB storage devices from being mounted, which stops defenders from introducing recovery tools or bootable media via USB, and prevents potential data exfiltration paths from being used.
fp: Legitimate administrative hardening policies that disable USB storage on corporate endpoints

t: Use Short Name Path in Command Line
de: Detects the use of short name paths (8.3 format) in command lines, which can be used to obfuscate paths or access restricted locations. Windows creates short 8.3 filenames (like PROGRA~1) for compatibility with MS-DOS-based or 16-bit Windows programs. When investigating, examine: - Commands using short paths to access sensitive directories or files - Web servers on Windows (especially Apache) where short filenames could bypass security controls - Correlation with other suspicious behaviors - baseline of short name usage in your environment and look for deviations

q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessCommandLine contains "~1\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains "~2\\") and (not(((InitiatingProcessFolderPath in~ ("C:\\Windows\\System32\\Dism.exe", "C:\\Windows\\System32\\cleanmgr.exe")) or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\winget.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath contains "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\WinGet\\") or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\Microsoft.NET\\Framework64\\v" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\csc.exe") or ((FolderPath contains "\\AppData\\" and FolderPath contains "\\Temp\\") or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\")))) and (not((InitiatingProcessFolderPath =~ "C:\\Program Files\\GPSoftware\\Directory Opus\\dopus.exe" or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\aurora-agent-64.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\aurora-agent.exe") or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\thor\\thor64.exe" or (ProcessCommandLine contains "C:\\Program Files\\Git\\post-install.bat" or ProcessCommandLine contains "C:\\Program Files\\Git\\cmd\\scalar.exe") or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\WebEx\\webexhost.exe" or ProcessCommandLine contains "\\appdata\\local\\webex\\webex64\\meetings\\wbxreport.exe") or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\veeam.backup.shell.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\Everything\\Everything.exe")))

| where (ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "wmic.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\WMIC.exe") and ProcessCommandLine contains " qfe"

de: Detects execution of the Windows Kernel Debugger "kd.exe".
fp: Rare occasions of legitimate cases where kernel debugging is necessary in production. Investigation is required
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\kd.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "kd.exe"

t: Windows Recall Feature Enabled - DisableAIDataAnalysis Value Deleted
de: Detects the enabling of the Windows Recall feature via registry manipulation. Windows Recall can be enabled by deleting the existing "DisableAIDataAnalysis" registry value. Adversaries may enable Windows Recall as part of post-exploitation discovery and collection activities. This rule assumes that Recall is already explicitly disabled on the host, and subsequently enabled by the adversary.
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where (ActionType in~ ("RegistryKeyDeleted", "RegistryValueDeleted")) and (ActionType =~ "DeleteValue" and RegistryKey endswith "\\Microsoft\\Windows\\WindowsAI\\DisableAIDataAnalysis")

de: Detects the enabling of the Windows Recall feature via registry manipulation. Windows Recall can be enabled by setting the value of "DisableAIDataAnalysis" to "0". Adversaries may enable Windows Recall as part of post-exploitation discovery and collection activities. This rule assumes that Recall is already explicitly disabled on the host, and subsequently enabled by the adversary.
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where RegistryKey endswith "\\Software\\Policies\\Microsoft\\Windows\\WindowsAI\\DisableAIDataAnalysis" and RegistryValueData =~ "DWORD (0x00000000)"

t: Windows Recall Feature Enabled Via Reg.EXE
de: Detects the enabling of the Windows Recall feature via registry manipulation. Windows Recall can be enabled by deleting the existing "DisableAIDataAnalysis" value, or setting it to 0. Adversaries may enable Windows Recall as part of post-exploitation discovery and collection activities. This rule assumes that Recall is already explicitly disabled on the host, and subsequently enabled by the adversary.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\reg.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "reg.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "Microsoft\\Windows\\WindowsAI" and ProcessCommandLine contains "DisableAIDataAnalysis") and ((ProcessCommandLine contains "add" or ProcessCommandLine contains "0") or ProcessCommandLine contains "delete")

de: Alerts on trust record modification within the registry, indicating usage of macros
fp: This will alert on legitimate macro usage as well, additional tuning is required
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where RegistryKey contains "\\Security\\Trusted Documents\\TrustRecords"

t: Windows Terminal Profile Settings Modification By Uncommon Process
de: Detects the creation or modification of the Windows Terminal Profile settings file "settings.json" by an uncommon process.
fp: Some false positives may occur with admin scripts that set WT settings.
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\cscript.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\mshta.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\wscript.exe") and FolderPath endswith "\\AppData\\Local\\Packages\\Microsoft.WindowsTerminal_8wekyb3d8bbwe\\LocalState\\settings.json"

de: Detects registry modifications that disable Windows Update automatic updates or block access to the Windows Update service entirely. Malware and ransomware commonly disable Windows Update to prevent security patches from being applied and to stop update-triggered reboots that could interfere with their operation.
fp: Legitimate disabling of Windows Update via Group Policy or other administrative tools
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where (RegistryKey contains "\\SOFTWARE\\Policies\\Microsoft\\Windows\\WindowsUpdate" or RegistryKey contains "\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Policies\\Explorer" or RegistryKey contains "\\SYSTEM\\Internet Communication Management\\Internet Communication") and (RegistryKey endswith "\\AU\\NoAutoUpdate" or RegistryKey endswith "\\DisableWindowsUpdateAccess") and RegistryValueData =~ "DWORD (0x00000001)"
pr: #6236 new: closes #4542 - add rules for IFEO Debugger tampering, disabling usb storage and windowsupdate

de: Detects when the 'AllowMultipleTSSessions' value is enabled. Which allows for multiple Remote Desktop connection sessions to be opened at once. This is often used by attacker as a way to connect to an RDP session without disconnecting the other users
fp: Legitimate use of the multi session functionality
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where RegistryKey endswith "\\Microsoft\\Windows NT\\CurrentVersion\\Winlogon\\AllowMultipleTSSessions" and RegistryValueData endswith "DWORD (0x00000001)"

de: Detects execution of WinRAR in order to compress a file with a ".dmp"/".dump" extension, which could be a step in a process of dump file exfiltration.
fp: Legitimate use of WinRAR with a command line in which ".dmp" or ".dump" appears accidentally
Legitimate use of WinRAR to compress WER ".dmp" files for troubleshooting
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\rar.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\winrar.exe") or ProcessVersionInfoFileDescription =~ "Command line RAR") and (ProcessCommandLine contains ".dmp" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".dump" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".hdmp")

de: Detects a suspicious WinRAR execution in a folder which is not the default installation folder
fp: Legitimate use of WinRAR in a folder of a software that bundles WinRAR
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\rar.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\winrar.exe") or (ProcessVersionInfoFileDescription in~ ("Command line RAR", "WinRAR"))) and (not((FolderPath endswith "\\UnRAR.exe" or (FolderPath contains ":\\Program Files (x86)\\WinRAR\\" or FolderPath contains ":\\Program Files\\WinRAR\\")))) and (not(FolderPath contains ":\\Windows\\Temp\\"))

de: Detects modification of autostart extensibility point (ASEP) in registry.

t: WinSxS Executable File Creation By Non-System Process
de: Detects the creation of binaries in the WinSxS folder by non-system processes
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where (FolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\WinSxS\\" and FolderPath endswith ".exe") and (not((InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\Systems32\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "C:\\Windows\\WinSxS\\")))

t: WMI ActiveScriptEventConsumers Activity Via Scrcons.EXE DLL Load
de: Detects signs of the WMI script host process "scrcons.exe" loading scripting DLLs which could indicates WMI ActiveScriptEventConsumers EventConsumers activity.
fp: Dell computers on some versions register an event consumer that is known to cause false positives when brightness is changed by the corresponding keyboard button
q:
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\scrcons.exe" and (FolderPath endswith "\\vbscript.dll" or FolderPath endswith "\\wbemdisp.dll" or FolderPath endswith "\\wshom.ocx" or FolderPath endswith "\\scrrun.dll")

de: Detects the execution of a script event consumer. When scrcons.exe launches, it does so in response to the creation of an ActiveScriptEventConsumer instance and will execute registered JScript or VBScript code as a result. Script event consumers are a built-in Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) class that automatically executes a predefined script (in VBScript or JScript) whenever a specific system event occurs. Adversaries often abuse script event consumers to maintain persistence on a compromised host by executing a malicious script whenever a specific event occurs.
fp: Dell computers on some versions register an event consumer that is known to cause false positives when brightness is changed by the corresponding keyboard button
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath =~ "C:\\WINDOWS\\system32\\wbem\\scrcons.exe" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath =~ "C:\\Windows\\System32\\svchost.exe"

de: Detects the execution of a script event consumer. When scrcons.exe launches, it does so in response to the creation of an ActiveScriptEventConsumer instance and will execute registered JScript or VBScript code as a result. Script event consumers are a built-in Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) class that automatically executes a predefined script (in VBScript or JScript) whenever a specific system event occurs. Adversaries often abuse script event consumers to maintain persistence on a compromised host by executing a malicious script whenever a specific event occurs.
fp: Dell computers on some versions register an event consumer that is known to cause false positives when brightness is changed by the corresponding keyboard button
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath =~ "C:\\WINDOWS\\system32\\wbem\\scrcons.exe" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath =~ "C:\\Windows\\System32\\svchost.exe"

de: Detects execution of wbemtest.exe, the interactive WMI Test GUI. It is rarely used legitimately on endpoints and can be abused to query WMI, instantiate classes for execution, and create persistence (WMI event subscriptions) interactively.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "\\wbemtest.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "wbemtest.exe"
pr: #6094 Add Sysinternals tooling and driver/UAC detection rules

de: Detects threat actors proxy executing code and bypassing application controls by leveraging wmic and the `/FORMAT` argument switch to download and execute an XSL file (i.e js, vbs, etc). It could be an indicator of SquiblyTwo technique, which uses Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) to execute malicious code.
fp: The command wmic os get lastbootuptime loads vbscript.dll
The command wmic os get locale loads vbscript.dll

Since the ImageLoad event doesn't have enough information in this case. It's better to look at the recent process creation events that spawned the WMIC process and investigate the command line and parent/child processes to get more insights
q:
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\wmic.exe" and (FolderPath endswith "\\jscript.dll" or FolderPath endswith "\\vbscript.dll")

de: Detects the execution of WMIC to query information on a remote system
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\WMIC.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "wmic.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "-node:" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/node:" or ProcessCommandLine contains "–node:" or ProcessCommandLine contains "—node:" or ProcessCommandLine contains "―node:")) and (not((ProcessCommandLine contains "localhost" or ProcessCommandLine contains "127.0.0.1")))

t: Wow6432Node Windows NT CurrentVersion Autorun Keys Modification
au: Victor Sergeev, Daniil Yugoslavskiy, Gleb Sukhodolskiy, Timur Zinniatullin, oscd.community, Tim Shelton, frack113 (split)
de: Detects modification of autostart extensibility point (ASEP) in registry.
fp: Legitimate software automatically (mostly, during installation) sets up autorun keys for legitimate reason
Legitimate administrator sets up autorun keys for legitimate reason
q:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where (RegistryKey contains "\\SOFTWARE\\Wow6432Node\\Microsoft\\Windows NT\\CurrentVersion" and (RegistryKey contains "\\Windows\\Appinit_Dlls" or RegistryKey contains "\\Image File Execution Options" or RegistryKey contains "\\Drivers32")) and (not((RegistryValueData =~ "(Empty)" or isnull(RegistryValueData) or RegistryValueData endswith "\\Microsoft\\Windows NT\\CurrentVersion\\Image File Execution Options")))

de: Detects applications trying to modify the registry in order to disable any write-protect property for storage devices. This could be a precursor to a ransomware attack and has been an observed technique used by cypherpunk group.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessCommandLine contains "\\System\\CurrentControlSet\\Control" and ProcessCommandLine contains "Write Protection" and ProcessCommandLine contains "0" and ProcessCommandLine contains "storage"

de: Aversaries may use to interact with a remote network share using Server Message Block (SMB). This technique is used by post-exploitation frameworks.
q:
DeviceFileEvents
| where FolderPath contains "\\\\127.0.0" and FolderPath contains "\\ADMIN$\\"

t: Writing Of Malicious Files To The Fonts Folder
de: Monitors for the hiding possible malicious files in the C:\Windows\Fonts\ location. This folder doesn't require admin privillege to be written and executed from.
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (ProcessCommandLine contains "echo" or ProcessCommandLine contains "copy" or ProcessCommandLine contains "type" or ProcessCommandLine contains "file createnew" or ProcessCommandLine contains "cacls") and ProcessCommandLine contains "C:\\Windows\\Fonts\\" and (ProcessCommandLine contains ".sh" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".exe" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".dll" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".bin" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".bat" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".cmd" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".js" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".msh" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".reg" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".scr" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".ps" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".vb" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".jar" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".pl" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".inf" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".cpl" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".hta" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".msi" or ProcessCommandLine contains ".vbs")

| where ProcessCommandLine contains "Wscript." and ProcessCommandLine contains ".Shell" and ProcessCommandLine contains ".Run"

q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\wsl.exe" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\wslhost.exe") and ((FolderPath endswith "\\calc.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\cmd.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\cscript.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\mshta.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\powershell.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\pwsh.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\regsvr32.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\rundll32.exe" or FolderPath endswith "\\wscript.exe") or (FolderPath contains "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\" or FolderPath contains "C:\\Users\\Public\\" or FolderPath contains "C:\\Windows\\Temp\\" or FolderPath contains "C:\\Temp\\" or FolderPath contains "\\Downloads\\" or FolderPath contains "\\Desktop\\"))

t: XBAP Execution From Uncommon Locations Via PresentationHost.EXE
de: Detects the execution of ".xbap" (Browser Applications) files via PresentationHost.EXE from an uncommon location. These files can be abused to run malicious ".xbap" files any bypass AWL
q:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ((FolderPath endswith "\\presentationhost.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "PresentationHost.exe") and ProcessCommandLine contains ".xbap") and (not((ProcessCommandLine contains " C:\\Windows\\" or ProcessCommandLine contains " C:\\Program Files")))
